author: clintonjrobinson
body:
## What

Milestone 17b of D58 (the engine as one Rust library every server links). Stacked on #357 (the `types` generator writes `<T>Behaviors`).

A type in a DB schema that composes a behavior is now an **engine type**:
- Its instances are the engine's, in that DB service's database.
- `sql`, `orm` and migrations leave it out.
- A new `enginedoc` generator writes the document a server will hand the engine: namespace, meta-schema, tool options, behaviors, and one schema-file document per engine type.

API generators and the server generator still refuse an engine type, naming themselves. Milestone 18 lifts that when servers open the engine.

## Changes

- **Engine types and their refusals,** checked before any generator runs, one line per problem:
  - an engine type reaching a table, or holding another engine type. Use Links (D16).
  - a table, value type, queue message or projection referencing an engine type.
  - table-only declarations on an engine type: `@versioned`, `@optimistic`, a version graph, User or UserRole, a queue, a projection, `@jsonField`, `AutoGenerate` fields.
  - maps and unions in an engine type's closure, which today's engine refuses.
  - a behavior on an API's own type: behaviors compose on DB types.
- **sql, orm and sqlmigrate leave engine types out:** no table, no repository, no migration step. Turning an existing table into an engine type shows in a migration plan as dropping the table.
- **`enginedoc`:**
  - Last in the DB pipeline (`sql, orm, types, enginedoc`).
  - Writes `engine/<db>.json` in the Go types module, with constants `EngineDocument` (Go), `engineDocument` (TypeScript, exported only from `<types>/engine` so client bundles skip it) and `ENGINE_DOCUMENT` (Rust).
  - Removes a stale document when engine types go away.
  - Document version 1 holds:
    - the namespace;
    - the D11 tool options, in `EngineOptions.tools`'s shape;
    - each behavior with its package;
    - one `format --to=json` document per engine type, with the type and the value types, enums and scalars it reaches, and no imports;
    - the meta-schema from `schemafile.DefinitionFor` with the build's registry, as `superschematic json-schema` writes it, so extension decorators load.
  - Contract: `internal/generator/enginedoc/README.md`.
- **`outputs.engine.namespace`:** sets the namespace. It defaults to the DB service's name, checked against the engine's rule.
- **`RendersBehaviors`:**
  - Set on `sql`, `orm`, `enginedoc` and `envConfig`, so General schemas with behaviors build too.
  - Also set on acme's manifest generator, which lists type names only.
  - The cli tests, registrytest, the acme ext test, smoke.sh and the acme README are updated.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/extension-model.md`: §3.16, the core generator table and §7.
  - The CLI reference, the extension guide and the database tables guide.
  - The engine-behaviors guide gains "Engine types" and "The engine document".

## Verification

- **Fixture:** `fixture-engine-db-json`: tables Customer and Agent, value types Address and ContactCard, and engine types Account and Ticket with Workflow, Comments, Timers, and Links from Ticket to Account.
  - Goldens for the document and its constants, and for Postgres and SQLite DDL and the ORM, showing no engine types.
  - Migration models for both dialects.
  - The generated Go types and ORM compile.
- **`TestEngineDocumentLoadsInTheEngine`:** the generated document loads in today's `@superschematic/engine` under Bun.
  - It defines and publishes every schema, then creates an Account and a Ticket linked to it.
  - It checks normalization, defaults, Workflow, the link and the Timers deadline, and type-checks the TS types package.
  - It ran with `SUPERSCHEMATIC_REQUIRE_TS_CHECKS=1`.
- **Unit tests:** every refusal, imported-type inlining, extension packages, a custom invocation policy and tool hooks.
- **Commands:**
  - `make behaviors-check schema-file-types-check catalog-check cli-smoke`. cli-smoke now builds the engine fixture and checks the document exists and that the DDL has no `ticket` table.
  - gofmt, `go vet`, golangci-lint and the scrub check.
- **`go test ./...`:** passes except failures that come from main:
  - servergen's `TestEntrypointCompilesAndServes`: a worker missing `SHOP_MEDIA_BUCKET_NAME`, from #336 meeting #334.
  - servergen's Docker tests.
  - acme ext's `TestCoreRegistryHasNoAcmeSurface`: it expects core kinds without Bucket and Site, which D54/D55 added.
  - A tsrestgen runtime test raced a concurrent rebuild of the http runtime, and passes alone.

author: faofha
body:
## HappaTAS V2.37: fewer lines, more performance

`wow` is now V2.37. It keeps every feature, and old `.tas` files still load. Recording, saving, loading,
optimizing and playback give the same results as V2.36. This was checked with frame-by-frame traces of
both builds in the headless mock. **It has not been tested in a live Roblox game.**

This PR also contains the commit from #1 (V2.36 source and tests), so merging this one is enough.

### Fewer lines
| | V2.36 | V2.37 |
|---|---|---|
| `wow` (the file you run) | 10,045 lines, 414 KB | 8,721 lines, 331 KB |
| Code only (no comments / blank lines) | 9,036 lines | 8,719 lines |

- The menus are built from compact data. Each style is a base for its class plus what differs from it,
  and helpers build the rows, help entries and update log. The built interface is identical: the test
  compares every instance and property.
- Repeated code is shared:
  - core: `holdAt`, `unpauseFrom`, `holdPose`, `liveRows`
  - client objects: `listRemove`, `restorePart`
  - animation engine: `pick`
  - menu: merge buttons, mobile tabs
- `wow` is a release build with comments and blank lines removed (`tools/release.sh`). The commented
  source stays in `src/parts/`.

### More performance
Engine calls (property reads and method calls) per frame, from the headless benchmark. About 11 of
these per frame are the mock's own.

| Mode | V2.36 | V2.37 |
|---|---|---|
| Idle (stats on) | 28 | 18 |
| Create, recording | 46 | 33 |
| Create, paused | 37 | 16 |
| Test playback | 54 | 43 |
| Recording with Sync Client Objects (400 parts) | 2,473 | 904 |
| Paused with client objects | 481 | 72 |
| Playback with client objects | 504 | 98 |

Changes:
- **Client objects**
  - Transparency, CanCollide, Color, Size, Material and Anchored are tracked with change signals instead
    of being read every frame.
  - Properties are still re-read on the same frames as before, but only when one of them changed.
  - A part whose CFrame didn't change skips the velocity maths.
  - Poses and property writes are reused while a part's state is the same.
  - Poses are built with fewer CFrames.
  - The decoder uses `bit32` flag tests.
- **Stats panel:** it remembers what it wrote instead of reading it back.
- **Per frame:** no closure for `Humanoid:ChangeState`, no `AdjustSpeed` when the speed didn't change, and
  the menu check only runs when the cursor needs it.
- **Startup:** style enums are resolved once per style, and properties are set without a closure each.

### New tools
- `tools/test_all.sh`: every suite, plus the traces when given an old build.
- `tools/diff_builds.sh`: behaviour trace of two builds. Tests: `test_diff.lua`, `test_diffco.lua`.
- `tests/test_bench.lua`: cost per frame in every mode.
- `tools/strip.py` and `tools/release.sh`: the release build.

All suites pass (smoke, profiler, core, scale, perf, textline), headless.

author: nick-potts
body:
The verify lab can now run each Machine on its own daemon, so a check can cover a Cluster where Servers run different Ployz versions.

```bash
run=$(scripts/verify-cluster up --machines 2 --cloud --daemon checkout --daemon machine-2=0.2.3)
scripts/verify-cluster update "$run" --daemon machine-2=checkout   # one Machine, downgrades included
SERVERS=2 DAEMON="checkout machine-2=0.2.3" dashboard/scripts/verify/up.sh
```

## What changed

- `--daemon [MACHINE=]SOURCE` repeats on `up` and `update`. A bare source sets every Machine. A named source overrides one Machine. On `update`, Machines it does not name keep their source.
- The manifest stores `daemon` (source, version, binary hashes) on each Machine. `doctor` checks each Machine's running hash and its `ployzd version` output against that Machine's choice. On `--cloud` runs it also checks that Cloud reports each Machine's `daemon_version`.
- When every Machine boots the same release, the run still uses that release's cached image. A mixed run boots the base image and installs each Machine's daemon.
- `releases.prepare` became `releases.resolve`, which only names a version. `acquire` is unchanged.
- The skill docs drop the "daemon version must equal the CLI version" rule. That rule was wrong, as the next section shows.

## Cloud enrollment: harness bridge, `synchronize_daemon` untouched

The first live run had machine-2 boot the 0.2.3 release and join Cloud directly. 0.2.3 reports version `0.2.3`, the same as main's CLI. The join still failed:

```
ssh://root@… runs a Ployz that cannot report its join token. Upgrade Ployz on this Server, then retry.
```

So an equal version string does not mean an equal protocol. A release Machine on a `--cloud` run now enrolls on the checkout daemon. Right after enrollment, the harness installs that Machine's release. The one exception is when HEAD is the `v<version>` tag commit of the release. The harness can do this on its own, so `synchronize_daemon` needed no change. One side effect is that `--cloud --daemon stable` off a release commit now compiles the daemon.

Installing a release older than 0.2.4 also removes the `ployz-observe` unit that a newer daemon left behind. 0.2.3 ships no observer. Before this change, the leftover unit pointed at a binary that no longer existed.

## Live evidence

Run `20261013T055145-42da24b691`, Incus, `--cloud`, 2 Machines, machine-1 on checkout and machine-2 on 0.2.3:

- `up` took 183 s in total (build 14 s, boot and install 120 s, join and ready 62 s). `doctor` passed. machine-1 ran ployzd sha256 `0d31016ee5ac…`. machine-2 ran the 0.2.3 release, sha256 `fa9465fcf6cb…`. Both report `0.2.3`. Cloud's `server ls` listed both as up with daemon 0.2.3.
- `update --daemon machine-2=checkout` and then `update --daemon machine-2=0.2.3` each passed `doctor`. That covers an upgrade and a downgrade of one Machine.
- The first attempt, `20261013T054903-d59239bc1e`, failed with the join-token error quoted above and tore itself down.

## Product findings (reported, not fixed here)

1. **Deploy to a 0.2.3 Server fails with an empty cause.** With machine-2 on 0.2.3, a Cloud deploy of a 2-replica busybox Service failed on machine-2 with `create Container failed` and cause `[""]`. machine-1 was marked `not attempted`. machine-2's ployz journal logged nothing for the request, so the request is probably rejected before it reaches the handler (inferred). After `update --daemon machine-2=checkout` the same deploy succeeded on both Machines.
2. **Logs on a mixed Cluster.** I could not reproduce "older Server shows empty logs". With machine-2 back on 0.2.3, `ployz logs ticker --since 1m` through Cloud printed machine-1's 31 lines and exited 3 with `Server machine-2 needs a newer Ployz. It cannot serve ployz.logs.history.v2.` The older Server produces an explicit refusal, not empty output. With both Machines on checkout, logs showed lines from both.

## Not proven

- `--cloud --daemon stable` on a release tag commit, the path that skips the bridge, was not run live.
- `up.sh` with `SERVERS=N DAEMON=...` was checked with `bash -n` only.
- Join and update readiness came close to the 60 s `wait_ready` deadline but passed.

author: prabhu
body:
Moves chen to Scala 3.10.0 and sbt 2.0.10.

Most of the work is sbt 2 rather than Scala. sbt-antlr4 and sbt-github-packages have no sbt 2 builds, so a small in-process ANTLR task and a GitHub Packages auto-plugin take their place, and the build files are now Scala 3. A few sbt 2 defaults would have changed behaviour quietly, so they are pinned back:

- bare settings in the root build.sbt now apply to every subproject, so `publish / skip` and `createDistribution` live on the root project (otherwise `sbt publish` publishes nothing)
- suites run one at a time inside the forked test JVM (`testForkedParallel := false`), and test resources stay plain files (`Test / exportJars := false`)
- packaged projects stage under their own `target/universal/stage` again, where the frontend scripts expect them
- delombok gets lombok's jar explicitly, since sbt 2's test worker has a different `java.class.path`

CI runs `testFull` because sbt 2's `test` only reruns what changed, and calls `sbt --server "a; b"`: on Windows the thin client exits 0 even when a command fails, and PowerShell hands `"a;b"` to sbt.bat unquoted, which splits it. `COURSIER_REPOSITORIES` now uses the pipe separator coursier expects.

Tested on macOS and Windows 11 ARM64 with `testFull` (the edga tests ran on macOS against a local edga build), `createDistribution`, and atom's suite against a local publish of this branch. Artifacts built with 3.10 need consumers on Scala 3.10 or later, so https://github.com/AppThreat/atom/pull/281 should land with it.

author: petterannerwall
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"petterannerwall"} -->
_Requested by **Petter** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01CCrkz4xcSSvCuB3AaZXULJ?thread=cmsg_01CCrkz4xcSSvCuB3AaZXULJ81E7Gzi2hX8QCqm6H5zHHP)_

## What and why

CI now fails a change to what only the paid evals can test (the agent file `voice/agent.py`, the Business facts `voice/business.txt`, and the `pipecat-ai` line of `pyproject.toml`) unless a receipt from a passing full `make eval` matches those files. Closes PET-46.

Rebased onto `main` after PET-45 (#6) and the manual Evals workflow (#9) merged; the workflow's full run already prints the receipt this writes.

```text
make eval (full, all passed)  ->  node scripts/eval-receipt.js write  ->  eval-receipt.json {file: sha256}
CI: make guards -> eval-required.js
  listed file changed vs $GUARD_BASE? no  -> pass
                                      yes -> recompute hashes; differ from receipt -> fail, fix = `make eval`
```

Evidence: on the real repo, editing `voice/agent.py` made the guard fail; after `eval-receipt.js write` it passed. In a scratch copy: stale receipt, missing receipt, changed pin and a missing listed file fail; an unrelated change, a fresh receipt and CRLF line endings pass. The committed fixture makes the self-test fail as the contract requires. `make check` is green.

## First principles

1. **Why did the problem occur?** The evals are paid and local, so nothing ties a prompt edit to a run; an agent can change the prompt and merge without one. The fix is a receipt of the files an eval run saw, checked in CI, which never runs the evals.
2. **What could be removed or simplified instead?** One config (`scripts/eval-required.json`), one hash function shared by the writer and the guard (rule 5), no change to the fenced `tests/evals/run.py` (the Makefile target writes the receipt, and PET-44 is rewriting run.py). Left out: scenario ids and timestamps in the receipt, a parity test with `low-risk-paths.json`'s "never" list.
3. **Is this the best solution, or just the proposed one?** It is the ticket's design. Alternative considered: Python hashing inside run.py, which would be a second implementation of the hash and conflict with PET-44.

## Not live yet

- **No `eval-receipt.json` is committed.** Until a full `make eval` passes (Petter's PC or the manual Evals workflow, his approval) and the receipt is committed, any PR that changes `voice/agent.py`, `voice/business.txt` or the pipecat pin fails this guard. PET-44's eval run will produce it.
- Known limits: a hand-written receipt passes (review checks it came from `make eval`); an edit to the list, the hash code or the guard does not trigger it, but those are `scripts/` files that `merge-check` never calls low-risk. `voice/web.py` and the Scenarios/checks are not on the list (DECISIONS.md); the evals-approved fence already covers `tests/evals/**`.
- Not built: the open offer to let re-recorded Caller audio skip the `evals-approved` label (logged in DECISIONS.md).

## Checklist

- [x] `CLAUDE.md` § Definition of Done holds (check green; skeptic-pass skipped: no Stop and ask area touched, the guard runs no evals and spends nothing; DECISIONS.md lines added)

**Merge danger:** two-way door (revert the guard and Makefile line); blast radius is CI for PRs touching the listed files.

- [#351](https://github.com/reg-viz/storycap-testrun/pull/351) [`b07db94`](https://github.com/reg-viz/storycap-testrun/commit/b07db947042aebe2d030032af2175dbb8dfacc65) Thanks [@re-taro](https://github.com/re-taro)! - Only rewrite the tester iframe's inline style when its size has to change

On Linux tiling compositors (reported on Hyprland), a second Herdr window has no close button, and nothing in the menus closes a window, so there was no way to close it from the app.

This adds a **Close Window** command, built the same way as Cycle Through Windows:

- **Window menu**: Close Window, after Cycle Through Windows.
- **Keybinding**: `ctrl-alt-w` on Linux (next to New Window's `ctrl-alt-n`) and `cmd-alt-shift-w` on macOS (`cmd-w`/`cmd-shift-w` already close panes and tabs). You can change it under `[keybindings]` as `close_window`.

author: intikhab49
body:
The archiving that `tools/mark_checked.py` did by hand now runs every Monday as part of the watch workflow.

**What the weekly watch does now**
- `verify` (unchanged): a changed or removed page opens or updates the `watch` issue and fails the run.
- `archive` (new): when no page changed or disappeared, it runs `tools/mark_checked.py`. Every page's checked date moves forward. Each page Microsoft has updated gets a new Wayback Machine snapshot, which is recorded only if the cited rows are in it. The job then rebuilds the site, runs the tests and opens one pull request from `re-confirm/main`. Later runs rebuild that same pull request from `main` until it is merged.
- `stale` (unchanged): goes red when a page hasn't been re-confirmed for 90 days, which now means those pull requests stopped being merged.

**`tools/mark_checked.py`**
- `--summary FILE` writes the pull request's description: the pages Microsoft updated, their new snapshots, and the pages left alone.
- A page whose snapshot fails keeps its old `page_updated`, so the next run tries again. Before this change the date moved forward anyway and the retry was lost.
- It stops asking the Wayback Machine after 3 failures in a row, since each try can take minutes.

The weekly commits are authored as intikhab49 and committed by github-actions[bot]. A pull request opened by a workflow doesn't start the `ci` workflow, so the archive job runs the tests itself and links that run in the description.

**Tested**
- 54 tests pass (4 new). actionlint is clean.
- End to end on a throwaway branch, with one page's date set back a day to force a real snapshot:
  - Run 1 ([log](https://github.com/intikhab49/fairfax/actions/runs/38373296121)): `verify`, `archive` and `stale` passed in about a minute. From GitHub's runner it saved a Wayback Machine snapshot of `ctc-overview`, checked that the snapshot holds the cited rows, re-confirmed 33 of 33 pages, ran the 54 tests and opened #2. The data diff was the 33 checked dates plus that page's date and snapshot.
  - Run 2 ([log](https://github.com/intikhab49/fairfax/actions/runs/38373756771)) and run 3 ([log](https://github.com/intikhab49/fairfax/actions/runs/38374664639)) updated #2 in place instead of opening another pull request.
  - #2 was closed without merging, and both test branches were deleted.

**Repo setting changed:** "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" is now on. The job can't open its pull request without it.

**Merge the weekly pull requests with Rebase and merge.** When a person squash-merges a pull request opened by github-actions[bot], GitHub credits the bot as the commit's author even when the commit inside is authored by that person (for example `rh-gitops-midstream/release` PR 1764 and `j620656786206/vido` PR 774). Rebase and merge keeps the commit authored as intikhab49. Each weekly pull request says this in its description.

author: cao-xiao-hao
body:
## Summary

`close()` presses onto the closed stop on purpose and reports `ok = true` when it
stalled within `MotionConfig::stop_tol` (0.02 rad) of the calibrated limit.
`MotionEngine::recover_to_interior()` — the drive-in every move entry runs when
the measured position starts outside the red lines — tolerated only a flat
0.01 rad past that limit. A park in the band between the two windows was
therefore called good by one path and refused by the next with "the measured
position is outside the unit's own validated travel — automatic recovery
refused, inspect the mechanism": a message about a mechanism sitting exactly
where `close()` was told it could leave it.

The window becomes `max(kRecoveryTravelToleranceRad, stop_tol)` — at least as
wide as the tolerance the engine is allowed to call a successful press.
`kRecoveryTravelToleranceRad` keeps its own job as a **floor**, not the width: a
status frame quantized to the 0.0103 rad grid must still read as "on its stop",
so a config with a smaller `stop_tol` cannot narrow the window back into the
disagreement.

Nothing changes for a start that was already accepted. The band between 0.01
and 0.02 rad past a calibrated limit changes from a refusal to a recovery.

## Changes

- `src/motion.cpp`: `recover_to_interior()` computes
  `window_rad = std::max(kRecoveryTravelToleranceRad, config_.stop_tol)` once
  and uses it for both the low and the high bound.
- `src/motion.cpp`: the comment on `kRecoveryTravelToleranceRad` now says it is
  a floor rather than the whole window, and why.
- `test/test_motion.cpp`: `test_recovery_window_follows_stop_tol()` (registered
  in `main()`), three cases:
  - a park 0.015 rad past `pos_closed_rad` — inside `stop_tol`, so `close()`
    calls it good — now recovers, and does so through the recovery crawl;
  - 0.035 rad past the limit is still refused with `SafetyFault` and no frame
    sent, so the window is `stop_tol` wide and not unbounded;
  - a `stop_tol` of 0.002 does not narrow the window below the 0.01 floor.

## Testing

```
$ cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j"$(nproc)"
$ ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
...
14/14 Test #14: test_control_loop ................   Passed    3.17 sec

100% tests passed out of 14

Total Test time (real) =   3.25 sec
```

Negative control — the new test does catch the bug. With only `src/motion.cpp`
reverted (`git stash push src/motion.cpp`), `./build/test/test_motion` aborts on
the first case:

```
[litegrip] entering a safety mode: open (press onto the stop)
[litegrip] entering a safety mode: open: recovering from outside the red lines
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'litegrip::SafetyFault'
  what():  open: the measured position is outside the unit's own validated travel — automatic recovery refused, inspect the mechanism
exit code: 134
```

**Not reproduced on hardware.** There is no bench unit here, so the issue's own
reproduce step — a real `close()` landing more than 0.01 rad beyond
`pos_closed_rad`, followed by `grasp()` or `move_at_speed()` — was not run. The
test drives the same code path through the `FakeIo` seam the rest of
`test_motion.cpp` uses.

## Issues

Closes #15.

author: pablopardogarcia
body:
`@arizeai/openinference-instrumentation-openai` (4.4.1, the latest) records no usage on embeddings spans: its embeddings wrapper sets the vectors and nothing from `response.usage`, while its chat and completions wrappers do, and so does the Python instrumentor. An embeddings call from a Node app therefore reached Rius with no `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`: unpriced and missing from token totals.

**This is a stopgap** until the fix lands upstream (a separate PR to OpenInference JS is being opened). Raw JS traffic sent straight to the sink, without this SDK, stays without embeddings usage until that ships.

## How

`src/embeddingsUsage.ts` wraps `OpenAI.Embeddings.prototype.create` and, when the call resolves, copies `usage.prompt_tokens` / `usage.total_tokens` onto the instrumentor's embedding span as `llm.token_count.prompt` / `.total`. The normalizer already maps those to `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, exactly as for the Python instrumentor.

- **Placement is the point.** The instrumentor runs the method it wrapped inside its span's context and ends the span in its own `.then`. So this wrapper is installed on the exact build the instrumentation is about to patch, right before it patches (a `prepare` hook in `patchActiveBuild` and the injected-modules path), and ends up underneath: the active span inside it is the embedding span, and its `.then` runs before that span ends. Installed on top, it would only ever see ended spans (mutation-checked).
- **Only the embedding span:** it acts when the active span's `openinference.span.kind` is `EMBEDDING`. The instrumentor's tracer hands out its `OISpan` wrapper, which keeps the SDK span in a `span` field; attributes are read from there, writes go through the wrapper so its masking config still applies.
- **Counts only, never content**, so they survive `captureContent: false` (tested). A count already on the span is left alone; once the instrumentor records usage itself, its `.then` runs after this one and writes the same values.
- **Never breaks the call:** errors are swallowed, a non-promise result is returned untouched, and an `APIPromise` stays one (`_thenUnwrap`).
- **Teardown and re-init:** the uninstall restores the client's method when ours is on top; shutdown runs it before the instrumentation is disabled, so ours can survive underneath, deactivated, and the next `init()` reactivates it in place instead of stacking a second (tested, plus a re-init end to end). If `create` was already wrapped by someone else, nothing is installed.
- **Residual gap, same as the providers':** a CJS `openai` first required after `init()` is patched by the instrumentation's require hook alone and gets no counts.
- The two keys are spelled as literals, as `normalize.ts` spells these same instrumentor keys. They are inputs, not keys this SDK emits as conventions, and adding them to `semconv.ts` would show up in rius-semconv's parity check as unregistered SDK keys.

## Tests

- `tests/embeddingsUsage.test.ts` (12): the wrapper against a stand-in client: records on an embedding span, leaves other spans and no-span calls alone, keeps an `APIPromise`, passes non-promises through, survives an unreadable response, uninstalls, is reused rather than stacked under another wrapper, does not install over a foreign wrapper, keeps an existing count, ignores non-integer counts.
- `tests/openaiEmbeddingsUsage.test.ts` (4): real OpenAI client, real OpenInference instrumentation, `init()` pipeline: `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` arrives, still arrives with content capture off, the caller gets the client's response, and a re-init keeps recording.
- `tests/normalizeEmbeddingsAndResponseId.test.ts`: the test that pinned the missing count now expects it.
- Mutation-checked: never installing, installing on top of the instrumentation, dropping the kind check, and overwriting an existing count each fail tests.

Found while writing the tests, not changed here: the OpenInference wrapper returns a plain `Promise` for embeddings and chat, so `.withResponse()` is unavailable on instrumented calls with or without this change.

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: User enumeration and timing attack in login endpoint.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could determine valid usernames in the database by observing distinct error messages ("User doesn't exists" vs "Password is wrong") and measuring response latency differences caused by skipped bcrypt comparison.
🔧 Fix: Standardized error response to 401 with generic message 'Invalid username or password', and added dummy bcrypt hash comparison when user is not found to equalize response times.

author: abdonpijpelink
body:
[Preview](https://deploy-preview-2953--condescending-goldwasser-91acf0.netlify.app/documentation/ops-optimization/optimizer/)

The Optimizer docs page hadn't been updated in a while and needed some love.

**High level:**

- Adds documentation for the config mismatch optimizer (was missing).
- Add animated diagrams for each of the optimizers to help explain what each of them does.
- Lead with per-collection configuration of the optimizers, as Cloud users cannot edit the config.yml.

**In detail:**

Intro
- A new intro paragraph explains storage, from collections to shards to segments, and appendable vs. non-appendable segments. It now holds the link to the storage page.
- The intro introduces the optimizer and summarizes what it does, and the paragraphs flow better.
- One clause mentions calling `optimize` on Qdrant Edge, with a link to the Edge docs.

New content
- Config mismatch optimizer section 
- **Optimizer Resource Usage section (new):** covers `optimizer_cpu_budget`, `max_optimization_threads`, and `max_indexing_threads`, and links to the read-write contention page.

Diagrams
- Added four interactive animated diagrams, one per optimizer section: vacuum, merge, indexing, and config mismatch. Each one has its own `index.js` and `index.css` under `content/documentation/headless/optimizer/`.
- Added a static SVG fallback for each diagram, with alt text, in `static/documentation/ops-optimization/`.
- Gave each diagram a caption explaining what it shows.
- Removed the old generic "Segment optimization" image from the vacuum section.

Corrected facts
- The `default_segment_number` default now "depends on the number of available CPUs".
- A segment is vacuumed when *more than* 20% of its points are deleted.
- `vacuum_min_vector_number` is described in terms of points, not records.
- The deprecated `memmap_threshold` is gone.
- The intro says that at most one optimizer selects a given segment per round, and that every rebuild removes deleted points and applies the current configuration.


API configuration first
- The vacuum and merge sections each have a new update-collection snippet: `vacuum-thresholds` and `segment-number-and-size`. Both include all eight languages and the generated files.
- The indexing section uses the existing `simple` snippet.
- The YAML examples are gone from the individual sections. The text uses the API parameter names (`max_segment_size`, `indexing_threshold`) and says they're in kilobytes.
- "Per-Collection Optimizer Configuration" is renamed to "Optimizer Configuration". The old anchor is kept as a hidden `<span>`.
- That section leads with per-collection configuration and the `simple` snippet. A second paragraph says self-hosted users can set global defaults in the configuration file, and that those defaults only apply to new collections. A full YAML example covers all the optimizer settings mentioned on the page.

Review guidance: this looks like a large PR, with all the code snippets and diagram files, but the main file to review is: `qdrant-landing/content/documentation/ops-optimization/optimizer.md`

author: samarmstrong
body:
Closes #2225

`approval_actions` timestamps are naive columns holding UTC. `_row_to_pending` wrote them out with a bare `isoformat()`, so the browser parsed them as local time. A new decision then read "waiting 1 h" at UTC+1, or "0 min" west of UTC until the offset had passed.

- `core/response/approval_service.py`: `_row_to_pending` now writes `created_at`, `approved_at` and `executed_at` through the existing `_iso_utc` (`core/storage/schemas/base.py`), so each one carries `+00:00`. Empty values are handled as before. This fixes `GET /api/approvals/needs-you` and every approvals router response.
- Same file: the action id is built from `utcnow()` rather than `datetime.now()`. The format is unchanged; it now uses the same clock as `created_at`.
- `core/workflows/run_bridge_router.py`: the `resolved_at` fallback now uses `_iso_utc(utcnow())`, so it has the same shape whichever branch sets it.
- No frontend change. `waiting()` and `fmtTime()` already parse ISO strings that carry an offset correctly.

Following the groom notes, this doesn't touch other `isoformat()` call sites. One left as it is: the case header's "Opened … · 09:02" is the case row's own timestamp and still shows UTC. It belongs to the broader sweep that #2225 scoped out.

## Verification

**Ran**
- `pytest tests/unit/response tests/unit/api tests/unit/workflows -m "not external_service"`: 525 passed.
- DB-backed tests against a throwaway Postgres 16: `tests/unit/response`, `tests/unit/storage` and `test_workflow_phase_approval.py` with `-m external_service` gave 71 passed, 1 skipped. `test_needs_you.py` plus every test touching `run_bridge` gave 59 passed. New assertions: `needs_you()`'s `created_at` is `…+00:00`, and `_row_to_pending` stamps `approved_at`/`executed_at` with the offset.
- `tests/unit/storage/test_orm_schema_parity.py` (the `orm_serialization_golden.json` check): 97 passed, unaffected.
- black, isort and flake8 on the changed files: clean.
- Live API: started the backend and raised a pending approval tied to `case-tz-2225` at 09:02:23 UTC. `curl /api/approvals/needs-you` returned `"source_id": "action-20261013-090223-276023"` and `"created_at": "2026-10-13T09:02:23.276147+00:00"`. The id and `created_at` now agree on the clock.
- Live UI, Playwright driving real Chrome with `timezoneId` set, at 1440 px (the console's minimum width per `docs/design/console/PRD-phase1.md` D10) and 1920 px:
  - Case page (`/cases?case=case-tz-2225`), Africa/Lagos and America/New_York, 1440 and 1920: the card reads "Needs your decision · waiting 11 min" (or 12), which matches the real age. Before the fix, Lagos would have shown about 1 h 11 min and New York "0 min".
  - Decisions → Pending Approvals, Africa/Lagos and America/New_York, 1440 and 1920: Created shows "Oct 13, 10:02" in Lagos and "Oct 13, 05:02" in New York. Both are correct local times for 09:02 UTC.
  - No horizontal overflow on any of the 8 screen/zone/width combinations: the document's scrollWidth is not greater than its clientWidth, and no element overflows. I looked at the screenshots and the layout is unchanged, as expected for a data-only change.

**Did not run**
- The full unit and integration suites. CI runs them; I ran the suites that cover the changed code.
- An LLM-backed run. Nothing here touches model calls.

**Blocked by the machine**
- `agent-browser screenshot` hung until timeout, even on a `data:` page. Navigation and `eval` worked. I took the screenshots with `playwright-core` driving the installed Chrome instead.
- There was no Python venv in the workspace. I created one with `uv` on Python 3.12, because a default 3.11 interpreter can't resolve `numpy>=2.5.3` from `requirements.txt`.
- Ports 6987/6988 were taken by other workspaces' stacks, and the Vite proxy target is hardcoded to `127.0.0.1:6987`. I ran the backend on 6225 and Vite on 6226 through a temporary untracked config that overrides the proxy target. Postgres was a container I started by hand.

author: mryesss97
body:
## Summary

Adds `ListeningQueriesModule`: list, get, create, patch, soft delete and restore under `/api/v1/projects/:projectId/listening-queries` (FR-051…FR-057). Create normalizes the value (BR-004/BR-005), blocks active duplicates case-insensitively (BR-006, `409 QUERY_DUPLICATE {existingId}`, race-safe), and schedules the first run immediately when enabled (FR-056). PATCH rejects `queryValue`/`queryType` with `QUERY_IMMUTABLE_FIELD` (BR-009); enable/disable and restore keep `next_run_at` consistent with the scheduler claim (FR-055, BR-010). Every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction with the request id (BR-034). No migration: the table and partial unique index already exist.

Open questions from the plan were decided per the researcher's defaults and recorded on the issue (2026-10-13): `lastJob`/`matchedPosts` are placeholders until T-045, PATCH on a deleted query → 404, unknown PATCH keys are stripped, enable/disable writes its own audit action, no NFC normalization, one PR, list newest first.

## Issue

Closes #38

## Docs updated

- [ ] N/A — no behaviour/contract change
- [x] Updated: `docs/02-architecture/05-api-contract.md` §5 (edge cases: immutables, idempotent delete/restore, 409 on restore, scheduling, placeholders), `docs/01-product/04-functional-requirements.md` FR-054 (`initialBackfillDays` mutable), `docs/01-product/02-personas-rbac.md` (GET `:queryId`), `apps/api/src/modules/listening-queries/README.md`, `apps/api/src/modules/audit/README.md` (`@RequestId()`)

## Screenshots / evidence

API only, no UI change.

```
POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/listening-queries
{ "displayName": "Eventista", "queryValue": "#Eventista", "queryType": "topic_tag" }
→ 201 { "queryValue": "Eventista", "searchMode": "TAG", "scheduledSearchType": "RECENT", "enabled": true, "nextRunAt": "<now>", ... }

POST same body with "EVENTISTA"
→ 409 { "error": { "code": "QUERY_DUPLICATE", "details": { "existingId": "<id>" }, ... } }

PATCH :queryId { "queryValue": "x" }
→ 400 { "error": { "code": "QUERY_IMMUTABLE_FIELD", "details": { "fields": ["queryValue"] }, ... } }
```

## Test evidence

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: immutable-field pipe, DTO mapper, service (diff, enable/disable scheduling, audit count, P2002 race), contracts
- [x] Integration tests added/updated: `listening-queries.int-spec.ts` covers TC-LQ-002…012, roles, project scope, 404s, list filters/cursor/count, concurrent create. Uses the T-014 helpers; `sample-factories.int-spec.ts` TODO(T-042) replaced with a real `POST → GET list` case. `rbac.int-spec.ts` (TC-AUTH-012) green with the matrix switched to `implemented`.
- [x] Manually verified on local: `pnpm verify:quiet` pass, `pnpm --filter @how-about-me/api test:int` 127/127 pass on a local Postgres.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional commit title (squash merge uses it)
- [x] No secrets in code, fixtures, logs or screenshots
- [x] Role decorators on new mutations; Zod validation on inputs
- [x] Business rules referenced (`BR-xxx`) where applicable
- [x] Contracts/OpenAPI updated when API shape changed
- [x] Prisma migration reviewed: no migration in this PR
- [ ] QC task notified (link)

## Follow-ups

- `prisma/seed.ts` still checks query duplicates with `mode: "insensitive"` (ILIKE), so `_`/`%` act as wildcards. Should switch to `lower() = lower()` like the API.
- `lastJob` / `matchedPosts` are placeholders (`null`, `{0, 0}`) until T-045 (#41).
- Audit metadata for `query.updated` uses `{ fields, before, after }` instead of nested `changes`, because the audit sanitizer's depth limit would drop arrays such as `excludeTerms`.

## Definition of Done

- [x] `pnpm verify` pass trên `5d60348`: prisma generate · format:check · lint · typecheck · unit test · script test.
- [ ] E2E: repo chưa có script `test:e2e` ở root, không chạy.
- [x] Screenshot trước và sau: không cần. Branch không đổi file giao diện nào trong `apps/web/src`.

body:
Banco comune `crates/mzlab-core/tests/robustezza_comune.rs` (+ `tests/robustezza/mod.rs`): per ogni lettore (Agilent `.D`, `DATA.MS`, Thermo `.raw`, Sciex `.wiff`+`.scan`, contenitore OLE e parser dei metodi, mzML, mzidx) un seme valido e ~1500-2500 mutazioni deterministiche (xorshift a seme fisso): tagli, byte capovolti, conteggi a `u32::MAX`/`u64::MAX`, zeri, file vuoto/1 byte, ripetizione, testa valida + corpo casuale.

Ogni caso gira in un thread: controlla assenza di panico, blocco (20 s), chiave `err.*`/`error.*`, picco e richiesta massima di memoria (allocatore contatore per thread, tetto 8 MB + 64 × byte) e letture oltre la dimensione. Un test verifica che il banco stesso prenda panico, allocazione enorme e chiave estranea. ~13 s, senza `MZLAB_DATI`; i semi `.wiff` usano python3 e si saltano senza.

Nota: il crate `mzlab-lettori` non esiste (i lettori stanno in `mzlab-core::lettori`), quindi i test sono in `mzlab-core/tests/`. Risultato: nessun bug trovato da questo banco (0 guasti); i casi specifici per formato sono nella PR 2.

author: fcbhcd1997
body:
## Eisenzeit
- **Stadtmauer:** innen jetzt dieselbe Steinfront mit Balkenköpfen wie aussen, statt einer Grasrampe.
- **Speicher und Fürstenhaus:** verschoben, damit nichts mehr ineinander steht. Das Festmahl des Fürsten steht frei vor dem Haus.
- **Brunnen:** mit Seilwinde, Kurbel und Holzeimer. Eine Frau lässt den Eimer hinunter, kurbelt ihn voll wieder hoch und giesst das Wasser in den Krug am Boden.
- **Dachleiter:** liegt auf dem Strohdach, der Dachdecker steht darauf und stopft Strohbündel ins Dach.
- **Werkzeuge in der Hand:** Schwerter, Schilde, Speer, Sichel und Stab sitzen sauber in der Faust (neue Hilfen `fist`, `aimHand`, `gripAt`, `routine`).
- **Schmied:** ganzer Arbeitsablauf mit Esse → Amboss → Esse → Amboss → Abschrecken. Danach Werkbank (schleifen, Griff anbringen), Schwert ins Fass und ein neuer Eisenstab.
- **Frau am Blasebalg:** schüttet zwischendurch Holzkohle in die Esse.
- **Schmelzofen:**
  - Ein Helfer füllt Holzkohle und Erz ein und zieht die glühende Luppe heraus.
  - Ein zusätzlicher Träger bringt die Luppen den ganzen Weg zum Schmied.
- **Pflug:** Der Boden wird Streifen für Streifen hinter dem Pflug aufgelockert, Erdbrocken fliegen, die Stoppeln verschwinden.
- **Schuhmacher und Zimmermann:**
  - Der Schuhmacher näht mit Ahle und Faden auf dem Leisten.
  - Der Zimmermann stemmt mit Stechbeitel und Holzhammer ein Zapfenloch.
- **Druide:** Kessel mit Zaubertrank, Misteln, Kräutergestell, weisses Tuch und Eichenkranz.
- **Götterplatz:** geschnitzte Figur des Cernunnos mit Geweih. Ein Mann betet, eine Frau bringt Opfergaben, ein Krieger opfert ein Schwert.

## Alle Zeitalter
- **Gang der Menschen:** mit Stand- und Schwungphase.
  - Die Schritte richten sich nach der zurückgelegten Strecke, die Füsse rutschen nicht.
  - Am Hang setzen die Füsse auf dem Gelände auf.
- **Tiere:** Die Gangart richtet sich nach Strecke und Beinlänge, der Körper neigt sich am Hang.
- **Infokarten:**
  - Der gestrichelte Rahmen bleibt am Kartenrand.
  - Die Karten öffnen immer oben.
  - Statt der Nahaufnahme gibt es ein Bild: 21 Ausschnitte aus den Arbeitsblättern (neuer Ordner `bilder/`) und 64 gezeichnete Cliparts.

## Geprüft
- Alle vier Welten laden ohne Fehler, die Eisenzeit auch in hoher Qualität.
- Die Abläufe habe ich mit Standbildern bei festen Animationszeiten angeschaut, nicht live durchgespielt.
- Die Infokarten habe ich am Desktop und in Handygrösse geprüft.

author: emregunay212-cyber
body:
## Klavye Kâşifi — kesintisiz akış (sahip isteği, 13 Eki 2026)

**İstek:** "Sonraki Seviye" / bölüm geçme katmanı iptal; çıkılmadıkça bölümler kendiliğinden geçsin. Sıra önce klavyedeki tüm harfler, sonra heceler, kelimeler, cümleler; ayrıca rakamlar ve noktalama. Bölüm sayısı artsın: 35 dakikalık bir derste klavyeyi bilen öğrenci bile usta değilse bitiremesin.

**Sahip kararları:** sıra Harf → Hece → Kelime → Cümle → Rakam → Noktalama · kaldığı yerden devam yok · yaş 4-10 · **istenen kısım/bölümden başlanabilsin** (ör. 3. sınıf doğrudan kelimelerden).

### Ne değişti
- **Başlangıç seçici:** oyun açılınca (hub kartı, derin bağlantı, son katmandaki "Tekrar Oyna") 6 kısım kartı + 39 bölüm numarası. Kart kısmın başından, numara o bölümden başlatır; sonrası düğmesiz sona kadar. Seçim motoru o kısımla yeniden başlatır (araç çubuğu noktası + yıldız kaydı doğru kısma); kısım ortasından başlanırsa yıldız yalnız oynanan bölümlerden. İlk odak Harfler kartı (Enter = baştan).
- **Akış:** 6 kısım (motor seviyesi, araç çubuğunda 6 nokta) × **39 bölüm** (eskiden 3 seviye). Bölüm sonunda düğmesiz şerit ("Bölüm 7 tamam! Sıradaki: …", 1,8 sn), kısım sonunda yıldızlı şerit (2,8 sn) — kutlama katmanı **yalnız en sonda** açılır. Sol üstte bölüm sayacı (`7/39`).
- **İçerik** (`js/games/klavye-kasifi-icerik.js`): klavyedeki 32 harf (orta/üst/alt sıra yanan tuşla, sonra sesli/sessiz harfler) → açık/kapalı/üç harfli heceler → 2–10 harfli kelimeler (Türkçe harf bölümü dahil) → noktalamasız cümleler (atasözü, tekerleme, usta cümleleri) → rakamlar ve sayılar → `. ,` tuşları, Shift ile `? !`, noktalı/soru/ünlem/virgüllü/sayılı cümleler, usta paragrafları. 372 tur, ~4.500 vuruş.
- **Süre bütçesi** (hatasız, okuma payı sıfır alt sınır): ~30 kelime/dk ≈ 39 dk, ~36 kelime/dk ≈ 34 dk, 48 kelime/dk (usta) ≈ 27 dk. Test kilitler.
- **Klavye:** rakam satırı (Shift karakterleri kapakta), `, ;` ve `. :` tuşları, iki Shift; ekranda Shift'e dokunup tuşa basılır; `? !` hedefinde Shift tuşları da yanar. Fiziksel tuşta `e.key` ve `e.code`'un TR Q kapağı aday, beklenenle uyuşan seçilir → işletim sistemi İngilizce dizilimde olsa da TR kapaktaki karakter kabul edilir.
- **Motor** (`js/engine.js`): `cbs.onLevelUp(stars)` — seviyeyi katman açmadan bitirir (yıldız `Progress`'e, araç çubuğu ilerler, modül yeniden init edilmez). Diğer oyunlara dokunmaz.
- **Kayıt:** `levels` 6, yaş 4-10 (Anaokulu, 1-2, 3-4. sınıf rafları), `cat` "Klavye", `minutes` 30, metinler; `npm run catalog` + `python seo/build_seo.py`.
- **Yıldız:** kısım başına hatalı tur oranı ≤ %15 → 3, ≤ %50 → 2, üstü → 1.

### Doğrulama
- `npm run test:klavye` **8/8** (yeni, CI'a eklendi): içerik kapsamı ve sırası, 35 dk süre bütçesi, Harfler kısmının düğmesiz bitmesi + sessiz yıldız kaydı, son kısımda katman + "Tekrar Oyna" → seçici, TR Q ve İngilizce dizilim (TR kapak), ekran Shift'i + yanlış sayımı, başlangıç seçici (kart/numara → doğru motor seviyesi, yıldız o kısma), çıkınca seçici yeniden. Kaynak ağaç ve `SITE_ROOT=.build-check`.

author: bartbeecoders
body:
Closes #89 (dynamic topology landed in #95).

## What
- **Multires modifier** (`levels`, `level`): shows level k of the input's Catmull–Clark subdivision, with each level displaced after it is made: `P_j = S(P_j-1) + D_j`.
- **Storage (`OB_MRES`):** displacements live on the object as a reference-counted block, shared with undo steps exactly like meshes.
  - The block carries the base topology's fingerprint; on another topology it is ignored.
  - Subsurf adds the displacements level by level, using cache entries separate from plain subsurf.
- **Sculpting a level:** sculpt mode works on a copy of the chosen level, and a stroke adds its moves to that level's D in a new block.
  - Finer levels follow and keep their own detail; coarser levels keep their shape.
  - Level 0 sculpts the base cage.
  - Dyntopo is refused on a multires level.
- **`multires.propagate_down`:** coarser levels take the finest level's shape (subsurf in fit mode), and the finest level stays exact.
- **Apply** keeps the level shown; displacements that no longer fit the base are dropped.
- **Files and duplicates:** the MRES chunk saves the displacements in `.bee` files, and duplicates share them.
- **HUD:** shows "multires level N" while sculpting a level.
- **Fix:** `mod_apply` now sets the evaluation owner, which modifiers that read their own object (boolean, multires) need.

## Tests (`fakewl multires`)
- A stroke at level 2 adds +0.338 volume there; level 1 changes by exactly 0, and Ctrl+Z restores it exactly.
- A stroke at level 1 carries up to level 2 (+0.0086 → +0.0086), and the level-2 detail is kept.
- Propagate down: level 1 changes (+0.31), and level 2 changes by 0.
- The displacements survive a `.bee` save and reload exactly.
- `ci/local.sh` is green, goldens included.

author: poisongodv
body:
After the primary kills the replication link in `diskless loading short read`, the replica only logs the outcome once it has parsed the RDB bytes already sitting in its socket receive buffer and reached EOF. The ~5s budget (500 tries x 10ms) is therefore a bet on replica-side parse throughput, which is milliseconds on an idle machine but can exceed 5s on loaded sanitizer / TLS runners.

This raises the budget to 6000 tries (~60s) at the same 10ms poll interval, in both copies of the assertion:

- `tests/integration/replication.tcl` (#4325)
- `tests/unit/moduleapi/testrdb.tcl` (#4874)

`wait_for_log_messages` returns on the first match, so healthy runs are unaffected.

Root cause analysis is from @madolson in https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/issues/4325#issuecomment-5692479550; this PR applies the same fix and extends it to the moduleapi copy of the test, which fails the same way (#4874).

### Reproduction

Following the approach in #4325, on a copy of the moduleapi test with 5 attempts, `debug populate 100000`, `loading-process-events-interval-bytes 16384` on the replica, and `key-load-delay 2000` set on the replica right before the kill:

| budget | result | kill-to-outcome window |
|---|---|---|
| 500 x 10ms (current) | 3/3 runs fail with the CI error | n/a |
| 6000 x 10ms (this PR) | 3/3 runs pass | up to ~37s |

Without the delay, the window is 3-20ms and the test passes either way.

The full `unit/moduleapi/testrdb` (26 tests) and `integration/replication` (140 tests) suites pass locally with this change.

Fixes #4874
Refs #4325

## 왜

방향 확정(재영, 10-13): **고객이 보낸 KREAM 링크(상품·사이즈)를 기준으로 재고를 확인**하는 흐름.
지금 관리자 화면의 「소싱 후보」는 가격만 적는 칸이라 「어디에, 그 사이즈가, 언제 확인했을 때 있었나」를 남길 수 없었다.
사업계획서 MVP-03(재고 확인 결과 — 매장·옵션·조회 시점·상태, 오래된 정보 구분, 수동을 자동처럼 표시하지 않음)에 맞춘다.

## 무엇을

| 파일 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `assets/js/stock.js` (신규) | 재고 상태 4종(재고 있음·소량 = 살 수 있음 / 품절·확인 불가), 오래된 확인 판정, 입력 검증(가격은 선택 — 품절이면 없어도 됨), 신청 건 재고 요약, 목록 필터 |
| `assets/js/admin.js` | 05 패널 「소싱 후보」 → **「재고 확인 — 신청 사이즈 X」**. 확인 시각(몇 분 전·KST·수동)·「오래됨」·「지금 다시 확인함」, 재고 상태를 표에서 바로 변경(시각 갱신), 다른 사이즈 표시. 목록 행에 재고 배지, 「재고 확인 필요/있음/없음」 필터, CSV 재고 열 |
| `admin.html` · `admin.css` | 설정에 「재고 확인 유효 시간」(기본 24시간), 재고 필터, 배지·상태 색 |
| `assets/js/admin-view.js` | `toCsv` 재고 열(선택), `shiftSampleTimes` — 샘플을 넣을 때 시각을 지금 기준으로 민다(며칠 뒤에도 데모가 「오래됨」 투성이가 되지 않게) |
| `assets/demo/sample-applications.json` | 재고 상태 추가(품절 공식몰 · 소량 해외 · 재고 있는 매장 · 이틀 전 확인 · 다른 사이즈) |

### 최저가 규칙
**신청 사이즈 · 살 수 있음(재고 있음·소량) · 최근 확인**만. 최근 확인이 없고 오래된 「재고 있음」만 있으면 그 최저가를 「최저(오래됨) · 다시 확인」으로 보인다.
품절·확인 불가 행은 KREAM 대비를 계산하지 않는다. KREAM 대비는 「KREAM 수수료·배송비 전」이라고 붙인다(계획서: 확인되지 않은 비용을 확정값으로 쓰지 않음).

### 호환
예전 「소싱 후보」 기록(같은 `sourcing` 칸, 재고 칸 없음)은 재고 「확인 불가」로 읽는다 — 살 수 있는 곳으로 세지 않는다.

author: connorwang
body:
## What this fixes

A hub token issued under an OIDC session carries the session's id (`sid`). `Service.GetUserFromToken` asked the session only when a session checker was set, which it is only when `auth.oidc.session` is configured. With no checker, the token was validated as an ordinary hub token: signature, expiry and the user's record.

So a hub that had sessions on, and was then restarted with them off, let back in every holder of a token whose session had **ended**: a user who had signed out, or one the provider had refused. That lasted until the token's own expiry, 24 hours by default and up to 365 days by configuration. No sign-in was needed and no session existed to end.

## The rule now

A token that names a session is refused with `ErrInvalidToken` when no session checker is set. The holder gets a 401 and signs in again, which with sessions off issues an ordinary token.

- It applies to the token, not to the kind of user, and whether or not the session had ended: with sessions off nothing can say that it has not.
- With a checker set, nothing changes.
- A token that names no session is validated exactly as before in both modes: builtin administrator, password users and OIDC users on a hub without sessions.
- API keys and webhook tokens do not go through this path and are untouched.
- A hub that never had sessions on has issued no token with `sid`, so the default is unchanged.

Turning sessions off on a hub where they were on therefore signs every OIDC user out, once.

## What did not change

- `ValidateToken`, `Claims`, `SessionChecker`, `SetSessionChecker` and every signature. `ValidateToken` still returns the claims of a session-bearing token with sessions off; it gains a comment saying that its result alone lets nobody in. Its only caller outside the service is the sign-out handler, which is registered only when sessions are on.
- No configuration, wiring, server, template or UI file. One file of code: `internal/service/auth/service.go`.
- Every path that accepts a hub token (the API middleware, the builtin middleware and the terminal handler) goes through `GetUserFromToken` on the one auth service the hub builds, so the rule is in one place.

## Tests

`internal/service/auth/session_test.go`:

- `TestATokenThatNamesASessionIsNeverAnOrdinaryToken` follows one token: accepted with sessions on; refused once its session ends; refused by a service restarted over the same users and signing key with no checker; refused when the checker is taken from the running service; refused again with sessions back on. A builtin user's token is the control and is accepted at every step. A session token whose session never ended, and one issued to a builtin user, are refused with sessions off. The refusal is `ErrInvalidToken`, not `ErrSessionCheckUnavailable`.
- `TestSessionsOffChangesNothingForATokenWithoutASession` replaces `TestSessionsOffChangesNothing`, which asserted the old behaviour on purpose for the session-bearing case.
- `TestSessionsOffRefusalComesAfterTheUserChecks`: a disabled user is still told so.

`internal/service/frontend/auth/oidc_session_test.go`:

- `TestSessionsTurnedOffRefuseEveryTokenOfASession` uses the real session manager, a fake provider and the real middleware: three sign-ins, one signed out through the endpoint, one ended as refused, one live. A hub restarted with sessions off answers all three with 401 and `WWW-Authenticate`, no `Retry-After`, and does not ask the provider. The administrator's token gets 200. A new sign-in with sessions off works.

Nine mutations of the rule and its neighbours, each caught by a failing test, are listed in the evidence.

## Limits

- This closes the re-admission by turning sessions off. It does not close a connection that is already open when a session ends (TXE-4110), and it is not approval to turn `auth.oidc.session` on for a live hub.
- The claim is narrow: turning OIDC sessions off no longer turns a session-bearing token into an ordinary one. It is not a claim that no configuration can give access back. Setting the authentication mode to `none` admits every request with no token at all, as it always did.
- Rotating the hub's token signing key, or disabling the user, were and remain the other ways to cut a token off.
- Between hub processes that share a store, an end that exists only as a marker beside the session record reaches another process at its next refresh of that session or its next round. That is the session manager's behaviour from PR 61 and is unchanged.
- Nothing was run against a provider or a deployed hub. The provider in the tests is a fake.

TXE-3415 is the parent.

Closes TXE-4120

author: pooyaraki
body:
> Code and description written by Claude Code at the author's request, then reviewed by the author. ## What it solves Resolves: no ticket, reported directly. When Safe Shield flags a risk, Sign and Execute stay disabled until you tick "I understand the risks". The new Execute step ignored that tick: 1. You tick the box, sign as the last signer, and continue to Execute → Execute is disabled, and the step shows no checkbox to tick again. 2. You open a fully signed tx from the queue and tick the box on the review step → the Execute step still shows Execute disabled. ## How this PR fixes it The Execute step reloads the signed tx from the gateway and puts it in `SafeTxContext`. `SafeShieldContext` reset the confirmation whenever the tx **object** changed, so the reload cleared it. The reset now keys on the tx **content** (`safeTx.data`, lowercased because the gateway returns checksummed addresses). New signatures keep the confirmation. A changed tx, nonce or risk result still clears it. ## How to test it 1. Use a Sepolia Safe that is **not** in your accounts. The untrusted Safe check alone requires the checkbox. 2. 2/2 Safe, first signer: create a send → tick the checkbox → Sign → done. 3. Second signer: open the tx from the queue → Confirm → tick the checkbox → Sign → the Execute step opens with **Execute enabled**. 4. 1/1 Safe, or a tx that is already fully signed: open it from the queue → Execute → review step shows the checkbox, Execute stays disabled until you tick it. 5. Tick it → Continue → the Execute step shows **Execute enabled**. 6. Failure path: do step 4 without ticking. Execute stays disabled on the review step, as before. 7. Edit check: create a tx, tick the box, go Back, change the amount, continue → the checkbox is unticked again. ## Affected flows - Last signer signs, then executes in the same flow (m/n and 1/n) - Executing a fully signed tx from the queue ## Blast radius One line of logic in `SafeShieldContext.tsx`: the deps of the `isRiskConfirmed` reset effect. Every tx flow reads `isRiskConfirmed` (Sign, Execute, ExecuteThroughRole, Propose, Counterfactual, batch execute, `TxFlowProvider.isSubmitDisabled`). The only behaviour change: a new tx object with the same content no longer clears the tick. Message signing has no `safeTx`, so its key stays `undefined`, same as before. Nothing under `packages/`, so no mobile impact. ## Risks / not checked | Risk | What happens | Cover | |---|---|---| | A content change that only differs in letter case | The tick survives it | Every field in `SafeTransactionData` is hex or a number, so case does not change the tx | | Threat analysis refetches on reload (Blockaid compares data case-sensitively) | Severity goes `undefined` while loading, which still resets the tick | Not covered. Only if the created and reloaded `to` differ in casing | - I did not run the steps above in a browser. - I did not run jest, lint or type-check locally. CI covers them. ## Visual summary ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Review as Review step (checkbox) participant Shield as SafeShieldContext participant Exec as ExecuteTxStep Review->>Shield: setIsRiskConfirmed(true) Exec->>Exec: createExistingTx(txId), same data + signatures Exec->>Shield: SafeTxContext.safeTx = reloaded tx Note over Shield: before: new object → reset to false
after: same content key → stays true Shield-->>Exec: isRiskConfirmed = true → Execute enabled ``` ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 (web-only change) - [ ] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 (no analytics change) - [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻 - [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯 --- ## CLA signature With the submission of this Pull Request, I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms of the [Contributor License Agreement](https://safe.global/cla). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: roiglinik
body:
## Summary

The Holmes server caches one tool executor, under the key `([core, cluster], enable_all_toolsets_possible=False)`. `GET /api/info` and `POST /api/oauth/callback` asked for it with the CLI defaults, `([core], True)`. Each call rebuilt the executor from scratch and replaced the server's cached one: every toolset was re-checked, every signed-in OAuth user's tools were reloaded, and the next chat or refresh rebuilt it again, bypassing `status_refresh_interval_seconds`.

Fixes ROB-1525 and ROB-1501 (`/api/info` reported the statuses of that other executor, not the one the chat uses).

- Adds `SERVER_TOOLSET_TAGS` (in `holmes/core/tools.py`) and `Config.create_server_tool_executor()`. Removes `ToolsetManager.server_tool_tags`, which returned the same tags and only fed two leftover `ToolsetManager` methods; they use the constant now.
- `/api/info`, the OAuth callback, the refresh loop, toolset sync, admin reload and the tool-call worker use the helper. Chat, the conversation processor and health checks pass `SERVER_TOOLSET_TAGS` to `create_toolcalling_llm`.
- The refresh loop's first cycle and the tool-call worker no longer build the executor through the disk-cache prerequisite mode. That mode checked MCP servers twice and wrote `toolsets_status.json`, which fails on a read-only filesystem. They now run live checks, like the refresh's own cold path.

## Tests

- `tests/test_server_executor_cache.py`: one test per server caller, checking that it reuses the cached executor and opens no MCP session, also after a refresh inside the interval. Plus `/api/info` statuses vs the chat's (ROB-1501), admin reload, and the first build by the refresh loop and by the tool-call worker (one session, no file written).
  - 5 fail on master (`api_info`, `oauth_callback`, the ROB-1501 test, both first-build tests); all pass here.
  - The callers already correct on master are covered too; each test fails if its call site's key is changed.
- The `clock` fixture moves from `tests/test_status_refresh_interval.py` to `tests/conftest.py`, so both test files can use it.
- Full non-LLM suite: the only failures are 9 environment-specific tests that fail the same way on master locally.
- E2E: real server with a stdio MCP server and a fake OAuth MCP server, including a real OAuth callback (200). Master → this branch:
  - `/api/info`: a full rebuild (1 new MCP session and OAuth check per server) → nothing.
  - OAuth callback: a full rebuild plus the user's tool load → only the token exchange and the user's tool load.
  - Refreshes after each call: a rebuild each → nothing.
  - Master wrote `toolsets_status.json`; this branch writes nothing.

## Out of scope (pre-existing, not made worse)

Follow-up PRs opened from this review:

- #2591: `refresh_tool_executor` can overwrite an executor an admin reload rebuilt while it ran. Fixed with a compare-and-swap, still reporting the status changes the refresh found. Independent of this PR; either can merge first.
- #2595: on a cold start the refresh loop builds the executor and then refreshes it in the same cycle, so toolsets without a status refresh interval are checked twice (master does the same, and checked MCP servers more). Stacked on this PR, so merge this one first; it also removes the "Known issue" comment this PR adds for it.

Noted in "Known issue" comments at the code, no PR yet:

- The OAuth callback loads the user's tools into the executor it fetched before the token exchange. If a refresh replaces the executor in between, the new one lacks that user's tools until the next rebuild (the `_connect` placeholder still works). Rarer now, since the callback no longer evicts.
- `create_toolcalling_llm` still defaults to the CLI's key, so a new server caller must pass the server key explicitly (documented on `create_server_tool_executor`).

## Scope

Two P0 tracks continued: evaluate the twelve unresolved jurisdictions without inventing permissions, and individually verify remaining fields in source-reviewed cities.

### Fifteen newly confirmed government code/guidance fields
- Prescott Valley AZ: 4, current Town Code §6-02-030(B) (fowl count, rooster, no ordinary keeping/coop permit except construction involving utilities, 1-ft property/easement offset)
- Anaheim CA: 3, Code §18.38.030 (combined small-animal/other species density, rooster exceptions by zone, distinct 50-ft dwelling and 20-ft lot-line separation)
- Folsom CA: 3, agricultural combining-district Chapter 17.40 ONLY (small-livestock rule and conditional-use permit over 100 head **not** ordinary residential poultry permission, special-zone coop setbacks)
- Beaverton OR: 1, Chapter 5.09.015/025 location and enclosure (>=5000sf, owner/tenant terms, 20ft from NEIGHBOR DWELLING not property line)
- Portland OR: 1, city chicken-keeping guidance expressly states no standard livestock permit, separate structure/zoning requirements still apply
- Lake Havasu City AZ: 3, §14.03.03(E)(9) (6 hens, no male birds, enclosure standards). **Material correction**: §14.03.02 use table's A(2) means in flagged zoning districts backyard fowl is restricted to residents of detached dwellings existing Sept 13, 2024; no blanket all-residential allowance.

Result: **131/400** primary clause/guidance-checked; **221** source-recorded; **48** unverified, with **88** of 100 city summaries having at least partial government sources and **12** still fully `needs_review`/noindex.

Boulder: separate City Boulder CO vs Boulder County vs Boulder City Nevada; do not mix. Queen Creek: official 2026 zoning Article 6 PDF search excerpt and AZ §9-462.12 located, direct PDF blocked (403) and adopted/uncodified amendments not conclusively inspected; leave pending. author: amebus
body:
## What changes

Every selector that reads a value from the element also accepts a **property key** (`string`, `symbol` or `number`) in place of the function, as `min`/`max` already did with `Comparer<T>`:

```ts
from(orders).map('customer');                      // IIterableLinq<string>
from(orders).sum('price');                         // only the keys whose value is a number
from(orders).groupBy('customer');                  // IIterableLinq<[string, Order[]]>
from(orders).collectToMap('id', 'customer');       // Map<number, string>
from(teams).innerJoin(players, 'id', 'teamId', (t, p) => …);
```

- Operations: `map`, `flatMap`, `sum`, `average`, `distinct`, `except`, `intersect`, `union`, `groupBy`, `innerJoin`, `groupJoin` (both keys), `collectToMap` (key and value). Keys and functions can be mixed.
- `key` behaves like `v => v[key]`: prototype chain and getters, no index, `SameValueZero` keys (ADR 0024), and a `null`/`undefined` value throws the native `TypeError`, which closes the source (ADR 0008).
- Typing: one extra overload per selector (`P extends keyof T` → `T[P]`). New public types `KeysOfType<T, V>` (`sum`/`average`/`flatMap`; optional properties left out, tuple indices as numbers) and `KeysOverlapping<T, V>` (the two keys of a join: values in common in either direction, so an optional foreign key is accepted).
- Validation: `Validations.throwIfNotSelector`. **Breaking** (minor before 1.0): the message of these selectors becomes `The "<name>" must be a function or a property key`, and a string/number/symbol that was rejected is now read as a key — see the new *Migrating to 0.13.0* page.
- Predicates, reducers, taps, `equals` and the `result` of the joins keep functions only.

## Why this implementation: measured, gate before the rollout

The plan required a go/no-go gate: the key no slower than the lambda (**A**), and the lambda no slower than on `main` (**B**), measured outside Vitest with the method of #181 (one process per variant, then both forms in one process in both orders, 3–5 repetitions, ns per value at 1k and 100k, `--trace-opt --trace-deopt`).

- Resolving the key into `v => v[key]` (the `toCompareFunction` way) **failed A**: 2–10% slower than the lambda, and with both forms at the same call site `sum` with a lambda became 2.5× slower (the polymorphic call of #152).
- The key is therefore **read inline**, with three patterns ([ADR 0025](https://github.com/Amebus/iterable-linq-utility/blob/feat/property-key-selectors/docs/decisions/0025-property-keys-as-selectors.md)): an iterator class for the key (`map`, `groupBy`, `distinct`, `flatMap`), a key field in the existing no-selector branch (`except`, `intersect`, `union`), a property field next to the function field (joins); in an Action one function per loop (`sum`, `average`, `collectToMap`).
- One finding worth knowing: in `sum`, an early `return sumOfKey(…)` before the selector loop, **in the same function**, slowed that unchanged loop by 14% (isolated factor by factor; same Maglev→TurboFan path, no deopt). Moving each loop to its own function brought it back to `main` (1.262 vs 1.263 ns/value).

Final standalone results (median; noise = half-spread between repetitions):

| op | A: key vs lambda | B: lambda, branch vs main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| map | −7% | −2…0% |
| sum | −8…−19% | −4…0%; without selector 0% |
| average | 0…−1% | −6…−16% (main ran both loops in one function) |
| flatMap | −2…−3% | −1…+1% |
| distinct | −4…+5.5% (±11%) | −4…+8% (±11%) |
| groupBy | −5% (±10%) | −6…−7% (±10%) |
| union / except | −3…−5% | −8…+8% (±6–9%); without selector 0% |
| innerJoin | −1…+0.5% | −0.2…+0.1% |
| collectToMap (key / key+value) | +0.4…+1.5% / −1…−4% | −3…+0.4% / −0.5…+0.3% |

`groupBy` and `distinct` have a ±10% noise even for `main` between rounds: a smaller difference cannot be excluded, though the code of their function form is unchanged.

## Verified (devcontainer)

- `pnpm lint`, `typecheck`, `check:since`, `check:structure`, `check:instructions`, `check:changeset`, `check:commits`, `build`, `check:package`
- `pnpm test:coverage`: 2790 tests, 100% of `src/`
- `mkdocs build --strict`
- Every new test was seen failing before the implementation
- A whole-branch review by a fresh reviewer; its findings (tuple indices in `KeysOfType`, one-directional join key check, the ADR wording, four minors) are fixed in the last commits

## Benchmarks (`pnpm bench:report` on the 12 functions)

Measured at `e1cf82b`; the later commits change types, JSDoc and documentation only. In Vitest the key is as fast as the lambda or faster on every operation (e.g. `sum/property` 7,633 vs 1,626 ops/s, `groupBy/key` 424 vs 263).

author: parns
body:
Fixes PAR-837

Only the downtime reconstruction, the forecast archive and the H5 profile bounded their reads; every other heavy reader ran with the server default of 0. This routes the rest through `queryWithLimits` (or `SET LOCAL` in the Python service). Limits come from the production slow-query log of 2026-10-10.

| Caller | Measured max | Limit | Factor |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ml-service/db.py` `fetch_training_data` | 42.6 s | 300 s | 7x |
| `ShowsService.rebuildSchedulePatterns` | 24.5 s | 180 s | 7.3x |
| `DowntimeProfileService` coverage + profile read | 12.3 s | 120 s | 9.8x |
| `AttractionOutageService` (4 per-park reads, request path) | none above 10 s | 30 s | at least 3x |
| `DowntimeMeasurementService` outage scan / erasure | 30 s for 30 days (reconstruction) | `reconstructionReadLimits` (10 min floor, 10 s per scan day) | 20x at 30 days |
| `DowntimeMeasurementService` census | small tables | 30 s | at least 3x |

Not changed: the `INSERT INTO catboost_daily_forecasts` and the p90 forecast read from the issue table no longer exist (job and tables retired in PAR-870). The write transaction in `DowntimeProfileService` is not a read and is left alone.

**Ran:** `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (240 suites, 3687+ tests), `pnpm build`, `pytest ml-service/tests/test_read_limits.py`.
**Not run:** `pnpm test:e2e` and the `pg_stat_activity` check (no Docker/DB in the cloud); handed to the local runner, hence Draft.

**Review:** Sonnet, 1 pass, 1 important finding fixed (spec for the show pattern read), 3 notes: erasure read spec added; the extra round trips per outage read (BEGIN + SET LOCAL + COMMIT) are accepted on the request path and not measured here; the Python wiring is checked through the helper only.

## Verified on the production host (local runner, 2026-10-13)

**Ran:** `pnpm lint` (13.8 s), `pnpm test` (241 suites, 3,689 tests, 40.7 s), `pnpm test:e2e` (23 suites, 169 tests, 255.9 s, exit 0). All green. The 23 e2e suites build the real `AppModule`, which is what covers the new import of `reconstructionReadLimits` into `src/admin/downtime-measurement.service.ts` against a dependency cycle — no unit test can see that, because every one of them mocks the counterpart.

**The deadlines bind on a real server.** `pg_stat_activity` cannot carry the counter-check the hand-off asked for: the view has no column for a GUC, and another session's setting is not readable from outside it. So the check ran against a throwaway TimescaleDB container (`timescale/timescaledb:2.24.0-pg18`, PostgreSQL 18.1 — never the live stack), with this branch's code, reading the settings back from the server inside the transaction `queryWithLimits` opens. The limit values were read out of the service sources rather than retyped, so the mapping caller → value is evidence:

| Caller | From source | `statement_timeout` in force | `lock_timeout` | `idle_in_transaction` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ShowsService.rebuildSchedulePatterns` | 180000 / 10000 / 30000 ms | 3min | 10s | 30s |
| `DowntimeProfileService` (coverage + profile) | 120000 / 10000 / 30000 ms | 2min | 10s | 30s |
| `AttractionOutageService` (4 request reads) | 30000 / 2000 / 10000 ms | 30s | 2s | 10s |
| `AdminDowntimeMeasurement.capabilityCensus` | 30000 / 2000 / 10000 ms | 30s | 2s | 10s |
| `AdminDowntimeMeasurement` erasure + outage (30 d) | 600000 / 30000 ms | 10min | 30s | 0 |
| `ml-service/db.py` `fetch_training_data` | 300000 / 10000 ms | 5min | 10s | 10min (from `connect_args`) |

A `SELECT pg_sleep(5)` under a 400 ms deadline died server-side with **SQLSTATE 57014** after 402 ms, and after the commit the same pooled connection was back to `statement_timeout=0` — `SET LOCAL` does not leak, as the helper's docstring claims.

**The Python path was exercised for real, not through the helper.** A probe imported `ml-service/db.py` itself — its engine, its `sessionmaker`, its `apply_read_limits` — in a container against the same throwaway Postgres. This was the open question, because `SET LOCAL` outside a transaction block is only a WARNING in Postgres and leaves the setting at 0, which the mocked pytest cannot see. Inside the training transaction: `statement_timeout=5min`, `lock_timeout=10s`, `application_name=parkfan-ml-service`, no warnings; a fresh session read back 0; the cancel came as SQLSTATE 57014.

**What the wrapper costs on the request path** (the note this PR left unmeasured): same trivial read 200 times each way, alternating, after 20 warm-ups, own container — median 0.14 ms bare vs. 0.36 ms through `queryWithLimits`, p95 0.51 ms vs. 1.47 ms. **0.22 ms per read**, so about 0.9 ms for all four reads of one request, against reads whose deadline is 30 s.

**Production was read only:** the server default is still unset (`statement_timeout` boot_val and reset_val 0, nothing in `pg_db_role_setting` or `pg_file_settings`), which is the before-figure this PR acts on. Nothing was written, and the after-figure against production needs the deploy.

**Review:** Sonnet, 1 pass, 0 critical, 0 important, 1 note — only one of the four outage reads has a deadline assertion in its spec. Left as it is: the four reads share one `REQUEST_READ_LIMITS` constant and go through the same helper, which the container check now covers end to end, and widening the specs is scope this issue does not have.

body:
## What changes for you

Settings has a Keyboard name field. Renaming joins the normal reviewed draft
and Apply, appears in the keyboard menu, and travels with backups. Ark follows
the keyboard through the firmware's safe USB restart and reads it again.
Held keys and macros may delay departure; the return timeout starts after
disconnection. Ark excludes known other keyboards and requires the original
serial when available. If identity is ambiguous, or Chrome cannot identify a
cleared built-in name, you choose the keyboard yourself.

Recovery restores and explicitly saving the built-in text also expect a
possible restart. Reconnect failures retain the recovery-copy location, and
backups with settings v6 translate to v7 without losing their profile data.

## Why

The keyboard owns its name and reports it as the USB product name used by
Chrome's chooser. Ark needs the current settings codec, editor, labels and
reconnect handling to follow that behavior safely. Imports and dependency
pins are refreshed to the published firmware and BK commits.

body:
## Problem
`~/jingler/agent-resources/agents/worker.md` is one file shared by every session, but `pi-session-factory.ts` rewrote its `tools:` line from the **last-started** parent's `registry.capabilitiesFor(spec.role, spec.mode)`. Any read-only/review parent starting stripped `command_execute`, `workspace_write` and `workspace_edit` from every worker launched afterwards (observed 3× today: workers looped on `command_inspect` and committed nothing). Vendor `defaultContext: fork` also came back on each regeneration.

## Fix
- New `subagentProfileToolIds(registry, agent)`: the on-disk profile lists the conversation/auto ceiling; `advisor`/`oracle`/`reviewer` keep review/read-only.
- Per-parent narrowing is unchanged: the capability broker still issues tokens with `grantedToolIds` from the parent's real role/mode, so a read-only parent's worker gets `403 forbidden-tool` on write tools.
- `rewriteAgentProfile` forces `defaultContext: fresh`.

## Tests
- `subagentProfileToolIds`: worker gets read + execute + mutate tools; reviewer gets read only.
- Bootstrap test asserts `defaultContext: fresh` in worker.md.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/cli-adapters/src/runtime/{subagents,agent}`: 257 passed, 3 skipped. cli-adapters typecheck clean, biome clean.
