## Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for this static HTML portfolio website.

### What Was Implemented

**Project Analysis:**
- Identified project as a static HTML website (no framework, no build process)
- Found 3 HTML pages: index.html, experience.html, and projects.html

**Implementation:**
Following the official Vercel Analytics quickstart documentation (https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart), I added the Web Analytics script to all HTML pages.

**Modified Files:**
1. `index.html` - Added Vercel Web Analytics script in the <head> section
2. `experience.html` - Added Vercel Web Analytics script in the <head> section
3. `projects.html` - Added Vercel Web Analytics script in the <head> section

**Code Added:**
Each HTML file now includes the following script tags just before the closing `</head>` tag:

```html
<!-- Vercel Web Analytics -->
<script>
  window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

### Implementation Details

**Framework-Specific Approach:**
- For static HTML/JavaScript sites, the documentation specifies using inline script tags
- The script initializes the `window.va` function to queue analytics events
- The deferred script loads from `/_vercel/insights/script.js` (Vercel's standard path for static sites)

**Why This Approach:**
- No package manager (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) is used in this project - it's pure HTML/CSS/JS
- No build process or dependencies to install
- The `/_vercel/insights/script.js` path is automatically served by Vercel's platform when Web Analytics is enabled in the dashboard
- The `defer` attribute ensures the script doesn't block page rendering

**Location in Files:**
- Placed just before the closing `</head>` tag in each HTML file
- This ensures analytics loads early but doesn't block initial page rendering
- Added a clear HTML comment for easy identification

### Verification Performed

✓ All three HTML files have valid structure (DOCTYPE, html, head, body tags)
✓ Analytics script correctly added to all pages
✓ Script placement follows best practices (in <head> with defer attribute)
✓ No syntax errors introduced
✓ Preserved all existing code structure and styling

### Next Steps for Deployment

1. **Enable Web Analytics in Vercel Dashboard:**
   - Go to your project in Vercel Dashboard
   - Navigate to the Analytics tab
   - Click "Enable Web Analytics"

2. **Deploy to Production:**
   - The analytics script will automatically start collecting data once deployed to Vercel
   - Data will appear in the Vercel Analytics dashboard after visitor activity

3. **Verify After Deployment:**
   - Visit your site and check browser Network tab
   - Look for requests to `/_vercel/insights/script.js` and view tracking calls
   - Check Vercel Dashboard Analytics section for data (may take a few minutes to hours)

### Technical Notes

- No dependencies were added (this is a static site)
- No build process required
- No package.json or lock files to update
- Implementation follows the official Vercel documentation exactly
- Analytics will work automatically once Web Analytics is enabled in the Vercel Dashboard

author: cgyegcvcecvoc
body:
## Why

v1.0.1 is stuck as an unpublished draft: it carries the four macOS installers but **no Android APK**, so it can't be published as the dual-platform release. Every Android run since the v1.0.1 smoke gate was added failed the same way — `Timeout waiting for emulator to boot` — which skipped *Collect the APKs* and *Attach the APKs to the release*.

## Root cause (proven, not guessed)

A manual emulator boot with the verbose log published into `build-out/` showed the emulator dying instantly:

```
FATAL | Not enough space to create userdata partition.
Available: 6737.46 MB at .../premiumtv-test.avd, need 7372.80 MB.
```

Only ~6.7 GB is free on the runner once the SDK, Gradle and this checkout are in place, and a default AVD data partition needs ~7.4 GB. KVM, GPU mode and RAM were all innocent.

## Fix (CI-only, `.github/workflows/android-build.yml`)

- New *Free disk space for the emulator* step deleting preinstalled toolchains this job never uses (dotnet, GHC, ghcup, CodeQL, PowerShell, docker images).
- `disk-size: 2048M` for the AVD, `-gpu off` (the smoke script only installs the APK and dumps the UI hierarchy), 600s boot wait for the 2-core runner.

The smoke assertions themselves are unchanged: install, cold launch and relaunch must all show the bundled channel count and channel cards (`android/tools/smoke_apk.py`), on top of `testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug`.

## Proof

- This branch's Android run **38389191492: all steps green in 5m10s**, including *Smoke test cold launch and relaunch of the built APK*, *Collect the APKs* and *Attach the APKs to the release*.
- Local: 343 Python tests OK, 32 Node tests OK.

After merge, the v1.0.1 draft will be retargeted to main, both platform builds dispatched against that exact SHA to complete the draft (APK + `SHA256SUMS-android.txt` alongside the Mac installers), then published — the release-triggered rebuilds re-verify everything from the tag.

Betreiberentscheidung vom 2026-10-13: Ebene 1 und Ebene 2 haben je **unbegrenzt viele** Vertriebspartner. author: tomaspinolini
body:
Cierra **BOX-60**. Pantalla `/admin/circuits` detrás de `RequireAdmin`: listado, alta, edición y baja de circuitos desde la app.

**El backend no se tocó.** Todos los endpoints y guardas ya existían, incluido el rechazo de `externalId` duplicado con `CIRCUIT_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

## Qué se copió de temporadas y qué no

Se reusó el molde: un formulario en dos modos (alta y edición en el mismo lugar), servicio propio, hooks con invalidación, `ConfirmButton` antes de la baja y la guarda por rol. **No se extrajo ninguna abstracción compartida** — es el segundo caso de tres, y el ticket pide esperar al tercero para saber qué se repite de verdad.

Cuatro diferencias que el molde no cubría:

1. **La baja es lógica**, no física: marca `deletedAt`. El texto de confirmación dice lo contrario que en temporadas, donde sí borra.
2. **`externalId` es obligatorio y único**, un campo que temporadas no tiene.
3. **La longitud es opcional**: un string vacío se convierte en `undefined`, porque el backend lo declara `optional` y no `nullable` — si viajara como `NaN` o `null`, lo rechazaría.
4. El guard del backend sólo cuenta carreras **futuras**, no todas.

## Lo que se agregó fuera del "Done when", y por qué

La tabla muestra el **`ID externo`** y el campo lleva una ayuda asociada por `aria-describedby`.

Es el único dato que un admin no puede deducir mirando el circuito: sale de Jolpica, no del mundo real. Y cargarlo mal **falla en silencio** — el circuito se crea igual, y recién semanas después el sync no reconoce esa carrera. La columna además hace diagnosticable el duplicado: antes el error decía "ya hay un circuito con ese ID externo" sin dejar ver cuál.

Se descartó autogenerarlo desde el nombre: produciría `autodromo-oscar-y-juan-galvez`, que no existe en Jolpica, y convertiría un error ruidoso en uno silencioso.

## Verificación

- **125 tests** en 25 archivos (8 nuevos para esta pantalla). `tsc --noEmit`, `build` y `lint` con exit 0.
- **Smoke manual** contra la app corriendo, con el circuito proyectado para el regreso de la F1 a la Argentina: Autódromo Oscar y Juan Gálvez, Buenos Aires, 4,87 km, `externalId` `galvez` — el id real de Ergast/Jolpica. Se creó, apareció en el listado, y repetirlo mostró el error de duplicado en castellano.

author: koalageo
body:
Fixes #1

## Problem

Uploaded and zipped filenames were used directly to build filesystem paths (`tmp_dir / file.filename`) in `/validate/` and `/convert/`, so a caller-controlled name containing an absolute path or `..` was written **outside** the per-request temp directory. In the shipped container `/code/app` is owned and writable by `appuser`, so this write primitive could reach the app's own `.py` files and Jinja templates (→ potential RCE).

Verified before the fix: a multipart upload with an absolute-path or `../` filename wrote a file outside the temp dir.

## Change

- New `safe_filename()` helper in `app/routes/utils.py` that keeps only the basename and returns empty for empty / `.` / `..` / directory-entry names.
- `/validate/` and `/convert/` now sanitize both the direct upload filename and each zip member name with it.
- Zip members are read via `ZipFile.read()` and written to a contained path instead of `ZipFile.extract(name, ...)`; directory entries and macOS `__MACOSX` metadata entries are skipped.

## Verification

- After the fix the absolute-path and `../` uploads are reduced to their basename and nothing is written outside the temp dir.
- New regression test `test_validate_rejects_path_traversal_filename`.
- `flake8 app/ test/` clean; `test_validate.py` + `test_convert.py` pass (62 tests).

Note: this PR overlaps `app/routes/validate.py` / `convert.py` with the event-loop (#5) and temp-dir-leak (#6) PRs; whichever merges first, the others will need a trivial rebase.

author: nuimanlp
body:
Owner request 2026-10-13: a "compat" setup that auto-detects the OS / architecture of the host (today's VM), plus a Raspberry Pi 5 path where the data can live on an external / USB HDD or SSD (or NVMe) or stay on the internal microSD.

`sudo deploy/scripts/host-setup.sh [--profile auto|vm|pi5] [--data-disk boot|/dev/…] [--tailscale [--lan-ip IP] [--ts-hostname NAME]] [--dry-run]` — run **before** `provision.yml`.

- **Detect** (key=value): `/etc/os-release` (Ubuntu 26.04/24.04 supported; Debian/RPi OS warned), `dpkg --print-architecture` (amd64/arm64 only), x86-64 level v1/v2+, page size (refuses ≠ 4096 — RPi OS 16K kernel breaks Redis/jemalloc), Pi 5 from device-tree, RAM, boot disk (walks `lsblk -s` up to the disk; LVM-safe).
- **vm profile:** report only — writes nothing unless `--tailscale`.
- **pi5 profile:** choose the data disk by flag or numbered menu (model / serial / size / usb|nvme / HDD warning); `boot` = keep on microSD with a wear warning. Boot disk, its partitions, mounted / swap / LVM / RAID disks refused. **Never formats** — a non-ext4 target is refused and the exact `sfdisk`/`mkfs.ext4` commands are printed for the owner. Mounts `/srv/pos-data` by UUID (`nofail`; new fstab verified with `findmnt --verify` before it replaces the old one), `daemon.json` data-root + `containerd-snapshotter: false`, systemd drop-in `RequiresMountsFor=/srv/pos-data` (Docker never starts on an empty SD dir). Refuses an existing different daemon.json or existing volumes. Backups stay on the boot disk (other device than pgdata).
- **`--tailscale`:** signed repo for the detected distro/codename (skipped when already installed), `ip_forward` sysctl, `tailscale up … --advertise-routes=<lan-ip>/32 --advertise-tags=tag:pos-server --snat-subnet-routes=false`, or `tailscale set …` when already joined. Never takes an auth key.
- `provision.yml`: Docker apt repo `linux/ubuntu` → ubuntu|debian by `ansible_distribution` (identical on mob04).
- `server.yml`: paths filter + test step in `nginx-check`. Docs: `07_CICD_DEPLOY.md` §6; Tailscale plan as-built (SNAT off, owner SSH grant, dashboard SSH tunnel).

**Process:** plan (Opus) → `/scrutinize` (dropped `--format`, backups bind, added snapshotter/page-size/dpkg arch) → build → `/code-review` (fixed: fstab half-write on failed verify / missing trailing newline, late refusal after write, `--tailscale` re-installing on mob04, boot-disk lookup failure, menu `00`/`08`) → read-only `--dry-run` on mob04: `ubuntu 26.04 resolute, amd64, x86_level=v1, page 4096, boot /dev/sda, profile=vm`, `--tailscale` proposes only `tailscale set --advertise-routes=172.30.58.20/32 --snat-subnet-routes=false` → 3 cosmetic fixes. Test: 89 checks, stubs only.

**Not yet proven on a real Pi 5:** lsblk/findmnt output on SD/USB/NVMe boot, `RequiresMountsFor` at boot with the disk unplugged, Ubuntu Pi kernel page size.

author: muskanbandta23
body:
Adds a **ZopDay One-click Deployment button** alongside Render, PikaPods and Hostim in the **One-click Install** section.

## One-Click Deploy

ZopDay's One-Click Deploy feature lets users quickly deploy an application to ZopCloud or their own cloud via ZopDay, without the usual manual deployment setup.

The feature supports applications from GitHub repositories and Docker images, while Helm Charts can be deployed to the user's own cloud Kubernetes cluster.

**Supported deployments**

- GitHub Repositories → ZopCloud / Own Cloud via ZopDay
- Docker Images → ZopCloud / Own Cloud via ZopDay
- Helm Charts → Own Cloud Kubernetes clusters only

Users can use a shareable deploy link to open an application in ZopDay and deploy it with one click. They can also include preset environment variables, so required configuration fills in automatically when the user opens the deploy link.

Try it out: https://zop.dev/zopday/app/deploy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=one_click_pr&utm_content=sure

One-Click Deploy with ZopDay: https://zop.dev/zopday/oss?utm_source=github&utm_medium=one_click_pr&utm_content=sure

## What changed

One button added after the Hostim button, in the same plain-badge style. `README.md` only, +2/−0. No new docs pages or config files.

## What it offers

Click the button and a deploy screen for Sure opens, with the `ghcr.io/we-promise/sure:stable` image, port 3000 and `SELF_HOSTED=true` already set. Choose ZopCloud to have it run fully managed, or connect your own AWS or GCP account and ZopDay sets it up there instead. PostgreSQL and Redis are created from ZopDay in the same cloud and connected to the service.

## How it differs from the existing options

- **Render, PikaPods and Hostim** run Sure on their own platforms and billing.
- **ZopDay** covers the case where the cloud account already exists: the same flow on ZopCloud, or a deploy into an AWS or GCP account the user already owns. Sure holds bank balances, transactions and account details, so for a lot of self-hosters the point is that this data sits in an account they control. With ZopDay the app, its Postgres and its Redis all run inside their own AWS or GCP account, under their own IAM, VPC and billing.
- ZopDay also supports Helm Charts into a Kubernetes cluster the user already runs.

So it complements the existing entries rather than duplicating any of them.

## Deploy to ZopDay Button

[![Deploy to ZopDay](https://zop.dev/deploytozopday-inkhard.svg)](https://zop.dev/zopday/app/deploy?image=ghcr.io/we-promise/sure:stable&port=3000&name=sure&env=SELF_HOSTED=true&utm_source=github&utm_medium=one_click_pr&utm_content=sure)

Badge SVG: https://zop.dev/deploytozopday-inkhard.svg

## Notes

- Helm Charts are supported only when deploying to the user's own cloud Kubernetes cluster, not ZopCloud.
- Using ZopDay requires a ZopDay account, the same as the other providers in this section.

author: vishal29bhp
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"vishal29bhp"} -->
_Requested by **Vishal** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RaYkP1nVZo2zyCx225ekPc?thread=cmsg_01RaYkP1nVZo2zyCx225ekPcBrEXPHjesGGP6kCVTnbqrA)_

Before: AirYatra used a navy and slate palette with system fonts. `design_guidelines.json` described the old "Aero-Swiss" system.

After: every screen has the Vaayu Prive look: aubergine surfaces (`#17111F` page, `#221A2D` cards, `#3A3046` borders), IBM Plex Sans body text, Barlow Condensed ExtraBold uppercase headlines, JetBrains Mono, and 4px corners. Dark is the default theme. The orange accents are unchanged for now (see below).

## How
- `frontend/src/index.css`:
  - shadcn variables for the dark default (`.dark`) and the light theme (`:root`, with `#F2EEF6` page, white cards and `#17111F` text).
  - Global h1/h2/h3 heading fonts.
  - The deck's overline pattern as the `.ay-overline` class.
- `frontend/tailwind.config.js`:
  - `font-sans`, `font-heading` and `font-mono`, plus `lime` and `amber` brand colours.
  - **The `slate` scale is remapped onto aubergine.** The screens use `slate-*` for nearly every surface, border and secondary text (about 10,000 usages). The remap themes all of them through tokens, with no per-component overrides, as the master prompt asks.
- `public/index.html`, `manifest.json` and `offline.html` get the Google Fonts link (`display=swap`), the theme colours and the first-paint colours.
- `ThemeToggle.js` gets the aubergine variables, and dark is now the default.
- `design_guidelines.json` is rewritten for the theme.
- `docs/design/THEME.md` lists every token and its WCAG ratio.
  - Two slate shades are lighter than the deck so that body text passes AA. slate-500 was 3.5:1 with the deck value and is now 5.0:1.
- **Not in this PR:** moving the orange and blue accents to lime. That is about 2,600 usages, mostly white text on orange, and lime needs black text, so a global remap would break contrast. It needs a per-screen pass with one lime action per view, in the master prompt's order: Landing, Booking, Login, Customer dashboard, Payment, Operator and Admin.
- No logic, route or API changes.

## Tests
- `craco build` compiles. The output CSS carries the aubergine values and the font stacks.
- Contrast for every token pair is computed in `docs/design/THEME.md`. All body-text pairs pass AA.
- I took a landing page screenshot at 1366px and 360px from the production build. The theme fonts and photos did not load in the sandbox, because Google Fonts and Unsplash are not reachable from it.
- There is no frontend CI in this repo yet. The repo also has no lockfile, and a fresh `npm install` needed `ajv@8` added by hand before CRA would build. That is pre-existing and worth fixing with a committed lockfile.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Resumen ejecutivo ### Qué cambia Al regenerar un segmento o clip H3 sin escribir un prompt nuevo, el Director ahora respeta el texto que el usuario ya aprobó en la pausa de revisión. Antes volvía a aplicar el candado de «sin texto visible» y quitaba letreros o letras que había pedido a propósito. ### Para qué sirve Evita que un Regenerar gaste una toma H3 cara y entregue un vídeo distinto al prompt aprobado. ### Impacto para el usuario Si en la revisión escribió un cartel o texto en pantalla y luego pulsa Regenerar (sin abrir el editor), el modelo recibe esas letras. Un plano que no se editó sigue bloqueando el texto visible, como antes. ### Riesgo - [x] Bajo - [ ] Medio - [ ] Alto ### Estado - [ ] En desarrollo - [x] Listo para revisión - [ ] Bloqueado por CI o revisión - [ ] Requiere migración o acción manual ## Summary `rerun_h3_segment` treated only a fresh `prompt_override` as a user-typed prompt. Clip-level regenerate honors `_director_typed_prompts` from the review pause, then delegated to H3 with `prompt_override=None`. The no-text lock ran again (`compose_direct_video_prompt` and `_saved_prompt_contract`), stripped lettering directions, and the new take no longer matched the approved prompt. The dashboard H3 segment button always sends the stored prompt, so that path was safe. The common clip Regenerar button (and Workspaces, when not editing) does not. ## Overview 1. Review pause: user edits a video prompt to include readable text (e.g. a sign reading `OPEN`). `continue_pipeline` marks `_director_typed_prompts`. 2. First generation keeps the lettering (locks already skip typed fields). 3. User clicks Regenerar without opening the editor (`prompt_override` is omitted). 4. `_rerun_clip_video_impl` contracts the prompt as typed, then calls `rerun_h3_segment` without that override. 5. Before this fix, H3 re-locked the saved segment. After, it reads the same review mark and leaves the lettering. A plan that was never edited still gets the no-text lock. ## Detailed changes ### Backend `rerun_h3_segment` now sets `typed` from `prompt_override` **or** `_typed_at_review` on `video_prompt`, `window_prompts`, or `h3_segment_prompts`. body:
Design spec for `@spokospace/labels-niimbot` (#10). Docs only, no code.

The spec is `.ai/specs/2026-10-13-labels-niimbot-template-import.md`. It covers three parts:
- **`extractTemplates(bytes)`** reads templates and the font catalogue from the NIIMBOT desktop app's Isar database. The scan is defensive and runs in the browser, so the file never leaves it.
- **`importTemplates()`** maps them to `labels-render` v1 templates. It reports warnings per template and a failure entry for each template it cannot convert. Every emitted template passes `validateTemplate()`, and the output is deterministic, as `BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md` requires for the import output.
- **`niimbotFonts`** bundles the OFL fonts that real templates use: Inconsolata, Baloo Paaji, Markazi Text and Cookie. They come from upstream at pinned commits. The three Chinese display fonts are skipped.

The maintainer answered Q1 to Q11 on #10. author: mindaugasr
body:
TypeScript rewrite: editors, part 1. This PR converts `_baseEditor`, `textEditor`, `checkboxEditor`, `numericEditor`, `passwordEditor` and the editor registry (`index`).

## What changes

- **`BaseEditor` and `TextEditor` are ES classes now.** They were constructor functions with prototype methods.
  - `extend()` now returns `class Editor extends Base {}`.
  - Both ways of writing a custom editor keep working: `FreeGrid.editors.TextEditor.prototype.extend()` (older style) and `class MyEditor extends FreeGrid.editors.TextEditor`.
  - The type tests (`test/types/editors`) and the editor specs pass.
- **Class-field trap avoided.** The base constructor calls `init()`, which creates the textarea and other fields. These fields are `declare`d, so subclass field definitions do not reset them to `undefined` after `super()`.
- **`saveValue`** uses min/max for the Ctrl+Enter range, with the same result.
- **`checkEditorSection`** returns early; the result is the same.
- **`RegisteredEditor`** is a class with `#private` state. `getEditorInstance` and `_getEditorInstance` are both still exported.
- **`EditorGrid`** is a typed alias for the grid. `core.js` is not typed yet, and editors reach deep into it; the alias carries a lint reason.
- **The date editor** is still JavaScript and is cast in the registry. It is typed in part 2.

**Possibly breaking for custom editors:** one that calls the parent as a function, `TextEditor.call(this, instance)`, no longer works, because ES classes cannot be called without `new`. `extend()` and `class … extends` are the documented ways and keep working.

## Commits

1. `git mv` only.
2. The classes and types.

## Tests

- typecheck, lint and the type tests pass.
- The unit tests (511) show no regressions; dist (23) passes.
- E2E in Chromium: 2095 specs, no regressions.
- The merge queue runs Firefox and WebKit.

Part 2 covers the handsontable, autocomplete, dropdown, select and date editors, and moves the date picker to `#private` fields.

author: doonminus2
body:
## CORE-17: async Submit (service, API, pages, sweeper)

Submit now answers at once. The Student's code is saved with the true submit time and judged in the background, so the Student can do other things while the page refreshes. If the server restarts mid-judging, the Submission is picked up again and the Instructor sees a red banner saying so. Late is always decided from the time the request arrived.

**This PR must merge together with the OPS-30 PR.** The service calls repository methods that only the SQL adapter in OPS-30 provides. On its own, a real-database Submit fails and the sweeper logs an error every 15 seconds. Everything in this PR is tested on the in-memory fakes. Same pairing rule as CORE-16 and OPS-20 in `docs/task-scope.md`.

### What changes

- **States.** A Submission is `received`, `judging`, `done` or `failed`. One transition table in `core/submissions/models.py` owns the legal moves, and every repository write is a compare-and-set on the status. A `recovery` marker (`none`, `reconnected`, `rejudged`) only moves up.
- **Submit.** `SubmissionService.submit` stores a `received` row with `is_late`, `max_score` and the Version in force at receive time, then the handler starts `service.judge` as a background task, the sync pattern from ADR-0010. The JSON route answers `202` with `Location: /api/v1/submissions/{id}`, and `GET /api/v1/submissions/{id}` shows the status.
- **Judging.** `judge` starts the batch, saves the Judge0 tokens, holds a 90 second lease, and collects the result. It grades against the Version the Submission was received on, not today's Test Cases. Judge0 unreachable releases the lease so the sweeper retries. A batch Judge0 lost is judged again once. Anything unfinished 15 minutes after receive becomes `failed`.
- **Restart recovery.** A daemon thread calls `recover()` every 15 seconds. It starts only from `questly.main:app`, never inside `create_app`, so tests spawn no thread. `recover` takes rows whose lease expired and reattaches to the saved tokens (`reconnected`) or sends the code again (`rejudged`).
- **Rules.** While a Submission is pending, Submit and Run answer `409 submission_pending`. A `failed` Submission does not count and does not use up the single Submit. Counted Submissions, PostingStats and classroom stats use the latest `done` one.
- **Judge0.** `Judge0CodeRunner` also implements the new `BatchRunner` (`start`, `collect`). `run_many` is now `collect(start())`, so Run behaves as before. `CodeRunner.run` and `run_many` are unchanged.
- **Pages.** S-02a is S-02 while a Submission is pending: code read-only, no Run or Submit button, `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2">`. A `failed` Submission shows an alert and Submit works again. The Instructor sees a "Judging" badge, a red "Recovered" badge and a red banner with the true submit time. No JavaScript.

### Not in this PR

The database side (columns, migration, SQL adapter, ADR-0011) is the OPS-30 PR.

### For the reviewer

- The JSON Submit changes from 201 to 202. ADR-0011 in the OPS-30 PR records it and supersedes ADR-0007 sections 5.5 and 11 for Submit only.
- `judge` and `recover` take no Actor, because authorization happened at receive and no route exposes them. `tests/architecture/test_conventions.py` gets a named exemption for exactly those two methods.
- A batch Judge0 lost marks `rejudged` even when the same worker notices, so the marker means "the original run was interrupted", not only "a worker vanished".
- Risks: a stuck Judge0 can hold one threadpool thread for up to 15 minutes. A background task delayed past the lease can leave one orphaned Judge0 batch.
- `CONTEXT.md:100` still defines the Counted Submission as the latest one. It is now the latest `done` one. `AGENTS.md` line 25 is also stale. Both are outside this task's row.
- CORE-13 edits `core/submissions/` in parallel, so a merge conflict is possible.

### Verification

Local, on head `10bd492`: `uv run pytest` 1084 passed and 139 skipped, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean, no `<script>`, `javascript:` or inline handlers in the templates. `scripts.demo` with the unsafe runner, driven over HTTP: Submit returned 303, the page showed "Judging attempt 2, 2 tests…" with the refresh tag and no Submit button, then the result a second later.

Not verified: the `judge0` smoke tests are SKIPPED because no real Judge0 was reachable. That Judge0 answers `null` for an unknown token is an inference from its docs.

CI result for the head commit: pending, to be added once it finishes.

body:
Part of #181 (laptop checks, Fedora, Intel Iris Xe, Google Chrome).

## What the full e2e run found
`npm run e2e -- --workers=2` on `main` (f008972): **81 passed, 8 failed**.

| Failure | Cause | Here |
|---|---|---|
| `doc-pdf:155`, `doc-pdf:216`, `export-cli:24` | 3D snapshots never drew: the document never reached `data-doc-ready` | **fixed** |
| `towers:108` every referenced file | 404 on `report-studio` `output/dev-squad.pdf`, an `optional: true` file not committed (#137) | **fixed** (test skips `missingOptional`) |
| `voice:204` | page mocked as a hub, `/api/hub/alerts` not mocked: 404s | fixed on `main` in v0.10.0 too (same mock) |
| `hub:146` | same 404 | already fixed on `main` by 2ceeb43 |
| `towers:80` Syllabus Forge, Forge Studio | 180 s timeout at load 11-14 on 8 cores (software WebGL, see below) | not a code bug |

## The snapshot bug
Chrome stops animation frames in an iframe it considers unseen: off screen (`left: -10000px`), `visibility: hidden` or `opacity: 0`. The snapshot iframe was all of these, so r3f never rendered and each capture hit the 25 s timeout, three tries per tower. Measured with the bare snapshot page on this laptop:

| iframe | result |
|---|---|
| as shipped (off screen, hidden) | timed out |
| off screen, visible | timed out |
| on screen, `visibility: hidden` | timed out |
| on screen, `opacity: 0` | timed out |
| on screen | PNG in 11.2 s |
| on screen, under the page (`z-index: -1`) | PNG in 11.0 s |

It passed on the test server because there the run used Playwright's Chromium headless shell, which does not throttle that iframe; the installed Chrome (the e2e `channel: 'chrome'`, `export --pdf` when the headless shell is missing, a user's desktop browser) does. The fix keeps the iframe on screen at `z-index: -2` under a full-viewport veil in the page colour (`z-index: -1`); Chrome does not track occlusion. A mid-build screenshot shows only "Building the document…" on white.

## Verified
- `doc-pdf:216` alone: 3/3 figures drawn in all three runs (was 0/3); `doc-pdf:155` and `export-cli:24`: pass (10.5 min).
- `voice:204`, `towers:108`: pass on the current `main`.
- `npm run check`: typecheck clean; one `tests/cli.test.ts` history test timed out at 5.1 s under load and passes alone (4 s).

## Squad review round
- Security (DeepSeek 4.1 Flash, $0.0045): approve, 5 low findings. Applied: the capture frame was reachable with Tab (now `inert`, `tabIndex -1`, `aria-hidden`), and could print mid-capture (`.snap-capture` hidden under `@media print`). Not applicable: `--paper` is always defined on the document page; `isSnapMessage` is outside this change.
- Review (GLM 5.3 FlashX, $0.0074): changes, 3 findings. Applied: print (as above) and the optional-file skip per node instead of per tower. Not applicable: the document page has no dark theme.
- Coder (Claude Haiku 5.5): step 01 $0.0023, step 02 $0.0011. Lead check in Chrome: the level-2 document still draws 3/3 figures with an inert frame; `towers.spec` referenced-files passes on a clean server.
- Merged `main` (v0.10.0): `voice.spec` takes main's identical alerts mock; `towers.spec` keeps the per-node skip (main's tower-wide `paths.delete` depends on node order and is the case GLM flagged). The changelog entries moved to Unreleased.

## Not in this PR
- `e2e.log` is not committed: the run was not green. A full rerun follows on this branch.
- Headless Chrome here uses SwiftShader even with a GPU (`ANGLE (Vulkan, SwiftShader)`), so the laptop is not faster than the server for 3D in e2e: #209, together with the PDF export always forcing SwiftShader.

author: satran004
body:
## Summary
This PR proposes ADR-0057 (status: Proposed): run ZeroJ from JavaScript (Node.js and browsers), Python, Go and Rust with no JVM, using GraalVM 25.3 Web Image (WebAssembly) and `native-image --shared` (a C ABI library).

A proof of concept built the **released `0.1.0-pre13` jars, unchanged**. In wasm (Node 22 and Chrome 155) and as a native library (Python ctypes and Bun FFI), it compiled circuits, ran a dev setup, and **proved and verified Groth16 BLS12-381**. It also ran Poseidon, Pedersen, BBS, confidential notes and EdDSA-Jubjub.

- Deterministic outputs are byte-identical to the JVM.
- A proof made in any runtime verifies in the others and in snarkjs.

The ADR proposes:
- opt-in `zeroj-wasm` and `zeroj-native` modules, kept out of the default build and the BOM;
- an export surface in tiers;
- four core fixes for the gaps the POC found.

**Docs-only.** This PR adds `docs/adr/0057-webassembly-and-native-library-bindings.md`. No implementation, test or build files change. Accepting the ADR is design acceptance only.

## Gaps found by the POC
| ID | Gap | Proposed fix |
|----|-----|--------------|
| G1 | **Web Image 25.3 backs `new SecureRandom()` with `Math.random()`.** ZeroJ constructs `new SecureRandom()` in 12 classes, including the Groth16 prover's blinders, so a proof made in the browser would leak the witness. | D3: the binding installs a WebCrypto `SecureRandom` (verified with a constant-filler probe), and ZeroJ adds a fail-closed guard. |
| G2 | The `zeroj-blst` jar registers `BlstBls12381Provider` and `BlstPairing` for reflection **without conditions**, so blst (JNI/FFM) is reachable in every image. | D4: conditional metadata plus an `AbortOnTypeReachable` guard. |
| G3 | `ProverToCardano` and `SnarkjsToCardano` compress points with blst. | D5: use `Bls12381Codecs`. The POC shows identical bytes to blst. |
| G4 | The proving-key store memory-maps files, which Web Image doesn't support. | D6: load keys and import zkeys from bytes, with the same validation. |
| G5 | Wasm is single-threaded. Proving is about 2.2× slower than one JVM core. | Recorded; worker sharding is future work. |

## Decisions
| ID | Risk | Proposes |
|----|------|----------|
| D1 | R2 | Opt-in `zeroj-wasm` / `zeroj-native` modules behind `-PincludeBindings`; not in `zeroj-bom-core`; default build unchanged |
| D2 | R2 | One transport-neutral facade on every target; it uses only existing validating ZeroJ APIs; `{ok, value \| error}` envelopes; parity fixtures |
| D3 | R2, security-critical | WebCrypto `SecureRandom` provider in the binding, plus a ZeroJ fail-closed randomness guard under Web Image |
| D4 | R1 | blst never reachable in a binding image (conditional metadata + reachability guard) |
| D5 | R1 | Pure-Java compression for the Cardano encoding; blst stays as the differential oracle; identical on-chain bytes |
| D6 | R1 | Load proving keys and import zkeys from bytes, accepting and rejecting the same bundles as the file loader |
| D7 | R2 | Export tiers: Tier 1 verify/encode (no secrets) first; Tier 2 prove/sign/seal gated; Tier 3 never in wasm |
| D8 | R2, escalated | Secret operations in a browser fall outside ADR-0039 §3.1, so they get an explicit "browser (unassessed)" label, run in a Worker, and make no constant-time claim |
| D9 | R0 | Circuits are compiled into bundles: a generic bundle, plus app bundles built by a Gradle task |
| D10 | R0 | Pin the GraalVM release line (25.3), Binaryen ≥ 119, Node ≥ 25 or the flag |
| D11 | R2 | C ABI conventions following Mesmo; platform matrix; wrappers |
| D12 | R0 | Size work measured against the POC baseline (13.4 MiB / 4.9 MiB gzip) |

## Points needing a maintainer decision
1. **Q1: offer Tier 2 (secret-bearing) operations in the browser at all?**
   - Options: (a) never; (b) behind the D8 label and a Worker, after external review; (c) only for named low-value circuits.
   - Lean: (b). Client-side proving is the main privacy benefit, and a server prover sees the whole witness.
2. **Q2: distribution channels.** npm, PyPI, a Go module, or GitHub releases. Lean: GitHub release assets first.
3. **Q3: GraalVM line.** Stay on 25.3, like Julc, or move to 25.4. Lean: 25.3, then re-run parity before switching.
4. **Q4: the D4 mechanism.** Conditional metadata, or splitting `zeroj-verifier-groth16`'s blst dependency. Lean: conditional metadata, which changes no coordinates.
5. **Q5: where the bindings live.** Opt-in modules here, or a separate repository as Mesmo is for CCL. Lean: here, so parity runs against the same commit.
6. **Q6: commit the POC as evidence?** It is currently outside the repo. Options: commit it under `bindings/poc/`, attach it to this PR, or let M2/M3 supersede it.
7. **Q7: a circuit-agnostic prover.** A separate ADR if wanted.

## Related findings (out of scope)
- Small-circuit proving takes the same time on 16 cores as on 1 (2,930 and 5,370 constraints). Worth a profiling issue.
- `zeroj-codec` uses Jackson data binding for snarkjs JSON, which likely adds to bundle size.
- Building a 2^20-leaf Poseidon tree takes about 3 minutes in wasm.

## Test plan
- [x] Docs-only: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` shows only the ADR (1 file, 609 lines).
- [x] Claims verified against the code at `43c7b32`:
  - `new SecureRandom()` appears in 12 classes (15 occurrences);
  - `zeroj-blst` `reflect-config.json` has 2 entries with 0 conditions;
  - `ProverToCardano` / `SnarkjsToCardano` import `supranational.blst.P1_Affine` / `P2_Affine`;
  - `MmapG1File.map` uses `FileChannel.map(..., Arena)`.
- [x] POC evidence (GraalVM 25.3.4.1, macOS arm64):
  - wasm and native smoke runs;
  - `snarkjs groth16 verify` → `OK!` for proofs made in wasm, on the JVM and in the native library;
  - blst vs pure-Java compression identical for 2 proofs;
  - constant-filler randomness probe: identical proofs with the patched RNG, distinct proofs with the real one;
  - `javap` of `Target_sun_security_NativePRNG_Web.engineNextBytes` shows the call to `WebImageUtil.random()`.
- [x] References fetched 2026-10-13:
  - GraalVM Web Image reference manual and API guide ("`@JS.Export` is not implemented yet");
  - W3C Web Cryptography Level 2 FPWD (22 April 2025) §10.1.1.
  - The Native Image C API docs are marked unverified in the ADR.
- [ ] Reviewer: check the D3 guard design (G1 is the one finding that silently breaks zero knowledge).
- [ ] Reviewer: check D8 against ADR-0039 §3.1, and whether Tier 2 belongs in the browser at all.
- [ ] Reviewer: check the D5 validation-difference table plan, and the D6 equivalence criteria.

author: mgifford
body:
## Summary

Phase 1a of making the maintenance rollup useful for deciding which Dependabot PRs to merge. In the current `maintenance-rollup.public.json`, all 16 Dependabot PRs read `needs_review` with `ci_status: pending`, so nothing was actually triaged.

- **CI status bug:** the scanner read only the legacy commit-status API. GitHub Actions reports through check runs, and the legacy API says `pending` when there are no statuses at all, so every Actions-only PR looked pending forever. It now combines check runs and legacy statuses. Skipped and neutral runs are ignored. A new `ci_status: "none"` value means the PR has no checks at all, which is why it can never auto-merge. The schema enum is extended to match.
- **Grouped PRs:** "Bump the npm_and_yarn group … with N updates" titles carry no versions. The scanner now parses each `Updates \`x\` from a to b` line in the body. Update type takes the riskiest bump, and dependency class is combined conservatively (any unknown → unknown, any production → production). It also parses `Update X requirement from …` titles (pip/bundler).
- **Transitive npm dependencies:** dependencies not listed in `package.json` (e.g. `brace-expansion`) are now classified from `package-lock.json`. npm's `dev: true` flag means dev-only; anything else, including `devOptional`, counts as production. It uses the manifest directory the PR touches, so nested packages work. Each manifest is fetched at most once per run.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 146 pass, 0 fail (24 new, in `test/rollup-pr-triage.test.js`).
- **Not verified:** a live run against GitHub. The next scheduled `maintenance-inventory` run is the first real test.
- Not covered: yarn and pnpm lockfiles still fall back to `unknown`, and only `classifyFromPackageLock` handles transitive dependencies (npm only).

## Notes

- Total diff is above AGENTS.md's 200-line batch guidance. Roughly 140 of those lines are tests.
- No policy changes: production updates still need review. The difference is that dev-only transitive updates with passing CI can now reach `eligible`.
- The "PRs to consider merging" page view follows in a separate PR.

author: andrew-barvas
body:
## Summary

Fifth item from the dead-code/tools/CMS/admin survey. Decodes JWTs the target itself issues — in a Set-Cookie header, the response body, or the request/response URL — and reports on their own header/payload fields. Deliberately never forges a token or replays anything against the server: `docs/NEXT-STEPS.md` already lists "JWT forging" as an attack, not scanning, out of scope for this product, so every check here is either pure decoding (a JWT's header/payload are base64url, never encrypted, so reading them needs no secret) or a local, offline HMAC recomputation against a short list of publicly known weak secrets — zero extra requests sent to the target.

- `src/worker/tools/jwtAnalysis.ts`: extended-tier, no binary, same `api` profile placement as `sessionCheck.ts` (the closest existing analogue — HTTP-based, no third-party tool). Flags: `alg:"none"` or an empty signature segment; no `exp` claim; a signature that matches one of ~30 common weak HMAC secrets (jwt.io's own playground default, `"your-256-bit-secret"`, is literally #2 on real-world wordlists); transmission over plain HTTP; appearing in a URL at all. checkIds are `jwt-analysis.<type>:<url>#<sha256(token)[0:12]>` — a per-token fingerprint, never the raw token — except `sent-over-http`, which is scan-level.
- Verified the HMAC recomputation against a real token: the fixture `JWTIO_DEFAULT` constant in the test file is jwt.io's actual published playground example, confirmed to match `"your-256-bit-secret"` via Node's own crypto before being used as a fixture.
- `compliance.ts`/`fixDifficulty.ts` get explicit entries (`sessionCheck.*` never did — the gap stays there, not duplicated here).

## Test plan

author: vanlueckn
body:
## Summary

An `[onlyeditor]` child of a crossing was run as a plain sound object with no traffic-light controller, so its script read `TrafficLightPhase = -1`. Gerolstein's `BÜ Gong` (light 4 of the station crossing) treats anything outside 6–8 as red and rang every 2 s without pause.

Editor-only crossing lamps that have a script are now registered as mesh-less `LightObject`s of their crossing, like visible lamps, so their script and sound follow the crossing's light. Other editor-only sound objects are unchanged.

Fixes #303

## Impact

The level crossing gong at Gerolstein station only rings while the crossing is closed. The same applies to any map that uses invisible scripted lamps as children of a crossing.

## Reference behavior

From the issue: in OMSI 2.2.032 the gong only sounds while the crossing light is red and the gates close. Removing `[onlyeditor]` from the object made neoOMSI behave the same, which shows the object and its script are correct and the editor-only placement path was at fault. Not re-checked in OMSI by me.

## Validation

- New test `scene::crossing_tests::an_editor_only_lamp_follows_its_crossing_light` (synthetic crossing + editor-only gong child, through `prepare_tiles` and `commit_upload`). Fails without the fix in either `place.rs` or `upload.rs`.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 1347/1348 pass; the failure is `texture::dds_precedes_exact_names_but_preserves_folder_priority`, which also fails on `main` in my environment.
- Headless Gerolstein run (Linux, entry "Gerolstein, Bahnhof (Bussteige B1-B4)", 120 s): before, both gongs stayed at phase -1 / `Red = 1`; after, they follow light 4 of crossing 297405 (`Red = 1` only during phase 2). Not listened to in a windowed session.

## Reviewer notes

- `commit_upload` now extends the tile's `light_objects` instead of replacing them, so the lamps added during `place_tile` survive the upload.
- The lamp resolution block was moved, unchanged, above the editor-only branch.
- Not addressed: an editor-only crossing object with its own script and sound still gets `controller: None` in that branch. No map showing it is known.

body:
## What does this PR change?

The weekly macOS check (#399) failed again on the manual run [38402961712](https://github.com/scenario-labs/blender-plugin/actions/runs/38402961712) on `main`, this time for a different reason than #396's stale expectation:
- **macOS:** the full installed suite runs as one Blender process, and on the hosted macOS runner it reached `tools/test_blender.py`'s 300-second default `--timeout` during its last module, `test_waveform_worker`. That module starts child Blender processes.
- **Windows:** the same run passed in about 3 minutes.
- **Last week:** the macOS full suite took about 3 minutes.

The suite has grown since, so 300 seconds no longer leaves headroom on that runner. Every test that ran before the timeout passed.

A likely root cause is fixed separately in #443. On the hosted macOS runner, the first local MCP server start in each Blender process stalls about 35 seconds in a reverse DNS lookup of `127.0.0.1`, costing roughly 105 seconds per macOS suite run. This budget complements that fix and does not replace it.

- `.github/workflows/blender-os.yml` passes `--timeout 900` to the weekly full-suite step. The job keeps its 30-minute `timeout-minutes`, so a real hang still ends the job.
- `docs/development/validation.md` says the weekly full suite runs with a 900-second per-process timeout, and why.
- The weekly-platform-CI evidence records note the run; `lane-evidence` gets a digest note.

`ci.yml`'s baseline runs the default suite, not `--suite all`. It finished in 1.5 to 2.5 minutes on today's PRs and is unchanged.

After merge, dispatch `blender-os.yml` on `main`. If both legs pass, #399 can close. #400 (Windows) is closed on today's passing Windows leg.

Refs #399

author: k3noxofficial
body:
Refs #165 (finding 10 of the process roll-up, "Release notes are the '## [0.1.0]' CHANGELOG section only ..."). `Refs`, not `Closes`: #165 lists other findings this PR does not touch, so it must stay open when this merges. Multica K3NOX-248 (part of K3NOX-95; complements K3NOX-108, the fold itself, and K3NOX-151).

Requirement: none in GOAL.md fits exactly; this is release-process hygiene around F3 (updates ship from release notes users read).

## Cause
`scripts/release/release.sh` builds the release notes from the `## [X.Y.Z]` CHANGELOG section alone (step 4) but its preconditions only required that heading to exist, and `docs/RELEASING.md` step 1 said to add a section without saying to fold `## Unreleased` into it. A release cut with entries still under `## Unreleased` published notes that left them out.

## Change
- `release.sh`: new precondition. `## Unreleased` (or `## [Unreleased]`) must hold nothing except blank lines and `###` subheadings. Otherwise `problem` reports it: `--dry-run` prints `a real release would refuse: ...`, a real run stops with `refused: ...` before the check or any build. The message says how to fix it.
- `docs/RELEASING.md`: step 1 says to rename `## Unreleased` to `## [X.Y.Z] - <date>` and start a fresh, empty `## Unreleased`; the "refuses unless" paragraph lists the new condition.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: one line under Unreleased / Changed.
- Consequence to know about: on current `Main` the `## Unreleased` block has 86 content lines, so `release.sh 0.1.0` is refused until K3NOX-108 folds it. That is the intended effect.

## Tested
New tests in `core/tests/test_local_ci.py` run a copy of `release.sh` in a throwaway repo (bare origin, VERSION 1.2.3, stub tools, a check.sh that fails so a run that gets past the preconditions stops there and builds nothing):
- `test_release_refuses_while_changelog_unreleased_has_content[False|True]`: real run and `--dry-run` both report the problem; the real run exits 2 with "1 precondition(s) failed; nothing was built or published" and never reaches the check.
- `test_release_accepts_an_empty_changelog_unreleased[...]` (4 cases: `## Unreleased` and `## [Unreleased]` with empty `###` subheadings, real and dry): the preconditions pass.

Without the fix (unmodified `release.sh`): `cd core && uv run pytest -q -o addopts="" tests/test_local_ci.py -k changelog_unreleased` -> `2 failed, 4 passed` (the two "refuses" cases; the "accepts" controls pass either way).
With the fix, same command: `6 passed`; whole file `uv run pytest -q -o addopts="" tests/test_local_ci.py` -> `31 passed`.
`uv run ruff check src tests ../scripts` and `uv run ruff format --check . ../scripts` clean; `bash -n scripts/release/release.sh` ok.

`scripts/ci/check.sh --changed` on kokadock (commit 023aef5 is on top of origin/Main 934ae07): areas shell, secrets and core selected.
- shell: could not run, shellcheck is not installed on this host. secrets: could not run, gitleaks is not installed. panes: not selected (no Go on this host either).
- core: ruff check and format pass; pytest has one failure, `tests/test_installer.py::test_without_a_checksum_tool_a_no_git_checkout_is_refused` (`FileExistsError` on a symlink to `/usr/local/bin/orca`). It fails the same way on an unmodified `origin/Main` worktree on this host (`1 failed`), so it is not caused by this change.
- The full run (`scripts/ci/check.sh`) was not done; it needs those tools.

author: deepontology
body:
## What changed

- **`scripts/test-headers.ts` (new).** Parses `static/_headers` the way Cloudflare reads it and asserts the CSP directives, HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and the four deliberately-scoped CORS blocks. It runs in `npm run test`, so a regression in the header policy fails the gate with no build and no browser.
- **`scripts/test-recovery.ts`** added to the `npm run test` chain. It asserts Ed25519 parity between the WebCrypto and JS paths; it was not previously run by the gate.
- **`community/identity.ts`.** The freshness window now requires `issued_at` to be an integer. A non-numeric value made the subtraction NaN, and every comparison against NaN is false, so the skew check could be skipped.
- **`community/api.ts`.** An unhandled error is logged server-side and answered as `{ "error": "internal error" }` instead of echoing the driver message to the caller.
- **`src/lib/components/media/ArticleLayout.svelte`.** A narrative link renders as a link only for `http(s)`; any other scheme, for example `javascript:`, is inert.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `feed.yml`, `release.yml`.** The three actions are pinned to commit SHAs, keeping the version in a trailing comment.
- **`static/.well-known/security.txt` (new).**

`npm run data`, `npm run test` (response headers 20/20, recovery 33/33) and `npm run check` (0 errors, 0 warnings).

author: dsn27
body:
The three items of #403's findings that needed a decision, resolved as discussed:

**#424, Make3D**
- `MakeRuledSolid` and `MakeRuledShell` return null when the paths cannot be connected (different number of segments, an open path for the solid, a failing surface), as their documentation promised and as `Constr3DRuledSolid` and `Constr3DRuledFace` expect, instead of throwing `NotImplementedException`.
- `Make3D.Intersection(Solid, Solid)` delegates to `Solid.Intersect`, like `Union` and `Difference` delegate to `Solid.Unite` and `Solid.Subtract`.
- The members left over from the implementation on top of an external modelling kernel are marked `[Obsolete]` with the replacement where one exists: `MakeOffset(Solid, double)` and `MakeOffset(Shell, double)` (use `Shell.GetOffset`), `Difference(Shell, Solid)`, `Difference(Face, Solid)`, `Difference(Solid, Face)` (use `Solid.SplitByPlane`), `Intersection(Shell, Solid)`, `Intersection(Face, Face)` (use `Face.Intersect`), `PlaneIntersection` (use `GetPlaneIntersection`), `GetShape`, `GetShapes`, the `MakePrismMiter` overload with a polygonal path, `ImportDtk`, `Curtail` and `RemoveBoundaryOffset`. They behave as before (throw or return null) and are to be removed in the next minor version. No code in the repository calls them, so the build stays free of CS0618.

**#423, the Measure action**
- `"MenuId.Measure"` is a sub menu, so the `case` in `FrameImpl.OnCommand` that started `new Measure()` was dead code (and threw when reached programmatically). It is removed.
- `CADability.Actions.Measure` is marked `[Obsolete]`, with its doc comment pointing at the construction actions of the sub menu, and is to be removed in the next minor version.

**#428, `EFontFlag`**
- `DimensionStyle.EFontFlag` is a `[Flags]` enum with the values 1, 2, 4, 8, so `DimFontBold` can be stored and `DimFontStrikeOut` no longer equals italic plus underline. Checked before changing it: the font flags are written neither in the JSON nor in the binary format and the DXF import and export do not touch them, so no file has to be converted. The other two parts of #428 (`Clone`, `DimBreakDimLine`) were fixed in #435.

Tests: `MakeRuledSolidTests` (a box from two squares, null for different segment counts, a shell but no solid for open paths), `Make3DIntersectionTests` (overlapping and disjunct boxes) and `DimensionStyleFontFlagsTests` (single bits, bold stored, strike out independent). The whole `CADability.Tests` suite passes except the two `VolumeTests` of #401, which fail on master as well. CADability.Forms builds.

Closes #423, closes #424, closes #428.

author: hobeone
body:
## What

With `enable_filejoin` or `enable_tar` off, the unpack stage skipped a split (`.001`/`.002`) or `.tar` archive but then treated it as extracted.
`extractArchive` returned an empty `Result` and a nil error for the skip, so `extractPendingArchives` logged `Extracted ... successfully` and appended the archive to `allSuccessful`.
`cleanupArchives` then queued its parts for deletion at finalize.
The downloaded payload was deleted instead of delivered.

## Fix

`extractArchive` now owns the "skipped" verdict.
It returns a third value, `attempted`, which is false when no extractor ran: a disabled split, a disabled tar, or an unrecognised type (the `default` arm, which had the same empty-success shape; `unpack.Scan` does not produce `UnknownArchive` today, so that arm is latent).
`extractPendingArchives` checks `attempted` before anything else and moves on.
The consumers that act on a success all sit behind that check, so none needs its own test.

`extractedAny` (the re-scan trigger) stays false for a skipped archive.
A skip puts nothing new on disk, and the archive is already marked in `processed`, so a further pass would find nothing.

The job's status and fail message do not change: a skip set no `UnpackError` before and sets none now.
The visible differences are that the stage log no longer says `Extracted <name> successfully` for a skipped archive, and the parts reach the final directory.

## Sites (Rule 4)

Consumers of `extractArchive`'s result.
`git grep -n 'extractArchive(' -- '*.go' ':!*_test.go'` returns the definition and one call, `extractPendingArchives`:
- `extractPendingArchives`: fixed. A skip now returns before the error branch, the success log, the command and output capture, the containment check, the `allSuccessful` append and `extractedAny`.

Consumers of `allSuccessful`.
`git grep -n allSuccessful -- '*.go' ':!*_test.go'` returns only `internal/postproc/stage_unpack.go`. It has two writers and two readers:
- writer `extractPendingArchives`: fixed (above).
- writer `handleDirectUnpack`: already sound. It appends `job.DirectUnpackSets`, which comes from `DirectUnpacker.Results()`. `settleLocked` writes `successSets` only when `extractSet` returned nil, and `extractSet` returns nil only after it publishes the staged extraction. So every set there was actually extracted.
- reader `cleanupArchives` (queues parts for deletion): fixed by the writer fix. Pinned by the new test's `pendingDeletions` and FinalDir assertions.
- reader `applyPermissions` (runs only when `allSuccessful` is non-empty): fixed by the writer fix. Pinned by the new test's file-mode assertion (`Permissions: "700"`; it was 600 on the unfixed tree).

Other paths that might report success without touching the bytes:
- Recursion and the re-scan loop: already sound. Each pass goes through `extractPendingArchives`, so it gets the same verdict. A skipped archive is marked in `processed` and is not retried.
- DirectUnpack: already sound (see `handleDirectUnpack` above).
- `extractArchive`'s `default` arm: fixed (reports a skip, as above).

## Tests

- `TestUnpackStage_DisabledArchiveType_IsDelivered` (new, in `config_toggle_test.go`) covers both cases: a split pair with file join off, and a `.tar` with tar off. It uses `Cleanup: true` and `Permissions: "700"`, runs unpack and then `FinalizeStage`, and asserts:
  - no `UnpackError`
  - empty `pendingDeletions`
  - no `Extracted ... successfully` line
  - the mode is unchanged
  - every part reaches `FinalDir` with its content intact
- `TestUnpackHelpers`: the "disabled split" subtest now covers a disabled split, a disabled tar and an unknown type, each asserting `attempted == false`. `assertExtractEngine` asserts `attempted == true` for the RAR and 7z extractor scenarios.

Red against the unfixed tree:

```
config_toggle_test.go:89: pendingDeletions = [data.001 data.002]; want none for a skipped archive
config_toggle_test.go:93: stage log reports a skipped archive as extracted: "Extracted data successfully"
config_toggle_test.go:101: data.001 mode = 600; want 644 (permissions apply only after an extraction)
config_toggle_test.go:112: data.001 not delivered to FinalDir: ... no such file or directory
config_toggle_test.go:89: pendingDeletions = [x.tar]; want none for a skipped archive
```

`internal/postproc/testdata/skipped_archive.spec`: all 5 mutations KILLED.
| mutation | evidence |
|---|---|
| disabled file join reported as attempted | `pendingDeletions = [data.001 data.002]; want none for a skipped archive` |
| disabled tar reported as attempted | `pendingDeletions = [x.tar]; want none for a skipped archive` |
| unrecognised type reported as attempted | `test.bin: attempted = true; want a skip` |
| extractors reported as skipped | `scenario A: attempted = false; an extractor ran` |
| `extractPendingArchives` ignores the skip verdict | `pendingDeletions = [data.001 data.002]; want none for a skipped archive` |

## Docs

`docs/post-processing-contract.md`: the `unpack` row now describes the skip. The PP = 2 bullet cited `stage_unpack.go:363`, a line number that no longer points at the cleanup. It now names `UnpackStage.cleanupArchives`.

## Not done

- `enable_unrar: false` and `enable_7zip: false` do not stop RAR or 7z extraction while any other unpack type is enabled. They feed only `SetEnabled(EnableUnrar || Enable7zip || EnableFileJoin || EnableTar)`, plus DirectUnpack's gate for `EnableUnrar`. `extractArchive` has no per-type gate for RAR or 7z. That is a separate config-honouring bug and is left for its own issue.

Closes #943

author: doonminus2
body:
## OPS-30: schema and SQL adapter for async Submit

The database side of the CORE-17 async Submit PR. It adds the columns that let a Submission be saved before it is judged and found again after a restart.

**Merge together with the CORE-17 async PR.** This branch is stacked on `feat/CORE-17-async-submit`, so until that PR merges this diff also shows its commits. The OPS-30 changes are the last seven commits: ADR-0011, the migration, the table and adapter, the end-to-end test, an ADR fix, a test wording fix and the status flip.

### What changes

- **Migration `8e231a36283b`**, written by hand, `down_revision = "a2ec7512fb2c"` (the only head). It adds `status` (existing rows backfilled to `done`), `recovery`, `runner_tokens text[]` and `claimed_until` (the lease) to `core.submissions`, makes `score` nullable, and adds `CHECK ((status = 'done') = (score IS NOT NULL))` plus a partial unique index `uq_submissions_one_unfinished` that allows one unfinished Submission per Student and Posting. Downgrade deletes unfinished rows and restores `score NOT NULL`.
- **`SubmissionRow`** declares the same columns, checks and index.
- **`SQLSubmissionRepository`** implements `receive`, `claim_due`, `started`, `renew`, `finished`, `requeued`, `released` and `failed`. Each is one `UPDATE` that names the status it moves from, so a stalled worker cannot overwrite a row that moved on. `claim_due` is one statement with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so two processes never take the same row. `finished` writes the score, the result rows and the status in one transaction.
- **ADR-0011** records the decisions, the 201 to 202 change, the lease and marker rules, and the open risks. It supersedes ADR-0007 sections 5.5 and 11 and ADR-0008's deferral of `status`, for Submit only.
- **Tests.** The shared repository contract from `tests/contracts/submission_repository.py` now runs on Postgres (13 new cases). New `tests/db` tests cover two threads draining `claim_due` without overlap, `SKIP LOCKED` passing over a locked row, the score/status check and the unique index. `tests/db/test_submit_recovery_on_postgres.py` (8 tests) drives the whole flow through `create_app` on Postgres: a normal Submit, restart ending `reconnected` or `rejudged`, the Instructor banner, the 409 on a second Submit, and unposting mid-judging.
- `docs/task-scope.md`: CORE-17, OPS-30 and FE-07 go to `done` in this PR, which completes the pair.

### Verification

Local, on head `0646529`, against a throwaway Postgres 17 container (pgvector image), not Neon: `uv run pytest` with `POSTGRES_TEST_URL` set gave 1228 passed and 7 skipped. `tests/db` alone passed before the restack (136 passed) and with the new end-to-end file (144 passed). Without the variable the suite gives 1084 passed and 151 skipped. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean, and `tests/architecture` passes (32). The migration ran upgrade, downgrade, upgrade on that container, and bad rows were refused by the expected constraints.

**`scripts/run_integration_tests.py` has not been run yet.** AGENTS.md requires its result for a PR that touches `database/` or `alembic/`. The author will run it against a Neon branch and add the output here before merging. CI does not run `postgres` tests.

CI result for the head commit: pending, to be added once it finishes.

### For the reviewer

- `claim_due` writes the pending filter with literal statuses so Postgres can match the partial index under a generic plan. That reasoning is an inference and was not tested with a prepared plan.
- No extra index for `claim_due`: on 100,002 rows with 1 pending the planner used `uq_submissions_one_unfinished`, which only holds pending rows.
- Migrating a database before the CORE-17 async code is deployed breaks the old `add` path, because `status` has no default. Deploy them together.

author: frostney
body:
Array-literal spread (`[...a, ...b]`) was one of the few workloads where bytecode trailed the interpreter: 0.60–0.77x on `spread into new array` (#1347) and 0.32–0.60x on `reduce flatten (10x5)` (#1348). Each spread ran the full iterator protocol into a temporary array, then copied that array again through `GetProperty(IntToStr(I))`. Callgrind put half of the bytecode instructions in `IterableToArray` and its per-element string keys.

Both modes now read an array's elements directly when doing so cannot be observed. Bytecode is now 2.1x the interpreter's speed on #1347 and 1.35x on #1348, up from 0.86x and 0.58x on `main`.

## What changed

- `ArrayUsesIntrinsicIteration` (`Goccia.Values.Iterator.Concrete`) decides when the direct read is safe. All of these must hold:
  - the source is an Array whose prototype is the realm's `Array.prototype`;
  - the array has no own `Symbol.iterator`;
  - `Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` is still a data property holding `%Array.prototype.values%`;
  - `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%.next` is still the intrinsic.

  The guard reads own data descriptors only, so it never runs a getter. Two new realm slots, `%Array.prototype.values%` and `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%.next`, record the intrinsics when the realm creates them.
- With the guard in place, each value comes from `ArrayIteratorValueAt`, the function the array iterator itself uses (renamed from `GetArrayIteratorElement` and exported). Holes read through the prototype chain, so inherited values and getters are seen. The live element count is re-read every step, as `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%.next` does.
- Any other source still runs the full iterator protocol. Its values go into the target without per-element string keys. The VM pre-sizes the target array in both cases.
- The interpreter's `SpreadIterableInto` used to copy every `TGocciaArrayValue` with no check at all, so it ignored a replaced or own `Symbol.iterator`. It now uses the same guard and observes those, as bytecode already did. This covers array and call spread.

## Measurements

All numbers come from `--prod` builds of `main` at `2d32eda7` and this branch, on the same x86_64 Linux host.

Benchmark runner (`GOCCIA_BENCH_CALIBRATION_MS=100 GOCCIA_BENCH_ROUNDS=7`), on the two issue benchmarks copied verbatim from `benchmarks/arrays.js`. Runs were in ABBA order and serialized under the perf lock. Cells show the median ops/sec of each run (A1 / A2 for main, B1 / B2 for this branch).

| Benchmark | Mode | main | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| spread into new array | bytecode | 305,287 / 304,137 | 814,237 / 814,367 | 2.67x |
| spread into new array | interpreted | 355,663 / 350,378 | 391,690 / 395,153 | 1.11x |
| reduce flatten (10x5) | bytecode | 24,687 / 24,339 | 79,949 / 80,719 | 3.28x |
| reduce flatten (10x5) | interpreted | 42,217 / 41,133 | 59,595 / 59,633 | 1.43x |

Bytecode compared with the interpreter on the same build: on `main`, 0.86x on #1347 and 0.58x on #1348. With this PR, 2.07x and 1.35x.

Callgrind instruction counts (Ir) cover the whole process, including about 28.7M Ir of startup. Each workload calls the bench closure a fixed number of times and checks its result: 20,000 calls for #1347 and 2,000 for #1348.

| Workload | Mode | main Ir | this PR Ir | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #1347 spread into new array | bytecode | 1,028,726,944 | 436,730,626 | −57.5% |
| #1347 spread into new array | interpreted | 1,673,600,392 | 1,585,323,425 | −5.3% |
| #1348 reduce flatten (10x5) | bytecode | 1,319,704,593 | 406,334,221 | −69.2% |
| #1348 reduce flatten (10x5) | interpreted | 893,732,627 | 608,894,067 | −31.9% |
| Guard: non-array spreads (Set, string, generator, call spread) | bytecode | 924,777,703 | 782,541,009 | −15.4% |
| Guard: array iteration, for-of, destructuring, iterator helpers (no spread) | bytecode | 1,702,365,268 | 1,702,353,090 | 0.0% |

<details>
<summary>Guard benchmark files and host load</summary>

The serialized ABBA runner pass over `arrays.js`, `for-of.js`, `iterators.js`, `destructuring.js`, `collections.js`, `generators.js` and `typed-arrays.js` ran while peer sessions held the host at a load average of 12–14. Two runs of the same binary differed by up to 60%, so that pass cannot accept or reject a change. The guard workload above runs the same non-spread paths (forEach, find, map, filter, reduce, `Array.from`, `Array.of`, sort, for-of, array destructuring, flat, iterator `take`, Set construction). Its Ir is identical on both builds, within 0.001%.

</details>

## Spec

ECMA-262 es2026, snapshot `0248456c758431e4bb8e5d26333ff1865123c9cd` (tc39-mcp 0.6.3):

- `sec-runtime-semantics-arrayaccumulation`, §13.2.4.1 ArrayAccumulation, SpreadElement: `GetIterator(spreadObj, sync)`, then `IteratorStepValue` and `CreateDataPropertyOrThrow` for each value.
- `sec-runtime-semantics-argumentlistevaluation`, §13.3.8.1 ArgumentListEvaluation: call spread iterates the same way.
- `sec-getiterator`, §7.4.4 GetIterator, and `sec-getiteratorfrommethod`, §7.4.3 GetIteratorFromMethod: `Symbol.iterator` is read once per spread and `next` is captured once, so changes made during iteration are not observed.
- `sec-array.prototype-%symbol.iterator%`, §23.1.3.40: the initial value is `%Array.prototype.values%`.
- `sec-createarrayiterator`, §23.1.5.1, and `sec-%arrayiteratorprototype%.next`, §23.1.5.2.1: `next` re-reads the length each step (step 9) and returns `? Get(array, ToString(index))` (step 14.b). This is why holes read through the prototype chain and a getter that resizes the source changes how many values come out.

## Tests

`tests/language/expressions/spread/array.js` and `function-calls.js` now cover:

- a hole reading an inherited value;
- a hole getter that grows or shrinks the source;
- an own index getter;
- a replaced `Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]`, for both array and call spread;
- an accessor `Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]`, read once per spread;
- an own `Symbol.iterator` on the array;
- a replaced array prototype;
- an `Array` subclass.

When the guard was changed to accept every array, five of these tests failed in both modes.

test262 at `7ab7fafa`, with sparse `language/expressions`, `language/statements` and `built-ins/{Array,ArrayIteratorPrototype,TypedArray,Reflect}` checkouts, was run on `main` and this branch in both modes. The two branches failed exactly the same tests, so nothing went from PASS to FAIL.

## Known limitation, unchanged

A replaced `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%.next` is still not observed by spread, for-of or destructuring in either mode. When it is replaced, the guard declines the direct read, but the protocol fallback then calls the native iterator's `DirectNext` / `AdvanceNext`, which skips the `next` property. This PR leaves that unchanged. Fixing it means changing every iterator consumer, which is a separate change.

Closes #1347
Closes #1348

body:
## Summary

Register the upcoming Tailscale MCP for every bot and client. The server is native HTTP with a bearer token (home#3065), deployed in-cluster under the existing `mcp` namespace and ingress pattern (home#3066). Client configs store the env var name `TAILSCALE_MCP_API_KEY` only. Cluster, Tool Updater, and Worker should call `list_devices` on this MCP instead of the shared box `tailscale` CLI.

Refs #32

## What changed

- Client fragments for Codex, Grok, Gemini, agy, and OMP point at `http://tailscale-mcp.archer.casa/mcp` and reference `TAILSCALE_MCP_API_KEY`.
- `scripts/setup_agents.sh` and `scripts/install-homelab-mcp.ps1` (called from `setup_agents.ps1`) register the server for Codex, Grok, and agy (`~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`). DNS failure uses the Traefik Tailscale VIP plus a `Host` header, same as Immich.
- Secret loaders resolve `TAILSCALE_MCP_API_KEY` from `mcp/tailscale-mcp-secret` key `API_KEY` (process, then kubectl, then cache). The optional probe hits Tailscale `/health`, not Paperless.
- `validate-homelab-mcp.sh` and `.ps1` fail when the key, client entry, or endpoint is missing. They probe `/health` and `/mcp` with a short timeout and do not perform an MCP handshake or call `list_devices`. In-cluster checks are read-only `kubectl get`. A `tskey-` shaped value in a client config fails the scan without printing the match.
- `mcp/README.md` tells bots to use the MCP instead of box `tailscale`.

## Validation

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` — 85 tests OK
- Re-ran Tailscale, Immich, and secret-load tests after the final comment tweak — 36 tests OK
- `python3 scripts/promote_model_matrix.py --check` — pins match
- `python3 scripts/sync_agent_surfaces.py --check` — surfaces match
- `bash -n` on `scripts/setup_agents.sh`, `scripts/validate-homelab-mcp.sh`, and `shell/homelab-mcp.env.sh`
- No `scripts/validate-manifests.sh` and no `package.json`, so those checks were not run
- Isolated bootstrap (`HOME` / `CODEX_HOME` / `GROK_HOME` under a temp dir, `kubectl` and `tailscale` shadowed) registered `tailscale` for Codex, Grok, and agy. `validate-homelab-mcp.sh --skip-network --skip-cluster` passed with placeholder env values that were not written to disk
- Live `~/.codex`, `~/.grok`, and `~/.gemini` configs were not modified
- No `tailscale` or `kubectl` mutations

## Risks and manual steps

- Host, path, and secret names follow the Paperless/GitHub MCP pattern. home#3066 is not deployed yet, so those names are not confirmed by a live manifest. If the deployed Service, Ingress host, or secret data key differs, update the fragments and validators before relying on them.
- `validate-homelab-mcp` treats HTTP 401 as a loud failure. Unauthenticated `/health` is expected to return 401 until `TAILSCALE_MCP_API_KEY` is set.
- The in-cluster presence check fails until `deploy/tailscale-mcp`, `service/tailscale-mcp`, `ingress/tailscale-mcp`, and `secret/tailscale-mcp-secret` exist. The pre-existing Paperless check still uses `kubectl run`; this change does not. Run the validator with `--skip-cluster` until you want the read-only gets.
- PowerShell was not executed here (`pwsh` is not installed). Review `install-homelab-mcp.ps1` and `validate-homelab-mcp.ps1` on Windows.
- A real `list_devices` smoke is manual. The validator does not call it.

Josh, after home#3066 is Synced/Healthy:

1. Confirm the ingress host is `tailscale-mcp.archer.casa` and the secret is `mcp/tailscale-mcp-secret` data key `API_KEY`.
2. Load `TAILSCALE_MCP_API_KEY` (length only in logs) and re-run `scripts/setup_agents.sh` or `setup_agents.ps1`.
3. Run `scripts/validate-homelab-mcp.sh` without `--skip-network` once the edge answers.
4. From Cluster, Tool Updater, and Worker, call `list_devices` on the `tailscale` MCP server. Do not use box `tailscale`.

body:
The first automatic production deploy (run 38403758909) switched prod to 748aee1, which reported `Application startup complete` at 13:22:50, a minute after starting. The job still failed with "did not report startup in time".

`activate_release.sh` waited with `journalctl … | grep -q …` under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits on the first match, `journalctl` gets SIGPIPE, and pipefail turns the found line into a failure. Staging's journal was short enough to be written before grep exited, so it passed there. The check now counts matches with `grep -c`, which reads the whole journal.

## Verification

- Against prod's real journal (read-only), for that restart: the old expression says not found, the new one finds 1 match.
- Deployed this branch to staging with its own `infra/deploy.sh` (exit 0, startup reported, health OK).

## Tested on staging

This changes the deploy scripts, which `deploy-staging` can't test because it always runs `main`'s scripts. I deployed it to staging with the branch's `deploy.sh` instead and set the `staging` status by hand. `docs/staging.md` now describes that path.

Prod is healthy on 748aee1 (NRestarts 0, /healthz 200). Merging this deploys it to staging and prod, which also checks the corrected wait on prod.

author: derekmarshall
body:
Fixes the Linux CI failure on #662, which was in `claude_metrics::follow_tests::the_watch_wakes_on_append_and_is_silent_at_idle`: `left: (878, 3)`, `right: (750, 2)`.

## Cause

inotify reports one append twice: the write's `Modify`, then `IN_CLOSE_WRITE` (`Access(Close(Write))`). `agent::tail::watch::relevant` dropped only read-side access events, so the tail watcher, which both the Codex and Claude HUD feeds use, read every append twice on Linux. When the second read landed in the test's 200 ms idle window, the test failed. macOS uses the kqueue backend and never saw it.

## Fix

- `relevant` ignores every `Access` event. A write reports its own `Modify`, and the close adds nothing to it, so this halves the read work per append on Linux. The directory watcher in `app::watch` keeps `Close(Write)` on purpose, since it serves listings rather than tails, and it's unchanged.
- The idle test now waits until the append's own events stop producing work before it measures, so it checks the requirement (no work while nothing changes) rather than one backend's event count.

## Validation

- `make check-ci`: `=== GATE: PASS ===`, 3,151 library tests. `make lint-linux` passes.
- The filter test now lists `Close(Write)` and `Open(Write)` as irrelevant. Restoring the old filter fails it.
- This CI run is the Linux check.

GitHub предупреждал в журнале выкладки о двух вещах:
- `ubuntu-latest` переходит на Ubuntu 26.04 с 19.10.2026;
- действия на Node 20 устарели.

Этот PR переводит workflow заранее, а его собственный прогон тестов — проверка нового образа.

## Что изменено
- Все три задания запускаются на `runs-on: ubuntu-26.04`. Метка указана явно, чтобы обновление образа не застало выкладку врасплох.
- Тесты идут на Node 24 (`node-version: 24`), как локально (v24.21).
- Действия обновлены до версий на Node 24:
  - `actions/checkout` v4 → v7;
  - `actions/setup-node` v4 → v7;
  - `actions/configure-pages` v5 → v6;
  - `actions/upload-pages-artifact` v3 → v5;
  - `actions/deploy-pages` v4 → v5.
- `shivammathur/setup-php@v2` остаётся: он уже поддерживает Ubuntu 26.04. PHP по-прежнему 8.1 — самая старая версия, которую должен поддерживать сервер.

## Что проверяет прогон этого PR
- **PHP 8.1** устанавливается на Ubuntu 26.04.
- **MySQL** в образе теперь 8.4 вместо 8.0, в нём другой способ входа по умолчанию. Серверные тесты на MySQL это проверят.
- **Chrome 154** — для сквозного теста.

## На что обратить внимание
- С v4 `upload-pages-artifact` не кладёт в публикацию GitHub Pages файлы с точкой в начале имени. Pages их и так не использует: `.htaccess` нужен только Спринтхосту, на хостинг файлы идут отдельно через SFTP. Заодно в публикацию перестанет попадать служебная папка `.claude`.
- Задания публикации запускаются только на main. Их новые версии проверятся при первой выкладке после слияния.
