author: gerchowl-flock-release[bot]
body:
Prepares v3.0.0 on `dev`. Opened by the Promote workflow.

When this merges, release-follow-up.yml waits for the merged commit to pass its checks on `dev`, then fast-forwards `main` to it and tags it `v3.0.0`, which starts the Release workflow.

### Added
- The PR poller now records CI and PR outcomes as durable events (#1020, ADR-0028 §2). The same batched GraphQL request that drives the sidebar badge also reads each PR's head commit and its check results, so no request is added. Three kinds land in the event log: `pr.ci_completed { repo, branch, pr, head_sha, conclusion, failed_checks }`, once per head SHA when every check on it has concluded; `pr.merged` and `pr.closed`, once per PR. The first conclusion on a SHA wins, so a CI re-run on the same SHA is not announced again. A head with more checks than one page (100) holds does not conclude. Each fact is emitted once across repeated polls and server restarts, because the poller seeds its record from the log, read off the main loop, on the first round after a start. PRs that round already sees merged or closed are treated as history and not announced. A commit with no checks never produces `pr.ci_completed`. These kinds need a reader that skips unknown kinds (#1058) in the release before this one, so a downgrade keeps its log.
- Global `--format json|text`, with `--json` as its synonym, accepted before the verb or among a verb's flags, never inside the text `pane run`, `pane send-text`, `agent send` and the other text-typing verbs pass through, and never after a `--` (ADR-0029 §3). Verbs keep their default output; `--format text` picks a verb's text form where it has one. `pane read` and `agent read` keep their own `--format text|ansi` (#1024).
- Under `--json` / `--format json`, an error prints on stdout as `{"id", "error": {"code", "message", "retry", "exit", "data"}}` (`id` is `null` for a failure the client found without a request; `exit` is always the process's exit status), with the code's retry class and the command's exit status, and a one-line `error: <code>: <message>` on stderr, so a pipe into a JSON parser always has a document (ADR-0029 §4). No server is `transport`, the version gap `server_version_gap` (exit 78). An `unconfirmed` / `abandoned` send's result goes to stdout under `--json`. Without `--json` nothing changes. No exit code changes value; usage errors outside `delegate` and some verb-local failures do not print the envelope yet (#1150) (#1024).
- MCP tool errors carry `data.retry` and `data.exit` beside `data.refusal`, from the same registries as the CLI (#1024).
- The server emits durable supervisor events derived from each local agent's `state` (ADR-0028 §2): `agent.phase_changed { agent_id, pane, from, to, state, held_ms }` once a phase has held for the 20 s settle window (not configurable yet, #1152), plus `agent.needs_human`, `agent.limit_reached` and `agent.gone` as kinds of their own for routing. A status that flips back inside the window emits nothing, and a restart or live handoff does not repeat the last announcement. Read them with `events.read` or `flk events wait --kinds agent.phase_changed --subject <agent id>`. Older servers skip the new kinds in the log (#1027)
- Registered waits (#1031, ADR-0028 §5). `agent.get` and `agent.list` report an agent's oldest open wait as `state.waiting` (`{"on": {wait_id, predicate, since, deadline}}` with the predicate in canonical text, sourced to `wait_registry`), and an idle agent with one open reads `phase: waiting_on_event`. A held `events.read` (`flk events wait`, MCP `flock_events_read` with `wait_ms`) is a wait while it is held, recorded against the agent whose pane runs the caller, so a `flk events wait` started under Claude `run_in_background` reads `waiting_on_event` instead of `finished_with_background`. The new `wait.park` socket method, `flk wait park --until PREDICATE --deadline DUR` and MCP `flock_wait_park` open a wait and return at once, so the agent can end its turn. Predicates: `delegate:<id> phase in [<phases>]` and `reply:<correlation id>`; `pr:<n> ci_completed` and `any-delegate-of-mine changed` are refused with `wait_predicate_unsupported` (exit 2) until #1250, and a delegate on another host with `peer_incompatible`. A park lasts at most 24 h (`wait_deadline_too_long`, exit 2) and an agent holds at most 16 (`too_many_waits`, exit 10). A wait still open at its deadline is announced once as the durable event `wait.expired` and cleared. Protocol 30: against an older server (any protocol below 30, including 29) `flk wait park` exits 78 (`server_version_gap`). Parks end at their deadline until #1032, and do not survive a restart or live handoff yet (#1240).
- The server now keeps a goal record per agent (ADR-0030 §1, ADR-0031), the first slice of goal supervision (#1034). Nine new durable event kinds record it: `goal_armed`, `goal_amended`, `goal_status_set`, `goal_subtask_changed`, `goal_verdict`, `goal_met`, `goal_paused`, `goal_resumed` and `goal_disarmed`. Each is keyed by the agent's id, not a pane. The record is folded from the log once per server start, in the same read as the delegation edges, and every open goal is re-issued on start and after each log rotation so a quiet goal is never rotated out. Removing an agent disarms its goal. Nothing writes goal events yet: the `goal.*` verbs, `flk goal` and the MCP tools come in #1155 and #1156. Servers from 2.0.0 skip these kinds; a 1.x server quarantines a log that holds them, so every server sharing a log must be 2.0.0 or newer before goals are armed.
- Channel adapter contract, first part (#1037, ADR-0028 §8). Declare external channel bindings as `[[channels]]` entries with `name`, `owner_node`, `target` (`fleet`, `repo:<name>` or `agent:<id>`) and `scopes` (`notify`, `send_to_agent`, `reply`). The owner node issues a capability token per binding into `<data dir>/channel-tokens/<name>.token` (mode 0600) at startup and on reload. Delete the file to revoke the binding, and reload to rotate its token. An adapter starts with the new `channel.hello` socket method, or `flk adapter hello <binding>`. A wrong token or an unknown binding is refused with `channel_unauthorized`, a binding served by another node with `channel_not_owner`, and every hello is logged without the token. Protocol 29: against an older server the hello exits 78 (`server_version_gap`) before it is sent, so an adapter refuses to start. Inbound mail (#1153) and the coalesced outbound feed (#1154) follow.
- `agent.get`'s `state.attention` now carries the question when a Claude Code `AskUserQuestion` form or a Codex `request_user_input` form is on screen (ADR-0028 §8a): `needs_human { reason: question, question: { question_id, source, harness, state: open, header?, prompt, options: [{ id, label, description? }], multi_select, allow_other } }`. `question_id` is derived from the agent, the turn cursor and the event-log sequence at open, and a whitespace-folded fingerprint, so a redraw or a rewrap keeps it, no new open ever reuses an id, a torn frame does not close the question, and a restart or a live handoff keeps it for a dialog still on screen. New durable kinds `agent.question_opened { agent_id, pane, question_id, question }` and `agent.question_closed { agent_id, pane, question_id, reason: withdrawn, question }` (the question with `state: withdrawn`) are emitted at once, with no settle window. On screen, an answer typed at the pane cannot be told apart from a cancel, so it also closes as `withdrawn`. Older servers skip the new kinds in the log (#1038)
- `flk goal arm|status|pause|resume|stop` and the socket methods `goal.arm`, `goal.status`, `goal.pause`, `goal.resume` and `goal.stop` (#1155, ADR-0030 §1), the second slice of goal supervision. They change and read the per-agent goal record: arm a goal with its frozen checks, pause it for `--minutes` or until resumed (recorded as `goal_paused` and `goal_resumed`), and stop it. `--agent` defaults to `self`, the agent whose pane runs the command.

author: ael-dev3
body:
The bow/skinning overlay recreates saved joint transforms every frame even though it modifies the same joints. Reuse private weakly cached restoration records, copying the current animation pose on the first modification of each frame. Restoration still clears the active map; no pose mathematics, geometry, materials or lighting changes.

**Before/after repro:** `node tools/repro-hunting-pose-records.mjs --baseline 0b45a36 --out hunting-pose-proof` exercises the delivered hero across 121 aim/draw/skin/slung/unequipped steps. Vector/quaternion clone calls fall **6,216 → 4,236 (32%)**. Every local transform matches exactly, and four software-WebGL colour/directional-shadow captures have **zero changed RGB pixels**. [Receipt, source hash and screenshots](https://github.com/ael-dev3/Tervain/blob/1bf0a4ec2/docs/perf/HUNTING-POSE-RECORDS.md) are committed.

**Validation:** build/typecheck and 33 bow/hero tests pass. A new regression check alternates aim/skinning against changing walk poses on two independent rigs and asserts exact restoration of every bone.

This proves a bounded allocation cut; it does **not** identify GC as the cause of the tracked 32 ms bow frames or claim hardware frame-time improvement. The clone counter excludes one-time creation of cache records and is not a total heap-allocation counter. Full-world hardware play gate remains required.

author: abhineetjain13
body:
## Why

SPEC-05 §8, PR 6: the ownership and intent stages of resolution (SPEC-05 §4.6, ARCHITECTURE §8.2 rule 3, §10). They decide which entity a detail page is about, and which candidates belong to it.

## What changed

- `resolve/ownership.py`: `EntityGraph.of(entities, vocabulary)` merges every collector's entities into one tree (it adds the `page` entity if no collector did, and refuses duplicate ids, unknown parents and cycles). `owner_of(candidate)`, `ancestors(entity)`, `owned_by(candidate, target)`: a candidate belongs to the target when the target holds it, when the page holds it, or when an Offer whose parent is the target holds it.
- `resolve/intent.py`: `primary_types(schema, vocabulary)` and `select_target(request_url, final_url, canonical_url, graph, primary) -> Entity | AmbiguousTarget` (`reason="intent_ambiguous"`), following §4.6 steps 1–4.
- `collect/base.Entity` gets `via: str | None = None`, the schema.org property of the parent that holds the entity, and a `PAGE` constant (the OG collector now uses it). The JSON-LD collector sets `via` for nested nodes and for nodes referenced by `@id`; the microdata collector sets it from the holder's `itemprop`/`property` name. Intent needs it to exclude entities under `isRelatedTo`/`isSimilarTo`. `CollectResult` now also refuses parent cycles, and `EntityGraph.of` reuses that validator for the merged entities.

## Scope

Covers: ownership, intent, and the `via` link from JSON-LD and microdata.
Leaves out:
- turning `AmbiguousTarget` into per-field `conflict` outcomes and the record outcome (PR 8/9);
- preference and atomic offers (PR 7), which will call `owned_by`;
- listing rows (PR 12): `select_target` is for detail pages only.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ownership.py tests/unit/test_intent.py tests/unit/test_jsonld_collector.py tests/unit/test_microdata_collector.py tests/property/`: all pass.
- Full backend unit, property and contract suites: `uv run pytest tests/unit tests/property tests/contracts`: 1679 passed. DB tests run in CI.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src tests migrations`, `lint-imports` (5 kept), `complexipy --no-ignore`, `site_literal_scan.py --public`: all clean.

Row done-when, "Multi-entity cases" → `tests/unit/test_intent.py`:
- one primary entity is the target whatever its URLs; a subtype (`IndividualProduct`) counts as primary;
- related and similar products, and products in an `ItemList`/`ListItem`, are not candidates. Each test fails if its rule is removed, because the excluded entity has the matching URL;
- several candidates are settled by the request, final or canonical URL, compared after canonicalization;
- no URL match, or several matches, gives `AmbiguousTarget`;
- primary entities that are all excluded give `AmbiguousTarget`, not the page;
- a page with no primary entity targets `page`;
- end to end through the JSON-LD collector: a product page with related products, a product referenced by `@id` under `isSimilarTo` and an `ItemList`; two top-level products settled by the request URL, or ambiguous.

Ownership → `tests/unit/test_ownership.py`: the target's own candidates, the page's, an Offer's and an AggregateOffer's are owned; an Offer inside an AggregateOffer, a Brand, a related product and its Offer, and another top-level product are not.

## Evaluation report

This PR adds `resolve/` modules and changes `collect/jsonld.py` and `collect/microdata.py`, but nothing calls ownership or intent yet: `extract_page` arrives in PR 9. JSON-LD and microdata candidates are unchanged; the only change is the new `via` attribute on entities. The gate reports `no_baseline` until milestone M, so acceptance rests on tests and review.

## Decisions

- **Entity `via`** · `decided` · Decision: `Entity.via` is the schema.org property of the parent entity that holds the entity: a full schema.org IRI anywhere, or a bare term under a schema.org context. Through untyped objects it is the property on the entity, not on the object in between. A node referenced by `@id` takes the property of its one reference, and gets none if its one referrer references it under two properties. Microdata: the one name the holder's element gives the item (or the untyped item on the way); an element naming two properties names none. Alternatives: exclude every primary entity nested in another primary entity; parse the property out of the locator. Why: §4.6 names relation properties, and an `@id` reference or a microdata item doesn't show its property in its id. Reversible: yes.
- **Primary types** · `decided` · Decision: the root types of the required fields' `schema_org` paths, without Offer (and its subtypes) unless Offer is the only root. `required_groups` members don't count. Alternatives: include Offer, which would make every Offer of the product a competing candidate. Why: an Offer belongs to the item it offers (schema.org `offers`/`itemOffered`; §4.5, §4.7). Reversible: yes.
- **Exclusion** · `decided` · Decision: an entity is excluded when any ancestor is an `ItemList` or `ListItem` (or a subtype), or when somewhere up its chain it sits under `isRelatedTo`/`isSimilarTo` of a primary entity. A primary entity nested through another property stays a candidate, and the URL decides. Alternatives: exclude every nested primary entity. Why: the literal reading of §4.6 step 1. Reversible: yes.
- **All candidates excluded** · `decided` · Decision: when primary-type entities exist but all of them are excluded, the result is `AmbiguousTarget(candidates=())`, not the `page` entity. `page` is the target only when the page has no primary-type entity at all. Alternatives: fall back to `page`. Why: §4.6 step 4 says "primary type absent", and a list of products is not a page about one of them. This is the conservative reading. Reversible: yes.
- **Offer ownership** · `decided` · Decision: `owned_by` accepts an Offer (or subtype, so also AggregateOffer) whose parent is the target. An Offer nested inside an AggregateOffer is not owned. Alternatives: any Offer descendant. Why: §4.5 and §4.7 say "an Offer child of the target". Atomic offers and `lowPrice` belong to PR 7. Reversible: yes.
- **D-0383 review note** · `decided` · Decision: page-level candidates (OG, meta, text) belong to the target whatever the root type of the field's path, so an `Organization.name` field still gets `og:title`. Alternatives: own page-level candidates only for fields rooted at the target's type. Why: §4.6 step 4 attributes page values to the target without a type condition. Measure on dev before changing it. Reversible: yes.

## Checklist

- [x] I did not add a site literal: no hostname, site, brand or retailer name, or string copied from a page outside `backend/src/crawlerai/adapters/` (C3). Adding a commercial site, retailer or job board to `tools/site_literal_allowlist.txt` is a C3 violation.
- [x] I did not add a list entry, word, selector or regex for a single page (C4, C5).
- [x] No §22 candidate implemented (C13).
- [x] Aggregate report attached, if `collect/`, `normalize/`, `resolve/`, `llm/`, `config_ir/` or `acquire/` changed: dev delta shown, hidden gate passed, no improvement claimed from hidden (C10).
- [x] Property or replay tests added; no test is named after a site or asserts one site's output (C9).
- [x] Decisions recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, or listed above for the orchestrator to record.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"solver33"} -->
_Requested by **Fall3n** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_015D4a58ajkPc14EbmCGDm93?thread=cmsg_015D4a58ajkPc14EbmCGDm935JNMKYPe2M25H3F4fA4XxH)_

Before: in game, thick trees had roots that stood up as stakes beside the trunk. Thin stems such as birches sat in small pits in the grass. Pieces of branches hung in the air next to pine and oak trunks.

After: thick trunks flare into a few low, rounded buttress lobes made of stump pieces. Every trunk stands on the Conquest grass layer and reaches down into it, with no pit round it. All the wood of a tree holds together, and wood the ground cuts off from a tree is left out.

**How**
- **Roots.** The roots were branch posts. Thick trunks now draw their foot as one shape: the trunk circle plus a few lobes (`Plan::blob`). Slivers along its outline that meet nothing are pruned.
- **Pits.** A thin piece used to replace the layer block round it. Now only a full block replaces a layer. Anything thinner moves up onto the layer and reaches down into it: `down=true`, or `extension_toggle=true` on vertical slabs, which the kit now writes. A bare branch post becomes a pillar as wide. Foot pieces left standing apart where the ground swallowed what they leant on are pruned (`Plan::prune_apart`).
- **Loose branches.** There were several causes, each fixed:
  - Limbs now start in the wood they grow from. A trunk slab or quarter there swells into bark.
  - A branch running through a thin trunk slice takes the cell, and `jointed` keeps linked cells meeting by a face.
  - Trunks thinner than a pillar stay over the cell below, and step across with a joint.
  - Birch clump stems are joined at the foot.
  - A new `Trees::cut_off` pass drops wood the ground separates from the tree. It depends only on the ground, so map pieces still agree.
- **Test.** `trees::tests::wood_holds_together` builds every species at five sizes, on layered and on flat ground. Using the renderer's piece shapes, it checks that no wood comes apart and that no thin piece sits in a layer cell. It needs the CR catalog, so CI skips it like the other catalog tests. Locally it ran with 8 seeds, and with 400 seeds (14,000 trees), and found 0 problems.
- **tree-render.** `--feet` draws close-up renders of trunk feet. `render::gallery` gained a `feet` argument and `render::sheet` a `top` argument (both additive). The tool also compiles again against the per-cell-biome `chunk_tag` from #10.

Checked:
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (core and tools/tree-render), `cargo test -p vistaforge-core` with the catalog.
- Generated a 1024 `old_growth_forest` map (24,502 trees). `tools/check_world.py` reports no problems, and `vistaforge preview` runs.

body:
## What and why

The skill tables and the hook hints abbreviate commands as `ct.mjs …` / `symbols.mjs …`. When the agent copies one literally into PowerShell or cmd on Windows, the bare `.mjs` path is opened through its file association instead of being run, and Windows shows a "Select an app to open this .mjs file" dialog on the user's screen. It happens occasionally, not on every session.

The skill now carries an explicit rule right after the prefix paragraph: always run `node "<prefix>/ct.mjs" …`, never a `.mjs` file directly, and it explains what happens on Windows otherwise. Hook hint texts are unchanged for now; if the dialog still shows up, the next step is putting `node` in those texts too.

body: Stacked on the compressed order/PredOrder/meet chain (#123–#125). Prove immediate covers in the compressed ancestor order are precisely next-selected-source-level extensions, so each compressed node has finitely many actual next children and at least one; degrees may vary arbitrarily and need no global bound. Package the newly constructed PartialOrder/OrderBot/PredOrder/IsPredArchimedean/SemilatticeInf node type as a Mathlib RootedTree and a pruned locally finite AmbientTree. Unlike strong thinning, no old selected-source frontier nodes are discarded. This is the concrete new tree required for Todorčević Remark 3.8; embedding the original heterogeneous factors into a suitable common compressed ambient and transferring the reduced dichotomy remains next. Three axiom checks. Require CI.

author: pland10
body:
Adds photo deletion to the inspection screen, as a multiselect, restricted to the **owner or an admin**.

## Behavior
- A **"Select photos"** button (shown only to users who can delete) turns the grid into a multiselect — tap tiles to check them, then **Delete (N)** removes them in one request (with a confirm), and the page refreshes.
- Everyone else sees the plain grid (tap to open), unchanged.

## Who can delete
- An **admin** (role admin / canDelete / canEditAll), or
- The inspection's **owner** — the user who created it (`created_by_user_id`).

author: edcs
body: Adds the eight hooks of `@inkbar/svelte`: `useDocument`, `useAnnotations`, `useTool`, `useSelection`, `useZoom`, `usePage`, `useHistory` and `useEmbedded`. Each returns an object with the same members as its React counterpart. Reactive members are getters over the root's state, so `useZoom().zoom` in a template or effect tracks the value. Actions are plain functions created once per call. Called outside `InkRoot`, a hook throws `[inkbar] useZoom() must be called in a component inside .`, the message the Vue and React packages use. ## Testing - `pnpm --filter @inkbar/svelte test`: each hook throws the readable error outside a root. - The getter behaviour is covered with `InkRoot` in the next change, where a component context exists. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the eight `@inkbar/svelte` hooks — `useDocument`, `useAnnotations`, `useTool`, `useSelection`, `useZoom`, `usePage`, `useHistory`, and `useEmbedded` — with an API mirroring their React counterparts. Reactive members are getters over the `InkRoot` state, so reading `useZoom().zoom` in a template or effect tracks the value; actions are plain functions created once per call. Called outside a root, each hook throws `[inkbar] must be called in a component inside .` — the same message the Vue and React packages use. Tests verify that error for all eight hooks. Written for commit a0f4677707ffb4a4dea721263f1fca035a5882e4. Summary will update on new commits.

author: ralsina
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Cloudflare Tunnel** section to the Access panel: a second exposure path for routed app domains, next to the managed caddy + lego wildcard path. A managed `cloudflared` container dials **out** to Cloudflare's edge — nothing listens on the server, no public IP needed — and Cloudflare terminates TLS and forwards each hostname to the app's local port.

## Changes

- `src/tunnel_settings.cr` — settings store (`<data-dir>/tunnel-settings.json`, 0600, holds the pasted tunnel credentials), pure renderers for the cloudflared `config.yml` (one ingress rule per routed app — every routed domain, not just base-domain ones — plus the mandatory `http_status:404` catch-all) and the compose stack (project `grafito-tunnel`, host network so `localhost:<port>` upstreams work like caddy's), write-on-change `sync_tunnel_files`, and `refresh` which restarts the running connector when app-store changes rewrite the config.
- `src/tunnel_panel.cr` — `POST /tunnel/settings|start|stop` behind the same gate as the rest of the access panel (`--enable-actions` + auth + cross-site rejection), and the panel section: settings form (blank credentials field keeps the saved secret), running/stopped status, start/stop as streaming jobs, ingress table with "needs its own DNS record" annotations, the one-time `*.base_domain → <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com` CNAME hint, and a teach-the-commands explainer.
- `src/compose_appstore.cr` — `TunnelSettings.refresh` alongside `AccessPanel.refresh` after install/update/uninstall, so tunnel ingress stays in sync with routed apps.
- `src/access_panel.cr` / `src/grafito.cr` — route registration from `AccessPanel.register_routes` (tunnel is a sub-feature of `/access`, not a new view) and the section rendered in `panel_fragment`.
- Specs: settings round-trip + 0600 perms, config/compose rendering, write-on-change sync, credentials-kept-when-blank, gate 403s (normal builds; demo opens actions by design), 400 before configured, fragment contents.
- Docs: README section on the tunnel path; CLAUDE.md inventory now lists the access layer (previously missing) and the tunnel files.

## Out of scope (deliberately)

Quick tunnels (trycloudflare.com), multiple tunnels / tunnel CRUD via the Cloudflare API, custom ingress rules beyond routed apps, SIGHUP hot reload instead of container restart.

## Testing

- [x] `shards build`
- [x] `make test` — 579 examples, 0 failures
- [x] `make test-demo` — 558 examples, 0 failures
- [x] `make lint` — 44 files, 0 failures

body:
## O que muda
Leitor do plano, em TypeScript puro (sem Vue ainda). Roda no navegador: o plano colado nunca vai para o servidor.
- `lerTexto` / `lerPlano`: EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) → árvore normalizada (`src/plano/tipos.ts`)
- **Tempo total = média × execuções:** o `Actual Total Time` é por execução. No Nested Loop, o lado de dentro roda 1.204 vezes.
- **Tempo próprio** = total menos o dos filhos. Nunca fica negativo: com workers paralelos, os filhos somam mais que o pai.
- **% da consulta**, que é o que aponta o gargalo.
- **Entrada ruim vira mensagem do que fazer:**
  - plano em formato texto: "rode com FORMAT JSON";
  - JSON quebrado; JSON sem `"Plan"`;
  - nó sem `Node Type`.
- **Limites:** 2 MB, 5 mil nós e 200 níveis.

## Como testar
```bash
cd frontend && npm install && npm test
```
13 testes com **planos reais gravados** do banco de exemplo (`src/plano/exemplos/`, JSON minificado):
- **Seq Scan** de 1 nó;
- **Nested Loop** (o tempo do lado de dentro, multiplicado pelas execuções);
- **junção de 7 nós:** a soma dos tempos próprios fecha com o total;
- **plano sem ANALYZE.**

288 linhas, incluindo 4 linhas de fixtures minificadas. Base: PR do `banco-exemplo`, por causa do CI. Não depende dos PRs da loja.

author: gmh5225
body:
## Why

The workbench had no way to edit a function, as IDA's right-click **Edit function...** does. It builds on the engine half (#942). The dialog was reproduced from IDA 9.4 running on a private display: its layout, access keys and menu positions.

## What changes

- **Action.** **Edit → Functions → Edit function...** (Alt+P, IDA's `EditFunction`) sits between Create function and Delete function. The disassembly's context menu lists it after the cross references, where IDA's does.
- **Functions window.** Ctrl+E edits the function a row lists. That is IDA's `ChooserEdit` key, recorded as a new `NEVERD_IDA_CHOOSER_COMMAND` row of `IdaActions.def`, and it wins over the window-wide Ctrl+E (Jump to entry point) while the list has the focus, as in IDA. The window gets a context menu with Edit function and Delete function.
- **Dialog.** `FunctionEditDialog` lays out IDA's fields:
  - Name of function (a change is a rename);
  - Start and End address (read-only: analysis decodes the extent);
  - Color, with a Choose…/Default menu;
  - the "Enter size of (in bytes)" fields: Purged bytes shows x86's `ret imm` pops, the other sizes are disabled with a reason;
  - the flags: Does not return, Library func and Static func are editable; Far function, BP based frame, BP equals to SP, Fuzzy SP and Outlined code are disabled with a reason.

  The access keys are IDA's; Cancel has none, as in IDA, so Alt+C reaches Color. The dialog reads `function_attributes` before it opens and sends only the attributes the user changed.
- **Worker.**
  - `function_attributes` is a read; `function_edit` is a command with history kind `function`, so it undoes and redoes like create and delete.
  - Both are advertised as capabilities and whitelisted in QueryService.
  - The mock engine models the attributes for the GUI tests.
- **Translations.** All 11 locales are complete, including the 14 CodeView/CodeText keys #936 added without catalog entries. That is fix-forward: `check_gui_i18n.py --check-sources` failed on dev without them.

## Not in this PR

- The listing does not paint a function's color yet, and the Functions window has no flag columns; both are noted in docs/gui.md.
- A rename and a flag change made in one dialog are two history steps.

## Tests

- WorkbenchTests:
  - Alt+P opens the dialog with the function's name and start;
  - checking Does not return writes `noreturn: true` to the sidecar;
  - Ctrl+E on the Functions row opens the dialog with the statement shown and does not jump to the entry point;
  - undo takes the statement back.
- The worker's `function_edits_test.py` (real engine) covers:
  - `function_attributes` before and after `function_edit`;
  - refused keys, values and empty edits;
  - history kind, undo and redo.
- `check_gui_i18n.py --check-sources`: 11 locales, 732 keys.

author: purplecowonwheels
body:
## Summary

Implements the TECH-7014 merge gate for `master` in `redesignhealth/paperclip`: Argus + CI authority published as the **RH PR Approval Gate** GitHub App (id `5166579`), replacing the human-review requirement once activated. Linear: https://linear.app/redesign/issue/TECH-7014

Replaces the legacy, unsafe prototype PR #28 (which granted authority to generic GitHub Actions app 15368 check contexts forgeable by any branch workflow). Do not close PR #28 until this PR is merged.

Authority is exact: for the current PR head H, the latest **completed `APPROVE`** Argus round for H **and** the canonical CI workflows green at H, published as the App checks `argus-gate` and `ci-aggregate` (pinned to integration 5166579). No auto-merge, no bypass except emergency administrator role 5, no self-approval.

Companion IAM PR (role trust in rh-data-platform): https://github.com/redesignhealth/rh-data-platform/pull/10510
Companion rh-paperclip PR: https://github.com/redesignhealth/rh-paperclip/pull/113

## Architecture & Security Controls

- **Source-Only Phase**: This PR is completely inert on merge until repository variables (`AWS_ROLE_ARN_PR_APPROVAL_GATE` and `PR_APPROVAL_APP_ID=5166579`) are provisioned, IAM trust is deployed, and rulesets are cut over.
- **Workflow Isolation**:
  - `auto-approve.yml`: Wrapper triggered on `workflow_run` (workflows: `PR`, `Docker Runner check`, `Gate Tests`, `Storybook Visual`), 15-minute sweep schedule, and manual `workflow_dispatch`.
  - `auto-approve-job.yml`: Reusable workflow with unprivileged `classify` and privileged `gate` jobs. Both jobs enforce immutable owner ID (`216950685`), repo ID (`1326789272`), and branch `refs/heads/master` in job `if` guards and shell preflights.
  - Dedicated runner venv with pinned `pyyaml==6.0.2` provisioned in both `classify` and `gate` jobs before credential acquisition.
- **Public Fork PR Support**:
  - Fork PRs are supported using fresh metadata-only reads (never executing PR code).
  - Open master PR listing matches `head_sha` + `head_repo_id` (not `commits/{sha}/pulls`).
- **CI Provenance & Exact Workflow References**:
  - `.github/workflows/pr.yml` at HEAD must call `paperclipai/paperclip/.github/workflows/pr-trusted.yml` at ref `master` or `refs/heads/master`. Arbitrary commit SHAs and untrusted repos are rejected (`UNTRUSTED_CI_DEFINITION`).
  - GitHub Actions API `run.referenced_workflows` is validated on `pr.yml` runs to contain exactly the two upstream entries (`pr-trusted.yml` and `ci-routing.yml`) at `refs/heads/master` (or `master`), recording their commit SHAs for audit.
  - Required anchor jobs on `pr.yml`: `ci / gate / Select trusted runner`, `ci / policy`, `ci / verify`, `ci / e2e` with all jobs carrying prefix `ci / ` and zero allowed skips.
- **Label-Conditional Storybook Visual**:
  - `.github/workflows/storybook-visual.yml` canonical data contract is validated from HEAD.
  - Required only when PR carries the `storybook-visual` label (recomputed from live metadata).
  - When applicable, `Storybook visual regression` must succeed, and the dispatch-only preview job (`Deploy selected branch Storybook`) is legitimately allowed to be skipped on PR runs.
  - Dynamic revalidation in `gate_run.py`: if PR labels change between initial classify/read and final evaluation, check runs are cancelled as superseded (`LABELS_CHANGED`), preventing stale green publishing.
- **Ruleset Files**:
  - `master-bootstrap-human.json`: Temporary 1-approval requirement (Team 16403522), no CODEOWNERS, admin role 5 bypass (`bypass_mode: always`).
  - `master-argus-review.json`: Permanent machine policy: 0 approvals, required checks `argus-gate` and `ci-aggregate` (app 5166579), admin role 5 emergency bypass.
  - `scripts/review-policy-machine-cutover.jq`: Offline transformer preserving admin role 5 bypass across `add-checks`, `machine-review`, and `restore-human`.

## Known Activation Prerequisites (Owner Actions)

1. **App 5166579 Permissions**: Org owners must elevate **Checks** permission to **Write** on the "RH PR Approval Gate" GitHub App and accept the prompt.
2. **Installation Repositories**: Installation `167295675` must include both `redesignhealth/rh-paperclip` and `redesignhealth/paperclip`.
3. **IAM Deployment**: Merge and apply `rh-data-platform` PR #10510 (dev apply for `rh-pr-approval-gate`).
4. **Repository Variables**: Configure `AWS_ROLE_ARN_PR_APPROVAL_GATE` and `PR_APPROVAL_APP_ID=5166579`.
5. **Ruleset Activation**: Bootstrap `master-bootstrap-human.json`, verify gate checks, and cut over using `review-policy-machine-cutover.jq`.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts/tests -p "test_*.py"`: 182 unit tests passed locally.
- Tests cover all security boundaries:
  - Wrong base / repo ID / upstream ID rejection.
  - Deleted fork / head moved / labels changed revocation.
  - Untrusted `pr.yml` outer definitions and untrusted `referenced_workflows`.
  - Storybook label-conditional gating, visual regression failure, and scoped preview skip.
  - PyYAML dependency provisioning order before credentials.
  - Offline ruleset cutover and rollback preserving admin role 5 bypass.

_Requested by **Yuki** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DRDpn3pjoEwHcXK39nKkm1?thread=cmsg_01DRDpn3pjoEwHcXK39nKkm1CwNp6dKBwjzL1jcpGueZZV)_

Before: a disk held at most 8191 files and directories, the most that block 0 can name (508 directory blocks plus the 4 fixed ones).

After: it holds 32767. Directory blocks past the 512 the superblock names are named by up to four extension blocks.

## Format (backward compatible)

- Byte 8 of block 0 (unused until now) names the first extension block. Word 0 of an extension block names the next one; words 1 to 511 name directory blocks `512 + 511*e + w - 1`.
- The first time the directory outgrows 512 blocks, the magic changes from `BSTDISK3` to `BSTDISK4` in the same sector write that links the first extension block. `BSTDISK2` and `BSTDISK3` disks mount unchanged and stay in their format until then. An older kernel sees `BSTDISK4` as a disk it does not know and leaves it alone.
- Crash order: a new directory block is written and flushed, a new extension block is written whole while nothing links to it, then one sector write links it. A power cut leaves the old directory or the new one, and unlinked blocks are free at the next mount.
- Mount follows the chain with a bound of four blocks (a loop or a longer chain is cut) and marks the extension and directory blocks used.

## Other changes this needed

- `DSLOTS` 32768, directory memory up to 8 MiB (still allocated lazily by doubling).
- `/proc` inode numbers and directory numbers (`INO_PROC`, `DIR_PROC`) now start past the file handles, which the larger table had made overlap them (listing a loop mount showed `/proc` entries).
- `test/fsck.py` and `test/crashsim.py` read `BSTDISK4`; `test/fsck_test.py` has cases for a looping chain, an extension block off the disk, a gap, and one a file also uses.
- The 40 GiB disk boot in `test/shell_test.sh` now fills the directory (over 30000 entries), checks the image is `BSTDISK4`, reboots and lists it.

## What is proved and what is trusted

Proved: every extension index and pointer is bounded, so no access leaves its buffer. Trusted: the order of the writes (checked by `fsck.py` on cut images, not proved). Not done: `disk_find` is still a linear scan, so a name lookup in a full directory is slow (a hash index is the next step).

## Checked

`make build/bastios.elf` (all proofs discharged), `test/fsck_test.py`, `make test`: everything passes except the sound test, which counted 916 half periods under load (unrelated to this change; it does not touch the disk).

body:
## Description

Regroups the primary menu into discovery, My Library, acquisition tools, requests, and settings sections. User List is nested under Settings, and the library route is labeled My Media.

Adds Discover/Swipe tabs across Movies, Series, Books, and Audiobooks discovery routes, including nested genre, keyword, language, studio/network, and upcoming views. Swipe keeps a validated in-app return URL so switching back restores the same route and filters. Desktop and mobile navigation render from one shared route and permission model.

AI assistance was used to implement and verify this change.

## Forward integration

Manually integrated SeerrNG `main` at `868e156d7e40cd676a3c7ca908d0091fd94566e1` in merge commit `af5c75380b476fea876108980f7fd197ce770621`. The request/scanner recovery changes from PR #214 are preserved. The only shared-file overlap was `src/styles/globals.css` and `docs/maintainers/ui-style-standard.md`; both were reviewed after merge, and the style-standard list numbering was corrected.

## How Has This Been Tested?

The complete exact-head GitHub Mode 2 validation passed for PR head `ea91033ccf64d9032575a8baf380b34b37ec4737` against main `868e156d7e40cd676a3c7ca908d0091fd94566e1`. Run [38421517621](https://github.com/snapetech/seerrng/actions/runs/38421517621) attempt 2 reconciled 19/19 applicable receipts successfully. The planned Helm case was skipped by its existing main-branch/chart-path filter. The bound plan had 733 files in its inventory: 533 Vitest, 87 tooling, 58 native Node tests, 3 documentation-security files, 46 Cypress specs, and 6 Playwright specs.

Executed results from the receipts:

- Vitest: 3,762 active passed, 5 skipped, 0 failures across 533 files.
- Native Node tests: 482 passed across 58 files.
- Cypress: 165 active passed, 32 pending, 0 failures across 46 specs.
- Playwright: 8 passed across 6 specs.
- i18n, release-note contract, documentation security/build/link checks, CodeQL, Jellyfin plugin, and build/lint checks passed.
- Exact-head PR Validation run [38426735242](https://github.com/snapetech/seerrng/actions/runs/38426735242) also passed.

The source-only Mode 2 attempt had one Cypress failure before forward integration. The fully integrated candidate later passed all six Cypress shards, including that spec; no root cause was established for the earlier failure. Visual inspection was not performed, and no host screenshots were taken.

- [x] The fragment includes audience, area, action, and breaking-change status.

author: edmlovers
body:
Adds `cargo fuzz` targets for the two functions that read untrusted text:

- `parse_tags`: every query a client sends. Also asserts it never returns more than `MAX_TAGS` tags.
- `validate`: the `sluice.rules` JSON an admin types by hand.

The property for both is "never panics".

## Result

Ran both for 30 minutes, seeded with a tagged query and a full rule set:

| Target | Runs | Crashes |
|---|---|---|
| `parse_tags` | 103M | 0 |
| `validate` | 78M | 0 |

No crashing inputs, so no new regression tests.

## Notes

- `cargo fuzz` needs nightly. The fuzz crate has its own empty `[workspace]` so the stable CI never builds it. Listing it in the root `workspace.exclude` doesn't work, because it sits inside the `sluice-core` member.
- To run it:

  ```
  cd crates/sluice-core
  cargo +nightly fuzz run parse_tags -- -max_total_time=1800
  ```

Merges `Frontend/` and `backend/` into ONE Next.js 16 app at the repo root: the public site at `/`, the admin CMS at `/admin`. One build, one Vercel project, one domain.

## What changed
- Public site upgraded from Next 14 / React 18 / Tailwind 3 to Next 16 / React 19 / Tailwind 4 (same versions as the admin), using the official codemods.
- Public site is route group `(site)`; admin is route group `(admin)` (each keeps its own root layout, fonts and CSS). Site-only code lives in `src/site/`; admin code stays in `src/components|lib|types`.
- `supabase/` and `public/` moved to the repo root; one `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `next.config.ts`, `.env.example` (placeholders).
- Public site's Supabase client no longer persists a session (it now shares a domain with the admin).
- Includes: Ads Manager hardening, the property landing page redesign (`/<slug>/project`), four design options at `/ppc-preview` (development only), and the `ponytail` and `impeccable` skills in `.claude/skills/`.
- `brain/`, `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` updated (path map from old folders to new).

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `next build` builds every site and admin route.

- NOT tested: a signed-in admin session, saving a property, uploads, or a Vercel deployment. ESLint reports 42 errors (not enforced by the build; not triaged).

author: bee9827
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"bee9827"} -->
_Requested by **티온** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0197zjXiErXRd6aWvrPQJAGq?thread=cmsg_0197zjXiErXRd6aWvrPQJAGqQmUk6JLhGYXtP7dL4wUP8M)_

## 요약

`@LoginMember Member`를 주입할 때 회원을 DB에서 조회하지 않고, id만 가진 프록시(`EntityManager.getReference`)를 넣는다. 로그인한 요청 하나가 커넥션을 2번 빌리던 것을 1번으로 줄인다.

Closes #343

## 배경

dev 스트레스 테스트에서 약 390 req/s에서 Hikari 풀(10개)이 먼저 고갈됐다. 요청당 커넥션을 평균 2.2번 빌렸고, 그중 1번은 open-in-view가 꺼진 상태에서 resolver가 서비스 트랜잭션 밖에서 `findById`로 회원을 조회하며 빌린 것이었다.
리틀의 법칙으로 계산하면 390 × 2.2 × 0.0132s ≈ 11 > 10이다. 다만 13ms는 모든 대여의 평균이고 회원 조회는 이보다 짧을 가능성이 커서, 처리량 개선 폭은 2배보다 작을 것으로 본다(추정). dev에서 같은 조건으로 처리량과 대여 1회당 보유 시간(`hikaricp.connections.usage`)을 재서 확인한다.

## 주요 결정

- 서비스마다 회원 조회를 흩뿌리지 않고 resolver 한 파일만 바꿨다. `@LoginMember`로 받은 회원에서 쓰는 값은 `getId()`뿐이라 확인했다.
- `MemberRepository.getReferenceById`도 시도했지만, 리포지토리 기본 `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`가 트랜잭션을 열면서 커넥션을 빌려 여전히 2번이었다. 그래서 트랜잭션 없이 `EntityManager.getReference`를 쓴다.
- 테스트를 먼저 썼다. `LoginMemberConnectionUsageTest`가 `GET /api/v1/travel-records` 한 번에 `hikaricp.connections.acquire` 증가량이 1인지 확인한다. 수정 전 2(빨간불), 수정 후 1(초록불)을 확인했다.

## 한계

- 회원의 존재를 확인하지 않는다. 토큰은 유효한데 회원 행이 없으면 `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`(404) 대신 아래처럼 응답한다. 최신 `backend-develop`에 합친 상태에서 없는 회원 id로 발급한 토큰으로 확인했다.
  - 조회(`GET /travel-records`, `/tags`, `/travel-records/statistics`)는 `200`과 빈 결과를 낸다.
  - 저장(`POST /tags`)은 외래 키 위반으로 `500`이다. ERROR 로그와 운영 알람이 함께 울린다.
- 지금은 회원 삭제 기능이 없어 생기지 않는다. 회원 행을 지우려면 `refresh_token`부터 지워야 해서(외래 키) 새 access token을 받을 수 없으므로, 생겨도 남은 access token 유효 시간(30분) 동안뿐이다. 회원 삭제(탈퇴)를 만들 때 함께 다룬다. 관련 컨트롤러 테스트 1건을 제거했다.
- 이 내용을 ADR 0009에 "2026-10-14 구현 업데이트"로 남기고, `travel-record-storage-and-query.md`의 `404 MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` 행과 resolver Javadoc을 고쳤다(831c6b9a).
- 주입된 프록시에서 id 외 필드를 읽으면 `LazyInitializationException`이 난다. 회원 정보가 필요하면 서비스 트랜잭션 안에서 조회해야 한다(Javadoc에 적어 둠).
- 기록 생성 시 Google 호출을 트랜잭션 밖으로 빼는 일(#350, 머지됨), Bucket4j 속도 버킷을 메모리로 옮기는 일(#354)은 별도 PR이다.

## 확인

- [x] 로컬에서 실행 확인 (`./gradlew clean build`, 테스트 392개 통과. 최신 `backend-develop`(#350, #352, #356 포함)에 합친 상태로도 421개 통과)
- [x] 비밀 정보(비밀번호·키·토큰)를 커밋하지 않았음
- [ ] 새 환경변수를 추가했다면 `.env.example` 갱신 (해당 없음)
- [ ] DB 스키마를 변경했다면 **새 마이그레이션 파일**로 추가 (해당 없음)
- [x] 실행 방법이나 환경 설정이 바뀌었다면 README 갱신 (ADR 0009, `travel-record-storage-and-query.md`)

author: tomokiakiyama06
body:
Refs #208

## 概要

PR 4b の 3b です（1 = Secret Store #232、2 = `paw-egress` #233、3a = Toolkit と MCP の Bridge #234、**3b = この PR**、3c = 本番の起動の口: Container・systemd の Template Unit・polkit・Image。Podman の確認は Human、4 = Codex の ChatGPT の Login は Smoke の後）。

**#234 の上に積んでいます**（Base は `claude/runtime-pr4b-bridge`）。#234 が Merge されたら Base を `main` に変えます。

Human の選択（Subscription の Credential）のとおり、**Claude Code の Subscription の Token（`claude setup-token`）** の経路から作りました。**CLI の段は組み立てで無効のまま**（`CloudPolicy` の Decision と Provider の規約の確認まで）。本番の起動の口は 3c で、今あるのは子 Process として動かす `SubprocessLauncher`（開発と Test）だけです。

## 中身

- **`agents/claude_stream.py`**（`stream-json` の読み取り、Decision 0087 の 4）:
  - `system/init`: Tool が PAW の Tool（`mcp__paw__<name>`）と外せない `EndConversation` だけ、`paw` の Server が `connected` で 1 つだけ、`mcp_server_errors` なし。でなければ拒否。
  - Model の呼び出しごとに `message_start`（id と入力 = `input_tokens + cache_creation + cache_read`）… `message_delta`（`usage.output_tokens`。`assistant` の Message の出力は仮の値なので読まない）… `message_stop` で 1 つの Turn。id で 1 回だけ数える。**`message_delta` の出力のない版は拒否**。
  - `api_retry` の `error`（認証の失敗の分類は `expired`、`rate_limit`）。`result` の `modelUsage`（全 Model、Subagent も）の合計。無い・0 は不明。
- **`agents/cli_session.py`**: Session の Directory（0750。Token の File 0640・MCP の設定 = PAW の Relay だけ・CLI の設定・空の `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`）。起動の口の Protocol（`CliLaunch` は Credential を `Secret` と環境変数の名前で持ち、どう渡すかは起動の口が決める）と `SubprocessLauncher`（環境は `PATH`・指定の変数・Token だけ、stderr は読まない、止めるのは Process Group ごとに SIGTERM → 5 秒 → SIGKILL）。
- **`agents/claude_cli.py`**:
  - `ClaudeSessionAdapter`: Decision 0087 の 4 の Option（`-p`・`--output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages`・`--tools ""`・`--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config`・`--allowedTools "mcp__paw__*"`・`--permission-mode dontAsk`・`--no-session-persistence`・`--setting-sources user` + Session の `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`・`--settings`・`--restricted`）。Token は `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`（`--bare` は使わない: この Token を読まないため）、Task は stdin。`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`・`ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false` など。止める条件: `init` の不一致・Turn の出力なし（`invalid_response`）、`on_usage` が `False`、Bridge の終わり（`submit`・試行の失敗）、認証の失敗（`expired`）。
  - `ClaudeCliRuntime`: 試行ごとに `NodeToolkit` を `McpBridge` で出し、`CloudGate` で送る。結果は Bridge の `submit` の Outcome か試行を終えた失敗、どちらもなければ `no_submission`（`escalate`）。Planner には使わない。`run_as_fallback`。Session の Directory は必ず消す。
- **`SessionRequest` / `AgentSessionRequest` の `attachment`**: 呼び出し側から Adapter への Session ごとの材料（Directory・Bridge・Token の File）。Service は読まずにそのまま渡す（Test あり）。
- `local.py` の Prompt の選び方を `node_prompts` に取り出した（Local と CLI が同じ Prompt）。

## Test

author: expikapaka
body:
Third stage: the first widget redrawn to the design. Stacked on
[#1](https://github.com/ExPikaPaka/vlc-ui-redesign/pull/1) because it
uses the colour tokens that PR adds; GitHub will retarget this to
`master` once #1 goes in.

## What it does

`CheckButton` was a pill with a round handle sliding inside it. The
[design's Toggle component](https://www.figma.com/design/16dIiUNet0ARMv0Sm15lRv/VLC-Redesign--Community-?node-id=536-1014)
is a rounded box of 68 by 32, radius 6, holding two blocks of height 26
and radius 3 that swap sides:

- **on**: handle on the right in Accent/Dim, caption block on the left
  in BG/Accent Bright reading ON in Accent/Main
- **off**: handle on the left in FG/A4, caption block on the right in
  BG/A4 reading OFF in FG/A3

The box itself stays BG/B2 in both states, so the state reads from the
caption rather than from the box.

## Things worth a look in review

- **The handle's travel changed.** It now runs between the margins
  (3 to 39) rather than 0 to width, so `_applyX`, `onWidthChanged` and
  `_animate` use `drag.minimumX` where they used a literal zero.
- **The caption follows `checked`, not the drag.** During a drag the
  handle moves and the caption stays put until the state commits. The
  two can overlap by about 3 points mid-drag.
- **ON and OFF are translatable** (`qsTr`), so a longer pair of words in
  another language will be clipped by the 33-point caption block. The
  design has no provision for that either; worth deciding whether the
  block should grow or the caption should be dropped in that case.
- `colorBorder` is gone from the widget's API, the design draws no
  border. The only caller, `TeletextWidget`, does not set it.
- **Checked with `qmllint`** (clean apart from the VLC module imports it
  cannot resolve outside a build). Not compiled or run.

author: guillaumeoj
body:
## What and why

Every object's 128-bit GUID (`EntityId`) now converts losslessly to and from the 22-character IFC GlobalId, so models can round-trip through IFC with stable identities.

- `EntityId::to_global_id` / `EntityId::from_global_id`. Decoding works on bytes: a wrong length is rejected without reading the input. Bad input returns a typed `GlobalIdError` (`WrongLength`, `InvalidCharacter`, `OutOfRange`) that never echoes the input (SEC-03), and nothing panics.
- New IDs come from an `IdSource`. `EntityId::from_random_bits` sets the RFC 4122 version-4 and variant bits for any random source. `SeededIdSource` is a deterministic source for tests, gated behind a `test-support` feature so it never ships.
- Known vectors: the example in the IFC 4.3 `IfcGloballyUniqueId` documentation, the `IfcProject` GlobalId of buildingSMART's Sample-Test-Files `Building-Architecture.ifc` (CC BY 4.0), IfcOpenShell's sample UUID, and the extremes. Property tests (fixed seed) check the round trip both ways and that decoding any string never panics.

Closes #21
Requirements: CORE-01, ENG-02 (property-based tests)

Out of scope, possible follow-ups: a `cargo fuzz` target for GlobalId decoding (ENG-02), a host random `IdSource`, and an allocation-free `GlobalId` type when the IFC interop crate lands.

## User documentation

N/A: internal change with no user-facing behaviour yet. Labelled `no-user-docs`.

body:
Prevents two cooperating Crunch Cartel instances from opening independent SQLite writers. The database opener canonicalizes the path and acquires a Windows handle-owned lock before SQLite starts, retains it until database close, and returns a distinct contention error. Failed initialization releases ownership; retained marker files do not block reopening after normal or abrupt process exit.

This is chunk 03b1, stacked on #1. Schema v1 and the preview UI are unchanged. Durable command/audit tables remain pending after backup-gated migration support. The guard does not protect against unrelated programs, hard-link aliases or mapped network drives; provisioned application paths and ACLs remain required before UI integration.

[GitHub-hosted Windows database checks](https://github.com/AliAhmedoo5/ResturantSys2/actions/runs/38524882517) passed at implementation commit `2eefd39cb9fcbe8e0981b33ec67bde27503fbb6e`: analysis, source/lockfile reproducibility and all 18 tests, including both separate-process ownership and normal/abrupt exit cases. CI compiles an isolated helper before tests to avoid replacing the runner's loaded SQLite DLL. The next commit records evidence only. All project execution occurred on GitHub-hosted runners.

Final commit `35e2e88` also passed [database checks](https://github.com/AliAhmedoo5/ResturantSys2/actions/runs/38525282935), [domain checks](https://github.com/AliAhmedoo5/ResturantSys2/actions/runs/38525282937) and [Windows preview analysis, tests, release build and startup](https://github.com/AliAhmedoo5/ResturantSys2/actions/runs/38525282945). body:
## What and why

The interim whole-work review of phase 1 (PR #97) found two ways to defeat the `exactVersion` pin that `scripts/ci/check-shared-pins.py` was meant to guarantee, one gap in local routing, and some stale docs.

### Shared-pin check (`scripts/ci/check-shared-pins.py`)

1. **A second entry that reaches the library.** `Apps/macOS/project.yml` with `CCLocal: {path: ../../../calendar-connectors}` under `packages:` passed. XcodeGen then emitted a local package reference and SwiftPM resolved the checkout over `exactVersion`. Now every `packages:` entry other than the pinned `CalendarConnectors` key must be either an external dependency whose url, path, github shorthand or other value does not mention the library (Sparkle and KeyboardShortcuts still pass), or `path: ../../Packages/<Name>` for an existing sibling directory spelled exactly. Every `localPackages:` entry (string or `{path:}` form) must be `../../Packages/<Name>` likewise. An entry that names the library and is not the pinned key fails with a message naming that key.
2. **Versioned manifests.** SwiftPM prefers `Package@swift-X.Y.swift` over `Package.swift`, and only `Package.swift` was scanned. The check now scans every `Package*.swift` directly in `Packages/*/` with the same allow-list.

Probe results on a copy of the real tree: the pre-change script printed `PASS: shared pins` for both probes (`CCLocal` entry; `Packages/TimeTugCore/Package@swift-5.9.swift` with `.package(path: "../../../calendar-connectors")`); the new script fails both and still prints `PASS: shared pins` for the unmodified tree.

### Local routing (`scripts/dev/verify.sh affected`)

Edits to `Packages/*/Package.swift`, `Packages/*/Package@swift-*.swift` and `Apps/macOS/project.yml` now also set `WANT_CONTRACTS=1`, so `shared-pins` runs locally for the files that can change the pin. The rest of the mapping is unchanged.

### Docs and tracker

- The iCal subscription spec and the phase 2 spec pointed at a plan, an API document and a phase 1 design that live in the library repository now; they link to them at the `1.0.0` tag.
- `AGENTS.md`: raise `exactVersion` for every adoption, raise the `from:` floors only when the code needs the new version (and on a major bump).
- `docs/architecture.md`: the nested parenthetical is readable (same meaning).
- `running-live-calendar-tests` skill: the Phase 5 spec's "Live findings" is in the library repository.
- Windows program tracker: the two overlapping `timetug-bot` owner items are one (under phase 1), the flip item is ticked (merged), and a 2026-10-13 session log line records the state.

## Tests

Test first, each seen failing before the change:

- `scripts/ci/tests/test_check_shared_pins.py`: 29 existing plus 16 new (45); 12 failed before the fix, 45 pass after. New cases cover a second key with a path to the library, a second key with a `Calendar-Connectors.git` url, the `github:` shorthand, `localPackages` entries (string and mapping form) at the library and outside `Packages/`, legitimate sibling and Sparkle-style entries passing, missing and case-variant sibling paths, a non-mapping entry, and `Package@swift-5.9.swift` failing and passing.
- `scripts/dev/tests/test-verify.sh`: `Packages/TimeTugCore/Package.swift`, `Package@swift-5.9.swift` and `Apps/macOS/project.yml` changes must run `check-shared-pins.py` (failed before the change).
- Also green: `test-check-shared-pins.sh`, `test-use-local-connectors.sh`, `check-shared-pins.py` and `check-repository-contracts.py` on the real tree, `bash -n`, and `scripts/dev/verify.sh release-tools` (19 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped as not selected).

## Not here

Required-check settings are the owner's: add `release-tooling` and `core-linux` to Protect master. No settings were changed and nothing is merged or set to auto-merge.

author: drjamesarobertson-design
body:
## Summary
James's report: no way to close the "Resume Work in Progress" banner if it wasn't wanted, and it kept coming back even after being acted on.

Root cause: `clearAutosave()` (`storage.ts`) already existed, documented for exactly this, but nothing in the app ever actually called it — the banner's title was also read fresh via a direct `loadAutosave()` call inline in JSX on every render rather than tracked state, so there was no way to make it go away short of browser storage filling up or being cleared by hand.

- Converted to real state (`resumeAutosaveTitle`), refreshed each time the landing menu comes into view.
- Added an explicit ✕ next to the button that calls `clearAutosave()` and updates the state.

Deliberately left Save to File / Add to Library untouched — the autosave is documented as a separate, independent crash/reload recovery net from those explicit saves, so auto-clearing it there would undermine that safety net while you're still actively editing.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, help-text consistency check — all clean
- [x] Created a taxonomy, typed content, went Back to Menu — confirmed the resume banner appears
- [x] Clicked the new ✕ — confirmed the banner disappears immediately
- [x] Did a full page reload afterwards — confirmed the banner stays gone (proves the dismissal actually cleared `localStorage`, not just the current render)

## Fallback: trusted publishing first, token second
The auth step has `continue-on-error: true`, and the publish step reads `${{ steps.prm_auth.outputs.token || secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || secrets.CARGO_TOKEN }}`. 1. **Encrypted Archive Discovery (`CommonData/scripts.rpg`):**
   - The retail game executable (`Worms W.M.Dx64`) contains uncompressed files in `CommonData/Scripts/Equip/`, but they are completely ignored at runtime.
   - `GameApp::OpenScriptsZip()` (address `0xd0e0a0`) mounts an encrypted in-memory archive located at `CommonData/scripts.rpg` over `scripts:/` and `bootScripts:/`.
    - **Cipher & Key:** AES-256 in Counter (CTR) mode with key `b"WormsWMD40F22820D081C3747DFEA0B\x00"`. Counter block is 16 bytes with initial stream offset initialized to the total file size (`struct.pack("<QQ", file_size, 0)`). Decrypted payload is a standard ZIP archive containing all 436 script files.
   - Modifying weapon parameters requires unpacking, modifying, and re-encrypting `scripts.rpg`.

2. **Lockstep Multiplayer Synchronization & Desync Mechanics:**
   - Evaluated the game's peer-to-peer network model. Worms W.M.D uses deterministic lockstep simulation with continuous checksum verification (`WS_DestructionManager::GetCheckSum`, `WS_CollisionManager::__DebugColManCheckSum`, `NetGame::UpdateDesyncChecker`).
   - Mismatched weapon data between clients triggers `kResult_SocketDesync` as soon as the weapon detonates.
   - Documented two working multiplayer solutions:
     - **Steam Remote Play Together:** Host runs the mod, clients stream without installation (0% desync risk).
      - **Symmetric Installation:** Both players install the patched `scripts.rpg` in private lobbies, preserving deterministic simulation hashes.

body:
Fixes found by browser QA of the live site after #70 (`evidence/11-live-captures-after`, on branch `qa/live-captures-after`).

**1. A finished thread vanished from the sidebar after reloading (P0).** Root cause, reproduced with a real double reload: opening `/threads/<id>` ran `registerThread` in the `useChatRuntime` mount effect before `useDbHydration` had read PGlite, so the id looked unknown and got a fresh ephemeral row titled "New conversation". The SQL upsert then overwrote the stored persisted, titled row. After the second reload the list was empty (the live QA saw this; a single reload can still win the race). Fix: a `hydrated` flag in `thread-registry-store` set by `initFromDb`; `use-db-hydration` always calls it (also on an empty or failed read); the register-if-unknown effect waits for it. When the model title is unavailable the thread is named from the question (`titleFromQuestion`, whitespace collapsed, cut at a word boundary to 60 characters). The earlier unit test (`thread-registry-store.lifecycle.test.tsx`) never reloaded, so its "not a bug" conclusion was wrong. New e2e `thread-list-reload.spec.ts` was red on the double reload and green after the fix.

**2. A permanent 190 to 243 px blank band above the composer (P1).** The sticky footer is already in the flow after the last message; the end spacer added a second footer-height block. Removed. The footer-height var, scroll padding and the re-scroll to the end after history loads stay. Expected gap above the composer: about 36 px instead of 226 px (read from the library code, not measured).

**3. Smaller:** the scroll-to-bottom arrow is not shown in an empty thread; at 320 the tab bar returns after a reply finishes (hidden only while the composer is focused and a run is active or text is typed); "understands you." stays on one line in the empty-thread heading.

**Verified (Node 24.21, the pinned version):** `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint 0 errors (4 warnings), `npm test` 72 files passed, 1 skipped, 768 tests passed, 11 skipped. The e2e spec `thread-list-reload.spec.ts` passed 2 of 2 before the last edit to an unrelated unit test; I did not rerun it.

**Not verified:** every layout claim in 2 and 3 is browser-only (the blank band is gone, the remaining gap size, the 320 heading, the arrow, the tab bar). The sidebar fix is proven in the mocked-UAR e2e on the app build, not on the live site with real UAR timing. author: metaphorica
body:
## Finding
Codex Security Cloud `network.upnp-untrusted-endpoints` (CWE-918, CWE-346), observed at `d5274b4752bd5a37bb35e6bb47796916c21e514c`.

## Fix
- Require SSDP `LOCATION` to contain the numeric IPv4 address of the UDP response sender; reject unrelated discovery targets.
- Allow only on-link, non-loopback SSDP responders from active interface prefixes before fetching the description; reject returned gateways that change hosts.
- Require `URLBase`, `controlURL`, and SOAP requests to retain the description's literal IPv4 host; never follow gateway-directed HTTP redirects.
- Require the user-configured public IPv4 hint to agree with `GetExternalIPAddress` before installing a UPnP mapping and advertising that address. This intentionally disables UPnP publication without an independently configured public IPv4 hint; NAT-PMP remains available.

## Regression coverage
- Forged SSDP `LOCATION` vs sender.
- Off-host `URLBase`, `controlURL`, description redirects, and SOAP redirects.
- Off-link, self, link-adjacent/loopback, and mismatched discovered gateways.
- Missing, mismatched, private, and confirmed public address hints.

## Validation
CI (`go test -count=1 ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gojgp lint ./...`, cross-platform builds) runs on pull requests. The local environment has Go 1.23 but the repository requires Go 1.27, so CI is the authoritative validation environment.

author: zianncupcake
body:
## What it does

At 09:00 on the 1st of a month, by a user's own clock, the bot looks at what they spent in the two calendar months before and offers the spending that looks monthly as patterns to add. Each offer is the question that is asked before `/pattern` is run, with "Do it" and "Cancel". Nothing is saved without a press.

- A merchant with a purchase in both months is offered with what was spent there in the later one: one charge, or the total of many small ones, as fares.
- A merchant is known by the first word of its text, and by the second unless that has a digit in it. So a text that ends in a number that differs is one merchant, and the name is always held by the texts it came from.
- Left out: what one of the card's patterns counts already, what was offered for the card before, a group with no cap, and a merchant whose name or text the product's rules place in another group than its purchases are in. Five at the most, the largest first.
- One user in a run, after the reminder and before the mail; neither can keep the mail from being checked.

Migration `0012_review.sql` adds `users.review_at` with its index, and the table `pattern_offers`, whose rows go with their card.

## Known limits

- Two monthly merchants of which one's text holds the other's name: accepted both, one hold is not paid off.
- `/timezone` sent in the minute before a review is due, or to a zone where the 1st at 09:00 has passed, moves that review to the next month.
- An outlet whose text has a number goes by the chain's first word; other outlets go by their own two words.
- An offer whose command is too long for a button is sent as the line to copy.
- A merchant bought once at the end of a month and once at the start of the next is offered; its user presses "Cancel".

## Checked

- Typecheck, and the whole suite: 52 files, 1,793 tests.
- Two independent rounds, then a second pass: a year of three users' spending through the every-minute run (36 user-months, 2,565 purchases), pressing "Do it" on every offer. 32 offers, none against the wrong cap, and "To come" under the right group in 422 of 430 checks (the other 8 are the chain limit above).
- Each user offered only their own, in their own chat; two and three runs at once send one set of messages; a failed send offers the same a month later.
- A run with a reminder, a review of five and mail at its most: 41 queries and 30 requests, against 50 each.

author: haythemsellami
body:
## Why

Recovering history needed a manual `BACKFILL_RESET` in Render, and even then it lost part of a day. The replay only covers **closed** UTC days and the live tail only reads forward, so a reset applied mid-day recovered every day except the one it was deployed on. Metric v1 (deployed 2026-10-12) is the case in point: midnight → deploy stayed decoded without the v1 sources, and prod serves **$572k for Oct 12** against ~$3M on the days around it.

## What

**1. Re-read today on every reset.** After the closed-day replay, the core re-decodes today from midnight to the tail's cursor and **SETs** the venue's day bucket (`rereadToday` in `live.ts`).
- The bulk is read while the tail keeps running. The remainder and the apply happen between two tail cycles (`inTail`), so the SET is computed against exactly the cursor the tail counted to.
- Fills: an identically decoded fill is kept, with its live markouts and curve; a changed fill is replaced; one the decode no longer produces is deleted (`planReread` → `VolumeStore.reconcileFills`).
- The pending marker (`reread_day_<vid>`) is committed in the same snapshot as the bucket. A restart that carries it past midnight turns it into a closed-day replay of that day (`carriedRereadTarget`).
- A reset starting **today** is now valid (today only) instead of refused.
- Reads go through the HOT pool: the blocks are under a day old, and they are the blocks the tail itself reads.

**2. Resets declared in code.** `VenueAdapter.historyRevisions: [{ id, from? }]` feeds the same pipeline as `BACKFILL_RESET`. Each entry has its own marker (`history_revision_<vid>_<id>`) and is applied once per database, on the first boot of the build that declares it. The PR that changes a decode now also ships its history repair, and that repair gets reviewed. `BACKFILL_RESET` stays as the operator override.
- Revisions only run when both `BACKFILL` and `MARKOUT_BACKFILL` are on, so a partial run can't mark one as applied.
- A test fails on any invalid or duplicate entry in the registry.

**3. A reset never moves a scan cursor forward** (`rewindCursor` in `db.ts`). Previously, a targeted reset on a fresh DB, or on one whose lifetime scan was still crawling, jumped the cursor to the start block and silently skipped everything before it. Revisions run on every database, so this had to be fixed.

No adapter declares a revision yet. Metric's Oct 12 gap was already recovered on prod with `BACKFILL_RESET=metric:2026-10-12` (applied 2026-10-13 11:09 UTC; Oct 12 now shows 5,421 swaps / $2.40M). A Metric revision would replay those days a second time and throw away their live markout curves, so this PR does not add one. With this PR, the next decode change ships its own revision instead of needing that env step.

**Known cost of any revision:** the closed-day half deletes and re-inserts fills (unchanged from `BACKFILL_RESET`), so days it replays lose their live-captured markout curves and are re-marked from CEX archives. A follow-up can give the closed-day replay the same keep-unchanged-fills rule the today re-read uses.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm -w server run test` (749 passing, 26 new in `history-revisions.test.ts`), `npm run build`.
- **Live, Metric only, scratch DB, real RPC:**
  1. First boot (with a temporary Metric revision from 2026-10-12, since removed): the revision applied and the today re-read rebuilt 2026-10-13 from midnight → **2,686 swaps, $1,042,667.42**, identical to prod's `/api/volume`.
  2. I corrupted today (bucket set to $5, 3 fills deleted, 1 inflated, 1 phantom added) and re-armed the re-read. On restart it converged to the **exact prod total** (`fills +4 −2`).
  3. Re-armed again: `+0 −0`, totals unchanged, and the revision did not re-apply.
  4. On the fresh DB, the lifetime backfill cursor stayed unstarted instead of jumping to Oct 12.
- Not exercised live: keeping a fill's live markouts during the re-read. No Metric swap landed during the runs, so that path is covered by the unit test only.

author: baileyrd
body:
## Bug

Focused follow-up to merged #634, addressing all six findings in https://github.com/Rusty-Mill/rusty_mill/pull/634#issuecomment-6144679964 and the postmerge status https://github.com/Rusty-Mill/rusty_mill/pull/634#issuecomment-6147549988. Owner explicitly authorized these corrections and this draft PR. Do not merge yet.

Base: `main` at `4be0744fc609831c85763fa94aa09e26e9f0dcc1`. Original reviewed head `dd95401f28f36ba81b54303b47a605022a1a24f6`, merged as `28b4aa09cf6d919f02f227f1f9965eb412b7026a`. Working tree was clean before branching; no unrelated changes were discarded. No applicable `.agents/skills` files were present in this checkout.

## Root cause

The report regex stopped at escaped quotes and exempted prefixes. Counter analysis buffered all frames and silently kept identity state across failed decodes. Automation cleaned up by process name, flattened watcher arguments, discarded its handle, and ignored native exit codes. Ordinary Rust CI did not exercise these scripts.

## Fix / acceptance mapping

1. **Privacy:** `Scrub` consumes full Rust Debug string tokens; only exact configured bot names become bot labels. Tests cover escaped quotes/backslashes/Unicode escapes, both name forms, prefix and case collisions, and unterminated names.
2. **Lifecycle:** undecodable bundles now fail the complete analysis before report emission. Synthetic down → malformed frame → reused-ID return regression.
3. **Streaming:** one reusable u16-sized payload buffer, immediate folding, no whole-recording buffering or FrameDecoder suffix copies. A generated 100,000-frame short-reading reader checks bounded requests; valid streamed summaries retain prior behavior. Summary storage still grows with lifecycle transitions/maps.
4. **Ownership:** preflight refuses matching preexisting processes; cleanup uses only pinned handles, waits for exits, and never name/PID-based kills. Mock tests cover missing binaries with unrelated matching processes, cleanup, and ambiguous Epic ownership. An entry-point test substitutes a safe library and verifies failed-preflight report/exit without desktop calls.
5. **Watcher:** separate .NET argument entries, unique run/script paths, readiness handshake, retained handle and exit checks. Mock tests cover space-containing paths, startup exit, timeout and later death. No real watcher is launched in tests.
6. **Analyzer status:** explicit native exit checks and passed/failed/skipped status for each required stage; missing inputs or any non-passing stage produce a failed run. Tests include native pwsh exit stubs, missing analyzer, independent stage failures/skips, and a truncated-recording Rust CLI test returning nonzero with no report.

README/research note distinguish author-reported observations from unproven login/session explanations, and 117,869 framed bundles from 224,376 event wrappers. Document hardcoded paths. ADR-0084 records fail-closed decisions. Change fragment added. No roadmap/spec implementation status changed.

**Behavioral limitation:** Epic URL activation commonly delegates through an existing launcher. A newly appearing PID/name is not proof of ownership. Unless a direct child of the retained still-live launch process can be verified, startup aborts and leaves the game for manual operator cleanup. This may prevent automatic Epic startup; no live compatibility is claimed.

## Testing

Using the preinstalled pinned Rust 1.98.1 (`PATH=/workspace/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_HOME=/workspace/.cargo RUSTUP_HOME=/workspace/.rustup`):

Passed:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p rb_rl_game_bridge --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked -p rb_rl_game_bridge --all-features` — 92 tests, 0 failures; includes 8 counter unit tests and the new CLI regression.
- `cargo test --locked -p rb_rl_game_bridge --bin rb_rl_demo_count` — 8 passed.
- `cargo doc --locked -p rb_rl_game_bridge --no-deps` — succeeds with three preexisting private-intra-doc-link warnings in lib.rs.
- `cargo metadata --locked --format-version=1 --all-features > /tmp/rl-metadata.json`
- `python3 .github/scripts/check_workspace_deps.py /tmp/rl-metadata.json`
- `python3 .github/scripts/check_workspace_layers.py /tmp/rl-metadata.json`
- `python3 .github/scripts/generate_workspace_map.py /tmp/rl-metadata.json --verify docs/WORKSPACE-MAP.md`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_*.py'` — 192 passed after fixing the new job's required concurrency policy.
- `python3 .github/scripts/changes.py check`
- `git diff --check`

Affected-crate planner selects only `rb_rl_game_bridge`; scoped Rust checks follow root monorepo CI rather than building unrelated applications. Initial plain `cargo` failed because it was not on PATH; using the existing installation fixed that. Offline full metadata initially failed on uncached `ab_glyph`; locked online metadata then passed without manifest/lockfile changes. Existing manifest profile/unused-key warnings remain.

Unavailable locally / not claimed:
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File crates/apps/rocket_league/rusty_bullet/tools/rl_live_test/test-safe.ps1`: PowerShell is absent in this Linux environment. Added a Windows hosted CI job and included it in `required-gate`; that job must pass before approval.
- actionlint, cargo-deny and cargo-shear are not installed; their hosted checks remain required. No toolchains or tools were installed/changed.
- Windows desktop/game/Epic integration deliberately not run. No real game, bots, desktop automation, watcher, private recordings, screenshots, names or credentials were captured/uploaded. Synthetic recordings and mocked process operations only. Historical live evidence remains author-reported.

## Checklist
- [x] Regression tests added; Rust regressions validated locally
- [x] PowerShell safety suite validated on Windows CI
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed or logged
- [x] Focused diff, no dependency/toolchain/security/TLS changes
- [x] Non-obvious decisions documented
- [ ] Independent review and exact-head hosted CI (draft; not a merge request)

Source diff self-reviewed; no independent reviewer was available in this execution session. This is not independent review or Windows integration validation.

## Initial-head hosted validation

Head: `4a57fe85524fc28db66c6ccd13823c56cfc39739`.
[CI run](https://github.com/Rusty-Mill/rusty_mill/actions/runs/38417177172): the Windows **RL live tooling mocked safety tests** job passed, closing the local PowerShell availability gap. Workflow lint, fmt, planner unit tests and cargo-shear also passed. Remaining jobs were still running when this update was recorded; no claim of an all-green aggregate gate. No desktop/game integration was run.

## Summary
Removes localStorage persistence of the `threadId` variable across three locations in the messages script. The threadId is now managed only in memory during the current session.

Closes #357

## Changes
- Removed `localStorage.setItem('threadId', createdId)` when a thread is created via event listener
- Removed `localStorage.setItem('threadId', data.id)` when creating a new thread from the home page
- Removed `localStorage.setItem('threadId', threadId)` when retrieving threadId from URL on page load

## Details
The threadId variable continues to be assigned in memory at these three points, but is no longer persisted to localStorage. This simplifies thread state management by relying on in-memory state and URL parameters rather than browser storage, reducing potential state synchronization issues between sessions.
