author: davidalucas
body:
This PR implements F6/F7 in both targets. It follows the D2 defaults table (#318) and the maintainer's [2026-10-13 decision on its eight open questions](https://github.com/spatialanalyzer/briosa/issues/243#issuecomment-6147618560). Every change is a D7 major-3 change. The contract stays 2.0 on main, and the freeze PR bumps it. #243 stays open, because the fit seed still waits on #311. Commits: - `3a1f11c`: the decision's table rows and the guard. The guard fails against main. - `f77bdac`: the mapper changes in both targets, the rewritten tests, protocol comments, and the regenerated appendix. - `5991cd4` and `3171d1b`: the docs. ## The rules, by decision | Decision | What changes on the server (both targets) | |---|---| | D2 point 2 | `nominals_group`, `template_chart_name`, `profile_file_name`, `resulting_high_plane_name` and `resulting_low_plane_name` are added only when the field is set. An absent plane name lets SA use its default name (probes 5 and 6). | | D2 point 3, Q1 | An explicit empty value is rejected before dispatch with InvalidArgument, NotStarted and `request-validation-failed`. "Empty" means an empty or whitespace name in a set message, whatever its collection says. | | Q2 | An explicit empty USMN nominals group is sent blank, with empty collection and object names, as probe 1 sent it. | | Q3 | Rule 1 covers the arguments listed in the table. The 228 (2026) and 222 (2024) optional strings still sent blank when absent stay as they are and are listed in the appendix. | | Q4 | No server change. Clients may offer an explicit all-disabled tolerance value (see the client requirements below). | | Q5 | The guard: a transcribed test table per target, a per-target test, and a root agreement script. | | Q6, R1 to R7 | An absent field is rejected before dispatch. This covers:
- R1: the six robot joints;
- R3 and R4: the three scale factors;
- R5: the 22 robot model-link parameters and the robot parameter value;
- R6: the three destructive indexes;
- R7: the eight destructive names and patterns, where an empty or whitespace value is also rejected.
The new `RequiredValueMapper` does the check. | | Q6, R2 | `set_automatically` is required. Temperature, pressure and humidity are required when it is false. When it is true, SA ignores them, and an omitted value is still sent as 0. | | Q6, R10 exception | The manual-guide `measure_immediately` defaults to true, like the other measure operations (#297). | | Q7 | **Not in this PR.** The `device_config` reclassification is on branch `243-device-config-reclassification`. See open item 1. | | Q8 | CI runs `audit_scalar_presence.py --check`. | Rejection happens before dispatch, so none of these changes sends anything new to SA. The [argument defaults migration](https://github.com/spatialanalyzer/briosa/blob/243-f6-f7-argument-rules/docs/development/argument-defaults-migration.md) lists each changed argument for callers. ## The table `eng/classification/argument-defaults-.csv` grows from 24 to 72 rows per target: - 47 `required_risky_default` rows (R1 to R7); - 1 `default_flip` row; - the existing rows, with Q1 to Q4 recorded. The relationship rows name the explicit all-disabled value (Q4). Two new outcome values cover the new rows: `rejected_unless:` and `sends_default:`. `argument-defaults.md` records the eight decisions. ## The guard, failing first (Q5) The guard follows the `conditional-ui.json` pattern (#293): - **`ArgumentDefaultsTable.cs`** (each target's `tests/Briosa.Server.Tests/`) transcribes the CSV, one row per line. - **`ArgumentDefaultsTests`** checks every row. It builds the real MP command three ways: with the field absent, explicitly empty, and set. It then requires the row's `major3_*` outcome: - Explicit empty is tried both as an empty and as a whitespace value. - A `rejected_unless` row is tried with its guarding field both false and true. - A removed row must be unregistered. - A separate test follows a rejection through the public gRPC seam. It requires InvalidArgument, `request-validation-failed`, NotStarted, and that the worker never receives the command. - **`eng/Test-ArgumentDefaults.ps1`** requires the CSV and both transcriptions to agree in both directions, and checks the outcome vocabulary. It runs in CI, next to the conditional-option check. **Against the unchanged mappers (`3a1f11c`), 53 of 73 tests failed on each target:** - 5: a now-optional argument was still rejected when absent; - 44: an R1 to R7 field was not rejected when absent; - 3: a weather value was not rejected with `set_automatically` false; - 1: `measure_immediately` sent false. The 19 unchanged rows and the vocabulary test passed. After `f77bdac`, all 74 pass on both targets. **Mutation proofs** (2026). I reverted one mapping at a time; each made the guard fail: | Mutation | Tests failed | |---|---:| | USMN explicit empty rejected instead of sent blank | 1 | | Chart template always mapped (absent rejected) | 1 | | Joint 3 sent as 0 when absent | 1 | | Weather values sent as 0 with `set_automatically` false | 3 | | Whitespace-only names accepted | 8 | | Manual-guide `measure_immediately` default false | 1 | | High plane name always mapped | 1 | **Agreement script mutations:** - a changed outcome in the C# table: 2 findings; - a CSV row dropped: 1 finding; - an unknown outcome value: 3 findings. `Verify-CiWorkflow.ps1` now requires the four reviewed table gates in `ci.yml`, and it rejects a copy of the workflow without the appendix gate. ## Other changes - **Tests.** Thirteen existing tests in eight files per target pinned the contract 2.0 defaults. Each is rewritten with a `#243` comment, and now asserts the rejection, the omitted setter, or the explicit value. - **Protocol.** Comments on the changed fields state the major-3 behavior. No field, number, type or presence changes. - **Appendix.** It is regenerated: - 476 (2026) and 474 (2024) presence-ignored scalars remain, down from 524 and 522. - Optional-input coverage shows 7 (2026) and 4 (2024) inputs still rejected when absent, each with a table row. - The resolved R1 to R7 and manual-guide review flags are dropped. - **Docs:** - `argument-defaults.md` and a new `docs/development/argument-defaults-migration.md`; - the changed-defaults table in `admission-profile-migration.md`; - the classification README; - the ScaleObjects and bounding-plane operation pages in both targets. ## Verification (both targets) The full locked run (`Invoke-WithVerificationLock`, owner `f6f7`, against `origin/main` `0601e60`) passed every step on both targets. - **Build:** locked restore; Release build with 0 warnings and 0 errors on both targets. - **Release suites:** | Suite | 2026 | 2024 | |---|---:|---:| | Server | 1207 | 1178 | | Worker | 359 | 376 | | LicensedProbes | 205 | 205 | | Protocol | 32 | 32 | The full Debug server suites also pass: 1217 on 2026 and 1188 on 2024. - **Debug:** reflection and manual-startup tests pass. - **Protocol and interop:** `Verify-Protocol` against `0601e60`, the MP naming policy, and the interop artifacts all pass. Only comments changed in the protos. - **Package smoke:** passes, with conformance 12/12 and client scenarios 10/10 on each target. - **Performance:** both CI performance steps (`Test-RuntimePerformance -NoBuild -IncludeGrpc`, `Test-ObservabilityPerformance -NoBuild`) pass on both targets. - **Root scripts:** all pass. - **Table checks:** - strict propagation: 40 changed twins, 0 findings; - `Test-OperationClassificationTwins -Strict`: 0 findings; - `Test-OperationConditionalOptions`: 0 findings; - the new `Test-ArgumentDefaults`: 72 rows per target, 0 findings; - `audit_scalar_presence.py --check`: all four generated CSVs current. - **CI on `5991cd4`:** all checks green, including the retained-client conformance for all six client products. The last commit, `3171d1b`, is a one-paragraph docs addition to the protocol model. ##

author: toddwbucy
body:
The second full run of `deploy/verify-lifecycle.sh` on 2026-10-13 passed steps 0 to 6 and every check of 6b up to its last one. In 6b, the unload on the drifted territory refused `boundary_unverified`, the force-unload answered unloaded, the marker read forced and nothing was published. Then the run failed on "no admin.log line was written: expected 10530, found 10712".

Admin wrote nothing; its own stderr said so. The 182 bytes are the trace relay's line: `{"actor":"relay",...,"detail":"the worker exited","event":"ended",...}`. The relay writes it through the descriptor admin handed it at the earlier load, which was judged, when the force ends the worker.

Implements: weaver-admin-Spec 3.0 outcome row 2 (K5) and section 8 (the operations log). The code under test conforms to both, and the verifier drifted:
- **3.0 outcome row 2 (K5):** admin publishes nothing and writes nothing into the territory that did not judge. It speaks of admin's writes, not of the file's growth.
- **Section 8:** the relay's lines carry a schema of their own (`actor` naming the relay, `event` one of `connect`, `replaced`, `refused`, `disconnect`, `truncated`, `ended`) and go to `admin.log`.

**The fix.** A new helper, `not_relay_lines_since FILE OFFSET`, reads the lines appended after the size recorded before the force. It names each one that is not the relay's, meaning a JSON object with `"actor":"relay"`, an `event` and no `verb`. Admin's own lines carry `verb` and `command`, and an unreadable line is named too. The check is now "admin wrote no admin.log line" and expects `none`; a comment says why the relay's `ended` line is let through. The `want` text is updated to match.

**Severity.** Every full run stopped in 6b, so this bites in normal use; fixed.

**Test** (`deploy/test_plans.py`, `LifecycleForcedLogTests`): the check and its helper are lifted from the script as it ships and run against a log fixture through a stand-in sudo.
- (a) The relay's `ended` line alone appended: passes.
- (b) An admin `force-unload` verb line appended: fails, naming the line.
- Perturbation: with the file-size comparison put back, (a) fails. Watched.

**Pre-screen of steps 7, 8 and 8b against the code**, so the next run does not stop on a verifier assumption:

| Step | Verifier assumption | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | after the kill, `show` answers `in_transition` naming `constituents`, or the unloaded `state` with none | `LifecycleAnswer::InTransition { constituents }`, snake_case tag; `AdminView::WorkerGone` / `Down` (verb_table.rs) | holds |
| 7 | with a constituent holding the lock, `load` refuses `agent_running` and `unload` answers unloaded with the marker left `open` | Spec 3.0 row S8b; main.rs `EndByEscalation`: `escalate_within`, then `conclude_ended`, the marker as it stands | holds |
| 7 | the load's `payload.reset.prior_run` is the crashed run, and `payload.reset.reason` is `no-clean-unload` | save_points.rs `reset_from`: `Open` gives `NoCleanUnload`; wire.rs `ResetReason` kebab-case; lifecycle.rs `reset_reason` writes the serde spelling; event.rs `Reset { prior_run, reason }` | holds |
| 7 | `payload.lineage.save_point` is manifest field 4 (the digest) of the last line | the same field is read in steps 4 to 6, which passed live | holds |
| 7 | every new manifest line arrived `recovered` | save_points.rs `Arrival::Recovered` is written `"recovered"`; the manifest reader prints `arrived` as field 2 | holds |
| 8 | `validate` refuses `config_invalid` with `field` `declaration-directory` | `refuse_retired_keys` runs before `judge_entries` and names the key; `FieldName` is a newtype, serialized as a string | holds |
| 8 | the plan exits 1 with `REFUSED: <agent>: its root <root> names a declaration-directory`, before any `== test` or `== build` | update-stack.sh's root loop `die`s with that exact text; `die` exits 1, no `say` runs before the loop, and `trap on_exit EXIT` is set after it; the root is `$ADMIN_BASE/<agent>`, the same string as the verifier's `R`, through `script_env` | holds, on one condition about the box (below) |
| 8b | measured only; the closing checks are `expect_no_acl`, the trace's lay and `expect_unloaded_alone` after a force-unload | no new assumption | holds |

The box condition at step 8: update-stack's loop walks every agent root under the base in glob order, so another agent's root that `die`s first (closed, a retired key, no territory) would name that agent instead. That is a fact about the box, not a defect in the verifier.

**Gates:**
- `bash -n` on every deploy script: ok
- `python3 deploy/test_plans.py`: 147 OK

No Rust touched. Answers no issue or epic item.

body:
Superseded at the contributor's request by https://github.com/aspectron/rusty-kaspa/pull/185, targeting Aspectron's sigma SDK branch already used by Kaspa NG. This closes the official-upstream proposal; no maintainer acceptance is implied.

Kaspa NG currently uses workflow-rs 0.19 and wasm-bindgen 0.2.126, while Rusty Kaspa v2.1.0 uses workflow-rs 0.18 and pins wasm-bindgen 0.2.100. Directly switching NG to the official v2.1.0 tag fails dependency resolution. This ports the existing Aspectron sigma SDK compatibility changes onto v2.1.0 so NG can embed the new node.

## Changes

- Update workflow-rs to 0.19 and align wasm-bindgen/js-sys/web-sys versions and ABI adapters.
- Forward wRPC TLS backend features, initialize the default ring provider for native client/resolver construction, and adapt HTTP/TLS configuration to workflow-rs 0.19.
- Carry over WASM build configuration and additional compile checks for WASM test modules.
- Refresh the release lockfile. Preserve v2.1.0's existing Windows-specific risc0 export-syscalls dependency instead of adding the redundant global dependency from sigma.

These changes are adapted from aspectron/rusty-kaspa sigma at `35616f7bfa10be97ad94891c328ca5b569a6adcb`; credit belongs to the original contributors. Base: official v2.1.0 (`01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16`). The upstream master checked during preparation (12db0f35d4bba48cf9962f59cc27d5adb5ae6324) merged cleanly with this branch. No new consensus rules are proposed.

## Integration and review scope

The companion Kaspa NG upgrade currently pins this SDK commit: `6aa2c21ae8f2d4b7752e070213394c0ec90f7a20`.
This is a dependency and SDK migration requiring review of TLS feature behavior, browser compatibility and downstream consumers, not just a node version bump. Maintainers may prefer to split or adapt the port before merging.

## Validation

Windows x86_64, Rust 1.95.0:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --tests --benches`: passed.
- `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --lib --test-threads 4`: **1022 passed, 14 skipped**. This run used the development profile, not the release profile recommended by CONTRIBUTING.md.
- All 13 WASM compile/clippy checks corresponding to the feature and test-module coverage in `check`: passed for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (including wasm32-sdk/rpc/core and the consensus/address/PSKT/txscript/client test modules).
- Downstream NG workspace checks, three existing NG unit tests, Windows development build and embedded node version query passed.
- Manual Windows retest (contributor-reported, 2026-10-13): full synchronization and a subsequent application restart both succeeded using the published optimized test build rk-2.1.0-multiplatform-test.2. Network selection and diagnostic logs were not independently verified. The earlier development-build observation (approximately 16%, then returning to pruning proof) remains unexplained; it is not treated as a confirmed regression.

All four native downstream release builds and executable smoke checks passed in https://github.com/Shantee-Chris/kaspa-ng/actions/runs/38412809242. Refs #1928

## Summary
Issue #1928 quarantined 30 nightly ids as "passes alone, fails in the Linux full suite". In fact **all 30 fail in isolation at main** (macOS, Python 3.12, same as CI). None of them is order pollution. Each is a stale contract or an environment dependency. This PR fixes 22 and un-quarantines them. The other 8 stay quarantined, with corrected causes.

## Root causes and fixes (22 ids)
| ids | cause | fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| audit_cli_contracts x2, render_brain_hub_coverage x2, p30 x1, pre_flash `quick_payload_includes_brain_hub_coverage_gate` | `brain_hub_audit` literal-evaluated `CANONICAL_STAGE_FLOW`; since 6a4c3a9a0 it is `[p.value for p in RUNTIME_PHASE_FLOW]`, so the audit always failed | `scripts/ops/brain_hub_audit.py` resolves the derived flow from `runtime_phase_contract.py` and requires the exact order S,P,D,X,R,A,C for both the RuntimePhase contract and the pipeline flow (the same order tests/engine/test_pipeline_phase_contract.py pins), so a reorder fails. Trees without the contract keep the legacy literal. New tests cover the derived-flow pass and the reordered-contract fail |
| pre_flash `quick_payload_skips_flash_style_repair_subset` | the payload includes a gate that reads gitignored `.nexus/reports/autodata` manifests | the test stubs only that gate (it has its own tests) |
| ab_runner `test_python_syntax_warning_detects_return_in_finally` | PEP 765 SyntaxWarning exists only on Python 3.14+ | `_python_syntax_warning` falls back to an AST check for return/break/continue leaving `finally` |
| ab_runner `test_h6_{0..6}_audit_report_lock` x7 | `h6_13` report quoted the forbidden needles literally (as false-positive notes) | reworded the report line; the lock itself is unchanged |
| ab_runner `test_run_with_nexus_codex_provider_delivers_nexus_context` | since #453 generic adapter gates fail closed | asserts evidence plus `gate_passed is False` plus a failure reason |
| ab_runner `test_nexus_with_local_model_adapter_alone_no_call` | since d9a3bb0e3 the adapter fails closed without a planner `signal_snapshot` | expects `local_only_blocked` |
| cueline_worker subprocess, workflow_repair salvage x3 | self-hosted contracts now require `verifier_commands` | the test requests supply them |
| openwiki_source_contract | the page listed 13 of 22 workflows | added 9 rows; the count is derived from the inventory |

## Still quarantined (8)
- workflow_repair `integrate_approved` x3 and engine `test_self_hosted_approve_exact_binding_and_mismatch`: they need persisted acceptance, authorization, a consumed one-shot grant and contract-kind fixtures; that code area is in flight in #1884.
- `test_stage_f`: a live-checkout end-to-end delivery gate. It needs a local `main` branch, runs the functional suite, and writes seals and `.nexus` state without restoring them.
- `test_benchmark_autodata_manifest_gate_accepts_real_flash_and_pro_manifests`: needs real gitignored manifests.
- clean_wheel_entrypoints: the `nexus-cueline-worker` console script was dropped in #770. Restoring it changes pyproject.toml, which needs a trusted dependency snapshot transition, so it goes in a separate PR. This PR leaves pyproject.toml and uv.lock unchanged.
- concurrency_red `test_target3_deadlock_happens`: **delete-candidate**. The target was fixed in ac87243dc, so the deadlock can no longer be reproduced; test_deadlock.py pins the fixed behaviour. The test file is unchanged from main.

- Touched test files plus tests/unit/verifiers/concurrency in one process (`-p no:randomly`) at base cc0db956e: base 47 failed, head 24 failed, 0 new.

body:
## What

Brings the shared Supabase project back in line with `supabase/migrations/` and closes a storage security hole. **Nothing has been applied yet** — see "How to apply" below. One person applies it, after review.

Closes #172
Closes #175

### `0005_add_landlord_profile_fields.sql` (renamed from the skipped `0002_…`)
- Same file, new number. It shared version `0002` with the grants migration, so Supabase treated it as applied and skipped it. Renaming is safe — the DB never recorded it.
- Adds `profile_completed boolean not null default false` (written by the profile forms but missing from every migration).
- **Backfill:** copies `contact_number`, `email`, social links and `profile_completed` from Supabase Auth user metadata into `profiles` for the 3 accounts that saved a profile while the columns were missing. Only fills empty columns; only for users who actually submitted a profile form (every user has an `email` key in metadata, and `profiles` is readable by all signed-in users, so we don't copy renters' emails).

### `0006_fix_listing_photos_storage_policies.sql`
The live storage policies (made by hand, not from 0004) let the `public` role — including logged-out visitors — **upload and delete** in `listing-photos`. This replaces them with:
- read: anyone
- upload / replace / delete: signed-in users, only in their own `<user id>/` folder (`ImageUploader.tsx` already uses that path; all 30 existing objects follow it)

Side effect: the `"public"` folder fallback in `ImageUploader.tsx` (used if no one is logged in) will now be rejected — which is correct; uploads only happen from the landlord dashboard.

## Checked (read-only)
- `npx supabase migration list --linked`: only `0001` and `0002_grant_table_privileges` recorded.
- 0003's columns and 0004's columns + bucket exist in the DB; 0004's storage policies do **not** (the three hand-made ones do).
- `db push --dry-run` currently wants to push 0003, 0004, 0005 → the repair step below is required first.

## How to apply (after merge, one person, tell the team first)

```bash
npx supabase migration repair --status applied 0003 0004
npx supabase db push --dry-run     # should list only 0005 and 0006
npx supabase db push
npm run db:types                    # once #171 is merged
```

Then: check landlord profile save + photo upload still work in the app.

## Follow-ups
- Type the Supabase clients with the generated `Database` type and fix the resulting errors (needs #171 merged + this applied).
- #173, #174 — RLS role gaps, need a team decision.

body:
Findings + workflow docs from the targeted-edit investigation, plus the `--draft` pipeline flag. Builds on #104/#105/#111.

## Key finding — HF moderation tightened
HF full-quality Seedance now false-positives `nsfw` ~14/15 on the **standard speech-ref + image recipe** — replaying the *exact* inputs that produced finished ArtAI shots (ai-4-v013, monster-1-v006) failed **0/6**. Not a reference-count ceiling; it's the full/final path. Two working paths:
- **HF `draft` mode bypasses it** — ai-4-v013 3/3, monster-1-v006 2/2, text-pose 16/16; full 560×752 output, comparable to finals.
- **MuAPI** (`--runner muapi`) — no moderation issue at all.

## Changes
- **`--draft` flag** on `shot generate` / `generate-batch` (`src/cli.js` SCALAR_PARAMS → `--draft`, threaded through `generate.js`, recorded in `output.json`). Higgsfield-only; ignored by `--runner muapi`. Unit test added; full suite green (457/457).
- **Skill `targeted-edit-author`** — new "Runner choice & the HF moderation situation" section, and the **text-pose variant** (describe the pose in prose, no pose keyframe — looser but needs no asset prep; verified rendering head-scratch/fist/finger-up/shock from text alone).
- **`docs/recipes/targeted-edit-backend.md`** — maps UI inputs → concrete pipeline calls (trim → pose prep → prompt → generate [MuAPI | HF `--draft`] → splice) to wire the **video-editing UI** to the backend. Variant cheat-sheet + caps/gotchas.
- **Diagnostic scripts** — `hf-baseline.js`, `hf-replay.js` (exact-input replay, `--draft-on`), `hf-textpose.js` (text-pose, start/end + speech, draft + rolls).

## For the UI session
`docs/recipes/targeted-edit-backend.md` + the skill are the integration contract. Preferred backend: **MuAPI** (reliable, full multi-keyframe + speech) or **HF `--draft`** (cheaper/native, clears moderation for the tested recipes). body:
## Plan package
M1 / P1, "Platform references and data files for Instagram and TikTok" (`docs/architecture/short-video-posts-2026-10-12.md`, section 6), with the round 3 corrections. Design rule 3: a platform adds files, not steps.

## What it changes
- New `shared/references/platforms/instagram.md`, `instagram.json`, `tiktok.md`, `tiktok.json`, written from the official pages re-opened on 2026-10-13. Every fact has a source tag, and each `.md` ends with a `## Sources` list of addresses and read dates. A value a page does not state is `not checked` or `not stated`, and is null in the data file.
- `README.md` of the folder: the video-post keys (`post.shape`, `post.formats`, caption keys reusing `post.max_characters` and `post.scheduling`, `max_hashtags`, `max_mentions`, `unit`, `media.types[].magic_offset`, the `video` block, `post.options` with closed values and `default: null`, `limits`); a "Keys by post shape" table; a "Post shape and formats" section that fixes the headings a skill reads (`## Post shape`, `## Format: <name>`) and the closed format names (`reel`, `video`, `carousel`, `static`).
- `linkedin.json` and `linkedin.md` are unchanged: the new keys are optional or null by `post.shape`, and a file with no shape is a text post.
- `scripts/tests/test_platform_references.py`: keys required or optional/null by `post.shape`; README coverage of every new key; tests for both new files (stable headings and format names, prose numbers equal the data file, sources listed, exact values, MP4/MOV/WebM signatures).
- `limits.approximate` (true for TikTok's "typically around 15", false for Instagram) keeps a figure from being read as a hard cap. A flag the API requires and the person never chooses (TikTok's `brand_content_toggle`) is the provider's, not an option of the file; the README says so.
- `skills/mkt-engage/scripts/tests/test_parse_notification.py`: `--platform instagram|tiktok` exits 2 with "no parser for the links", nothing on stdout, no traceback.

## Tests
- Offline only. `test_platform_references.py` and `test_parse_notification.py`: pass. `skills/mkt-publish` tests: pass. The earlier wide run (scripts/tests, runtime social and contained-run tests, mkt-publish, mkt-engage, mkt-vote-round) passed: 1371 passed, 7 skipped.
- `scripts/validate.py`: 0 errors (142 warnings, all existing `guard-cannot-fail`). `scripts/security_scan.py`: 0 findings.
- No lab test and no model call.

## Evidence
Adding these files ages no evidence. `case_context` (`evals/eval_status.py`) hashes only the references a skill cites and the references of the platforms a case names. I computed it for all 324 case/with-skill combinations before and after: identical. The README edit is outside every skill hash.

## Notes for later packages
- P9 and P10: an option's `when_unset` is `default`, `omit` or `refuse`, and `default` is null exactly when it is `omit` or `refuse`. `thumb_offset` is `omit` (absent means not sent). TikTok `privacy_level` is `refuse` (the person must choose, no default). P10's rule "refuse when an option with `default: null` is missing" must therefore read `when_unset: "refuse"`, or `thumb_offset` would be refused.
- P3: the shape and formats are in each `.md` under `## Post shape` and `## Format: <name>`; Instagram accepts `reel`, `carousel`, `static`, TikTok accepts `video`. `post.formats` in the data file lists the same names.
- `limits.posts_per_24h` is a list (Instagram `[100, 50]`, neither chosen; TikTok `[15]`); a reader that needs the real figure reads it from the platform.
- `post.url` is null for both platforms (no address template); the `.md` states the address shapes. Tokens, scopes, container states and chunk rules are left to the providers (P9, P9b) and plan section 3.

## Decision recorded
Instagram `share_to_feed`: the platform states no default. The maintainer decided `true` on 2026-10-13. The data file records it (`decided_by: "maintainer"`, `decided_on: "2026-10-13"`) and the `.md` says "The maintainer's choice (2026-10-13): `true`".

## Runtime side effect
`runtime/lab.py` `platforms_cited()` stages the reference of every platform in the folder when a skill cites the folder, so runtime runs of these skills now also stage the Instagram and TikTok references: `brand-identity`, `brand-profile`, `brand-strategy`, `core-skill-creator`, `mkt-engage`, `mkt-publish`, `mkt-social-copy`, `mkt-vote-round`. It touches no eval evidence.

## Latent incompatibility, fixed by P10
`skills/mkt-publish/scripts/payload.py` reads `media.types[].magic_hex` from offset 0 (it ignores `magic_offset`) and reads `post.first_comment.supported`, which is null for these platforms. It is never given these files today, since the tests and the runtime pass only LinkedIn's; P10 makes it read both.

## Deferred
Carousel and static publishing (decision D13), TikTok comment and address templates, and the facts marked `not checked` in the references (aspect of images, TikTok hashtag and mention limits, TikTok minimum duration).

author: jakobengdahl
body:
**Review-gated: opened for owner review, not to be merged by the session.**

## Summary

`GraphStorage.add_nodes` persisted the added nodes and then, in a second write, the added edges. On a snapshot-only backend each write serialises the whole graph, so a single call wrote the graph twice. On a transactional incremental backend (the file journal, Postgres) it was two journal records or two transactions, and a crash or failed write between them could leave the store holding the nodes without their edges.

Now `add_nodes` issues **one** `_persist` call after the edge loop: node upserts first, then edge upserts. That is one `apply_batch` on a transactional backend and one snapshot on a snapshot-only or non-transactional backend. Every failure exit (duplicate id, unresolvable endpoint, applicability rejection, any raise) still persists exactly what landed in memory through `persist_landed()`, so a rejected edge still leaves its nodes in place.

**Durability: what a successful mutation promises.**
- **Before:** a success result meant the mutation was applied in memory and its two writes were queued on the single writer thread. A graceful shutdown (SIGTERM, which uvicorn turns into the app shutdown hook and `shutdown_events()`) drained, healed and checkpointed them. A hard crash could lose whatever had not landed, and could land the nodes without the edges.
- **After:** a success result means the mutation is applied in memory and its one write is queued before `add_nodes` returns, still under the storage lock. The graceful-shutdown path is unchanged, so an acknowledged mutation is not lost on a normal shutdown or an instance replacement. The hard-crash window is the same: the write was asynchronous before and still is. The write now lands entirely or not at all on the journal and Postgres backends, so the nodes-without-edges partial state is gone. A failed write still sets the resync flag and is healed by the next write, `flush()` or shutdown.

I updated a stale comment on `_snapshotted_vector_revision` that described the old two-write shape.

## What was not changed (scope)

- **No dirty-flag or debounced flush.** On current `main`, every backend in this repo declares `incremental_writes`. A mutation already reaches the store as an entity operation (a journal append, or a row upsert), not a whole-graph `save()`. A whole-graph `save()` per mutation now happens only on snapshot-only third-party backends, on non-transactional incremental backends with more than one operation, and on the resync and migration fallbacks. Debouncing the journal or entity path would delay writes for mutations already reported as successful. That widens the hard-crash loss window beyond today's, so I did not build it. Whether to build a debounce for snapshot-only backends is left to the owner.
- **Bytes stored per mutation:** this PR does not try to prove a target here. That target depends on other storage work (vectors, history) and is not this change's to demonstrate.
- **Overlap:** open PR #898 also edits `backend/core/storage.py` (`get_incident_edges`). This diff only touches `add_nodes` and one comment, so the two do not conflict.

## Test plan

- `pytest backend/ -q`: 6148 passed, 483 skipped. After the follow-up test: `pytest backend/core/tests -q` gives 2304 passed.
- `python3 -m ruff check backend scripts` and `python3 -m ruff format --check backend scripts`: clean.
- `backend/core/tests/test_persistence_seam.py`: the assertions that pinned the two-write shape now pin one write.
  - `test_one_add_nodes_call_is_one_snapshot_on_a_snapshot_backend`
  - `test_adding_nodes_and_edges_is_one_batch_with_the_nodes_first`, which checks node ops come before edge ops
  - a non-transactional backend gets one snapshot
  - failure exits write once, carrying what landed
- `backend/core/tests/test_embedding_persistence.py::test_a_second_write_before_the_first_lands_does_not_resnapshot_the_matrix` (new). It holds the writer and issues two writes, so the in-flight sidecar dedupe guard is exercised directly. The old `add_nodes` test used to cover that guard only because `add_nodes` wrote twice. I checked that it fails with the guard removed.
- **Review loop:** one round with a correctness reviewer and a mutation reviewer (10 mutations, none survived the full suite). No production-defect. The one test-durability finding (the dedupe guard above) is fixed in this PR, so there is no residue.

## Screenshots affected

None.

## Security impact

The change alters the data-durability write path for `add_nodes`: how many backend writes one call makes, and their atomicity. Payloads, SQL construction, scope predicates and change-notification content (ids only) are unchanged. No authorization or input-validation surface is touched.

## Security review

A separate subagent reviewed durability and security only, apart from the correctness pass. It covered graceful shutdown, hard crash, failed writes and resync, an executor that has already shut down, multi-instance change notification, and batch size. **Result: no findings.**
- **Graceful shutdown:** a mutation reported as successful cannot be lost, because `shutdown_events` takes the lock, then drains, heals and checkpoints.
- **Hard crash:** the window is unchanged and partial state is no longer possible.
- **Failed write:** no new loss mode. The all-or-nothing batch replaces a case where a lone edge upsert could land without its nodes.
- **Large batches:** these can reach the Postgres NOTIFY payload cap sooner. That falls back to the documented whole-graph announcement, which costs performance and loses no data.
- **Security:** none.

No action was needed.

author: tauceti-ai-for-science
body:
This PR proves the odd-pole (Mittag-Leffler) expansion of the Haagerup–Zsidó weight `w(y) = tanh (π y / 2)` and uses it to evaluate the weight against two adjacent Cauchy resolvents: for `a ≥ 0`,

`∫_{y > 0} w(y) y ((y² + a²)⁻¹ - (y² + (a + 2)²)⁻¹) dy = 2 / (a + 1)`

(`TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_weight_mul_mul_inv_sub_inv`, with integrability `integrableOn_weight_mul_mul_inv_sub_inv`). By Fubini, the Fourier integral `∫ k(t) e^{itx} dt` of the kernel reduces to this `y`-integral at `x = a + 1`.

The general ingredients go in `SpecialFunctions`:

- `TauCeti.hasSum_cotTerm_two_mul` (`Trigonometric/TanhSeries.lean`): for `z ∉ ℤ`, the odd-indexed terms of Mathlib's cotangent expansion (`cotTerm`, `cot_series_rep'`) sum to `π cot (π z) - (π / 2) cot (π z / 2)`. Halving the argument keeps exactly the even poles (`TauCeti.cotTerm_div_two`), so the odd part is the difference of the two expansions.
- `TauCeti.hasSum_pi_div_two_mul_tanh`: for every real `y`, `(π / 2) tanh (π y / 2) = ∑_{n ≥ 0} 2 y / (y² + (2 n + 1)²)`. This is the previous identity at `z = i y`, combined with `coth 2u - coth u / 2 = tanh u / 2`.
- `TauCeti.integral_Ioi_sq_div_sq_add_sq_mul_sq_add_sq` (`Integrals/HalfLineRational.lean`): for `a, c ≥ 0` not both zero, `∫_{y > 0} y² / ((y² + a²)(y² + c²)) dy = π / (2 (a + c))`, with explicit antiderivatives for `a ≠ c` and `a = c`.

The weight integral then follows term by term. Each odd pole contributes `2 (1 / (a + 2n + 1) - 1 / (a + 2n + 3))`. The terms are nonnegative, so `hasSum_integral_of_summable_integral_norm` exchanges sum and integral, and the series telescopes.

Roadmap: OperatorTheory

Roadmap target: `OperatorTheory/SpectralSubspacePerturbation/README.md`, Part A, **Milestone A2 (Fourier, Laplace, and integrability identities)**:

- `SSP-A19` (odd-pole expansion of the weight, `w(y)/y = (4/π) ∑ (y² + (2n+1)²)⁻¹`): `TauCeti.hasSum_pi_div_two_mul_tanh`, since `w(y) = tanh (π y / 2)` by `HaagerupZsido.weight_def`. It is stated for every real `y` (both sides vanish at `y = 0`).
- `SSP-A20` (rational telescoping integral, `2 / (a + 1)` for `a ≥ 0`): `TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_weight_mul_mul_inv_sub_inv`.

`SSP-A14`, `A15`, `A17`, `A21`, `A22` are already on `main`. After this PR, the only open item in Milestone A2 is `SSP-A18` (Cauchy-kernel Poisson summation). The roadmap gives A18 as one route to A19; this PR proves A19 from Mathlib's cotangent expansion instead, so the next step, `SSP-A23` (exterior identity `∫ k(t) e^{itx} dt = 1/x` for `|x| ≥ 1`, Milestone A3), no longer depends on A18. A23 still needs the Fubini swap (via `integrable_kernelIntegrand`) and the Lorentzian pairing `integral_exp_mul_I_mul_exp_neg_mul_abs`, and then applies this PR's theorem at `a = x - 1`.

New files (387 lines):

- `TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Trigonometric/TanhSeries.lean`
- `TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Integrals/HalfLineRational.lean`
- `TauCeti/Analysis/Fourier/HaagerupZsido/OddPole.lean`

No Mathlib PR material is vendored. The kernel is from Haagerup–Zsidó, as presented in Albeverio–Makarov–Motovilov (cited in the file). The tanh expansion is the classical partial-fraction expansion, derived here from Mathlib's `cot_series_rep'`.

author: ligf-ai
body:
## Summary

Fixes all 6 issues from the external code review (verified against source before fixing; all 6 confirmed as real).

### P1-1: Duplicate OnNavigatedFrom on ClearStack/pop-to-existing
`QueueDeactivation` now takes `notifyLifecycle`: only the entry that was active at operation start gets `OnNavigatedFrom`. Already-inactive (covered) pages are disposed without a second callback.

### P1-2: Stale RegionNavigated events on reentrant navigation
- Service: `RegionNavigated` dispatch wrapped with a current-page check (`QueueRegionNavigatedEvent`) — an outer transition's event is suppressed if a reentrant navigation already moved on.
- Host: `OnRegionNavigated` verifies via `GetCurrentViewModel` before applying (defense in depth, also protects third-party `INavigationService` implementations).

### P1-3: Scoped vs page-scope design conflict
Microsoft DI has no public API to nest a scope inside another scope, so this is a contract clarification (documented on `AddElegantSeriesFlow`):
- Scoped mode isolates navigation *stacks* per window; page scopes are siblings under root, not children of the window scope.
- Window-level Scoped services are NOT shared with pages (use Singleton for shared window state).
- Page ViewModels must use the `Navigation` property, not constructor-inject `INavigationService`.

### P2-4: Guard vetoing no-op navigation
Same-type New-mode navigation (no refresh) now short-circuits before the leave guard runs.

### P2-5: Silent event-subscriber exceptions
New `INavigationService.SubscriberError` event for diagnostics; exceptions still swallowed to protect navigation state.

### P2-6: Generator reports only first error
`ViewForGenerator` now collects all mapping diagnostics and reports them together.

## Verification
- Solution builds: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- Core tests: 80/80 (75 existing + 5 new regression tests)
- Generator tests: 20/20 (19 existing + 1 new multi-diagnostic test)

## 这是什么

群岛框架（暂名）第 0 阶段的设计文档。**只有文档，没有代码。**

目标分支是孤立分支 `framework`，它和 `main` 没有共同历史，不会合并进 `main`，也不影响 rqly.com 线上（`scripts/release.py` 只发布 `main` 上的标签）。以后转成独立开源仓库时，把 `framework` 直接推成新仓库的 `main`。

## 文档

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `docs/concept.md` | 解决什么问题，和朋友圈、X、独立博客比，核心循环，QQ 空间功能对照，原则，不做什么，第一年的成功标准，风险 |
| `docs/protocol-v0.md` | 身份（域名 + Ed25519）、岛屿名片、动态、邻居、签名、收件箱、从别人的岛上发起互动、漂流瓶、灯塔、抓取规则、隐私、限制 |
| `docs/extensions.md` | 主题接口和预算、成长规则、通知事件和渠道、AI 管家（MCP，只读和起草） |
| `docs/deployment.md` | Cloudflare 免费档的额度和设计约束、自托管、测试环境 dev.rqly.com、rqly.com 以后的迁移、待核实事项 |
| `docs/roadmap.md` | 第 0 到第 5 阶段的内容和验收标准，拆成独立仓库的步骤 |
| `docs/decisions.md` | F1 到 F14，标明已定、建议、待定 |

请看 `docs/decisions.md`。标为"建议"的各项，确认后改为"已定"；有不同意见直接在 PR 里提。

author: rootkiller6788
body:
Playing a whole episode list (podcast details, latest episodes, queue screens on Wear) was leaving the same episode in the queue twice, so it came back around and played again at the end.

Two problems in MockEpisodePlayer.play(list):

- the remaining queue was rebuilt inside a map() over the new episodes and stored in a captured var, so every element overwrote it and only the removals for the last episode happened to survive. An episode that was both queued and part of the new list stayed in the queue.
- the currently playing episode was appended without checking whether the new list already contains it. LatestEpisodeViewModel/PodcastDetailsViewModel/QueueViewModel all set currentEpisode = episodes[0] right before calling play(episodes), so that episode was queued a second time.

I now compute the leftovers once with filterNot, and only add the playing episode back when the new list does not contain it. Two tests cover both cases - I ran them against the current code first and they fail with the duplicate entry, then pass with the change. All 11 tests in MockEpisodePlayerTest are green.

Note: I have no Android SDK on this machine, so I could not run the full Jetcaster build. I compiled MockEpisodePlayer and its test with a plain Kotlin/JVM setup (kotlinc 2.2.20 + kotlinx-coroutines-test) instead.

author: timmrkz
body:
Plan row 2.243. Tim felt the app lag while he worked in a clip, with no search running. His report of 13 October shows where: after each jump of the playhead the video's decoder took 60 ms on the median and 104 ms at the 90th percentile to the first frame of youtube.mp4, and 230 to 280 ms for a 4K video from a phone, while the request and the sound took 0 to 2 ms. The test below proves the fix against ffmpeg's own frames.

## Root cause

Every stream of picture opened its cursor with a seek, `open` in `cmd/framefairy-frames/main.go`: back to the key frame before the moment asked for, then every frame from there up to it. That held even when the cursor already stood a few frames before the moment, as it does for a play after a pause, an arrow key or a drag forward. About 300 of the 1714 seeks in the report were such short jumps forward. On the way, the decoder also decoded the B-frames, which nothing is made from and which are never shown. And the Go side handed a stream whichever cursor was kept last, `take` in `engine/episodeframes.go`, so even a cursor standing right before the moment was often not the one asked.

## The fix

- `goOn` in `cmd/framefairy-frames/main.go`: a cursor on the same grid at the same size reads on from where it stands when the moment is ahead and no more than 5 s away. It reads the packets up to the moment first, and seeks after all when a key frame shown at the moment or before it is among them, because decoding from that key frame is less work. The packets it read are kept and decoded in order, so nothing is read twice.
- `skipBefore` and `skipNonRef` in `flush.go`: on the way to the first frame asked for, a cursor of picture leaves out the frames nothing refers to, ffmpeg's `skip_frame` at `nonref`.
- `take` in `engine/episodeframes.go`: a stream of picture gets the kept cursor that stands closest before where it starts. When the closest is one whose stream has just stopped, it waits for that cursor to finish the few frames of its batch, since the decoder makes those first in any case. `give` keeps the cursor just let go of and closes the one kept longest when three are kept already.
- The decoder's line for a jump's first frame now says how many frames it decoded, so the next report shows the work per jump.
- Docs: [VIDEO-PREVIEW.md](docs/VIDEO-PREVIEW.md), and plan rows 2.242 (done with #214) and 2.243 in [GUI-PLAN.md](docs/GUI-PLAN.md).

## Proof

- `TestTheEpisodesDecoderDecodesAJumpNoFurtherThanItMust` makes an MPEG-4 file with a key frame every 2 s and two B-frames in three, jumps 0.2, 1.4, 3.1, 2.4, 4.3, 5.5 and 1.92 s, and checks 8 frames of each against ffmpeg's. It fails on main: every jump seeks, and the jump to 1.92 s decodes every one of the 48 frames from its key frame. Here the jumps to 1.4 and 5.5 s read on, and the jump to 1.92 s decodes 18 frames.
- Every other decoder test passes, frames identical to ffmpeg's, under `go test -race`.
- `make changed` passed, the walks included.
- What the cloud cannot check: VideoToolbox on a Mac, and the numbers on Tim's videos. The log now says them.

## How to test

1. Update the app to this pull request from the Updates page.
2. Open a video and a clip in it. Press the space bar to play, pause, and play again a few times. The picture should start at once each time.
3. Click on the clip timeline a little ahead of the playhead, a few times, and drag the playhead forward slowly. The video preview should follow without the short lag before.
4. If anything still lags, send a report with Report a Problem. The decoder now says per jump whether it read on or moved, and how many frames it decoded.

## Found along the way, not fixed here

- Keeping the frames around the playhead, and showing the nearest key frame first while the hand outruns the decoder, stay open in row 2.243 until the log says they are needed.

Stage 6B, v2-bosses (brief: docs/sessions/v2-bosses.md). Defaults are logged in `docs/decisions/v2-bosses.md`.

## What's in it
- **Posture/stagger.** Poise fills from precision hits and from well-timed rolls. Full poise opens a 3 s visceral window at 2× damage, followed by a 5 s lockout. A posture bar sits under the boss bar. Max poise scales through `PartyScaling`, tested at 1 and 8 players.
- **Fairness invariants** are locked constants in `logic/Fairness`, and configs are clamped to them. `ReadabilityTest` walks every boss config.
- **Attack archetypes.** Each boss has 2+ next to its v1 moves: ring, pools, leap, cross, beam, charge, summon-shield, burst, wisps, burrow, spiral and void moves. Feints are allowed from phase 2. Archetype params live in pure-Java `ArchetypeParams`.
- **Part breaks.**
  - Stormplate's left pauldron: breaking it removes the spear throw and the feint into it, and the knight gets +12% speed.
  - Ashwyrm's tail: breaking it removes `tail_sweep`.
  - Both have broken-part textures.
- **Movement vocabulary.**
  - Sidesteps against held aim (Furnace Knight, Stormplate, Pale Rider).
  - Sticking charges.
  - Burrow.
  - Hit-stop.
- **AttackPicker:** utility-scored `pickScored` with config weights.
- **Field-boss affixes.** Expedition only, from floor 2, on main's `common.mob.Affix`/`Affixes` contract. They add a tint and a name prefix.
- **Presentation.**
  - A name splash once per fight.

body:
Was reading through shippingservice and noticed getRandomLetterCode() does 65 + rand.Intn(25). That maps to 65..89, so tracking IDs could only ever start with A-Y and Z was unreachable. The alphabet has 26 letters, so I changed the bound to 26.

I also tightened the existing test. It sampled 100 codes and only asserted the result was between 65 and 90, which passes whether or not Z is reachable, so it could never have caught this. It now collects the codes from 10000 draws and requires every letter A-Z to appear. That version fails on the old Intn(25) bound and passes with the fix.

Every ShipOrder call goes through CreateTrackingId(), so the generator is on a real path, though the impact is small - it just means some tracking IDs are unused.

author: seantalts
body:
Stacked on #456. Two follow-ups from #455.

## Context

#456 left two things open:

- In the cogmod DDM models, `wiener_lpdf` was still evaluated twice per gradient.
- The radon models were about 1.06x slower on Linux because of where `gather_bwd` was placed in the binary.

Linux x86-64, GCC 13, one pinned core. Microseconds per gradient.

| | main | #456 | this branch | CmdStan |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| brms 4-parameter DDM | 448 | 326 | 255 | 300 |
| same, direct form | 371 | 262 | 188 | 262 |
| `radon_county` | 27.1 | 28.7 | 27.0 | |
| `radon_variable_intercept_slope_centered` | 55.3 | 58.5 | 55.4 | |
| `ch09_m9_1` | 0.81 | 0.85 | 0.81 | |

The other four radon models are also back to within 0.4% of main.

## Diagnoses

1. **`wiener_lpdf` in a mixture.** The forward pass keeps the partials. The reverse pass reused them only when the output adjoint was exactly 1. In the DDM models the log density feeds a mixture, so the adjoint is almost never 1. Of 64,167 backward calls on the 4-parameter DDM, 60,651 evaluated the density again.
2. **`gather_bwd` placement.** Its inner loop is 24 bytes. When the function starts at address 48 mod 64, the loop crosses a cache line boundary and the function costs about 30% more. Edits elsewhere in the runtime move the function by 16 bytes. The graphs, values and instruction counts of the radon models were the same as on main.

## Design choices

- **Reuse the kept partials for any finite output adjoint.** The partials are multiplied by the adjoint. The second evaluation stays for three cases: a non-finite adjoint, non-finite kept partials, and an input the forward pass did not differentiate.
- **Align `gather_bwd` to 64 bytes.** This uses a function attribute, as `run_program_impl` and `run_adjoint` already do. The attribute is empty on compilers without it. With GCC 13 the loop then starts at function offset 0x40 and stays inside one line.

## Numerics

- Gradients of the two DDM models move by at most 7 ULP against #456. `s2_wiener` and `cm_ddm` do not move.
- The weighted `wiener_lpdf` tests were bitwise against Stan Math's seeded gradient. They are now bounded at 10 ULP of the largest gradient entry. A bound of 10 ULP per entry does not hold: Stan Math's seeded and unseeded sweeps round in a different order, and one cancelling entry differs by 63 ULP. A new check requires the weighted gradient to equal the weight times the unweighted gradient bitwise.
- One `test_glm` check changes. With a weight of 1e308, Stan Math's seeded sweep overflows and returns NaN or infinity. Scaling the kept partial returns a finite value. The test no longer compares non-finite reference gradients when the weight is finite. It still compares them when the weight is infinite.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the second evaluation for large adjoints** to match Stan Math's NaN at a weight of 1e308. The finite value is the correct gradient there.
- **A value-only forward pass in weighted regions**, with the partials computed in the reverse pass. It needs a hint from lowering through the shared lane convention. Reuse needs a one-line change.
- **`-falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=32` for the whole runtime.** It fixed radon and moved other models by 4-17% in both directions.
- **Pinning the loop as well as the function.** Not needed with GCC 13. GCC 14 was not checked.

## Not fixed

`one_comp_mm_elim_abs` is still 1.10x slower than main on the Linux box. The time is in SUNDIALS code that did not change and sits at different addresses.

body:
## Problem
- `TextbausteinEditor.test.tsx` („zeigt das Vorlagen-HTML nur bereinigt …“) failed sporadically in full runs with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'querySelector')`.
- Shuffled full runs revealed more order- and load-dependent tests: `EmailCenter`, `ZeiterfassungZeitkontenTask9b`, `LieferantDokumenteTab`, `document-editor/index.test.tsx` (test 4).
- Deleting a text template happened on a single click without confirmation; network errors only went to the console.

## Root causes (each reproduced deterministically)
- **TextbausteinEditor:** React 19 rewrites `innerHTML` whenever the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` object changes identity, so every re-render replaced the preview nodes the test had found. A second load round (`fetchTemplates` depended on `selectedId`) caused exactly such a re-render – 6 instead of 3 requests.
- **EmailCenter:** the collapse test left `email_center_sidebar_collapsed` in localStorage → later tests rendered a collapsed sidebar (seeds 1 and 3 fail on main).
- **ZeitkontenTask9b:** describe-level `vi.fn()` kept its call history (`restoreAllMocks` no longer clears `vi.fn` in Vitest 4) → `calls.find()` hit another test's request (seed 2 fails on main).
- **LieferantDokumenteTab:** `shouldAdvanceTime` ticks the fake clock 20 ms per 20 ms real time; inside an async `act` one tick pushed 299 ms over the 300 ms debounce.
- **document-editor test 4:** queried `.ProseMirror` synchronously before tiptap had mounted it under load.

## Changes
- `TextbausteinEditor.tsx`: memoized `{__html}`, functional selection update → load once, placeholder chip no longer nested twice, `escapeHtml` also escapes `>`, „Neue Vorlage“ → „Abbrechen“ returns to the previously selected template, **delete asks first** (shared `useConfirm`, `variant: 'danger'`, explains that the template also disappears from the form templates' Standard-Texte – FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`; existing documents keep their text), error toast on network failure, `aria-label`s on icon buttons.
- Test infrastructure: `clearMocks: true` in `vitest.config.ts`, `setupTests.ts` clears local/session storage after each test; targeted fixes in `LieferantDokumenteTab.test.tsx` (synchronous `act` at the boundary) and `document-editor/index.test.tsx` (wait for the editor).
- Tests: preview queried fresh via `waitFor`, stricter assertions (exactly one chip), regression tests for single load, stable DOM, cancel and the delete flow (every new test fails against the old component); new e2e spec `textvorlage-loeschen.spec.ts` (pc-14zoll, pc-uebergang, pc-monitor, screenshots reviewed).

- After merging `origin/main`: full suite shuffled 3103/3103, lint clean, build green, `typecheck:e2e` clean, e2e spec green in all three sizes.

author: tgockel
body:
libc's system() sets SIGINT to SIG_IGN for the whole process while it waits for its child, as POSIX asks of it. An interrupt the host sent during that wait -- the automatic one or the user's Ctrl-C -- was discarded rather than deferred, and because the disposition is process-wide, one agent's os.system also swallowed an interrupt meant for another agent's wedge on the main thread. It was also the one common spawn that bypassed the Popen patch, so its output reached the exec's stderr as output.unattributed instead of its execution's result.

The interpreter now replaces os.system with a wrapper over subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True). It ends with KeyboardInterrupt like any synchronous run -- the shell killed, what the shell started not -- and goes through the Popen patch, so its output is billed. The return value is still the wait status: returncode << 8 for an exit, the signal's number for a signal; the core-dump bit is not reproduced. The command goes through os.fsencode because os.system takes a path-like and run refuses one with shell=True.

posix.system and a libc system() reached from native code or ctypes are not replaced and still discard the interrupt. runtime-protection.md and agent-placement.md say so. The 0003-06 task record still points at plan/next/os-system-discards-interrupts.md, which has since moved to the issue; it is left as the historical record.

Closes #463.

author: amarcozzi
body:
Closes #687

## Summary

Grid chunk JSON (dense and sparse) and point cloud tile JSON now write their large numeric arrays with orjson (`OPT_SERIALIZE_NUMPY`), straight from the numpy buffer, instead of `tolist()` + Pydantic. Decision and rationale are on #687.

- Pydantic still builds everything except the arrays: the response model is constructed with empty arrays, dumped with `model_dump(mode="json")`, the arrays are placed into that dict, and orjson writes the whole body. No string splicing. The 2D z-field rule (#487) and sparse `fill_value: null` still come from the models.
- `_json_values` (tolist + NaN rewrite loop) is replaced by `_json_array`, which only makes the array native-endian and C-contiguous (orjson rejects anything else) and widens bool to float64 to keep today's `1.0`/`0.0`. orjson writes NaN and ±Inf as `null`.
- The `asyncio.to_thread` offload, raw `Response`, `response_model=` (OpenAPI), size checks, 413s and error paths are unchanged and in the same order.
- Inventory JSON stays on Pydantic.
- New runtime dependency: `orjson>=3.13.0` (single compiled wheel, no transitive dependencies, `MPL-2.0 AND (Apache-2.0 OR MIT)`). The lock diff is only orjson.

## Contract change (Beta, deliberate, per #687)

float32 grid values print in shortest float32 form instead of the float64 widening:

```
before: [12.345600128173828, 7.099999904632568, null, 5.965000152587891, 0.30000001192092896]
after:  [12.3456, 7.1, null, 5.965, 0.3]
```

They decode to the same float32. Clients decoding as float64 see the shorter value; ~5% of values rounded to 2 decimals display differently at the edge (`5.965` → "5.96" vs "5.97"). float16 bands likewise print at float32-shortest precision and decode to the same float16. A sparse chunk's float `fill_value` is printed in the band's precision too, so it compares equal to the values it stands for. Integer, float64, bool and point cloud values are unchanged (exact). Field names, structure, nulls, status codes and OpenAPI are unchanged; the only other text difference is exponent notation for very large metadata floats (orjson writes `1e+16` where pydantic-core wrote `1e16`), which parses identically and does not occur for real transforms, bounds, scales or offsets.

## Verification

- Unit tests: 154 passed. The grid reference is the legacy `tolist()` encoder run through FastAPI with `response_model`. Fields outside the value arrays, integer and float64 values compare exactly; float32/float16 values compare as their band dtype with null positions matched. Coverage: all 12 dtypes (dense and sparse, with and without fill value), int64/uint64 extremes, shortest float32 text, `order=F`, sparse indices in both orders, 3D chunks with z fields, 2D z-field omission, sparse `fill_value: null`, float32 sparse fill printed like the values, NaN/±Inf → null, and big-endian / Fortran-ordered / strided inputs producing identical bytes. Point cloud: exact parity, including a multi-chunk table and an empty tile.
- Live router tests (grids, point clouds, inventories data routers) against a local server: 95 passed, 0 tracebacks.
- OpenAPI: all 10 `/data` paths and the 17 schemas they reference are byte-identical to main.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

Local timings (median of 15, dev machine; **not validated on Cloud Run**, which #687 requires before merge):

| Body | Before | After | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512×512 float32 dense chunk, 10% NaN | 16.6 ms | 2.5 ms | 4.50 → 2.43 MB |
| 250k points × 4 columns tile | 115.7 ms | 4.2 ms | 7.59 → 7.59 MB |

## Ripple checks

1. Breaking change to the API contract: **yes, deliberate (Beta)** — float32 (and float16) grid value text, as above. Nothing else.
2. FastFuels-Web docs: **cosmetic** — `documentation/src/code-examples/v2-beta/api/how-to-guides/fetch_grid_data/data_chunk_response.json` shows 17-digit values; regenerate or shorten. Decision for the maintainer.
3. Python SDK: no. Generated JSON clients still parse floats/ints; grid convenience methods use `/binary`.
4. Webapp API client: no after silvxlabs/FastFuels-Web#363 (binary) ships; before that, popup rounding as above.

author: tadasant
body:
iOS parity, slice B: **G2** (nothing updated live), **G3** (a session opened at the top), and **G7** (drafts were lost). The gap list is in [`ios/PARITY_AUDIT.md`](https://github.com/tadasant/zimmer/pull/1306).

App-only, with no server change and no auth change. It reads the same routes the app already reads, more often.

## Parity

| Behaviour | Web UI | iOS before | iOS now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A running session's page | Turbo streams new messages in | Loaded once; updated only on pull-to-refresh or your own action | Re-reads every 5 s while running or waiting, every 20 s otherwise, and again on returning to the app; a trashed session isn't polled |
| The board | Turbo streams rows | Loaded on filter change or pull | Re-reads silently every 30 s, and on returning to the app, while it's in front and not being edited or dragged |
| Opening a session | At the newest message | At the header; the conversation was below the cards | At the newest message, and follows new ones while you're at the end |
| Reading back | Stays where you are | — | A poll never pulls you back down while you're reading earlier messages |
| Drafts | Kept per session for 7 days | Lost on leaving the screen | Kept per session for 7 days (`DraftStore`), across leaving and relaunching |

## Decisions

- **Polling, not a socket.** The app has no Action Cable client. Polls are cheap reads of routes it already calls, and they stop when the page isn't in front.
- **A poll never undoes an edit.** Every change made on the page bumps a revision. A poll that started before an edit throws its answer away rather than overwriting the edit.
- **No polls under the queue manager or the editor**, so rows don't move under a finger.
- **Whether you're at the end is read from geometry** (`onGeometryChange` on the end anchor), not from `onAppear`, which was always true.
- **A poll leaves an action's error on screen.** A poll's own failures are never shown, so it has no error of its own to clear. CI caught an earlier version wiping a refusal the person had just been shown.

## Verification

- [x] CI green on the head commit (`b2e0b16d`): every check, including the `ios` simulator job and `ios_swift_linux`.
- [x] `LiveUpdatesUITests`:
  - new messages appear without a pull;
  - reading back isn't pulled to the end;
  - a session opens at its newest message;
  - a draft survives leaving the screen.
  The other UI tests pass too, including `SessionActionsUITests`, where the refusal banner must stay up while polls run.
- [x] ZimmerKit tests for `DraftStore` (save, expiry after 7 days, clear on send).
- [x] Fresh-eyes review (in-process subagent). Addressed:
  - Blocking: `atEnd` was always true.
  - Stale poll overwrites.
  - Polling under the queue manager.
  - Polling a trashed session.
  - The board's reads made silent.
  - Republishing only on change.
  - The hierarchy test's scroll direction.
- [x] Screenshot from the CI run: session #1044, a long conversation, opens at its newest message rather than at the header.

  ![A long session opened at its newest message](https://storage.googleapis.com/remote-filesystem-tmp-public/screenshots/pr-1307/session-detail-long.png?GoogleAccessId=remote-fs-mcp-server-tadas%40pulse-443819.iam.gserviceaccount.com&Expires=1799685863&Signature=a4dVrUbBdjsKj5j%2FI5KA9h1%2FkMpNDJRQdDjrZuDjDJmoQqF4nuDb99O8%2Bbs7%2F7az4hmtifxvhp1sApYEQ1MuMzbu8wJ6FO26ZFTTyVUK5dgNARSLnDspmXWkbemhWMtuhIYAv4w3GAqERiPf9uNGeziCCsOkxz3dUkDUPehExCU8VrS53jf03KlgNsTq4pIfiqmKo7Yf25nTsOYTJtO77Kk5M6e9Y7t9AvpoNgZHd0PptQ3xF2JeKoDRTYHpAz8JWDG5bKqVLLUmNs9t7Fb4MjlaZz%2FtH10B5vQOrDq8U0joFgDZF3Hq%2FcuhGXMbC7nz2uoH0ntXTPywqqlVmQD4JA%3D%3D)

author: alasharim
body:
Signing in from Welcome came back to Welcome every time, so Google sign-in
looked broken although Google and Supabase both succeeded.

The sign-in screen decided whether the first sync comes next by reading
first_sync_done after signing in. The background sync that starts with the
new session often finished first and set it, so the screen popped back to
Welcome and onboarding never started. Every later try found a session
already stored and popped back as well.

StartRouter.firstSyncAfterSignIn now decides: a session new to this phone,
an unfinished first sync, or a phone not yet set up all go to the first sync
screen. The screen reads whether someone was signed in when it opened,
instead of the flag the background sync races to set.

author: paynejd
body:
Relates to OpenConceptLab/ocl_online#454 (partial: the ticket tracks two more causes, listed at the end).

## Summary

Concept and mapping lists made several queries per row while serializing a page. For each row they looked up:
- the latest version's uri (`version_url`);
- `latest_source_version`;
- the from/to concepts' sources and the sources' owners (mappings);
- `created_by`/`updated_by`.

A 1,000-row page of mappings ran about 8,500 queries.

This change loads those once per page, after pagination:

- `SourceChildMixin.load_list_fields(instances)` prefetches each model's `LIST_PREFETCHES`. It then runs one `DISTINCT ON` query for the HEAD rows' latest version uris and one for each row's latest released source version (plus an `in_bulk` for those sources).
- `SourceChildPageSerializer`, a `ListSerializer`, calls it for the page. It's set as `list_serializer_class` on `Concept{List,VersionList,Detail}Serializer` and `Mapping{List,VersionList,Detail}Serializer`, so search results get it too.
- `version_url` and `latest_source_version` use the page-loaded values when they're there. Serializing a single object runs the same code as before.

It loads after pagination rather than annotating the page query, because a subquery annotation is evaluated for every row an OFFSET skips. On a deep page of a large source, EXPLAIN showed both subqueries running for the ~300k skipped rows.

## Collection-scoped lists (from review)

- **`latest_source_version` is back in collection scope**, as the source version the row's references in that collection resolved to (newest first; `HEAD` gives `null`). That's what TBv3 computes from `includeReferences` today; the plain latest release was the ocl_issues#2770 bug. It's loaded once per page.
- **Lookups only run for fields the response includes.**
- **Collection pages are flat too.** They no longer query per row for `previous_version_url`, `references`, names, descriptions, `source_versions` or `collection_versions`.
- **Three outputs now have a fixed order:** `source_versions` by `created_at`, `collection_versions` as a sorted list (was a set), and reference uris by id.

## Query counts

Local test stack, CIEL-shaped fixture, 1,000-row page of HEAD mappings:

| | Queries | Time (local DB) |
|--|--:|--:|
| master | 8,505 | 5.4 s |
| this branch | 14 | 1.3 s |

The local DB has no network round trip, so production saves more per query than this shows. Timings from before the change are recorded on the ticket.

## Tests

- `MappingListQueryCountTest` and `ConceptListQueryCountTest` (new, sharing `SourceChildListQueryCountMixin` in `core/integration_tests/test_utils.py`) cover HEAD, repo-version, collection and global lists, both default and `verbose=true`. Each checks three things:
  - a page of 4 runs the same number of queries as a page of 2;
  - the response equals the rows serialized one at a time;
  - `latest_source_version` and `version_url` have the expected values.
- `ConceptListQueryCountTest.test_revisions_in_no_released_version` covers search-result rows saved since the last release.
- The new tests fail on master. A page of 2 vs 4 takes 22 → 39 queries (mappings HEAD), 22 → 37 (mappings version), 9 → 13 (concepts HEAD), 11 → 17 (concepts version) and 12 → 24 (concept revisions). They pass on this branch.
- Locally, the full suite (2,539 tests) passes and `pylint -j0 core/` is clean.

## Review

- **Codex pass 1:** one P1 (F1.1), fixed in 61274f65. A concept revision in no released version still made one query per row through `get_source_version_before_creation()`.
- **Codex pass 2:** clean.
- **Simplification review:** 4 cuts, applied in 1744f476. One shared `latest_source_version` on the mixin, two redundant guards dropped, shared test mixin.
- **Codex check of the cuts:** clean.

Details are in the comments below.

## Not in this PR (tracked on OpenConceptLab/ocl_online#454)

- **Deep pages of a HEAD list.** The page query joins the from/to concepts for every row the OFFSET skips. The repo-version path already selects the page's ids first and doesn't have this cost. That's #937.
- **Rows without stored checksums.** These still calculate and save them during a GET (backfill: OpenConceptLab/ocl_online#475).

author: jcsoftdev
body:
Root cause: a real bug, not test timing. `createStickToBottom` only updated its `lastTop` baseline in the scroll handler. A programmatic follow-scroll (ResizeObserver) is delivered as a scroll event a frame later; if the reader scrolls up in that window the browser coalesces both moves into one event, and `nextStuck` compared the new top against a stale baseline, saw no upward move, and stayed stuck. Under CI load the original test's scroll landed in that window (flake on #70 and #61).

Fix: `toBottom` records the position it scrolled to as the baseline. The original test is unchanged and strict; a new deterministic regression test forces the coalescing (it fails without the fix).

Verification: 25 runs of the stick-to-bottom browser tests under CPU load (2x ncpu busy loops): 25 green. Full ui-core unit, browser, typecheck, lint, size pass.

author: davekim917
body:
Bash removes an unquoted backslash from a command name before looking it up, so `\rm -rf ~` runs `rm`. The guard's parser kept the backslash, so the name matched no rule. On main, each of these is **allowed**:
- `\rm -rf ~`
- `\git push --force origin main`
- `\psql -c "DROP TABLE x"`

`\rm` is the usual way to skip an `rm -i` alias, so honest agents write it.

The command name is now unescaped on all three paths that resolve it: the parser path, after a wrapper such as `sudo`, and the regex fallback.

## Evidence
- Five conformance rows (`\rm -rf ~`, `r\m -rf ~`, `sudo \rm -rf ~`, `\git push --force …`, `\psql -c "DROP …"`). All five fail against main's core and pass now.
- `plugins/workflow/hooks` guards: 876 pass / 0 fail. `plugins/workflow-agents` hooks: 33 / 0. `vendor-guards --check` passes.

Found by the fallback reviewer of #78. Independent of #78.

author: bearflinn
body:
## What failed

On #565, `[phone] chat-layout.spec.ts › keeps Send inside the box when the model name doesn't fit` failed in `openChat`. The feed stayed 860px above the bottom, with the Jump to latest pill showing.

## Root cause

This is an app bug, not a test race. The CI trace shows these steps:

1. The feed was pinned at the bottom (scrollTop 1299).
2. As the page settled around the feed, the browser moved the position back 4px, to 1295.
3. ep-003 was prepended before the feed handled that move's scroll event. ep-003 is 860px tall, the exact distance the test saw.

`FeedScroller` judges a move it hasn't had an event for yet (in `catchUpWithScroll`, and in the scroll event itself) against the layout at the moment it looks. So it measured the 4px move against content that had just grown by a whole episode. That read as the reader leaving the end by 860px, so the feed stopped following, and the ResizeObserver left it where it was. A real reader could hit the same race when opening a chat at a narrow width.

## Fix

Before the feed's items change, `Feed.svelte` takes in any scroll position it hasn't handled yet. A `$effect.pre` calls `scroller.catchUpWithScroll()`, which is now public. The move is then judged against the content it was made over. When the prepend lands, the reader is still following, and the scroller pins them to the new bottom as usual. A reader who really scrolls away is judged the same as before.

My first version judged every scroll against the last content end the ResizeObserver had seen. It broke `chat-feed.spec.ts › a reload under a reader who scrolled up keeps their place`: when the page deliberately scrolls into fresh content to restore the reload anchor, that scroll was judged against stale geometry. This version acts only at the point where items change.

## Tests

- A new component test in `Feed.component.test.ts` replays the CI sequence. The reader is pinned, the browser moves them back 4px with no event, older items are prepended, and then the scroll event arrives. Without the pre-effect, the test fails the way CI did: the Jump to latest pill shows. With the fix, it passes.
- The existing e2e test stays as the regression check. No wait, timeout or assertion changed.
- Local e2e runs used the production build (`E2E_SMOKE_ON_BUILD=1`). "Under load" means 6 workers plus 24 `yes` CPU burners, a load average of about 40 on 12 CPUs.
  - **Before the fix:** the failing test passed 30/30 quietly and 40/40 under load. The whole chat-layout spec on phone passed 255/255 under load. The race needs a forced layout to land between the nudge and the prepend, and I couldn't trigger that locally. The CI trace is what identifies the cause.
  - **After the fix:**
    - chat-layout on phone: 255/255 under load.
    - chat-layout and chat-feed on phone and desktop, ×10: 630/630 under load.
    - chat-feed, chat-layout, chat-turns and chat on both sizes, ×2: 178/178.

author: stelizhenets
body:
## Issue description

Games of different patch revisions play in the same matches. Since revision 3 (the battery rule) an older game and a newer one do not compute a match alike: they part at a team's last battery. The server only logs the revision a game says at its sign-in.

On the players' server on 2026-10-13, 12:30 to 16:43 UTC, 30 accounts signed in: 19 with revision 0, 1 with 1, 3 with 2, 2 with 3, 5 with 4. Revisions 0 and 1 are downloads from before the launcher, so those games never update by themselves.

A refusal at the sign-in (answer 0x22) was the first idea. It shows the game's own "You're using an outdated version of the game." and nothing else, and an old exe cannot be taught another text: the player is not told what to do.

## Fix description

The check is in the lobby, at Play (`lobby-server/src/v026g/patch_check.rs`). It is **off by default**; merging this changes nothing for anybody.

| Setting | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `SRP_PATCH_REVISION_CHECK` | off | `warn`: an older game is told how to update and plays. `refuse`: it is told, and its Play is refused |
| `SRP_MIN_PATCH_REVISION` | 4 | The least patch revision of a game that plays |
| `SRP_OUTDATED_TEXT` | `st_login_menu_status_invalid_version` | What the refusal's message box shows: a text key of the game, or a sentence |
| `SRP_UPDATE_HINT` | a sentence naming `Skhid.bat` | The chat line that says how to update; empty: no line |

- An older game signs in as before and has the lobby, the chat, its friends and the shop.
- Play (`2F`) and clan-team Play (`30`) are answered `84 <op> 00 <text>`. The client localizes the text, shows it in a message box and puts its Play button back. This is the path a kit without a weapon already takes.
- A line in the general chat, to that player alone, says what to do: when its game opens the general chat and at a refusal, at most once in 30 s. It is a line as the queue chat sends them.
- The late-join exe (revision 0x80) is over any minimum. A test bot (`SRP_BOT_ACCOUNTS`) signs in as revision 0 and is never checked.
- The home page says in its "Without the launcher" part what to do when the game says it is outdated.
- The four names are in `docker-compose.yml`, so they work from `.env`; `deploy/env-026g.example` shows them.

Read in the client for this (notes: `lobby_requests.md` section 4.2, `client_patch.md` section 6):

- `lobby_menu` 0x21D9D0: for `2F` and `30` the text is localized, shown by `show_system_message`, and the matchmaking and Play button are reset. Only `st_not_logged_id` does more (it signs the client out), and it is not used here.
- `text_translator::translate_text` 0x1FF0F0: a text that is no key of the game is used as it is, so `SRP_OUTDATED_TEXT` may be a sentence. It must stay under 0x200 bytes; the wire allows 255.
- `st_login_menu_status_invalid_version` is in all six localizations.
- The chat line (`A2`) is read into the fixed buffers of 0x26B6F0; the line is cut to 255 bytes and its sender name to 20, as the queue chat's.

## Fix effect

Tests: the 0.26g workspace, 1,144 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored. Nine new ones (`patch_check_tests.rs`): off by default, the refusal and its text, the hint and its 30 s, `warn`, clan-team Play, a game that does not listen to the chat, a sentence as the text, the bot, the setting's values.

For it:

- A player who is refused is told why in the game's own words, in their language, and how to update in the chat.
- Nobody is locked out of the lobby, so the instruction can reach them, and they can ask in the chat.
- `warn` allows a period in which everybody is told before anybody is refused.
- With `refuse` at 3 or more, every match is between games that compute the battery rule alike.

Against it:

- Not seen in a real game yet: the message box with this key at Play, a sentence as its text, and the hint line. The paths are the ones the weapon check and the queue chat use, but these texts were never on a screen.
- The hint is in the general chat. A player who never opens that tab sees the message box only, which says "outdated" and not what to do.
- The hint is one text for everybody: the server does not know a player's language. The message box is localized, the hint is not.
- With `refuse` today, 25 of the 30 accounts seen could not play until they update, and 20 of them have no launcher and must download the files by hand once.
- The revision is what the exe says of itself: a changed exe can say anything. This is a check for honest old games, not a protection.
- A squad with an older member cannot queue: that member's Play is refused, so the squad is never all ready. The others are not told why.
- Changing the settings needs a restart.

Not run before this was opened: the scan of the changed files for the hosts' secret values and account names (the changed text holds no address but 127.0.0.1 and no site but example.org).

  - New file: `Natamux-win-x64.exe` (NSIS, per user, no admin). The others keep the names of v0.1.2: `Natamux-mac-x64.dmg`, `Natamux-linux-x86_64.AppImage`, `Natamux-linux-amd64.deb`, `Natamux-linux-x64.tar.gz`.
  - Runs on pull requests that change the packaging, without a release. The `release` job runs only on a tag push, or a dispatch with `publish`.
  - `SHA256SUMS.txt` still covers every file: the release job hashes all artifacts. It is the update metadata for every system. The app does not use electron-updater, so there are no `latest*.yml` files.
  - Update dry runs skip with a notice while the latest release has no file for that system.
  - Artifacts: release packages 1 day, smoke logs 3 days, desktop.yml 3 days, CI desktop pictures, coverage and e2e reports 7 days.

With `NATAMUX_CLAUDE_COMMAND` set to a stand-in agent, that agent runs `natamux task show` through the app's own CLI shim, and the smoke waits for its output file.
- Windows: `natamux.cmd` uses `setlocal`, so `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` does not stay set in a cmd.exe shell. Settings JSON in the smoke steps comes from `jq`: printf broke `D:\a\...` paths.
- Docs: install guide, desktop guide, FAQ, README and packages/desktop/README list every system and the first-open step of each (macOS Open Anyway, Windows SmartScreen More info → Run anyway, Linux `chmod +x`). `scripts/readme.test.py` changed with them.

No changelog or release notes: those come with the release PR. That PR also updates `scripts/release.test.sh`, which still checks that the v0.1.17 notes say the builds are paused. The download links of the new files work once that release is published.

## Not in this PR
