author: bunsdev
body:
The plaza café table's switch now offers **Spades** beside dominoes and Hearts. You and the regular across partner against the regulars on your left and right.

## How it plays

- Bid the tricks you expect; nil means none.
- Spades are trumps, and can't be led until one is played.
- A partnership making its bid scores 10 a trick bid and 1 a bag (an overtrick). Every tenth bag costs 100.
- Short of the bid, a partnership loses 10 a trick bid. A nil scores ±100.
- First to 500 wins; falling to −200 loses.
- The round table shows the trick and hands, as in Hearts.

## What's in it

- **`spades-rules.js`** (new, pure): the deal, bidding, trick play, scoring with bags and nil, the game's end, and exact replay.
- **`spades-opponent.js`** (new): heuristic bids and play. Over 400 seeds, the average combined bid is 11.7 and 83% of contracts are made.
- **`plaza-spades.js` + `.css`** (new): bid buttons, a bid/tricks chip per seat, partnership scores with bags, and the dealer rotating.
- **The café switch:** three games in every café sheet. `main.js` keeps a `cafeGames()` map and clears the table only when the pieces change.
- **Salon Guide:** a Spades entry in the #321 format, with three pictures checked against the real rules.
- **Journeys:** `plaza-spades` (new).
  - `plaza-hearts` and the new journey wait for the X relabel instead of reading it at once.
  - That read was flaky on unchanged code: it failed 1 of 2 runs, and passed 3/3 after.
- **Docs:** `docs/multiplayer.md`. Ledger: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-plaza-spades.md`.

## Verification

- **Unit tests:** `node --test preview/tests/*.test.js`: 2873 pass, 0 fail. That includes the Spades tests (6/6) and the guide's picture test.
- **Journeys:** `plaza-spades` and `plaza-dominoes` passed; `plaza-hearts` passed 3/3.
- **Core gate:** `pnpm run verify`, run before pushing.

Practice only, like the other plaza games.

author: alrayyes
body:
Closes #922. #919 has merged; this is based on `main`.

Filter, order and chip-clear handlers weren't disabled while a page loads, so two fetches could overlap and whichever resolved last won, even when it was the older request. The table then showed results for a query the controls no longer described.

`latestOnly` in `audit-paging.ts` marks only the most recent request current. `go()` drops anything else on success, on error and for the loading flag, so a superseded failure shows nothing.

The journey holds back the oldest-first request so it resolves after the newest-first one that followed it, then checks the table matches the second. I watched it fail (rows in the wrong order) before the fix and pass after.

No visible change on the happy path, so no screenshots.

author: andypost
body:
Answers the decision item of https://github.com/freeunitorg/freeunit/issues/525 ("Answer the configuration PUT only after the store is on disk"). This is the contract change that issue asks a maintainer to decide, so the cost is first. If the answer is no, close this.

## Cost, measured

A test PUTs 40 configurations into a unitd in the `freeunit-test:latest` container on pro4s-2, with the state directory on the host's `/data` (one store is two `fsync(2)` calls). Two runs of each:

| build | average configuration PUT |
|---|---|
| master `3be75cdb` | 1.22 ms, 1.50 ms |
| this change | 25.45 ms, 25.70 ms |

A PUT waits one store longer, about 24 ms on that disk. That is the "slow day" figure of the issue rather than its 7 ms fast day, so the cost depends on the disk and is worth measuring again on the target hardware. Applying the configuration is unchanged; only the answer waits. A client that PUTs many configurations pays that per PUT.

## What the answer means

- 200 `Reconfiguration done.`: the store child wrote `conf.json`, wrote `version` when it was needed, and flushed both.
- 500 `Failed to store the configuration.`: the configuration runs, but a restart loads the one before it.
- A store that could not be sent at all is also 500. It was 200 before.

## Change

- `nxt_controller_conf_store()` registers an RPC on the controller port and sends the store with it (`src/nxt_controller.c`). It returns `NXT_ERROR` when the store cannot be prepared or sent, and the handler answers 500 in that case.
- `nxt_controller_conf_handler()` installs the configuration, sends the store and returns without answering the client. `nxt_controller_process_conf_store()` answers when main replies.
- Main keeps the reply target of the configuration store in its store state and answers it from `nxt_main_store_reply()` when the store child has ended: `RPC_READY` when it exited 0, `RPC_ERROR` otherwise, including when main killed it at exit, where the file may or may not be there but main cannot say that it is (`src/nxt_main_process.c`).
- `nxt_controller_store_in_flight()` includes a configuration store in flight, so the next request waits for the answer. That is what keeps one store outstanding at a time.
- One `Change` entry in the 1.37.1 block of `CHANGES` and `docs/changes.xml`.

## Tests

- `test/test_state_store.py::test_state_store_full_filesystem`: the 64 KiB tmpfs makes the store fail. The test now requires the PUT to be refused. On unpatched master, with the same test file, it fails with `AssertionError: the large PUT`, `assert 'error' in {'success': 'Reconfiguration done.'}` (`test/test_state_store.py:135`), while the log holds `pwrite(...conf.json.tmp...) failed (28: No space left on device)`.
- `test/test_state_store.py`: 12 passed in the container with `--privileged --restart` (the tmpfs case needs both).
- The module docstring, `wait_for_stored()` and `test_state_store_pending_at_exit` said the store is asynchronous. They are updated: the answer now waits, and the test is renamed `test_state_store_many_at_exit` because no store waits in line there any more.
- `test/test_configuration.py` needs the python module and skips in a tree without one (42 skipped here). The python legs of CI run it.

## Build and runs

On pro4s-2 (Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13.3.0), `./configure --tests --openssl`, `--debug --hardening=strict`: 0 `warning:` lines, `./build/tests` exit 0, `check-test-hooks.sh` exit 0. `git diff --check`, `check-version.sh` and the ast-grep baseline are clean.

## What this makes unreachable

The controller sends the next configuration only after the previous store has answered, so two `conf.json` stores cannot wait at the same time any more. The "a newer store replaces the pending one" path in `nxt_main_store_schedule()` and the exit-time SIGKILL of a `conf.json` store child in `nxt_main_store_cancel()` can therefore no longer be reached from the controller. Both stay, and `src/test/nxt_main_store_test.c` drives them through the test hooks. Removing them is a separate change. Main still waits for its store child at exit: a store job can still wait when main exits.

author: natekspencer
body:
Gives the BedJet more time to confirm an operating mode change, and stops Home Assistant briefly showing the old mode while it waits.

## Changes
- A BedJet 3 now gets up to 5 seconds to confirm a mode change, up from 1, the same as the V2. Devices can take longer than a second: #52's log includes `Could not confirm if operating mode was set in 1 second`. When that happens, a `climate.set_temperature` that follows `climate.set_hvac_mode` (the approach recommended in #23) could still be checked against the old mode's temperature range.
- While waiting, state callbacks are paused, so notifications that still report the old mode don't briefly revert the climate entity. Callbacks fire once when the wait ends, including on a timeout, so HA always gets the latest state.
- The three wait loops (V2 off, V2 mode switch, BedJet 3) now share one helper, and the timeout warning names the target mode.
- Mode changes run one at a time: `set_operating_mode` holds `_operation_lock` while it decides what to send, sends it and waits. This matters most on a V2, where off is sent by pressing the current mode's button again. Without the lock, an off request made during a pending HEAT→COOL change would press HEAT and turn heat on.
- A timeout from the Bluetooth write itself still reaches the caller. Only an unconfirmed mode change is logged as a warning.
- `_send_command` now returns whether it sent the command. When the BedJet is disconnected, the mode change returns immediately instead of waiting for the timeout and logging a misleading warning.

This is based on the callback-pausing approach in kdkavanagh/ha-bedjet@b99ba57 (from #44). It leaves out that commit's pause inside `update()`.

## Testing
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.
- With a simulated BedJet 3 that reports the old mode for 1.5 s before confirming: `set_operating_mode` returns once the mode is confirmed, with no warning, and only the confirmed state reaches the callbacks.
- With a device that never confirms: the warning is logged after the timeout and the latest state still reaches the callbacks.
- With a simulated V2 that toggles like the real device, HEAT→COOL and off requested together end in standby. Overlapping BedJet 3 mode changes reach the callbacks in order (COOL, then HEAT).
- A write timeout raises to the caller and releases the lock. When disconnected, `set_operating_mode` returns immediately.
- Not tested on hardware.

author: joshnorris-titan
body:
INTENDED CHANGE
A privacy policy page in Titan Time that anyone can open from a plain web address, without signing in. It explains, in plain terms, what the app collects (account details, timesheets, approvals and the customer approval emails), that the dashboard shows Titan's own LinkedIn posts — only the first line of each, linking back to LinkedIn — that we never read or store anyone's LinkedIn profile, that posts are deleted after six months, and who to contact (Rachael). Rachael pastes that address into the LinkedIn app form. Nothing else changes for consultants or customers, except that the policy now exists for them to read.

SUMMARY OF CHANGES

NEW PAGE — Core.PrivacyPolicy

- Blank layout (Titan_Theme.Titan_Blank), title "Privacy Policy". Static text only: no parameters, data sources or actions. Same card as the sign-in page, widened for reading.
- Ten sections: who we are, what we collect, content from LinkedIn, how we use it, who we share it with, how long we keep it, keeping it safe, your choices, contact (rachael@titanconsulting.net), changes to this policy. Dated 13 October 2026.
- Allowed roles: Core.Anonymous, Core.User, Core.Administrator, so signed-out visitors and every signed-in role can open it.
- Page URL "privacy", so it opens at <app>/p/privacy. No menu entry and no link from sign-in.
- Every widget is named explicitly (cntPolicy\*, txtPolicy\*, imgPolicyLogo) so the e2e suite has stable selectors.
- Documentation set, including that its LinkedIn claims must stay true of the TT-728 feed.
- Sits at the Core module root (the page-creation tool can't place it in a folder). Name kept as PrivacyPolicy; lint's info-level "page suffix" rule declined, matching Core.Login and Main.Customer_LinkInvalid.

UPDATED THEME — Titan_Theme core/widgets/_login.scss

- One block scoped to .titan-login-page.titan-policy-page: card widened to 720px and started at the top of the screen, plus section heading, paragraph and date styles. Scoped so it cannot reach the sign-in or approval-link pages (both re-checked: 0 pixels moved).

DECISIONS

- Split from TT-728 and ported ahead of it: LinkedIn checks the policy link before it approves the developer app, and TT-728's port is on hold until that approval.
- Signed-in roles were granted as well as guests, so a logged-in consultant following the link isn't refused.
- Fixed text rather than admin-editable: the policy rarely changes, and editable text would need new data, a screen and permissions.
- The wording is a draft based on what the app actually does; it is not legal advice.

REVIEW AND TESTS

- Gate 4 (level 3): no blockers. Fixed: the stylesheet's line endings (it was rewritten whole) and the card not staying at the top on tall screens.
- Gate 5: Studio Pro error check clean; lint 0 errors; unit suite 163 run, 0 failures.
- New e2e spec suites/70-tickets/tt785/verify-tt785-privacy-public.test.sh: a signed-out visitor at /p/privacy sees the policy and stays there. Proven red on cloud dev before deploy; goes green once deployed.

STILL TO DO

- Deploy to production, then hand <prod-app>/p/privacy to the LinkedIn app registration.
- Check that no access restriction (basic auth or IP allow-list) blocks /p/ on prod.

author: smdurgan
body:
## Contract (/wired)

**Sentence:** a firm person emails the Operator an ask of a kind it has never done on that seat; SMD is paged within minutes naming the request and the lane; SMD proves the lane with a full dry run on that request's real matter within hours (no Smokeball write, no email to the firm); the held job is then released and delivers to the requester.

**Terminal seam:** the requester receives the formerly held job's delivery; team@ got the `lane_unproven` card first; the proof is recorded on the seat's volume.

## What

Evidence: about 45 of A&P's 52 defects since 09-01 happened in a lane's first one to three live uses; wherever a dry run ran first, nothing reached the firm. The Captain's rule (2026-10-13): no new kind of job goes live on a real firm request until it has passed a full dry run on a real matter of that client.

- **The hold** (`medchron/lane_proof.py`, one call in `Daemon.claim_next`, inherited by all five lanes). A lane key is the queuing skill plus the drafting class (`document-drafter.discovery_set`). An unproven job stays `submitted`/`queued` (never `failed`: terminal), gets one same-state ledger note `lane_unproven: <key>`, and does not block proven jobs behind it. Once proven, the note is cleared BEFORE the claim (a stale reason on a delivered row once told a requester something false) and the job runs exactly as before.
- **The proven set:** `operator/customers/<slug>/lane-proofs.yaml` (seed, reviewed here, validated and staged to the vault by the provisioner, fetched fail-static by `entrypoint-lane-proofs.sh`) plus runtime events `medchron lane-proof accept|revoke` appends. Both root-owned on the seat: the agent cannot prove its own lanes.
- **The proof run** (`proof_run.py`, `proof_mode.py`). `.prove-<job>.json` in the lane queue; the lane runs the held job's twin when idle, every stage for real (pull, paid stages, gates, pre-delivery review, render), stopped at the write stage: chronology `upload`; demand/drafting/litigation `file`; negotiation through its dry run (#3119); drafting caption corrections journaled, not written. The twin's broker writes nothing, no wake is queued, a cursor lane gets a throwaway cursor, and the Smokeball connector refuses every non-read request while `MEDCHRON_PROOF_RUN=1` (so a runner that forgets its stop fails its proof instead of writing). Kept 72 h. HARD_STOP runs no proof.
- **Hands:** `medchron lane-proof status|dry-run|accept|revoke` (root, on the seat) and `operator/bin/lane-proof.sh <slug> ...` (plus `pull`, refused into a git checkout). `accept` needs a passed proof run of that job and a `vfy_` id. Runbook `docs/runbooks/operator/lane-proof.md`; handbook incident-response updated.
- **The page:** request card kind `lane_unproven` (migration 0125: kind, `negotiation` job lane, `lane_key`), email names the held job and the prove command; `.claude/bin/requests` lists it. Seat side: hermes-smd-overlay#445.
- **A&P seed** from its own ledgers (vfy_01M4V168KX39PHM10KG1K7RVV6): chronology, demand, mediation brief, negotiation watch, the router, file-work-requests. Deliberately unproven: `document-drafter.discovery_set` (rebuilt by #3137 after the withdrawn 10-12 set), the other drafting classes, `litigation-status` (never run on the seat's job ledger).

No new client-facing text: the requester keeps the acknowledgement the Operator already sent; the job is queued, which is true.

## Gates

| # | Gate | Layer | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hold, note once, no starvation, release clears note first | repo | met | test_lane_proof.py (25), mutation falsifiers below |
| 2 | Proof run writes nothing, records nothing, stops at each lane's write stage | repo | met | test_lane_proof.py |
| 3 | Console accepts and emails the card; D1 keeps keys only | repo | met | operator-request-card.test.ts |
| 4 | Card reaches team@ from a real seat | runtime | pending staging | |
| 5 | Held job released and run after accept on a real seat | runtime | pending staging | |
| 6 | A&P seat runs it | runtime | the lead session sequences the A&P deploy | |

Mutation falsifiers (each must fail the suite; each did): gate removed from claim_next (5 fail), judge accepts any verdict (2), twin broker writes through (3), connector refusal removed (2), note not cleared on release (3).

Suites: runner 1289 passed; substrate 2379 passed; smokeball connector 1162 passed; vitest 6489 passed (module-size ratchet included); ruff 0.15.17 check/format clean; pyright ratchet holds at 90; shellcheck clean.

body:
## Why

The app stored who created a job but not who assigned a worker to it. Any admin or manager can assign a worker to a job someone else created, so the assigner could not be recovered.

## What

- New nullable column `JobAssignment.assignedById`: the admin or market manager who put the current worker on the shift.
- Stamped on every assign path: single-date and recurring assign, released-shift assign, shift-request approval (both flows), direct-assign, and the Edit Shift modal's worker change.
- A worker's id can never be recorded: stamping goes through `assignerId()` in `apps/web/src/lib/assignedBy.ts`, which returns null for anyone but an admin or manager. Recurring rollover and clock-in materialization (which runs under the worker's session) copy the source row's value.
- Null while a shift is AVAILABLE. Approving a release clears it; an invite row is created without one and the later approval stamps it.
- Every hand-over writes a `SHIFT_REASSIGNED` or `SHIFT_RELEASED` audit row with the previous worker and previous assigner, in the same transaction as the change.
- Dashboard jobs table has an "Assigned By" column. "—" means not recorded or not assigned; "Deleted user" means the assigner's account no longer exists.

## Not included

- No backfill. Shifts assigned before this change stay blank.
- Not shown in payroll, the payroll CSV, or the mobile app.
- Deleting an assignment is not audited.
- The column records the account that was logged in, so a shared login is not attributed to an individual.

## Database

Requires `prisma/migrations/20261013000000_add_assignment_assigned_by`. The column is nullable and ignored by older code, so it is applied before deploying.

## Testing

- `apps/web/scripts/assigned-by-e2e.ts`: 49 checks against a scratch SQLite database through a running dev server, as admin, manager and worker. Covers every path above, exactly-one audit row per hand-over, rollback when the audit insert fails, rollover from cron with no session, and the dashboard output.
- That run was on a local branch carrying one extra unreleased commit. The files in this PR are identical to the tested ones except for that commit's own lines.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean on this branch.
- Not checked: the rendered dashboard column in a browser.

body:
## Summary

Fixes R6 from the WP00–WP05 code review. A slow request from an old session could log the user out of a new one: its late 401 was taken as the end of whatever session was current when it arrived. This is a client-side session correctness problem, not a server authentication bypass.

## Change

- **`apps/web/src/api/client.ts`**: a private session counter, increased whenever `setCsrfToken` sets a different value (logout sets none, login a new one). `call` reads the counter before sending. On a 401 `unauthenticated`, the token is cleared and `onUnauthenticated` called only if the counter is unchanged and a session exists. The error itself is still returned to the caller.

## Tests

Added to `apps/web/src/api/client.test.ts`, *ignores a 401 for a request sent under an earlier session*:

- a request sent with token `csrf-old`, then logout and login (`csrf-new`), then a 401 for that request: the call rejects with `unauthenticated`, the session is kept, and `onUnauthenticated` is not called;
- a request sent under `csrf-new`, with the same token set again before its 401 arrives (the reload probe): the session ends and `onUnauthenticated` is called once.

On unmodified `main` the first part failed: `hasSession` was `false` after the stale 401. The existing 401 test (a session that really ended, and the probe without a session) is unchanged and passes.

Full suite on this branch (base `main` at c2353ab):

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm check` | passed: format, lint, typecheck, 33 files / 518 tests, licences |
| `pnpm audit:prod` | no known vulnerabilities |
| `pnpm test:coverage` | passed all gates; 518 tests; 98.46% lines, 91.73% branches |
| `pnpm test:better-sqlite3` | 8 files / 105 tests passed |
| `pnpm build:web` | passed (existing bundle-size warning) |
| `pnpm test:e2e` (fake nodes) | 2 passed (desktop, phone) |
| BLAKE2b: `regtest check` / `test:regtest` / e2e | 12 passed, 0 failed / 48 passed, 1 skipped / 2 passed |
| SHA256d: `regtest check` / `test:regtest` / e2e | 12 passed, 0 failed / 49 passed / 2 passed |

The one BLAKE2b skip is `cross-chain invoices on sha256d` (`describe.runIf(chain === 'sha256d')`), which runs only on SHA256d.

## Security checklist

- Routes and permissions: unchanged. The server still decides every request; this only changes how the browser reacts to a late answer.
- Input validation: unchanged.
- Outbound calls: none added.
- Secrets: untouched. The CSRF token stays in memory only.
- Dependencies: none added.
- Spend paths: none.

## Caveats

- Query functions still do not forward TanStack Query's abort signal, so in-flight queries are not cancelled on logout. Their late results should land in the query objects that `queryClient.clear()` removed, not in the new session's cache, but this was not tested. Forwarding the signal and cancelling on logout is a possible follow-up.
- There is no browser test of the race. The client-level test drives the exact interleaving instead.

author: fontanf
body:
## Problem

`remove_aligned_vertices` removes the start of an element when it's aligned with the start of the previous element and its own end. For the first element, the previous element is the last one, which doesn't precede it in a path. When they're aligned, the first element of the path is removed and the path starts at the end of its first element.

For example, for the path (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (-2, 0), (-1, -1), the last element (-2, 0)-(-1, -1) is aligned with (0, 0), so the element (0, 0)-(1, 0) is removed.

## Change

The start of the first element of a path is always kept.

## Tests

- New parametrized test `RemoveAlignedVerticesTest`: an aligned vertex in a shape, an aligned vertex in a path, and a path whose first element is aligned with its last one. The last case fails without the fix.
- All 522 tests pass.

author: andychittock1
body:
The repo already said this should happen. README.md said `--check` could "be wired into CI alongside the test suites", and that the suites "exit non-zero if anything fails, so they're safe to wire into CI". Nothing was ever wired. #24 merged a privacy change to live Worker config and a tag release already serving two clients with zero checks on it, verified only by someone running the suites by hand and pasting the numbers into the description.

Both steps discover what to run rather than listing it. This repo gains a test file and a bundle per tag version, so a hardcoded list that someone forgets to extend is precisely the failure CI is here to prevent: a new version merging with nothing run against it, under a green tick saying otherwise.

The bundle check is the half that reaches clients. A stale bundle means the bytes a visitor downloads are not the bytes the suite just passed against, and nothing else in the repo catches that.

It can only check a version whose GTM file defines TAG_VERSION, which is 2.6.4 on. build-bundle derives the released date from the header line and requires the two to agree, so an earlier bundle fails for want of that constant rather than for having drifted. Those versions are frozen regardless: regenerating a bundle clients are pinned to is itself a live-traffic change. The step fails if it ever checks zero bundles, so a renamed constant surfaces as a red run instead of a green one that quietly did nothing.

A failing suite does not stop the others, so one run reports all of it rather than one suite per push.

Verified locally against the real tree before committing, failure paths included: all 15 suites pass and both steps exit 0; a byte appended to the 2.6.4 bundle makes the bundle step exit 1 naming that version; a deliberately failing suite makes the test step exit 1 while the other 15 still run.

### Scope
Independent audit repair stacked on PR #2163 at tested parent `14be28c52ac4ad2913b4455044652504901048f8`. ### Tests
New offline battery: concurrent 32 writes produce unique chain sequences, partial manifest failure restores both prior byte streams, interrupted crash pair refuses subsequent extension, tampering refuses append, alias paths refuse. Tests run with unittest; no StatsAPI/Odds API usage.

**DRAFT, NOT ACTIVATED**. Two-file storage is not crash-atomic (power loss between files leaves a detectable mismatch). Unsynchronized readers may see partial states. author: zbndev
body:
## Problem
Google limits Antigravity quota per **model group**, not per model vendor. The groups are *Gemini Models* and *Claude and GPT models*, and Claude and GPT-OSS share the one `3p-weekly` bucket ([Models docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/models/)). The OAuth source read the per-model `fetchAvailableModels` and grouped the result by `modelProvider`, so a single shared limit appeared on the card as two bars, Anthropic and OpenAI. The CLI (`agy`) source was already correct.

## Change
- `direct.rs`: the OAuth source now calls Cloud Code `v1internal:retrieveUserQuotaSummary`, which is the RPC the local `agy` server reports from. The response goes to the shared `parse_for_account`. The per-model parser (~850 lines) and its fixture are removed.
- `mod.rs`: one parser serves both sources. `status` is now `Option`, because OAuth has no `GetUserStatus`.
- `oauth.rs`: adds `current_project`. Without a project the summary returns `403 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED` (observed live). If a login has no stored `project_id`, it asks `loadCodeAssist` on every poll and does not persist the answer.
- Docs: `CONTEXT.md` and `antigravity/AGENTS.md`. The new fixture is a recorded live summary response.

The OAuth and CLI sources now differ only in authentication. Windows, keys (`gemini/w604800`, `3p/w604800`), titles and the Models rows are the same for both.

## Notes
- **History:** the old OAuth keys `google/…`, `anthropic/…` and `openai/…` stop receiving points; nothing already stored is deleted. Because OAuth now writes under the CLI keys, switching source no longer splits history.
- **Plan/Credits rows** still come only from the CLI source (`GetUserStatus`). Cloud Code's tier naming differs, so it is not substituted.
- **Risk:** an account for which `loadCodeAssist` names no project will get 403 from the summary. No such account was available to test.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `./scripts/check-layering.sh` all pass.
- Live smoke through `Antigravity::oauth` with a real login that has no stored project: project discovery worked, and the result was `gemini/w604800` and `3p/w604800`, titled "Claude and GPT models · 7 days", with the Models rows present.

Manual check: on an OAuth-sourced Antigravity card, there should be two weekly bars (Gemini, Claude and GPT) and no Anthropic/OpenAI bars.

**Lo que pasó:** al estrenar los avisos (o al cambiar las horas), la app calculaba por primera vez el aviso «Buenos días: ¿ya te levantaste?» de hoy y, como su hora ya había pasado, lo creaba igual: aparecía a las 11 de la mañana pidiendo confirmar algo que ya hiciste. Pasaría con cualquiera que estrene el aviso o cambie la hora a mitad del día, no solo contigo.

**Ahora:**
- «¿Ya te levantaste?» y «En media hora, a dormir» solo se crean hasta **90 minutos después de su hora**. Más tarde no salen, aunque sea la primera vez que se calculan.
- Si uno ya estaba pendiente, se quita solo (resolución automática) y **no se inventa ningún registro** de que te levantaste ni de que te acostaste.
- Para anotar la hora real sigue el botón «Me levanté» de Tu día (se pone al levantarte y se compara con la hora objetivo).
- El resto de avisos (agua, comidas, tomas…) no cambia: si la app los calcula tarde, siguen apareciendo.

**Probado:** 238 pruebas del backend (5 nuevas: no se crea horas después, sí se crea a tiempo, el pendiente viejo se quita sin registro, lo mismo con dormir, lo demás sigue igual). Al desplegar, el aviso que tienes pendiente se limpia solo en el siguiente minuto.

author: bashtage
body:
…omatic bandwidth

The kernel estimators that are not given a bandwidth select it with
kernel_optimal_bandwidth, the rule of Newey and West (1994). The rule estimates the
long-run variance with the autocovariances up to lag n = ceil(4 (t / 100) ** a), where
a is 2/9 for the Bartlett kernel, 4/25 for the Parzen kernel and 2/25 for the
quadratic spectral kernel. If n >= t - 1 these are all of the autocovariances, and
their sum is (sum x) ** 2 / t. It is zero, up to rounding error, for a series with a
mean of zero, as the scores of a regression and the deviations of the Fama-MacBeth
estimates from their average are, and the rule divides by it. That is the case with
fewer than 4 observations for the Bartlett kernel, 5 for the Parzen kernel and 6 for
the quadratic spectral kernel.

The function raised "cannot convert float infinity to integer" (an OverflowError) or
"cannot convert float NaN to integer" for some series, and returned t - 1, or another
bandwidth that was only rounding error, for the others. In 40 simulated panels of 30
entities and 5 periods, FamaMacBeth.fit(cov_type="kernel") with the quadratic spectral
kernel returned a result in all of them. Its standard errors raised the OverflowError
when they were first used in 20 of the panels, and used a bandwidth of 4 = T - 1 in
the other 20. IV2SLS, IVLIML, IVJIVE, AbsorbingLS, IVGMM, IVGMMCUE, IVSystemGMM, SUR,
IV3SLS, the asset pricing models and the Kleibergen-Paap statistics fail in the same
way, or return a bandwidth that is rounding error, usually nobs - 1.

kernel_optimal_bandwidth raises a ValueError now: "The automatic bandwidth of the
'bartlett' kernel needs at least 4 observations, but there are 3. Pass the bandwidth
explicitly." The estimators raise it from fit, or from the function that computes the
statistic. FamaMacBeth computed the bandwidth when its standard errors were first used,
so that fit returned and the error came later. The covariance estimator computes it
when it is created now, as it checks a bandwidth that is given, and its error speaks of
time periods and of the bandwidth that is passed to fit. The Driscoll-Kraay default
bandwidth is another rule and does not change.

A bandwidth that is not finite although there are enough observations raises a
ValueError that says so: a series of zeros, an estimate of the long-run variance that
is exactly zero (for example [1, -1, 0, 0] with the Bartlett kernel), or values that are
not finite or whose squares overflow or underflow. These raised the OverflowError or the
NaN error above, after numpy warnings.

With a bandwidth that is given, or with enough observations, nothing changes: the new
function returns the same bandwidth as the old one for all of the 22,637 random series
(seven kernel names, 1 to 4000 observations) for which it returns one, and the tests
compare it with the rule written out with plain loops. The default bandwidth of IVGMM,
IVGMMCUE and IVSystemGMM changed in 7.1 from nobs - 2 to this rule, so that these models
raise with the default and few observations, where they returned a result in 7.0.
optimal_bw=False or bandwidth=nobs - 2 restores the bandwidth of 7.0.

The docstring of kernel_optimal_bandwidth gets a summary line, a Raises section, notes
with the rule, the pilot lags and the fewest observations of each kernel, and a
reference, in place of its todo. The docstrings of FamaMacBeth.fit and
FamaMacBethCovariance say how many periods the automatic bandwidth needs, and the
example of FamaMacBeth.fit uses kernel="parzen", as "Parzen" is not a kernel name.

The 495 new tests are in tests/test_kernel_bandwidth_few_observations.py. The fewest
observations of each of the seven kernel names are computed from the closed form of the
pilot lag, the data of the boundary are integer series whose sum is exactly zero, and
the bandwidth above the boundary is compared with the rule written out in the test, for
the function, IV2SLS, IVGMM, IVGMMCUE, TradedFactorModel, FamaMacBeth and the kernel
weight matrices and covariances. 178 of them fail without this change. The others pin
what does not change: the results above the boundary, a bandwidth that is given and the
Driscoll-Kraay default.

author: scarmani
body:
## Purpose

Partition-B import-contract burn-down (structural-excellence mission, M4, second third), part 4: one registry
inversion. The baselined contract pair `aragora.debate -> aragora.integrations` disappears and plain `--freeze` shrinks
`scripts/baselines/import_contracts_baseline.json` from 39 to 38 pairs.

| resolved pair | old site | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `aragora.debate -> aragora.integrations` | `aragora/debate/post_debate_coordinator.py:1260` (`from aragora.integrations.decision_bridge import DecisionBridge` inside `PostDebateCoordinator._step_decision_bridge`) | hook `aragora/debate/decision_plan_bridges.py`, filled by `aragora/integrations/decision_bridge_registration.py` |

Fix class 2 (inversion through a hook in the lower package). The hook follows the pattern of
`aragora/events/approval_requests.py` (#10607) and the two hooks of #10626: a module-level slot, a register function,
and a lookup that, on its first miss, runs the registrations declared under a new `pyproject.toml` entry-point group
through `aragora.utils.declared_registrations.DeclaredRegistrations`, then raises a `RuntimeError` subclass if the slot
is still empty.

## Changes

- `aragora/debate/decision_plan_bridges.py` (new; group `aragora.decision_plan_bridges`):
  `register_decision_plan_bridge_factory`, `create_decision_plan_bridge`, `DecisionPlanBridgeNotRegisteredError`.
- `aragora/integrations/decision_bridge_registration.py` (new): `build_decision_bridge()` builds
  `aragora.integrations.decision_bridge.DecisionBridge()` (looked up on the module at call time);
  `register_decision_bridge()`.
- `aragora/debate/post_debate_coordinator.py`: `_step_decision_bridge` builds the bridge with
  `create_decision_plan_bridge()`; a missing registration is handled like the failed import was (debug log, `None`).
- `pyproject.toml`: the entry-point group, after `aragora.chat_connector_lookups`.
- `scripts/baselines/import_contracts_baseline.json`: plain `--freeze` (frozen from `a01b2692b9`, the parent on main);
  the removed pair is exactly the table above, nothing added.

A new bridge is built for every plan, as before. Existing patches of
`aragora.integrations.decision_bridge.DecisionBridge` still apply; no existing test changed.

## Tests

`tests/debate/test_decision_plan_bridge_hook.py`: an unregistered bridge raises; without a bridge the step returns
`None`; the step routes each plan through a new registered bridge; empty or failing bridge results return `None`; a
miss runs the declared registrations once; `pyproject.toml` declares exactly the integrations registration; the
registration builds `DecisionBridge` with default targets and reads the class at call time; a process that imports only
the debate hook and coordinator reaches `DecisionBridge` through the declared registration (fresh interpreter,
`aragora.integrations` not preloaded); `aragora/debate` holds no import of `aragora.integrations` at any scope.

Written red first: on base `a01b2692b9` the file fails at collection (the hook module does not exist) and the old site
imports `aragora.integrations.decision_bridge` at `aragora/debate/post_debate_coordinator.py:1260`.

## Verification (worktree at head, base `a01b2692b9`)

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `scope` | 297 changed lines including the baseline (6 files), <= 800 |
| `lint_changed`, `lint` (ruff check + format --check) | ok |
| `typecheck_changed` | mypy: no issues in 3 source files |
| `typecheck` (`mypy_with_baseline`) | new 37 <= 189, no changed file with new errors |
| `scripts/ci/check_import_contracts.py --json` against main's baseline | ok, 0 new, resolved exactly `aragora.debate -> aragora.integrations` |
| `scripts/ci/check_import_contracts.py` after `--freeze` | baseline holds 38 (was 39) |
| `scripts/ci/measure_import_graph.py --check` | 138 <= 140 |
| `scripts/regenerate_module_tiers.py --check` | no tier drift |
| smoke junit | 62 passed, floor 62 |
| red on base `a01b2692b9` (the test file copied in) | 1 collection error |
| green at head | 11 passed |
| scoped suite: the 32 test files that reference the coordinator or the decision bridge | 796 passed, 1 failed |
| `tests/ci` contract, membership and shims tests, `tests/utils/test_declared_registrations_source.py`, the four hook test files | 544 passed, 1 skipped |

The one scoped failure, `tests/integration/test_e2e_value_chain.py::TestFailurePaths::test_receipt_from_debate_result_no_consensus`
(`assert 'NO_EVIDENCE' == 'FAIL'`), fails the same way on base `a01b2692b9`; it concerns receipt verdicts, not this
change.

## Overlap

- `aragora/debate/post_debate_coordinator.py` is also listed by #10623 (`rf/m5-mound-debate-org-stamp`, draft). Its hunks
  are the constructor and `_step_ingest_outcome`; this PR changes the import block and `_step_decision_bridge`. No shared
  hunk.
- `scripts/baselines/import_contracts_baseline.json` is also listed by #10603 (`se2/m4-cli-review-seam-tier4`, a parked

- `pyproject.toml` is listed by foreign open PRs #10560, the readiness stack (#9997, #10005, #10027, #10049, #10052,

## Tier

Classifier tier 2 (no Tier 3/4 path, no authority-prefix or `review_queue` closure file). Merge after the exact-head
review gate.

Both families passed at the exact head (Claude through the `max-07` profile, because the default CLI hit its weekly
usage limit; OpenAI with no findings). Claude raised one P3: when `aragora.integrations` cannot be imported, the first
bridge lookup now logs one WARNING from `DeclaredRegistrations` before the coordinator's existing DEBUG line, where the

author: unak
body:
### Summary
This PR implements **Thunk Value Type Determination** and updates the documentation in `README.md` to reflect the refined dictionary typing and lazy evaluation semantics.

### Changes
- **Constant Literal WHNF**:
  - Added `evalLiteral` to evaluate scalar literals (`IntLit`, `FloatLit`, `StringLit`, `BoolLit`, `NilLit`, and negated numeric literals) eagerly to concrete values in WHNF.
  - Dict elements, tuple items, and variable bindings with literal expressions avoid creating lazy thunks.
- **Inferred Type Propagation**:
  - `types.Inferencer` now preserves AST expression types in `ExprTypes`.
  - Propagated inferred types to `Thunk.InferredType` when thunks are created.
  - Linked the inferencer between CLI/runner and evaluator.
- **Non-Forcing Type Check & Pattern Matching**:
  - `checkValueMatchesType` inspects `thunk.InferredType`. Incompatible types return `false` early without forcing evaluation or triggering deferred errors (e.g., `1 / 0`).
  - Compatible or dynamic `Any` values remain unforced to preserve laziness.
  - Added runtime tuple type checking support `(T1, T2, ...)`.
- **Documentation (`README.md`)**:
  - Documented strictly typed dictionary keys (`DictKey`).
  - Clarified WHNF evaluation for constant literals.
  - Updated the NOTE on `expr is {K: V}` to explain literal WHNF checks, inferred type propagation without forcing, and lazy dynamic behavior.
- **Tests**:
  - Added comprehensive test suite `TestThunkTypeDetermination` in `pkg/eval/eval_test.go`.

### Verification
- `go test -count=1 ./...` passed cleanly.

author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

A failing Bash or edit tool call fires `PostToolUseFailure`, while ruflo-core only registered `PostToolUse`. As a result, `hooks post-command` and `hooks post-edit` never see those failures and downstream command/edit learning is biased toward successes. This fixes #4127.

## Change

Register the failure event for Bash and Write/Edit/MultiEdit, reusing the existing cross-platform shim. The shim records `success: false` for failure events, extracts a numeric Bash exit status from Claude Code's documented `Exit code N` first line, and uses status 1 when no numeric code is available. It does not persist the raw error text. The existing successful-tool behavior and the mod ownership/deduplication handoff are preserved.

## Verification

- Reproduced the missing failure hook before the change (`No PostToolUseFailure hook with matcher=Bash`).
- Plugin hook smoke against a locally built CLI: **34/34 pass**, including exact argv checks for Bash failure with and without a numeric exit code, failed edit, and successful edit.
- `node --check` for both changed scripts; JSON parse of `hooks.json`; `git diff --check`.

The plugin smoke is configured in `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` for Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows; GitHub CI will verify those environments for this PR.

author: google-labs-stitch[bot]
body:
## Summary
This pull request introduces pre-allocated persistent `TypedArray` buffer pooling for back-to-front depth sorting in the 3D Gaussian Splatting engine (`GaussianSplatRenderer`).

### Problem
Previously, on every depth sorting pass / frame update during camera movement, `sortSplats()` allocated new `Float32Array` and `Int32Array` instances for distances, indices, sorted positions, sorted scales, sorted colors, and sorted rotations. For scenes with thousands of splat points, this generated hundreds of kilobytes to megabytes of temporary array garbage per second, causing memory thrashing and GC micro-stalls during interactive camera navigation.

### Solution
1. **Persistent Buffer Pool**: Allocated persistent `distances`, `indices`, `sortedPos`, `sortedScales`, `sortedColors`, and `sortedRotations` instance properties on `GaussianSplatRenderer`.
2. **Dynamic Buffer Resizing**: Implemented `ensureBufferCapacity(count)` which resizes persistent buffers when loading datasets with different splat counts (handling expansion for larger scenes and scaling down for smaller datasets without retaining unneeded excess memory).
3. **Allocation-free Sorting & Updates**:
   - Recycled a persistent comparator `this._sortComparator = (a, b) => this.distances[b] - this.distances[a]` to prevent allocating inline arrow functions during sorting.
   - Mutated geometry attributes directly via `.set()` from persistent scratch arrays.
4. **Render Loop Integration**: Integrated `sortSplats()` into `render()` to maintain depth sorting as the camera navigates smoothly.

## Visual Verification Screenshots
![Peoria Splat Desktop](https://github.com/Kaleaon/desktopscape/blob/stitch/pr-assets/pr-assets/89ae685b-48aa-412c-af41-d8c6ee295079/peoria_splat_desktop.png?raw=true)

## Verification Results

Closes #51

## Problem

Chat-only mode (the default) runs the CLI with `HOME` set to a temp dir. macOS finds the login keychain at `$HOME/Library/Keychains`, so the CLI could not read its saved login ("Not logged in") or save a token from `CURSOR_API_KEY` (`security` exit 154, keychain popup).

```
$ HOME=$(mktemp -d) security default-keychain
security: SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found.
```

Separately, when the ACP child exited before answering, the proxy logged `Cursor CLI failed (exit 1):` with nothing after it, because the CLI prints those errors as plain text on stdout and the exit resolved before any message was recorded.

## Changes

- `workspace.ts`: on macOS, link the real `~/Library/Keychains` into the temp home. Rules and config stay isolated; cleanup removes only the link.
- `acp-client.ts`: keep non-JSON stdout lines and, on an early non-zero exit, add them plus "ACP child exited with code N before responding" to the error. Also report a missing `sessionId` from `session/new`.
- README note on the keychain link.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the keychain link (including that cleanup keeps the target) and for early ACP exits in sync and stream mode. Full suite: 327 passed.
- End to end on macOS without an account pool, chat-only on: `main` fails with `Authentication required`; this branch returns `OK` in both CLI and ACP mode.

body: ## O problema Ao buscar um território no cartão **Territórios** (ex.: "Kiriri") e escolher na lista, o mapa vai até ele e o campo de busca fica vazio. Depois de arrastar o mapa ou fechar o cartão, não sobra nada na tela dizendo qual território a pessoa tinha escolhido — e ela pode esquecer. ## O que muda O território escolhido fica fixo no próprio cartão de Territórios (canto inferior direito do mapa), logo abaixo do título, **inclusive com o cartão fechado**: - aparece com a cor da camada, o nome e "camada · município · UF" — igual ao item da lista de busca; - **clicar no nome** leva o mapa de volta até o território; - o **×** desmarca (o mapa fica onde está); - escolher outro território na busca troca o que está marcado. Vale para **Monitoramento** e **Priorização**, que usam o mesmo cartão. ## Casos de uso | Caso | Antes | Agora | |---|---|---| | Buscar "Kiriri" e escolher | Mapa vai até lá; nenhum nome fica na tela | Mapa vai até lá e "Kiriri" fica no cartão | | Arrastar o mapa ou fechar o cartão depois | Não dá para saber o que tinha sido escolhido | O nome continua visível no cartão fechado | | Voltar ao território depois de navegar | Digitar e buscar de novo | Um clique no nome | | Não querer mais o território marcado | — | Clicar no × | ## Prints **Antes** — território escolhido: nada no cartão diz qual é **Antes** — depois de arrastar o mapa e fechar o cartão **Agora** — território escolhido aparece no cartão **Agora** — com o mapa arrastado e o cartão fechado, o nome continua ali **Agora** — clicar no nome leva o mapa de volta ao território ## O que não muda - A busca em si (lista, filtro por camada ligada, teclado) continua igual. - Desmarcar não mexe no mapa nem nas camadas ligadas. - O território escolhido não é salvo: ao recarregar a página, some — como a própria busca. ## Validação - `npx tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` nos arquivos alterados e `vitest --project unit` (2029 testes passando), com teste novo para o cartão fechado, o clique no nome e o ×. - Conferido na plataforma com login, buscando "Kiriri" no Monitoramento (prints acima). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## #665 — Validación de tipos de ejemplos sobre el inventario #959

**PR complementario apilado sobre #959**, no una implementación paralela ni reemplazo de `main`. El catálogo actual de #959 clasificaba booleanos, enteros, números, URLs y enums, pero el checker solo validaba la pertenencia del tipo al schema, no el valor de las plantillas. Un `PORT=not-a-number`, un `NODE_ENV=production-preview` o un `HIPICO_LAB_SEND_ENABLED=enabled` podían pasar si no había `safeSample` específico.

Commit `d150becc34809299ec7a58aa9b0eb14107ddbba1`, basado en HEAD `5c427ff26bf2c0b18434cc4e01cd5bd07eea31b8` de #959 (tras el fix de guardia pública y test correspondiente). author: hemna
body:
Adds a disabled-by-default switch (`type_seeds.premium.enabled`) that appends a `premium` volume type to the `cinder-type-seed` OpenstackSeed CR.

The seeded type mirrors the manually-managed premium type in KVM/NFS regions:

- `is_public: true`
- `description: premium_ssd(kvm)`
- extra_specs: `provisioning:type=thin`, `quality_type=premium`, `storage_protocol=NFS`
- no `volume_backend_name` (scheduling uses the `quality_type` capability published in backend extra_capabilities)

Regions opt in via their region values, e.g. `secrets/<region>/values/cinder.yaml`:

```yaml
type_seeds:
  premium:
    enabled: true
```

Verified with helm template: with the default (off) the rendered CR is byte-identical to current master output; with the flag on the diff is exactly the premium entry.

Note for reviewers: enabling in a region where the type already exists is expected to be a no-op for extra_specs (the seeder's volume-type handler only sets extra specs at creation time); enabling may align description/is_public to the chart values.

author: taipanbox
body:
## What

A cost decision can now be announced before it lands, so the anomaly detector judges its days against the announced step instead of raising the crew's own optimisation as an anomaly, and the forecast carries the step before it happens.

- **`driver.announced`**, a new decision class: service, window, signed expected change per day, optional team. Analyst roles (optimizer, optimizer-onprem, ai-spend-analyst, forecaster) propose it; only the **owner** applies it. No role decides it alone, and the apply path checks it again.
- **Detector:** for a day inside an announced window, history before the start is shifted by the announced amount, and the day is judged by the existing rule (3.5 robust deviations, at least $50). A miss is raised with the decision's name, the day's amount and the expected level. A real spike inside the window is still raised. A fall up to 7 days early keeps its finding and gains a hint.
- **Teams:** a service-level step is split across the desk's teams by each team's median spend over the 28 days before the start (integer cents, summing exactly to the step). A named team takes the whole step.
- **Bound:** a saving larger than the median daily spend it is a saving of is refused at save and at apply, with the reason. An increase is not bounded. The window is anchored on the latest landed day when the start lies beyond the data.
- **Forecast:** a window that has not landed yet is its own line (`daily_cents` times its days in the month); once a day lands, the measured rate wins. After close, each decision shows announced against measured; a missed month ranks the furthest decision first.
- **Pages:** the decision page shows announced, measured, the per-team split, and how many days before or after the start the owner answered.
- `drivers` gains two nullable columns (`expected_daily_cents`, `team`), added idempotently; rows from earlier versions read NULL and behave as before.

## Proof

- **Live run** on the generated estate, one EC2 decision applied through the owner's answer: announcing what was actually measured (-109.60/day) raises **0** new findings on the four EC2 team series; announcing -300/day raises **4**, each named after the decision. An over-bound saving is refused at the owner's apply with its reason.
- Red first for every new test, logs kept. **16 mutants**, each caught by a named test (shift removed, sign flipped, treated as recurring, supervisor decides alone, forecast ignores unlanded days, drivers not summed, early hint suppresses, NULL read as 0, rule text arithmetic, whole step to every team, remainder dropped, named team split anyway, bound removed, mean instead of median, anchor back on start, team dropped at apply).
- `features/an-announced-decision-is-not-an-anomaly.feature`: 14 scenarios, each bound. Invariant 96.
- `go test ./...` (1577 tests, 31 packages), gofmt, vet, features-are-bound (568 scenarios), roles-are-bound (36 classes), parity, govulncheck: clean. `gates-have-teeth.sh`: 522 of 522. staticcheck runs in CI only.

## Not proven

- Detection quality and forecast accuracy on real spend: the estate is generated.
- The 7-day early-hint window is a guess until real decisions are read.
- Split shares use all days, while the detector judges weekdays and weekends separately.

Adds the RC-1 race family's delay study: `packages/umami-fixture-rc1/host/race-delay-study.sh` runs the concurrent double-spend check inside a race kit image at several Toxiproxy latencies, checking the proxy before and after every round, and `packages/umami-fixture-rc1/evidence/rc-1-race-study.json` records the results.

Result on a native arm64 build (20 planted and 20 clean rounds per delay):

| Delay | Planted double spend | Clean false positives |
|---|---|---|
| 0 ms | 9/20 | 0/20 |
| 25 ms | 20/20 | 0/20 |
| 50 ms | 20/20 | 0/20 |
| 100 ms | 20/20 | 0/20 |
| 200 ms | 20/20 | 0/20 |

The smallest delay that gives 20/20 planted and 0/20 clean is 25 ms; 50 ms leaves more margin. The clean copy never double-spends at any delay. author: dragonire9
body: Resolves #19247 ### Problem After initiating a conversation merge, the involved rows stay in `mergingConversationIds` ("Merging…") indefinitely if the `merge_completed` push notification is never delivered to the running app (e.g. notifications disabled, missed push, or delivered in the background isolate which does not broadcast to the UI isolate). While merging, rows cannot be selected, opened, or swiped, and pull-to-refresh does not clear the merging state until the entire app is restarted. ### Solution 1. Added `watchMerge(List ids)` in `ConversationProvider` which periodically probes the involved conversations via `_conversationLifecycleFetcher` every `mergeProbeInterval` (4s) bounded by `mergeProbeLimit` (3 minutes). 2. When the server completes the merge (one survivor remains and neither is still in an active processing status), `onMergeCompleted` is invoked with the surviving conversation, settling the rows seamlessly. 3. If the FCM push arrives first, `_mergeWatchers` cancels probing immediately. 4. If the bounded deadline expires or the result is locked/unreadable, the rows are cleared from `mergingConversationIds` and handed back to a list refresh (`forceRefreshConversations()`), ensuring rows never remain stuck on "Merging…". 5. Properly clean up `_mergeWatchers` timers in `clearUserData()` and `dispose()`. ### Verification Added 5 comprehensive unit tests in `app/test/providers/conversation_provider_merge_watch_test.dart`: - Settles rows once server finishes merge without push - Network hiccup is not mistaken for a finished merge - Push settling first cancels the probe watcher - Locked/unreadable result hands rows back to list refresh - Timed out merge hands rows back to list refresh after limit Failure-Class: none UI-Evidence: none Line-Count-Exception: app/lib/providers/conversation_provider.dart | 2098 -> 2201 | watch merge completion asynchronously until server finishes merge

author: dkiesow
body:
## Summary

"Touchdown Publications ... purchased the Savannah Reporter on Oct. 9" in the December 2002 issue of Missouri Press News was offered as "by December 2002", because a date with no four-digit year was read as no date. A candidate now carries the date the page gives, read against its issue, and the note says "on October 9, 2002" and quotes the sentence that says it.

## Changes

- `history_event_candidate` gains `date`, `date_precision` (day, month, year) and `date_stated` (the page's words), migration 0019. The reading resolves dates against the issue:
  - "Oct. 9" in the December 2002 issue is 2002-10-09.
  - "last month" is the month before the issue.
  - "125 years ago", or a founding's "125th anniversary", is the issue's year less 125.
  - A month and day with no year fall in the year nearest the issue, at most two months after it.
  - A year merely present in the quote is no longer the event's date. It was usually someone else's ("owned by the Dorsey family since 1919"; "the Rays, who bought the paper in 1996, sold it to Touchdown").
- Proposed event and note:
  - The proposed event takes that date at its precision.
  - The note's sentence reads "on October 9, 2002" or "in October 2002".
  - The excerpt reaches the sentence holding the page's own date words.
- A quote the model shortened with "..." is found piece by piece, so the whole sentence is marked and quoted. Quotes found in their passages: 5,683 → 6,267 of 6,529.
- On accept:
  - A note left as offered is rewritten from what is recorded. Event 166 kept "in 1996" over a date corrected to Oct. 9, 2002.
  - A note the reviewer wrote stands.
- `import_history_event_candidates --refresh`:
  - Waiting candidates take a later reading's values, new readings are added, and waiting ones it no longer holds are removed.
  - Decided candidates are never changed, and a new reading of an event already decided is not added again; the command names each one held back.
- `docs/OUTLET_EVENTS.md` updated.

## Verification

- `tests/test_press_history_review.py`: the Savannah paragraph end to end, month precision, date words in another sentence, bad dates, note rewrite vs. reviewer's note, and every refresh path. `visuals/press_history.py` and the command at 100% coverage.
- Real reading (6,529 events) refreshed into a local copy: 6,308 updated, 221 added, 36 removed; Savannah note checked.
- Pre-push hook (`make check`) passed.

body:
Stacked on #7.

## Multiplayer
- Rooms hold 2 to 5 racers. Start unlocks at 2, and the button shows the count.
- Five-lane road with lanes picked by racer count. Five starter paints, so everyone gets a distinct car.
- When the first racer finishes, the rest get 15s to cross the line. Places decide XP: +50 / +25 / +10 for the podium, nothing for last.
- A racer leaving mid-race is parked and marked out. The race ends early only when fewer than two remain.

## Spectating
- **Live races** tab with a count badge. It lists rooms with status, each racer's live progress and the spectator count. It polls every second while open and every 5s otherwise.
- Watch link `/?watch=CODE`, copyable by players (room panel) and spectators (spectate bar). It needs no name.
- Spectator count with an eye icon, visible to everyone in the room panel and the race HUD.
- Spectators follow the leader, or select a row in the position tower (mouse or keyboard) to follow a racer. No XP and no rematch button, and they move back to the room when a rematch starts.

## HUD
- Progress strip with every racer as an initial marker (yours ringed), plus a finish flag.
- Position tower with sliding reorders on overtakes, gap in metres to you, and finished or out states.
- Speed and WPM bottom left, place bottom right, and a "You finished 2nd · results in 12s" banner while you wait.

## Colors and polish (repo skills)
- **better-colors**: rebuilt as neutral and accent ramps plus semantic role tokens. Every text pair was measured with APCA. Before, body text was Lc 53, hints Lc 24 and untyped words Lc 12. Now body is Lc 79, hints Lc 61, untyped words Lc 62, and wrong letters Lc 63.
- Solid accent instead of the gradient on the logo, buttons, badges and XP bars. The 3D scenes keep their art direction.
- **better-accessibility**: visible name label, keyboard rotation for the garage, inert background with focus moved into the results dialog, tower rows usable by keyboard when spectating.
- **better-writing**: verb-first labels ("Race again"), and errors that say how to recover.
- **better-ui / animate**: hover effects gated to fine pointers. Reduced motion keeps fades and drops movement.
- Fixed `[hidden]` being overridden by `.btn { display: inline-flex }`.

- `bun test`: 20 tests, including five-racer finish order, the grace period, leavers dropping out, and place bonuses.
- `bun run check` passes.
- Headless Chromium with the GPU, production build, 1280 and 390 wide: 3 racers plus a spectator from the watch link. Covers Start gating, spectator count on the host, the live list, follow-switching, finish banner and grace period, results for players and spectators, and rematch returning spectators to the room.

author: rwnq8
body:
Charter pillar: personal. agent_issues 2222 (companion publish stall, 89 h).

## Defect
The 21:00 UTC run of 2026-10-13 (companion_runs 5699-5731) held the analysis split on four of five drafts, at 36% to 57% analysis. The critic still rejected all five drafts. Each time, the writer had stated motives, mechanisms and reward systems as facts, for example "intended to signal toughness", "feedback loop" and "governor-legislator reward systems ... presented as facts".

The critic prune can only delete such sentences. That strips the analysis the reader asked for, and every fresh draft invented again.

## Change
On the first critic rejection for grounding or argument, one editor call rewrites each flagged sentence in place:
- An unsourced motive, cause, mechanism or likely behaviour becomes explicit reasoning.
- An unsourced event, action, payment or statement is deleted.
- Nothing new is added.

The editor runs on the writer's family, gpt-oss and then nemotron, at the critic's temperature with low reasoning. It never runs on the critic's first family, so the critic's re-read stays independent.

The edit is kept only when all of these hold:
- It passes `validatePiece` at the repair floor: names, years and figures in the sources, length floors, lede.
- It stays within 85% to 115% of the draft's length.
- It keeps its headings and its analysis line.
- The critic reads it no worse than the original.

The critic prune, the final read and the two-family fact-check follow unchanged.

## Tests
- New suite `reframe-repair.test.mjs` with 37 checks: the prompt, model choice, sampling, each refusal, and where the edit sits in the run.
- `systems-analysis.test.mjs` now accepts the editor in the temperature expression.
- All 22 companion suites pass locally.

author: juanvieiraprado99
body:
## Summary

Once closed (map click with `closeOnClick`, or the close button), an `ng-map-popup` was gone for good: changing its position only moved the removed popup.

**Research.** [mapcn's `MapPopup`](https://github.com/AnmolSaini16/mapcn/blob/main/src/registry/map.tsx) behaves the same way. Its sync effect only calls `setLngLat`, and its documented pattern is conditional rendering plus `onClose`. In Angular, though, `@if (x; as y)` keeps the view when `x` changes between truthy values, so hover and selection popups silently disappear. **The choropleth block shipped with this bug.** Reproduced in the browser: hover France shows the popup, a click hides it, and the popup stays hidden while hovering other countries.

## Changes

- **`open = model(true)`** on `ng-map-popup`. It is two-way (`[(open)]`): closing the popup writes `false`, setting `true` re-adds the **same** popup at the current position (invariant 2), and setting `false` removes it.
  - The default keeps today's behavior. A closed popup still stays closed when only its position changes (mapcn parity), so a popup following a moving object does not reopen after the user dismissed it.
- **Teardown** detaches the `close` listener before removing the popup, as mapcn does. Destroying the component no longer emits `popupClose` / `openChange` on destroyed outputs, which used to log "Unexpected emit for destroyed OutputRef".
- **Demo:**
  - The popups docs example uses `[(open)]`, and the docs explain it.
  - The hover popups (choropleth block, arcs docs) set `[closeOnClick]="false"`, since a click must not dismiss a hover tooltip.
  - The API reference, block sources and `llms.txt` are regenerated.

## Linked issue

Closes #34

## Type of change

- [x] `feat`: new feature or component (`open` model input)
- [x] `fix`: bug fix
- [ ] `docs`: documentation only
- [ ] `refactor`: no behavior change
- [ ] `perf`: performance improvement
- [ ] `test`: adding or fixing tests
- [ ] `build` / `ci`: build system or CI/CD
- [ ] `chore`: miscellaneous maintenance

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits (`type(scope): description`)
- [x] `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` pass
- [x] `npm run build:lib:prod` passes
- [x] Tests added/updated and `npm test` passes (when applicable). Ran `test:lib` (284 passed, 6 new), `test:demo` (118 passed) and `test:schematics` (28 passed). Did not run e2e locally.
- [x] Docs updated, and `npm run generate:llms` run if the public API changed
- [ ] Demo checked in both light and dark themes. Checked in light only; the change is behavioral.
- [x] Library invariants respected (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/juanvieiraprado99/ng-mapcn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#library-invariants))

## Verification in the demo (Playwright, built library)

- **Docs → Popups:** the close X closes the popup and writes `false` back (the "Show Popup" button appears). "Show Popup" reopens it. The inner "Close" button closes it again. No console errors or warnings.
- **Choropleth block:** hover United Kingdom shows the popup, a click keeps it open, and moving to France updates it. Before the fix, the click removed it.

## Pre-existing issues found while verifying (not fixed here)

- Choropleth data uses the key `'United States'`, but the feature's `NAME_LONG` is `'United States of America'`, so the US never shows data or a tooltip.
- In hover popups, `pointer-events-none` sits on the inner div, but `.maplibregl-popup-content` still captures the pointer. Moving the cursor up into the tooltip fires the layer's `mouseleave` and hides it.

author: zaewc
body:
## Summary
Adds `uv-cache`: `~/.cache/uv` or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/uv` (macOS, Linux), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\uv\\cache` (Windows), or `$UV_CACHE_DIR`, classified `tool_action` with `uv cache prune`.

## Why
uv's cache documentation says "it's never safe to modify the cache directly (e.g., by removing a file or directory)", and documents `uv cache prune` as removing "all unused cache entries and all centralized project environments". Only the tool's command may clean it (ADR-0021).

## Changes
- `crates/lumen-devkb/entries/uv-cache.json`
- `crates/lumen-devkb/src/lib.rs`

## Tests
- Validated by the existing devkb tests (rules plus JSON Schema conformance for every embedded entry).
- `cargo xtask devkb --max-age-days 180`: 5 entries, 0 stale.
- `just check` passes locally.

## Security
- No dry run: the CLI reference documents none. Note that `-n` on uv means `--no-cache`, not a dry run, so none is recorded.
- `uv cache prune` also removes centralized project environments, which uv recreates as needed; it is irreversible and labelled so (ADR-0021).
- uv hard-links or clones from the cache into environments, so reclaim must be measured before and after, not estimated from the cache size.
- Sources: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/cache/, https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-cache-prune.

## Risks
Low. Data only.

## Follow-up
- Further entries, one per PR.

`sw.js` em `personal-v10`; documentado em `public/README.md`.

## Por que
O rodapé do iPhone (PR nº 11) continua terminando antes do fim da tela: a captura depois do ajuste é idêntica à anterior. Pelas medidas, a faixa vazia tem ~47 pt (a altura da barra de status), o que sugere que o iPhone entrega à página uma área menor que a tela, ou que o app ainda está na versão velha. Em vez de adivinhar de novo, o diagnóstico mostra os números reais.

## Como foi testado
- Navegador do app: com 4 toques não abre, com 5 abre, tocar fecha. `node --test`: 167 passando.

## Para quem revisa
- Só adiciona uma função e um estilo; nada muda no uso normal. O painel do emulador não tem tamanho de tela, então os números só fazem sentido no iPhone.
- Depois do deploy: atualizar o app, tocar 5 vezes no título e mandar uma captura do quadro.

author: jkorous-apple
body:
A source transformation writes a SARIF report for each translation unit. Add a tool that merges the reports of the translation units of a link unit into one, the way clang-ssaf-src-edit-merge merges their edits.

Each report numbers its rules and artifacts on its own, so the tool renumbers every result against the merged run before it drops the ones that are identical, such as a finding in a header that several translation units include. clang lists a run's artifacts in URI order but numbers them in the order it first refers to them, so an artifact is known by its own index. The inputs must come from the same transformation, and a merged report can be merged again.

## Summary
This is the status section of TheZacillac/seer#189.

- **Generic status labels:** the old if-chain is now a `STATUS_LABELS` table. I added `Statut` (`.ga`, `.sn`), `Domain state` (`.md`) and `domaintype` (`.lu`).
- **`.kg`:** the status comes after the domain name, as in `Domain NIC.KG (ACTIVE)`.
- **`.kr` / `.한국`:** the KISA parser never read status. It now reads `Domain Status` from the English section, or `등록정보 보호` when the reply is Korean-only. The duplicate codes from the two sections are merged.
- **HTML entities:** these are now decoded in field and status values, covering named accented Latin letters and numeric `é` / `é`. `.tg` showed `Activé`. Unknown entities and a bare `&` are left alone.

## Verification
- **Corpus re-parse:** I re-parsed all 173 saved ccTLD replies before and after. Only these 7 status lists changed. The entity decoding changed nothing else in the corpus.
- **Live sweep:**
  - All 7 now report a status.
  - `.kr` and `.sn` match RDAP.
  - `.kg` and `.md` stay `partial` only because their replies have no registrar at all.
- **Tests:**
  - every new label, plus the `.kg` line with and without a status in parentheses

  - KISA status from both sections and from a Korean-only reply
- **Local checks:** fmt, clippy (default / no-default-features / otel), workspace tests and rustdoc all pass.

## Noted, not changed
`.md`'s registrant ends in `CIBERNETICÃÂ`, which is garbled text. I fetched the raw bytes: the registry sends text that was already converted to UTF-8 twice, and seer decodes those bytes correctly. "Repairing" it would mean guessing at the registry's data, so it is shown as sent.

body:
OnJoin used one global marker and never cleared it on disconnect. Two datapacks could suppress each other's callbacks, and reconnecting players received no event until reload.

Resolve joins through Sand's existing player lifecycle using namespace-owned leave-game and retained-baseline objectives. Initialize player State first, commit join state before callbacks, and dispatch handlers in stable path order before owned observation sampling. Reload resets only the owning pack's baseline, including offline players. Keep the legacy marker untouched for other packs.

Reuse private helper/objective collision checks and reject lifecycle declarations that claim private scores even with the same criterion. Update public Rustdoc, API context, the book and the generated project template to explain tick-observed reconnect semantics.

Add real exporter fixtures for independent namespaces, deterministic/concurrent exports, resource collisions and State/observation ordering. Add a live two-pack audit with two passive players, real reconnects while another player stays online, absent/retained statistics, callback reentry and selective/global reloads. The shared client harness retains separate session logs and waits for fresh join messages.

Closes #438.

Validation: the join export regression fails against the previous backend and passes with this change. Four focused export tests and 56 surrounding transition/State/observation tests pass; 13 Python tests pass. The complete Cargo-exported two-pack Minecraft 26.2 audit passes real reconnects, retained/absent statistics, callback reentry, selective/global reloads and legacy-marker coexistence. A separate real disconnect probe confirms vanilla’s leave-game statistic behavior. Formatting, documentation links and whitespace pass. The initial fixture compile and counter-name parser mistakes are corrected; no production assertion was weakened.

Rebased onto merged #437, preserving both live CI steps. Full scripts/check.sh, git diff --check and every hosted CI check pass at 21c567c. Codex completed its final-head review without findings.
