author: uditdewan
body:
Fixes #18985

## Problem

The aarch64 base repo publishes four `noarch` packages that come from SRPMs with `ExclusiveArch: x86_64` and depend on packages that exist only on x86_64:

| Package | Unresolved on aarch64 |
| --- | --- |
| `syslinux-nonlinux` | `syslinux` |
| `syslinux-extlinux-nonlinux` | `syslinux` |
| `rocm-rpm-macros-modules` | `rocm-llvm-filesystem` |
| `python3-tensile-devel` | `hipcc`, `rocminfo` |

rpm does not store `ExclusiveArch` in binary headers, and our publishing copies every `noarch` RPM into every arch repo, so all four fail `dnf repoclosure` on aarch64. Fedora avoids this because Pungi reads the SRPM's `ExclusiveArch`.

## Change

This uses the same workaround as `vmaf-models` (#16743): drop `BuildArch: noarch` so the packages are built as x86_64 packages and published only next to their dependencies.

- **syslinux**: new overlay file removes `BuildArch: noarch` from the `nonlinux` and `extlinux-nonlinux` subpackages. syslinux uses `release.calculation = "manual"`, so the existing release-bump overlay now goes to `0.35` to avoid an NVR collision with the published `0.34` build. `syslinux-tftpboot` stays `noarch` because it has no x86_64-only dependencies.
- **rocm-rpm-macros**, **python-tensile**: `BuildArch` is on the main package, so the whole build becomes x86_64. Both are moved from inline `components.toml` entries to dedicated `comp.toml` files with one overlay file each. python-tensile is pure Python, so the overlay also sets `debug_package %{nil}` to avoid an empty `debugsourcefiles.list`. rocm-rpm-macros already disables debuginfo.
- Refreshed locks and rendered specs.

Every consumer of these packages is already x86_64-only (`ExclusiveArch: x86_64` or `%ifarch x86_64` / `%bcond rocm` guards), including `kiwi-systemdeps-iso-media`'s `Requires: syslinux-nonlinux`, so nothing built on aarch64 loses a dependency. Each overlay carries a note to drop it once publishing honors the SRPM's `ExclusiveArch` for noarch packages.

## Verification

Run in the `azldev-runner` container from `.github/workflows/containers/` at the pinned `.azldev-version`:

- `azldev comp update` + `azldev comp render` for the three components. The only spec changes are the removed `BuildArch` lines, the `debug_package` line, and the release bumps (syslinux `0.35`, others `5`).
- `azldev comp build -p syslinux`, `-p rocm-rpm-macros`, `-p python-tensile` all succeed.
- `rpm -qp --qf '%{ARCH}'` gives `x86_64` for `syslinux-nonlinux`, `syslinux-extlinux-nonlinux`, `rocm-rpm-macros`, `rocm-rpm-macros-modules` and `python3-tensile-devel`. `syslinux-tftpboot` is still `noarch`.
- Mock chroot smoke tests (`azldev adv mock shell --add-package ...`):
  - syslinux: `syslinux --version` and `extlinux --version` print `6.04`, and `ldlinux.c32`, `memdisk` and `mbr.bin` are present under `/usr/share/syslinux`.
  - rocm-rpm-macros: `rpm --eval '%rocm_gpu_list_default'` expands, and the modulefiles are installed.
  - python-tensile: `import Tensile, Tensile.TensileCreateLibrary` succeeds.

Not covered: an aarch64 compose plus repoclosure run. That needs the publishing pipeline.

author: davehardy20
body:
# Preserve summarization overflow shape, guard every compaction path

## Summary

A provider context-overflow failure on the summarization request was flattened to
`compact error: provider request failed`, then the identical oversized transcript was
handed to native Pi compaction, which failed the same way in a loop. Two guards:

```text
runCustomCompaction catch
  classifySummarizationFailure(error)   # before compactErrorResult() erases the shape
    context-overflow | output-cap -> { requestOverflow: true, stable reason }
    provider-error                -> unchanged generic fallback

onSessionBeforeCompact
  attempt.requestOverflow -> per-request gate, then cancelCustom() or defer
  selectedMode === null   -> guardNativeSummarizationRequest()
  native-fallback route   -> guard the deferred payload too
  generic custom failure  -> guard the final fall-back too
```

`measureSummaryRequestTokens()` builds the exact request Pi would send and throws from
the injected stream function, so transcript plus the clamped output budget are measured
before any registry, credential, transport, or network work happens. The intent-evidence
budget in `compaction-intent.ts` uses the same primitive instead of carrying its own copy.

Pi's `OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` did not match the captured local server wording, and the error
was not retryable either, so classification has to be local:

```text
prompt (300932 tokens) + max tokens (1) exceeds the context (262144)
```

Reason strings stay constant: no provider text, digits, or credentials reach telemetry or UI.

## Behaviour added

- **Overflow classification before flattening.** `context-overflow` and `output-cap` keep
  their shape; a generic provider error is unchanged (`{ result: undefined, fallbackReason:
  "compact error: provider request failed" }`, no extra keys).
- **Whole-request guard on every deferral.** Each request Pi would actually send is
  measured: the history cut with the standard output budget, and on a split turn the turn
  prefix as a separate request carrying no custom instructions or previous summary and
  reserving `floor(0.5 * reserveTokens)`. Only an individual request that cannot fit is a
  cancel; merging the slices would over-cancel because Pi never sends them as one request.
- **Effective-usage pre-filter.** The summarized cut is a subset of the live session, so
  when Pi reports the whole session fitting inside `contextWindow - reserveTokens` the
  transcript is never serialized. The verdict is cached per unchanged cut, so a permanently
  oversized session is neither re-measured nor re-notified on every attempt. The cache
  key includes each slice's content character totals, so an in-place shrink of the same
  cut re-measures instead of reusing a stale overflow verdict.
- **Transcript-driven vs evidence-driven budget rejection.** When Compact+'s merged cut
  cannot fit, the intent budget re-measures it carrying no custom instructions. A baseline
  that also cannot fit is `transcriptOverflow`: reported as `requestOverflow` with the
  context-overflow reason and gated against the payload Pi sends. Only a genuine
  evidence-driven rejection gets the intent-evidence warning.
- **Attempt-scoped duplicate suppression.** `executeCompaction()` clears
  `lastOverflowReportedEpoch` at attempt start and the coordinator re-stamps it only when it
  declines during that attempt, so an overflow reported by an earlier attempt in the same
  session cannot silence a later, unrelated failure notice.
- **Intentional asymmetry.** Compact+ sends a superset of what Pi sends, because its
  rendered instructions carry intent evidence Pi never sends. On a split turn its
  provider-confirmed overflow is re-gated against Pi's separate requests; on a
  single-slice turn it is treated as authoritative and cancels.
- **Authority gate matches Pi's real split.** The custom-path overflow is treated as
  authoritative unless Pi actually splits the payload (`isSplitTurn` **and** a non-empty
  `turnPrefixMessages`). Compact+'s own boundary preparation reports `isSplitTurn: true`
  with an empty prefix, so keying on the flag alone downgraded that cut's
  provider-confirmed overflow to a silent deferral that performed no compaction and
  emitted no warning.
- **Manual declines always explained.** Only automatic repeats of an unchanged cut are
  deduped; a manual `/compact-plus` decline always surfaces the warning.
- **Output budget clamp.** A caller-supplied `reservedOutputTokens` is clamped to
  `min(fraction * reserveTokens, model.maxTokens)`, the clamp Pi applies, so the measurement
  never models an output budget larger than the one Pi reserves.
- **Guided requests are measured, not assumed to fit.** The effective-usage fast path bounded
  the transcript only. Pi appends `customInstructions` to the summarization prompt with no
  length bound, so a guided `/compact` could skip the guard and hand Pi an oversized request.
  Any caller guidance now forces the real measurement; an unguided session that already fits
  still skips it.
- **Kill switch.** `guardNativeCompaction` (default `true`), settings key
  `"guardNativeCompaction": false`, env `COMPACT_PLUS_GUARD_NATIVE_COMPACTION=false`.
  Disables both the estimation guard and the decline of a provider-confirmed overflow.
  `/compact-plus` status emits `guard-native-compaction=on|off`.

## Evidence

- **Test-first:** each round's new tests failed before the implementation for the expected
  reason (e.g. `test/compaction-overflow-recovery.test.ts` returned `undefined` instead of
  `{ cancel: true }`; `attempt.requestOverflow` was `undefined` for a transcript-driven
  budget reject; `reservedOutputTokens` was `120000` instead of the model cap `4096`).
- **Local validation at HEAD:** full `vitest run` exit 0 in ~9s, 0 failures;
  `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `biome check src test` clean apart from one pre-existing warning in
  `src/telemetry-validation.ts` (unused import, not introduced here).
- **Network-free proof:** the measurement tests spy on `fetch` and assert it is never called;
  one case performs a real `fetch` first so the assertion is not vacuous.
- **Live Strata probe (run before merge, single approved request):** `POST /v1/chat/completions` on
  `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs` (window 262144, maxTokens 8192) with a 1,750,011-char prompt
  and `max_tokens: 1` returned HTTP 400 in 1.1s:

  ```text
  request exceeds the context window: prompt (307489 tokens) + max tokens (1) exceeds the
  context (262144); requests are never truncated. Send a smaller max_tokens (at most 0 here),
  or add "fit_max_tokens": true to the model's strata-<model>.json to shorten it to the room
  left (#545)
  ```

  `classifySummarizationFailure()` on that exact live message returns `context-overflow` with
  the stable reason `summarization request exceeded the model context window`.
- **Live estimate behaviour, same model, no provider call:** `measureSummaryRequestTokens()`
  with `reserveTokens: 16384` returned

  | transcript chars | estimated tokens | + output | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1,200,000 | 300,319 | 308,511 | cancel (over 262,144) |
  | 1,000,000 | 250,314 | 258,506 | allow |
  | 800,000 | 200,327 | 208,519 | allow |
  | 400,000 | 100,316 | 108,508 | allow |

- **Probe caveat:** the provider tokenized that repetitive prose at ~5.7 chars/token while
  `estimateTokens` assumes 4, so for prose-heavy transcripts the estimate over-counts by
  ~40% and the guard is conservative (it can cancel a request the provider would have
  accepted). Dense content such as base64 or minified JSON tokenizes the other way. The
  estimate is the same estimator Pi uses for its own `contextWindow - reserveTokens` trigger,
  so the guard trips only above the full window, not above Pi's trigger.
- **Not covered:** a full live Compact+ session end-to-end. The probe exercised the provider
  wording and the measurement primitive, not a real 300k-token chat session under the
  extension.

## Merge Danger

**Do

author: ferhatsahin
body:
## Description

The touch sizes follow the screen's density and the interface scale on touch is a fixed 1.6, so an
iPad draws phone-sized menus and controls on a far larger screen (#170).

On iOS the three touch sizes now follow the screen's short side against the 1080 px phone the
layout is drawn for (`TouchScreenRules.PhoneScale`):

- `Platform.ScreenDpi()` returns the phone's 420 dpi times that ratio, which feeds the menu scale
  and the touch control scale;
- the default interface scale on touch is 1.6 times that ratio (`Config.UiScaleTouchDefault`).

For an iPad Pro 11" (short side 1668) that gives menu scale 3.41 (was 1.39), touch control scale
1.54 (was 0.70) and interface scale 2.47 (was 1.6), so the HUD canvas is 675 high as on the phone.
`UiScaleMax` rises from 2.0 to 3.0 and `MenuScaleMax` from 2.6 to 3.6 to make room for these; the
Interface Scale slider in Settings therefore reaches 300 % on every platform.

Not changed: Android and desktop touch screens keep the density rule (`Platform.SizedByScreen` is
iOS only, since that is what I could run). An iPhone keeps its sizes, because its short side and
density grow together. A saved `ui_scale` still wins over the default.

Tested: `dotnet build Client/LibreKO.csproj` and `dotnet test Client/tests/LibreKO.Tests` pass
(2863) on macOS only; I could not run Windows or Linux. The same rule has been running on an
iPad Pro 11" in my own iOS build of an earlier revision; this branch itself has not been exported
to the device.

Closes #170

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [x] I have created automated tests for my changes. (The ratio is tested; the values that read
      the display are not reachable from the test project.)
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to any documentation.

author: louve-rg
body:
## Summary
- **Investigated first** (per dispatch's STOP-and-report step): the API already supports inventory on an option-less product end-to-end -- every `/vendor/products/:id/inventory` route treats `?variantId=` as optional, keying on `variantId: null` as a first-class case (`InventoryService#ensureProductInventory`/`resolveTarget`). The gap was entirely frontend.
- `ProductEditorManager.tsx` fetched the product-level inventory row (`inv.product`) unconditionally but only ever rendered inventory controls inside the "has options" branch, via each variant's own `VariantCard`. A product born with zero options -- true for every new product today -- had **no inventory UI at all**.
- Extracted the existing adjust/settings/per-location workflow out of `VariantCard`'s `InventoryField` into a shared `InventoryControl` component, parameterized by an endpoint query (`?variantId=<id>` or none) and a current quantity instead of a `Variant`. `VariantCard` now delegates to it, behavior-preserving. `ProductEditorManager` renders it against the product's own row when `view.options.length === 0`.
- No API changes, no new pricing/stock concepts -- reuses the exact existing endpoints and adjustment semantics.
- Also fixed a pre-existing mobile overflow in the quantity stepper (flex-1 input's default `min-width: auto` let the "+" button push past its container at 320px), inherited by the extraction but never triggered before since the one existing fixture has adopted per-location tracking and never reaches that branch. author: oncoursemail
body:
## STAR Cache-Augmented Generation experiment — opt-in only

This branch now includes **two separate and default-off features**, built around STAR's existing stable llama.cpp conversation prefix and warm-up. It targets `star/next`, not `main`; no merge, release, automatic downloading, server startup or inference speedup has been proven.

1. **Owner-approved knowledge prefix:** `star/knowledge_bank.py` loads a finite, project-scoped, versioned, SHA-verified reference manifest from private STAR app-data only when `STAR_APPROVED_KNOWLEDGE_BANKS=on`. Up to 8 reviewed sources (1,200 chars each; 5,000-char rendered cap), with explicit type/license and original text hash. It joins stable system memory through `star/desktop_core.py`, so `star/warmup.py` preloads *exactly* the same prefix used by real turns. Invalid/stale/malformed manifests fall back to normal retrieval. Test: `tests/test_knowledge_bank.py`.
2. **Experimental llama.cpp slot checkpoint:** `star/cache_banks.py` and `star/warmup.py` add opt-in KV slot save/restore on an owner-run authenticated LAN server with matching per-project/chat/model/template fingerprint and explicit owner-supplied model revision. Env: `STAR_KV_BANKS=on` and `STAR_KV_BANK_MODEL_REVISION=<immutable revision>`. The local metadata index contains no prompt text or tensor state. Test: `tests/test_cache_banks.py`.

**No full-corpus CAG**: no automatic Roblox documentation crawler, no forced 80 GB allocation, no proof of KV reuse on every llama.cpp build, no model-weight training, no new Studio privileges. A cache saves prefill, not decode speed; long reference packets still consume context. llama.cpp slot save/restore is not atomic with other clients and should **not** be enabled on shared fleets without explicit exclusive ownership/leases. A/B compare cold vs warm latency, cache_n, VRAM/RAM, successful Luau tasks and stale-source regressions before adoption.

Documentation and manual owner setup: `docs/STAR_KV_BANKS_20261013.md`. Avoid duplicating separate ongoing Best-of-N PR #270 or resource planner PR #266. Draft-only, independent security/CI review required.

_Requested by **Mads** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WxpHdHcMhkAQ7nQ13sUJNJ?thread=cmsg_01WxpHdHcMhkAQ7nQ13sUJNJ7BgqErocM77xt4X2YLMXJD)_

**Before:** an account created on first Microsoft sign-in could turn on an authenticator app but never turn it off. Asking for a reset or magic link lifted the two-step throttle. OAuth tokens were never pruned, and revoking walked them one UPDATE at a time. Thirty good sign-ins from one office address locked out the next person. Approve/reject on an already-decided signup gave an error page. Two admins could demote each other to zero admins. SMTP and off-site settings audit rows were readable by the SiteAdmin's home-org Admins. Refusing to delete a private solution's last team read as "An unexpected error occurred". The Teams empty state promised access control "soon". Seven sign-in and tenant-isolation rules had no tests.

**After:** each of those is fixed or pinned by a test that goes through the public API. The only open point is the subject index L3 asks for, which needs a migration (see below).

**How:** no migration, no new `IgnoreQueryFilters()`. L2 ends the MFA run at the user's `LastLoginAt`, not at any success row. L6 takes `SELECT 1 FROM organizations WHERE id = @org FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction that spans the count and the save. L7 files rows for types with no organisation column under no organisation. L3 adds an `OAuthTokenPruneScheduler` (a `PolledScheduler`, `DISABLE_OAUTH_TOKEN_PRUNE_SCHEDULER`, documented in README) that runs OpenIddict's own `PruneAsync`, and switches to OpenIddict's bulk `RevokeBySubjectAsync` / `RevokeAsync(subject, client)`. L1 lets a Microsoft-linked account with a fresh step-up confirm without the password; the Account page hides the password box once the session is fresh and otherwise links to the step-up.

**Verification:** `dotnet build ALDevToolbox.slnx` clean. Ran these classes, all green (216 tests): MfaEndpointTests, AccountSecurityFlowTests, OAuthClientAdminServiceTests, AccountAdministrationTests, OAuthRevocationTests, CredentialChangeRevocationTests, AuditInterceptorTests, AuditServiceTests, AdminTeamsTests, TeamServiceTests, SiteAdminRoleMetadataTests, SignupDecisionEndpointTests, AccountServiceTests, PasskeyServiceTests, CimdClientResolverTests, BulkUserActionTests, IgnoreQueryFiltersBaselineTests, ServiceRegistrationTests, ArchetypeConformanceTests, AccountTabAddressTests, StrongAuthGateEndToEndTests, StepUpEnforcementTests.

- L1: Microsoft-only accounts could not turn off TOTP or email codes or get new recovery codes. Now a fresh step-up stands in for the password on accounts with a Microsoft link.
- L2: a reset or magic-link request ended the MFA failure run. Now only a completed sign-in does.
- L3: tokens grew forever and revoke was row by row. Now there is a 6-hourly prune of dead rows older than 14 days, and revoke is one set-based UPDATE. The subject index still needs a decision.
- L4: successful sign-ins counted toward the per-IP cap. Now password sign-in counts only refusals; the mail-sending flows still count every row.
- L5: a repeated approve/reject returned a 500. Now it redirects with "This request has already been decided."
- L6: concurrent demote/disable could leave zero admins. Now both serialise on an organisation row lock.
- L7: SystemSettings/Backup audit rows were filed under the acting SiteAdmin's org. Now they are filed under no org. Existing rows are unchanged.
- L8: the last-team refusal showed a generic error. Now it shows the refusal text (L9's "project" wording is handled separately).
- L10: the empty state said "soon". Now it points to the solution's Access tab.
- T1: reset expiry and the non-Active refusal were untested. Now both are tested.
- T2: passkey completion was untested. Now it is tested with a software ES256 authenticator: success, inactive account, step-up envelope used as a sign-in, foreign user handle, replayed counter, and the step-up pairings.
- T3: the challenge throttle was untested at the endpoint. Now five wrong codes then the right one gives `too-many-attempts` on both TOTP and recovery.
- T4: the CIMD resolver was untested. Now create, refresh, client-id mismatch and refusal to rewrite DCR/admin clients are tested with a stub handler and the real manager.
- T5: nothing read endpoint metadata. Now every `/site-admin` route is checked for the SiteAdmin role, and `ResetMfaAsync` calls `RequireSiteAdmin()` (separate fix commit).
- T6: OrganizationSettings secret redaction was untested. Now there is a per-secret test plus a reflective test over every `*Encrypted` column on audited types.
- T7: the team-id pin was untested. Now there is a cross-team test for `SetManagerAsync` and `RemoveMemberAsync` as a non-admin manager.

Left out, needs a decision: the L3 subject index on `oauth_tokens` (`(subject)` or `(subject, application_id)`) needs a migration. With the bulk revoke it is now one sequential scan per revoke instead of N updates.

author: zcsizmadia
body:
Follow-up to #77: the 32 MiB download was the one benchmark where SshSharp allocated more than SSH.NET (837 KB vs 613 KB).

## How it was found
`--peak` now samples allocations by type, by counting the runtime's `GCAllocationTick` events. In a 1 GiB stream:
- **About 80%** was async state machine boxes. `ReadPacketAsync`, `SshTransport.ReceiveAsync`, `SshChannel.ReadQueueAsync` and the channel streams' `ReadAsync` complete asynchronously for almost every packet, so each allocated a new box every time.
- **Two closures** were allocated per packet, although their lambdas rarely run. Roslyn merges a block's closure scope into the enclosing method's, so the closure is created at method entry. One belonged to the window adjustment in `SshChannel.Consumed`, the other to server-opened channels in `SshConnection.Dispatch`.

## Changes
- Those methods now use `PoolingAsyncValueTaskMethodBuilder`. Every caller awaits once, which is the `ValueTask` contract; .NET's own network streams pool the same way.
- Both lambdas moved into methods of their own: `PostWindowAdjust` and `OnChannelOpen`.

## Results
Local OpenSSH, 1 GiB stream: allocations went from **25 MiB to 3 MiB**, with no GC during the transfer. That's about 90 B per 32 KiB packet, which is the designed wrappers.

EPYC 7543 lanes, same setup as #77:

| | SSH.NET | SshSharp before | SshSharp now |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Download 32 MiB, allocated | 639 KB | 837 KB | **160 KB** |
| Command, allocated | 12.1 KB | 8.2 KB | 6.3 KB |
| Streaming 4 GiB, allocated | 62 MiB | 96 MiB | **15 MiB** |
| Streaming 4 GiB, GCs (gen0/1/2) | 3/1/0 | 6/1/0 | 1/0/0 |

Timings are unchanged within noise. `docs/benchmarks.md` has the new table.

## Testing
- Unit tests pass on net8.0 and net10.0.
- Interop against a local OpenSSH passes, apart from two tests that need a key passphrase not set in that environment. CI runs the full interop suite.

## Also fixed: EOF or data after CLOSE (found by this PR's CI)
The Dropbear interop job failed once with `Exit ... EOF for unknown channel 0`. That was an older race, made more likely by the new timing:
- `SendEofAsync` and `SendDataAsync` checked `_closeSent` and then sent.
- In between, the receive loop could answer the peer's `CLOSE`.
- So `EOF` or data could follow our `CLOSE`, which is a protocol error, and Dropbear drops the connection for it.

The transport now has `SendIfAsync`. Its condition is checked under the send lock right before encoding, so the decision and the wire order can't disagree. A test covers it.

author: rossgraeber
body:
## What

The Zenoh contract harness (`transports/zenoh/tests/contract.rs`) no longer probes a port and releases it. Each medium now **claims** its loopback rendezvous port for its whole lifetime.

- The port comes from 28000..32000, below the default ephemeral ranges of Windows, macOS and Linux (49152 / 49152 / 32768). It is disjoint from `liveness_tests` (20000-27999) and `presence_registry` (23000-24099).
- The claim is an exclusive OS file lock (`std::fs::File::try_lock`) on `<temp>/oac-contract-rendezvous-<port>.lock`, held until the medium is dropped. Concurrent processes and threads never claim the same port, and the lock of a process that dies is released.
- One bind probe skips a port a foreign program holds. Nothing else binds in this range, so that probe has no window.
- Tests: `a_held_claim_excludes_every_other_handle_until_it_is_dropped` (a new handle on a held claim's lock file gets `WouldBlock`; after the drop it can lock) and, on Linux, `the_rendezvous_range_lies_below_the_linux_ephemeral_range` (reads `ip_local_port_range`, so a lowered range fails loudly). A compile-time assert keeps the range below 32768 on every platform.

No contract check, spec text or product code changed. The shared suite crate `tests/protocol/contract/transport` is untouched; it has no `free_port()`. This PR changes only the Zenoh harness, not the shared suite in `tests/protocol/contract/`.

## Why

`free_port()` bound `127.0.0.1:0`, read the port and dropped the listener. In the window before the rendezvous bound it, another socket could take the port. `PeerTransport::start` then fails with "the loopback rendezvous port N is held by a program that is not an OAC transport".

Why not `:0` for the rendezvous: Zenoh does resolve `:0` itself (the TLS listener returns the bound `local_addr`, `zenoh-link-tls-1.10.1/src/unicast.rs:428-433`), and joiners already use it. The rendezvous, however, is a fixed port every transport of a medium must be configured with before the first one starts (`transports/zenoh/src/config.rs:181-204`), and Zenoh cannot adopt a pre-bound listener. The API that reports a bound locator, `Session::info().locators()`, is `#[zenoh_macros::unstable]` (`zenoh-1.10.1/src/api/info.rs:122`) and the crate does not enable `unstable` (`transports/zenoh/Cargo.toml:22`). A `:0` rendezvous would need a product-semantics change, so I took the issue's other option, a non-ephemeral allocator, made window-free with the lock.

## Residuals

- The lock files are never deleted: each is empty, at most one per port of the range (4000), left in the temporary directory.
- A Linux host whose `ip_local_port_range` starts below 32000 is not protected; the Linux range test fails there loudly instead.
- A port the operating system excludes from binding (Windows reserved port ranges) is skipped by the bind probe.
- Other tests of the crate still probe and release ports (#393), including `liveness_tests.rs`, which this PR does not touch.

## Evidence

- Deterministic repro of the old pattern: probe `127.0.0.1:0` (got 65357, an ephemeral port), release, let a stand-in for a parallel test bind it, then `PeerTransport::start`. It returns the exact "held by a program that is not an OAC transport" error. (Scratch test, not committed.)
- Natural-rate repro on `origin/main`: 6 concurrent workers x 5 = 30 runs of the contract binary gave 0 "held by a non-OAC program" failures. The race did not occur by chance in 30 runs, so the deterministic repro is the proof of the window.
- Fix: 7 concurrent workers x 8 = 56 runs of the contract binary (Windows, commit `00ee55a`) gave 0 "held by a non-OAC program" failures. The claim code is unchanged since, apart from the test and docs.
- The `IFC-TRN-030` failures seen under stress (1 of 30 on main, 2 of 56 on this branch) lose the ~1 MiB payload ("received 1 payloads of lengths [256], sent 2 of lengths [1048422, 256]"). That is a separate load sensitivity, tracked in #392 and not touched here. Port races elsewhere in the Zenoh tests are tracked in #393.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p oac-transport-zenoh --features test-support --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `scripts/check-test-listeners.mjs` are clean on the head.

### `node scripts/local-ci.mjs` (default tier), head `91eba21`

Earlier heads: on `00ee55a` the `test-listeners` step failed on my tuple bind (fixed in `0298688`). On `0298688`, one run failed in `liveness_tests::no_loss_reaches_a_watcher_once_shutdown_has_begun` ("rendezvous port 21609 held by a program that is not an OAC transport", the probe pattern in a file this PR does not touch, #393) and the rerun passed. The runs below are on the final head.

**Windows: PASS, 39 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (Linux loopback-sandbox steps), 18m13s.**

<details><summary>Windows summary</summary>

- **`GET /api/hunt-kit` + `/api/hunt-kit/{name}`** — public, GET-only, allowlisted static files (`KIT_FILES`), cached index with sha256. No DB, no outbound call, no user data (added to `PUBLIC_ROUTES` with reasons).

author: nickmotown
body:
Running the installer a second time no longer adds the games with an apostrophe in their name (Bucky O'Hare, Chip 'n Dale, Ghosts'n Goblins) to the Celeste mode list again.

**Cause:** the installer wrote a game's file name in its gamelist entry with the apostrophe escaped (`'`). EmulationStation saves its gamelists with a plain `'`, so after you had played once, a new install no longer recognised the entry and added a second one.

**Fix:** the installer now writes names the way EmulationStation does (only `&`, `<` and `>` escaped) and recognises both spellings. A duplicate an earlier install left is moved to `roms\celeste\_quarantine\` (nothing is deleted), so the play counts on the original entry stay.

author: mauriceisrael
body:
Closes #103.

## Le bug
Pour un projet basculé sur le Hub, `POST …/subjects/{id}/decision/assert` envoyait `retained_option` (un identifiant d'option d'Archinex) ; le Hub attend `decision` (le **texte**) et répondait **400** (`'decision' is required`). La route faisait `.catch(() => null)` puis tentait d'affirmer avec l'identifiant **d'Archinex** (inconnu du Hub), et, en « mode résilient », **écrivait la décision comme affirmée en local**. Résultat : une décision montrée comme prise, jamais enregistrée au Hub, sans aucun signal. Le faux Hub du test acceptait n'importe quelle forme : il validait le bug.

## Ce qui change
- **Forme** : le Hub reçoit le texte de l'option retenue, les options écartées (`rejected: [{option, reason}]`), la justification, la réversibilité et les faits. `HubDecisionInput` est aligné sur le contrat : le compilateur attrape désormais la mauvaise forme.
- **Auteur et valideur** (règle du Hub, K16) : la décision est **proposée au nom de son auteur** (`arbiterId` → e-mail), puis **affirmée par la personne connectée** avec l'identifiant renvoyé par le Hub. Clé d'idempotence stable : un rejeu ne duplique rien et n'affirme pas deux fois.
- **Maturité** : le sujet passe à L3 dans le Hub (système d'enregistrement), pas seulement en local.
- **Aucune erreur avalée** : si le Hub refuse ou est injoignable, la route refuse avec le code et la raison du Hub et **n'écrit rien en local** (sujet à L2, pas d'événement, pas d'énoncé).
- **Vocabulaire des faits** : seconde cause, découverte en corrigeant la première. Le Hub ne reconnaît que son vocabulaire typé (`topology.dc_count` entier, `topology.mode` énumération, `data.rpo_target_s` durée…). Celui d'Archinex (`resilience_mode`, `site_count`…) n'en recoupait **aucune** clé : même avec la bonne forme, tout fait aurait été refusé. Pour un projet basculé, l'extraction (types donnés au modèle) et l'affirmation utilisent le vocabulaire du Hub, lu dans son instantané. « 2 » devient 2 quand c'est sans ambiguïté ; sinon la valeur est refusée avec sa clé (`422 FACT_VALUE`), jamais devinée.

## Vérification
- `npm run verify` : denylist, **680 tests**, `svelte-check` 0 erreur, build.
- **Contre un vrai Hub** (`tests/contract/hub-decision-live.test.ts`, 5 essais, ignorés sans `LLMOPS_LIVE_URL`) : extraction dans le vocabulaire du Hub ; l'auteur ne peut pas affirmer sa décision ; une autre personne l'affirme et l'instantané scellé du Hub porte la décision (texte, alternatives, faits typés, `@carl` → `@dan`) avec le sujet à L3 ; rejeu idempotent ; valeur non typable refusée.
- Le faux Hub de `decision-survey-card.test.ts` applique maintenant le contrat du Hub (forme, faits typés, identifiants, auto-validation) ; 3 cas de refus ajoutés (Hub qui refuse, valeur de fait non convertible, Hub injoignable) : rien n'est écrit en local.
- Avant correction, le même appel contre le vrai Hub : `400 invalid_argument « 'decision' is required »`.

## Limites
- **Attribution des faits** : ils sont inclus dans la proposition faite au nom de l'auteur, donc le Hub les lui attribue, alors que c'est la personne qui affirme qui les a cochés. La personne qui affirme couvre l'ensemble, mais l'attribution fine est perdue.
- **Auteur identifiable** : si l'auteur de la décision n'a pas d'adresse connue, ou n'est pas membre de l'engagement côté Hub, l'affirmation est refusée (`ARBITER_UNKNOWN` / refus du Hub) plutôt que d'être attribuée à un autre.
- **Repli sans modèle** : le repli par mots-clés de l'extracteur ne connaît que l'ancien vocabulaire ; pour un projet basculé, sans modèle disponible, aucun fait n'est proposé (l'humain peut en ajouter).
- Un projet **non basculé** n'est pas touché.

**Problem.** A call can miss every precompiled variant of a frame, either under `fail_on_recompile` or under the `_RefuseRecompileCallback` that an installed `torch.compiler.precompile` artifact binds. When that happens, the error dumps each entry's whole `guard_manager` tree followed by its `check_verbose` result. For a real model that message runs to megabytes, and a serving process logs it on every uncovered request. The one line that answers "why did this miss" is buried after the tree.

**Fix.** Replace the dump with one line per distinct rejection reason, each naming only the failing guard and listing which variants it rejected:

```
Failed on all 2 precompiled variant(s):
  [0] tensor 'x' size mismatch at index 0. expected 2, actual 5
  [1] tensor 'x' size mismatch at index 0. expected 3, actual 5
```

## Why it is needed

```python
import torch
from torch.compiler import precompile

def step(model, x):
    return model(x)

model = torch.nn.Linear(4, 4)
with precompile.capture(step, artifact_path="m.py", cache_path="m.cache") as cap:
    cap(model, torch.randn(2, 4))
    cap(model, torch.randn(3, 4))

# later, in a serving process
f = precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache")
f(model, torch.randn(5, 4))
# before: PrecompileError: ... Failed on the following precompiled guards:
#         TREE_GUARD_MANAGER: ...   <- every variant's full guard tree
# after:  PrecompileError: ... Failed on all 2 precompiled variant(s):
#           [0] tensor 'x' size mismatch at index 0. expected 2, actual 5
#           [1] tensor 'x' size mismatch at index 0. expected 3, actual 5
```

For an installed artifact, this message is the body of the `PrecompileError` ("no captured variant matches this call ... Dynamo reported: ..."). It is the only diagnostic a strict serving process gets when a request falls outside the capture. Even a two-variant artifact over one `nn.Linear` produced a 26 KB message, and the answer, `size mismatch at index 0. expected 2, actual 5`, sat after the tree.

Naming only the first entries is not enough either, because variants of one frame often share a first failing guard. In one capture of a large recommendation model, a resume frame inside a block had 10 variants. Entries 0-4 were block instances that own an optional submodule, and all of them reported `KeyError on self._modules[...]` against an instance without it. The variants for instances without the submodule, which were the ones expected to match, were cut off. Grouping by reason keeps the distinct reasons visible.

## How the report is built (`_precompile_no_match_message`)

- Each entry contributes the failing `verbose_code_parts` from `check_verbose`. Symbolic shape guards are installed as one lambda guard whose parts list every clause. When there are several parts and the guard manager has a `global_scope` and `closure_vars`, they are re-evaluated one at a time and only the failing clauses are named. If no single clause can be shown to fail, all parts are named.
- The clause re-evaluation loop is moved out of `get_guard_fail_reason_helper` into `guards.failing_verbose_code_parts(guard_manager, f_locals, parts, limit=..., swallow_errors=...)`, which both call. It builds the evaluation scope (`{"L": f_locals, "G": global_scope["G"], **closure_vars}`) itself, so the two callers cannot disagree on it. `get_guard_fail_reason_helper` passes `limit=1` (or `None` when recompiles are verbose) and `swallow_errors` from `is_recompiles_verbose_enabled()`, the same as before, so its output does not change. This report passes `limit=6, swallow_errors=True`, so it stops re-evaluating after one more failing clause than it shows.
- A reason names at most five clauses, followed by `... (more clauses)`. Without that limit, the all-parts fallback for a real model's shape guard would be one line of hundreds of clauses.
- Each reason goes through `guards.strip_local_scope`, as cache-entry reasons in the same error do, so `L['x']` reads as `x`.
- Entries are grouped by reason, with index ranges (`[0-4, 7] ...`). At most five distinct reasons are listed, followed by a count of the rest.
- The report is built after the call has already missed, so it must not replace that error. A guard that raises during re-evaluation is reported as `<guard check raised ...>`, using only the first line of the exception text, cut to 200 characters. A guard that passes on re-check (a racing install or a nondeterministic guard) is reported as `<matched on re-check>`.

## Tests

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `test_fail_on_recompile_error_message` (updated) | the message names `[0] isinstance(x, bool)` and contains no `TREE_GUARD_MANAGER` |
| `test_fail_on_recompile_names_the_failing_shape_clauses` | of a two-clause lambda guard, only the failing `x.size(1) == 2` is named, not `size(0)`; for a seven-clause guard where every clause fails, re-evaluation stops after six and the first five are named plus `... (more clauses)`; when every clause raises on re-evaluation (name missing from `G`), all parts are named with the same cap |
| `test_fail_on_recompile_groups_precompiled_entries_by_reason` | eight entries render exactly as `[0-4, 7]` / `[5]` / `[6] <guard check raised ValueError: boom>` (the exception's second line is dropped); a 300-character exception message is cut to 200; with seven distinct reasons, five are shown plus "... and 2 more distinct reason(s) not shown."; a seven-clause entry with no `global_scope` falls back to all parts and renders the first five plus `... (more clauses)`; an entry whose check passes renders `<matched on re-check>` |
| `test_installed_shape_guard_on_a_global_reads_the_live_module_dict` (updated) | an installed package's shape guard on a global reports `[0] 2 <= G['PKG_DYN_ROWS']...` |
| `test_a_frame_the_entry_cannot_reach_is_served_installed` (golden loader) | an installed artifact's `PrecompileError` for a dtype miss says "dtype mismatch" and contains no `TREE_GUARD_MANAGER` |

Test Plan:

```
python test/dynamo/test_misc.py -k test_fail_on_recompile
python test/dynamo/test_package.py -k test_installed_shape_guard_on_a_global_reads_the_live_module_dict
python test/test_precompile.py -k served_installed
python test/dynamo/test_recompile_ux.py
python test/dynamo/test_recompiles.py
python test/dynamo/test_logging.py -k recompile
```

author: artkruglov
body:
Fewer locks and queries on the hot paths (perf #2, #3, #5). No migration.

## What changed
- **Editorial check on every link open** (`editorial.ts`, `assertEditorialShareAccessible`): a lookup by the unique `editorial_publications.share_id` first; the 8-table publication query (≈4 ms of planning for 0.06 ms of execution, three times per recipient open) runs only for a catalogued link, unchanged. Not deduplicated per request: the call sites are in `project-viewer.ts` / view routes owned elsewhere, and after the short-circuit a repeat costs one index lookup.
- **Shares** (`shares.ts`): a new link revoked older ones with `WHERE artifact_id=$1`, a seq scan of `shares`; now `AND NOT revoked` (partial index `one_current_share`). The trash (`artifact-trash.ts`) locks a work's links by `(tenant_id, artifact_id)` (`shares_scope`) and revokes only open ones; the tenant-wide revokes in `account-deletion.ts` and `provisional-maintenance.ts` skip revoked rows too.
- **`lockShelf`** (`shelves.ts`): an agent's call locked shelf, account and membership in `service-auth` and again in the service, in every transaction. `lockShelf` now remembers, per pooled client, the pairs its current transaction (`pg_current_xact_id()`) locked; a second call in the same transaction runs **one plain read with the same conditions** (current values, the transaction's own changes included) instead of three `FOR UPDATE`s. The entry goes at commit (`afterCommit`); after a rollback the transaction id no longer matches and the next call locks for real. `SHARE` held does not satisfy `UPDATE`. `service-auth.ts` is not touched.
- **Member list** (`shelf-members.ts`): `GET /api/shelves/:id/members` only reads — one query with the same checks as `lockTeamShelf` + `lockAccounts` + `roleOf`, no row locks. It took `FOR UPDATE` on the shelf and waited behind every save on it.

## Measured
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| one agent publish (new work, `POST /api/v1/publish`) | 90 queries, 4 transactions, 37 locking selects | **82** queries, 4 transactions, **25** locking selects |
| new version of a work | 101 queries, 40 locking | 93 queries, 28 locking |
| `assertEditorialShareAccessible`, link not in the catalogue | median 10.96 ms, p95 30.6 ms | median **0.65 ms**, p95 4.3 ms |
| `UPDATE shares SET revoked=true WHERE artifact_id=…` (41k shares) | Seq Scan, 1 160 buffers | Index Scan `one_current_share`, 25 buffers |
| trash: `SELECT id FROM shares … FOR UPDATE` | Seq Scan, 1 124 buffers, 2.4 ms | Index Scan `shares_scope`, 7 buffers, 0.06 ms |
| member list while a save holds the shelf | waits for the save (70 ms avg under publish load) | does not wait (test) |

Query counts: a temporary test wrapping `pg.Client.prototype.query` around one `POST /api/v1/publish` (not committed). Each of the 4 transactions now locks the shelf/account/member rows once; what remains is one re-lock of the upload row (`agent-capture` → `uploadBundleFile`), a no-op on a row already held.

## Tests
- `tests/team-shelves.test.ts`: a second `lockShelf` in one transaction makes exactly one statement without `FOR UPDATE`, keeps the role check (403), sees the transaction's own role change and a disabled account (404); after a rollback, the next transactions on the pool lock for real again. The member list answers while another transaction holds the shelf and the account `FOR UPDATE`, and is still 404 for a stranger.
- Full default suite: 1 116 tests, all pass except the 27 `bundle-runtime`/runtime-build tests that fail locally with a symlinked `node_modules`; live suite: all pass except 6 runtime-build tests (same cause). CI is the reference. `npm run check` green.

author: teancom
body:
## Is there anything about the code changes here that should be highlighted?

I noticed the iOS PR checks were taking waaaaay longer than Android or linting (again) so I had the robot pull down the logs of the last few runs, replicate locally, and this is what it came up with.

• iOS checks now also run on pushes to `main` (previously we could have something work on a PR but break silently after merging if it wasn't rebased just before merge. This doesn't prevent that but it does make it obvious).
• PR checks restore caches but never save them. We don't want just anyone to be able to open a PR and cause a cache write.
• Only a successful `main` run saves warmed Gradle and Kotlin/Native caches.
• Simulator caches use a separate namespace from release caches. 
• Each warming run gets a unique immutable key; restores prefer matching build configuration.
• Concurrency cancels superseded runs on the same PR or `main`.
• WebRTC caching is also restore-only for PRs, with saves restricted to successful `main` runs.

author: p0mvn
body:
## Summary

Once a receipt lookup gets three bad replies at the same block height, the wallet stops asking the PIR service for that receipt. The detail view still reported this as `Unavailable`, which also means "failed, will retry". So an app could not tell when to stop polling. If it kept polling or re-prioritising the receipt, a dishonest service could watch that reaction. This change adds `TransparentDisplayView::GaveUp`, which the SQLite view returns in exactly that case. Apps can keep showing it as "Unavailable" but should stop polling it. When the wallet has public authority, or once the transaction is mined at another height, the view behaves exactly as before.

It also updates the reaction-leak design note:
- Enhance's three-strike bound is per app session (counts are kept in memory).
- `Step::Wait` is removed.
- Apps may schedule queries only on events the service already knows about, and Vizor runs transparent recovery on block cadence.
- Given-up receipts now have their own state.

The integration guide is updated to match.

## Breaking changes

- DB: None
- API: `TransparentDisplayView` has a new `GaveUp` variant, so exhaustive matches must handle it (present it as `Unavailable`, without polling or prioritising).
- Other: None

## Validation

Extended SQLite tests cover these cases: a given-up lookup reads as given up without public authority and as before under public authority; it reads as given up again when private mode returns; it goes back to the ordinary view after the transaction is mined at another height. author: ni500
body:
## Qué cambia y por qué

Los avisos que la app le manda al equipo —el **aviso de rescatista**, los
**avisos retenidos por el modo relevo** y el **respaldo de `/ideas` y `/bug`**—
iban por correo a `AVISO_EMAIL`, un buzón personal. Este PR los lleva a un
**canal privado de mantenedores en Discord**, por webhook, con **retención de 30
días**, sin un bot que mantener vivo.

- **Un solo destino** (`operatorDestination()` en `src/notify.js`): con
  `DISCORD_AVISOS_WEBHOOK_URL` el aviso va **solo** a Discord; sin ella, al
  correo, como hoy. Por eso el orden del despliegue no importa: la variable se
  puede poner antes del merge y el correo se retira después.
  Si Discord falla **no** cae al correo: un aviso con dos copias lo atienden dos
  personas. El fallo queda en la bitácora (`contact_log`, canal `relevo`,
  `fallido`) igual que hoy.
- **`src/discord.js`** publica con `?wait=true` para recibir el id del mensaje y
  lo guarda en la tabla nueva `discord_avisos` (**solo** `message_id`,
  `webhook_id` y `created_at`; ni texto ni persona). Parte los mensajes de más de
  2000 caracteres y registra cada parte. `allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }`: un
  `@everyone` escrito en el formulario no notifica a nadie. Sin vistas previas
  de enlaces.
- **Retención:** cron diario `/api/avisos/purge` (`vercel.json`) que borra lo que
  tiene más de 30 días con el mismo webhook
  (`DELETE /webhooks/{id}/{token}/messages/{id}`). Falla cerrado sin API key ni
  `CRON_SECRET`, igual que `/api/report/send`. Si alguien ya borró el mensaje a
  mano (`10008`), suelta la fila; si el webhook ya no existe (`10015`), se
  detiene **sin** soltar nada. Los mensajes de un webhook anterior no se pueden
  borrar con el nuevo: se cuentan como `orphans` para borrarlos a mano.
- **`/api/diag`** dice a dónde van hoy los avisos (`operator_destination`:
  `discord` / `email` / `null`). Nunca la URL: es una credencial.
- **WhatsApp:** la app deja de tener credenciales de WhatsApp en producción. Ya
  degradaba bien: sin `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`, `sendWhatsApp` no llama a Meta, y sin
  `WHATSAPP_RELAY_SECRET` el `POST /webhooks/whatsapp` responde 403. Este PR
  **no borra** el código del canal (otra discusión, otro PR); agrega una prueba
  que fija ese estado: sin token no sale ni una respuesta automática.
- **Docs:** `docs/avisos-de-rescatista.md`, `agent.md`, `README.md`,
  `.env.example`. Describen el estado final, con las variables de WhatsApp ya
  retiradas.

## Esto lo decide una persona

Cae en las **tres** categorías de la regla 3:

1. **Lo que pasa con un aviso:** cambia a dónde llega.
2. **Esquema:** tabla nueva `discord_avisos`, en los dos adaptadores.
3. **Privacidad:** el aviso lleva el teléfono de quien avisa y dónde dice que
   está una persona. Pasa a vivir en Discord (un tercero) con 30 días de
   retención. Quien opera la app tendría que nombrar a Discord en `/privacidad`
   como encargado. Ese texto legal no va en este PR.

Toca rutas restringidas (`src/store/`, `src/notify.js`, `src/facematch.js`,
`src/routes/api.js`, `vercel.json`). Lo aprueba un mantenedor core distinto del
autor.

**No va en este PR, y queda propuesto para quien tenga CODEOWNERS:**
- `src/discord.js` cae en el catch-all `*`, pero transporta datos de personas a
  un tercero. Conviene sumarlo a las rutas restringidas.
- Borrar los mensajes de Discord de una persona cuando se ejerce el borrado ARCO
  (`DELETE /api/people/:id`). Hoy los cubre el tope de 30 días.

## Cómo lo verificaste

- [x] `npm test` en verde: **564/564** (12 pruebas nuevas en
  `test/discord-avisos.test.js`, contra un doble local del webhook, sin red).
  Esas pruebas fijan esto:
  - con el webhook puesto, el aviso de rescatista llega a Discord con
    `wait=true`, menciones vacías y `SUPPRESS_EMBEDS`, y **0** correos salen
    aunque `AVISO_EMAIL` siga puesta;
  - sin el webhook, el correo sale como antes;
  - con Discord fallando, 0 correos y la bitácora queda en `fallido`;
  - un relevo de ~5.000 caracteres se parte en mensajes de ≤2000, sin perder la
    primera ni la última línea, y cada parte queda registrada;
  - la purga no toca nada antes de los 30 días. Pasados, borra, suelta los que
    ya no estaban, reintenta al día siguiente el que falló, reporta 1 huérfano y
    deja el canal vacío;
  - con `10015` se detiene después de **un** intento y conserva las filas;
  - `/api/avisos/purge` responde 401 sin credencial y 200 con `CRON_SECRET`, y
    ni esa respuesta ni `/api/diag` contienen la URL o el id del webhook;
  - sin `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`, dos mensajes entrantes producen **0** llamadas a Meta;
    sin `WHATSAPP_RELAY_SECRET`, 403.

## Antes de mandarlo

- [x] Es **un** cambio: a dónde llegan los avisos al equipo, y su retención
- [x] No hay datos de personas reales: nombres sintéticos ("Persona Prueba …"), teléfonos `300 000 000x`
- [x] No hay credenciales; `DISCORD_AVISOS_WEBHOOK_URL` está en `.env.example` con un valor de ejemplo

🤖 escrito por Cris, agente de IA de PappCorn, en nombre de @ni500

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Novedades**
  * Los avisos del equipo y los respaldos de `/ideas` y `/bug` se envían a un canal privado de Discord cuando está configurado; si no, se usa el correo configurado. Cada aviso se envía a un solo destino.
  * Los avisos de Discord se conservan durante 30 días y se eliminan automáticamente. Se incluye una opción protegida para ejecutar la purga manualmente.
  * Los diagnósticos muestran el destino de los avisos y el estado de su configuración.

* **Documentación**
  * Se actualizan las instrucciones sobre avisos, despliegue y disponibilidad de WhatsApp en producción.

author: gabriel-sousa99
body:
## Problema
\`composer install\`, \`artisan\` e requests em sites PHP 5.6 falham com:

\`\`\`
Parse error: syntax error, unexpected ':', expecting '{' in /usr/local/etc/lerd/dump-bridge.php on line 56
\`\`\`

## Causa
\`dump-bridge.php\` é \`auto_prepend_file\` em todo PHP do lerd e usa type hints do PHP 7 (\`: bool\`, \`?string\`). O PHP compila o arquivo inteiro antes de rodar, então uma guarda interna não protege o 5.6. \`lerd dump off\` não ajuda, porque o ini fica sempre montado.

## Mudança
- \`dump-bridge.php\` vira um stub compatível com PHP 5.3. Ele retorna se \`PHP_VERSION_ID < 70200\` e, senão, inclui \`dump-bridge-impl.php\`.
- \`dump-bridge-impl.php\` guarda a ponte real, sem mudança de lógica.
- Novo \`config.DumpsBridgeImplFile()\`. \`dumps.go\` escreve, remove e garante o arquivo novo.
- Testes: os que liam o bridge passam a ler o \`impl\`. Novo \`TestDumpBridgeStubIsPHP5Parseable\`.

## Verificação
- Lint do stub no container PHP 5.6 e \`php -d auto_prepend_file=stub\` rodando sem erro.
- Lint do \`impl\` no PHP 8.4.
- \`go test\` em \`internal/podman\`, \`config\`, \`nativephp\` e \`nginx\` passa.
- \`internal/cli\` não compilou localmente por falta de \`ayatana-appindicator3\` (cgo do systray), sem relação com a mudança.

## Fora do escopo
O Composer 2.3+ não roda em PHP 5.6. Depois deste fix, sites 5.6 precisam do Composer 2.2 LTS.

body:
Notifications, 2ᵉ partie (choix de l'auteur, 13 oct. : « le moment poussé »).

## Le moment
À l'annonce d'un succès, dans la grammaire de la pose :
1. Le sceau de cire tombe et frappe : il s'écrase, et une onde d'or part du choc.
2. Il se fend : un trait d'or s'allume le long de la fente et le sceau tremble.
3. Ses deux moitiés tombent de chaque côté en lâchant une poussière d'or.
4. Dessous paraît le médaillon du succès (son image, sinon le sceau gravé du jeu) avec un halo qui respire.
5. Le nom se déroule sur le ruban rouge (celui de la page du Sceau), puis la description monte.

C'est du CSS seul (transform, opacity, clip-path), sans filtre ni minuterie de plus. La fenêtre reste 6,5 s au lieu de 5, le temps du moment (environ 1,8 s) et de la lecture. En mouvement réduit, le sceau est déjà rompu et rien ne bouge. Les textes ne changent pas.

## Dessins
Deux pièces ajoutées au HUD (`svg/hud/`) :
- **`sceau_cire`** : le sceau de l'icône du jeu, en grand. Une cire festonnée en dégradé, un bourrelet, une empreinte en creux, l'étoile en relief, des coulures et les rubans bleus.
- **`sceau_fente`** : le trait d'or de la fente.

Les deux moitiés sont le même dessin découpé le long de la fente. Les points de la fente sont dans `hud.json` (`zones.fente`) et repris en pourcentages dans le CSS.

## Vérifications
- `npm run lint` passe.
- Les 601 tests vitest passent.
- `vite build` passe.
- `verif_generateurs.mjs` : les 16365 dessins sont identiques à la bibliothèque.
- `verif_generateur.mjs` : aucun écart.
- `clipcheck` : rien ne dépasse.
- Banc au téléphone (390 × 844), image par image, avec et sans image de succès.

author: mottopanikeiku
body:
## Summary

The `code_rl` recipe trains on DeepCoder's `taco` split, but every TACO function-call problem fails grading, correct solutions included. `taco_to_lcb_format` leaves a function-call test's arguments and expected output as Python objects, and `_normalize_tests` then stores them with `str()`, e.g. input `"['foefet', 'toffee']"` and output `"True"`. The LiveCodeBench runner (`run_test` in `lcb_utils.TEST_UTIL`) decodes a call-based test with `json.loads`, one positional argument per input line plus the output, so it raises `JSONDecodeError` before running the solution.

This PR encodes each argument and the unwrapped expected output with `json.dumps`, the format the `lcbv5` rows of the same dataset already use (e.g. input `[[7, 2, 1], [6, 4, 2]]`, output `15`). Stdin/stdout tests are unchanged.

## Impact

The `taco` train split has 7,436 rows. In six 100-row pages spread across it, 81 of 600 rows (13.5%) were function-call problems, so roughly 1,000 training problems could only ever score zero.

## How I checked

I graded the first three tests of the real `is_anagram` row with the recipe's `run_test`, in a subprocess:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First test as stored | input `"['foefet', 'toffee']"`, output `"True"` | input `"\"foefet\"\n\"toffee\""`, output `"true"` |
| Correct solution | `JSONDecodeError` | `[True, True, True]` |
| Solution that always returns `True` | `JSONDecodeError` | `[True, True, False]`, Wrong Answer |

The new `code_grading_test.py` decodes reduced TACO rows (string, integer, boolean, nested-list and non-list arguments) the way the runner does, and checks that stdin/stdout tests are unchanged. The function-call cases fail on main. `ruff` and `pyright` pass on the changed files.

author: hassan-mohiddin
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"hassan-mohiddin"} -->
_Requested by **Hassan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VedhjS8GPgqShf1JaLuJqt?thread=cmsg_01VedhjS8GPgqShf1JaLuJqtBS2cCdkdW6PrnVMZkgwmWk)_

# Pull Request

## What this does

Before: everything in the Evaluate Behavior evaluator that depends on Pi (its arguments, events, RPC sessions, isolation and login, model calls, the shell probes' launch) was spread through the core, mostly in `lib/pi.mjs`.

After: the core is host-neutral and Pi sits behind one adapter interface, so a second host can be added without touching the core. Runs, records and outputs are unchanged. This is the first of two stacked PRs; the second adds Claude Code as a host.

- **Interface and registry:** `lib/hosts/index.mjs` documents the interface (`version`, `resolveExtensions`, `refreshLogins`, `effectiveSettings`, `prepareIsolation`, `removeCredentials`, `prepareLaunch`, `runOneShot`, `runSession`, `modelCall`, `probeShell`) and maps a host name to its adapter; an unknown name is an error, never a fallback to Pi. `lib/hosts/names.mjs` lists the names a definition may use.
- **Pi adapter:** `lib/hosts/pi/` holds the moved Pi code (`process.mjs`, `rpc.mjs`, `host.mjs`, `isolation.mjs`, `model-call.mjs`) and the Pi side of the confinement probes (`confinement.mjs`).
- **Core:** `lib/pi.mjs` becomes `lib/subject.mjs` and launches through the adapter. The runner, reuse, participants, review, judge and shell modules ask the group's host for its adapter instead of calling Pi directly. `model-call.mjs` routes a judge, reviewer or simulated user to its host.
- **Docs:** the dev doc gains the "one host-neutral core, one adapter per host" decision, code map rows and a Changes entry.

## Evidence

- `npm run test:skill-eval`: 295 tests, 291 pass, 2 skipped, 2 fail. The same 2 fail on `main` in the container I ran them in (`rpc.test.mjs` "RPC cancellation ... kills resistant subject descendants" and `run.test.mjs` "forced cleanup kills subject descendants": "descendant survived cleanup"). PID 1 there does not reap zombie processes, so a killed descendant still shows as alive. They should pass on a normal machine and in CI.
- `npm run check`: passes.
- No test was changed for this PR, so the existing suite is the check that behavior did not change.

## Risk

Pi runs are the only runs this touches, and every path they take now goes through the adapter. Pi's arguments, environment variables, record shapes and the confinement record key (`pi`) are the same as before. The unchanged test suite, which covers Pi's arguments, RPC sessions, isolation, probes and judges through a fake Pi, shows this.

## Not checked

- No real Pi run: Pi is not installed in the container where this was built. Only the fake-Pi tests ran.
- The two process-cleanup tests above could not pass in that container, before or after this change.

## Changelog

Select exactly one and keep the marker comments intact:

- [ ] Consumer-visible change; I updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `## Unreleased`. <!-- changelog:consumer -->
- [x] Internal-only change; no changelog entry is needed. <!-- changelog:internal -->

The generic "Card / Visa, Mastercard" row stays only while there are no saved cards. "Add payment method" opens Add card and, when a card comes back, pops Pay with with that card selected.
- **Ride selection**: `payments()` swaps the generic Card for the saved cards (`brand: 'card:<id>'`, `name: 'Visa •••• 4242'`, `detail: 'Expires 08/28'`); `hasSavedCard` follows the store; `_brandMark` draws the Visa / Mastercard asset for `card:` brands; choosing Card with no saved card opens Add card and then continues to Set location with the new card selected. The booking body carries `paymentMethodId: card:<id>` with the card name as label; Set location's payment row, fare split and the ride card show the card name.
- **Wallet / Payments**: saved cards under "Payment methods" with a trash icon and a "Remove card?" confirm sheet (black confirm button); "Add card".

## How

- `lib/features/payments/domain/saved_card.dart` — `SavedCard{id, brand, last4, expMonth, expYear, holder}` with `displayName`, `expiryLabel`, `methodBrand`, JSON.
- `lib/features/payments/data/saved_cards_store.dart` — `PrefsSavedCardsStore` (SharedPreferences key `movera_saved_cards`, one JSON string) + `MemorySavedCardsStore` for tests. Only brand / last4 / expiry / holder are written; never the full number or CVC.
- `lib/features/payments/application/saved_cards_controller.dart` — `CardInput` (Luhn, brand detection, grouping, expiry/CVC/name rules) and `SavedCardsController` (ChangeNotifier; `load`, `list`, `add`, `remove`, `byMethodBrand`, `displayName`, `expiryLabel`). Presentation only imports this file (architecture guard stays green).
- `AppScope.savedCards` is the shared instance; `RideSelectionController` takes an optional `savedCards` and exposes `savedCardItems()`, `savedCardFor()`, `loadSavedCards()`.
- Select ride loads the saved cards before restoring the remembered default so a remembered `card:<id>` resolves.

## Tests

- `test/payments/saved_cards_controller_test.dart` — Luhn, brand detection (incl. 2221–2720 edges, Amex/Discover rejected), undecided prefixes, grouping, expiry parse/future, CVC/name, add (keeps no number/CVC), Mastercard naming, rejections, remove, SharedPreferences persistence across instances, corrupt store.
- `test/payments/pay_with_saved_cards_test.dart` — card rows with mark/expiry/radio and generic Card hidden, generic Card kept without cards, Add payment method → fill form (auto-spacing, MM/YY, live preview) → Save pops both pages with `card:<id>`, Add card rejects other brands and expired dates.
- `test/ride/saved_cards_payments_test.dart` — `payments()` includes the cards in place of Card, select by name / persist / restore `card:<id>`, removal falls back to a valid method.
- Wallet tests updated to the new form ("Add card", 4 fields, demo note).
- `flutter analyze`: no issues. Full `flutter test`: 1312 passed.

Add card filled in (4242 4242 4242 4242, 08/28, 123, Anna Berg) · Pay with showing the saved Visa selected · Set location with the card on the payment row and in the fare split. Grid attached by the owner review step.

- **Requirements** table (Bun, Python, CLIs, Claude Code version for memory).
- **Install** per provider, with what the installer copies and what it skips.
- **Parity table** for Claude, Codex and Gemini: full vs. short agent instructions, skills, delegation, memory.
- **Using the team**: ask normally, or pick an agent explicitly per runtime; Claude-only extras (context forking, agent teams, hooks) restored from the previous README.
- **Skills**, **Jev routing** (what it is, that it is optional, fallback behavior, what it does not decide), **SDK examples** (including the Python one), **routing evals**, **customizing**, **repo layout**.
- `ios-reviewer` is no longer described as plainly "read-only": it has no edit tools in Claude Code, but can run shell commands there and in Gemini; Codex runs it in a read-only sandbox.

## Qué es

El userscript **Lector Universal** pasa a vivir en `lector/`: Voceiro da los titulares y el lector se encarga de lo que pasa al abrir la noticia (modo lectura, perfil de accesibilidad, pendientes, diccionarios, lectura rápida, «Abrir en…»).

## Cambios respecto a la versión que había fuera del repo

- **Puente con Voceiro solo en su página.** Antes escuchaba en todas las webs: cualquier script de un medio podía pedirle la configuración y la lista de pendientes, o cambiar los modos.
- **Sus atajos no actúan en Voceiro**, donde Alt+P, Alt+M y Alt+B son de Voceiro. La revisión completa de atajos queda para antes de publicar en tiendas.
- **Pendientes enteros por el puente** (antes se cortaban a 50).
- **«Abrir en…»**: servicios externos configurables por cada persona, como los diccionarios, vacíos por defecto, con importar y exportar en JSON. Sin el botón de Pocket, que cerró en 2025.
- **Capa de plataforma** (`02-plataforma.js`): lo único que depende del gestor de userscripts, para hacer luego la extensión.
- **Identidad nueva**: `Lector Universal`, espacio de nombres de Voceiro y `@updateURL` en Pages (se sirve en el siguiente PR).

## Construcción y comprobaciones

- `node lector/build.mjs` concatena `lector/src/*.js` y pone la versión `2.0.N` (N = commits que tocan `lector/`).
- `lector.yml` (aparte de los tests del buscador, para no congelar el front): construye, comprueba la sintaxis y que el lector solo enlaza a los dominios de `lector/dominios-permitidos.txt`.

## Cómo probarlo

Aún no se publica en Pages (siguiente PR). Para probarlo antes: `node lector/build.mjs` e instalar `lector/dist/lector.user.js` en Violentmonkey.

author: wasumiro
body:
Fixes #163

## Problem
`sniffbt -t airtag` / `sniffbt -t flipper` panic the ESP32 (`LoadStoreError`) and reboot within ~1 s. See the linked issue for the full serial dump and repro.

## Cause
`esp32_marauder/WiFiScan.cpp` — the AirTag and Flipper sniff callbacks do:

```cpp
size_t len = advertisedDevice->getPayloadLength();   // unsigned
...
for (int i = 0; i <= len - 4; i++) {
```

When a BLE advert payload is shorter than 4 bytes, `len - 4` underflows; the loop then indexes `payLoad[i]` far out of bounds → panic.

## Change
```cpp
for (size_t i = 0; i + 4 <= len; i++) {
```
Applied in both callbacks (`BT_SCAN_AIRTAG` and `BT_SCAN_FLIPPER`).

## Testing
- Board: ESP32-2432S028R "CYD 2USB", 4 MB, board `LOLIN D32`, Minimal SPIFFS.
- Before: `sniffbt -t airtag` → panic/reboot every time.
- After: `sniffbt -t airtag` → `Started BLE Scan` … `Scan complete! Found 0 devices`, no panic.
- Same fix applied to the `ESP32-1732S019` mirror is untested (no hardware).

## Provenance note
For transparency: the patch was developed with AI coding assistance and then built and verified on real hardware before submission

author: ericwinsor-aisi
body:
RFC 6455 makes the `Upgrade` token case-insensitive. Envoy's upgrade handling and the Lua filter already treat it that way, but the WebSocket route matched the header with `exact: "websocket"`, which is case-sensitive. So a request with any other casing, such as `Upgrade: WebSocket`, missed the route and never reached the relay.

This sets `ignore_case: true` on that match, with a short comment, and adds a CHANGELOG entry.

Testing: a new e2e test sends a raw `Upgrade: WebSocket` handshake to `/ws/echo` and expects a 101 from the relay; without the fix it gets httpbun's 404. The WebSocket e2e suite passes (8/8).

Overlap with #190–#195: the gRPC stack already matches case-insensitively and has its own casing test, so if this lands first, resolve the small rebase conflict by keeping the stack's version; no coverage is lost.

author: black-hill852
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in Hermes Core Discord interaction contract for plugins. Interaction callbacks run only after the adapter's existing slash authorization gate and receive a validated context containing the Discord interaction ID, verified SDK user identity, server ID (optional for DMs), channel ID, and command name.

Responses must be explicitly routed as private or public. Private replies use the deferred ephemeral interaction response and ephemeral followups; a private transport failure raises and aborts remaining delivery, never falling back to the public channel. Public replies use the existing channel adapter only when explicitly requested. The handler never publishes content and then deletes it. Legacy plugin/text slash command registration and `!` dispatch remain on their existing path.

## Scope

- Additive plugin registration and registry API, separate from legacy commands.
- Discord adapter registration for native plugin interaction commands.
- Explicit reply/context types, strict ID validation, fail-closed private delivery.
- Isolated tests for private replies/followups, public narrative, invalid context, auth-gate ordering, private transport failure, and legacy registration separation.
- Plugin developer documentation.

No commands were registered in a live Discord application. No Gateway restart, deployment, or production data change was performed. Plugin-level authorization (including Eternia's Owner check) remains the plugin's responsibility; ephemeral visibility is not authorization.

## Verification

- `scripts/check` — passed (12 checks).
- Focused compatibility suite — 151 tests passed across interaction contract, Discord slash auth/commands, plugin registry, and ownership ledger.
- `trufflehog filesystem` over all 9 changed files — 0 findings.
- `git diff --cached --check` — clean.
- Broader Discord suite was attempted; 24 unrelated test failures hit the test home-I/O guard when imports accessed `/root/.hermes/cache/scratch/manifest.json`. This environment issue is recorded separately; the focused slash/registry suite passed.

## Review / follow-up

Please review the transport and authorization boundaries before merge. After this Core PR is accepted, Eternia can implement its slash handlers against this API while retaining its server-side Owner check; command registration and production activation require a separate release step.

author: michaelyorkpa
body:
Image-packaging patch for `v0.33.33.50`, under the new release identity `0.33.33.51`. **Do not merge before an independent Codex review approves the final candidate.** The `v0.33.33.50` tag, image, checksums, and assets are unchanged.

## Why

`v0.33.33.50` could not be deployed. Its preview deployment passed every gate before the image pull, then the host's Docker storage could not unpack the image:

```text
failed to convert whiteout file "opt/.wh.yarn-v1.22.22": … invalid argument
```

That error is in the layer that removes the base image's package managers. The deployment stopped before any change, and the preview stayed on `v0.33.32.45`. `v0.33.32.45`'s image carries no whiteout. `v0.33.33.50`'s carries nine, in two layers.

## What changes

- **One filesystem layer.** The Dockerfile's former final stage is now `runtime-filesystem`, unchanged. The published `runtime` stage is `FROM scratch` with `COPY --from=runtime-filesystem / /`. It restates the base image's `PATH`, `NODE_VERSION`, `YARN_VERSION`, and `ENTRYPOINT`, then every setting of `runtime-filesystem` in order. BuildKit adds only an empty `WORKDIR` layer.

  The runtime itself is unchanged: its files, the Debian security updates, the absence of package managers, the non-root user, and the configuration.
- **Whiteout gate.** `npm run container:build` refuses an image if any layer carries an ordinary or opaque whiteout. Image publication applies the same check to the pushed digest after pulling it. `scripts/release/image-layers.mjs` reads the layers through `docker save`.
- **Equivalence proof.** `scripts/release/runtime-image-equivalence.mjs` builds `runtime-filesystem` with the image's build arguments. It proves every file identical (type, mode, owner, link, size, content hash, and extended attributes), and every configuration field.
- **Qualification.** The native lifecycle qualification's image job:
  - runs the equivalence proof for a proposed image;
  - scans every final image's layers, with published `v0.33.33.50` as a negative control;
  - compares the final image against `v0.33.33.50`;
  - now pulls a dispatched release's candidate before inspecting it. Without that pull, the `v0.33.33.50` image job failed.
- **Policy and documentation.**
  - A narrow `0.33.33.51` checkpoint rule, without the previous patch's dependency allowance.
  - The preview deployment, release, and versioning guides.

## Host probe before this release

The probe used exactly this packaging. Scratch run [38451074740](https://github.com/michaelyorkpa/Longtail-Forge/actions/runs/38451074740) built the published `v0.33.33.50` runtime artifact through `npm run container:build`, with this branch's Dockerfile. That run:
- proved the probe equivalent to its reference stage, with 7,363 paths and the configuration identical;
- saw the build refuse an unflattened Dockerfile;
- found nine whiteouts in published `v0.33.33.50`;
- started the probe healthy in isolation;
- published it under the non-release tag `probe-single-layer-bbecda3e7400` (`sha256:961667dc…`).

The operator then pulled the probe on the affected preview host, where it unpacked. It started healthy in isolation, with no network, a read-only root, and in-memory data, and was then removed. The preview's container, image, and identity were unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Local.** One canonical `verify:slice` at `db2b71a4`, over the change set `16b2040a...HEAD`, escalated to the full gate in a disposable full-history clone. Closeout, typecheck, 5,712 unit tests, lint, and all 348 regressions, including the permission harness, passed with no retried script. `checkpoint:validate` passed for the whole range, and a disposable boot of the final tree reported `0.33.33.51` at `/api/app-info`.
- **Seeded defects.** Every one was caught:
  - thirteen in the Dockerfile's structure and restated settings;
  - three in gate placement;
  - nineteen in the layer reader and refusal;
  - twelve in the equivalence comparison;
  - six in the checkpoint rule;
  - six in the qualification workflow pins;
  - four in the documentation pins.
- **This pull request, on the exact head `db2b71a4`.** Everything passed.
  - [Development](https://github.com/michaelyorkpa/Longtail-Forge/actions/runs/38468856065): the gate, browser smoke and accessibility, the maintenance release rehearsal, and dependency review.
  - [CodeQL](https://github.com/michaelyorkpa/Longtail-Forge/actions/runs/38468856084).
  - [Native lifecycle qualification](https://github.com/michaelyorkpa/Longtail-Forge/actions/runs/38468856077):
    - **The publisher.** The real publisher, whose post-pull whiteout check now runs, published the candidate with native `13.0.3`/`3.53.4`.
    - **The lifecycles.** The preview and demo lifecycles passed.
    - **Equivalence.** 7,363 paths and the configuration were identical.
    - **Whiteouts.** The candidate and `v0.33.32.45` carry none, while the `v0.33.33.50` control carries 9.
    - **Vulnerability evidence.** It is identical to `v0.33.33.50` under the same database: 228 findings, none fixable. Both npm audits report 0, Node core advisories affect 0 of 194, and the SBOM lists 183 packages.

## Independent review

Codex reviewed `db2b71a4` and requested changes. It found three gaps: the whiteout reader could miss whiteouts that Go names differently; the equivalence check could not see hard links, device numbers, or attribute bytes; and malformed archives could pass as clean. The fixes are separate commits on top of it.
- **`e0d30615`.**
  - The reader names entries by Go's archive/tar rules, judges whiteouts by containerd's cleaned path, and refuses repeated, global, or sparse metadata, unsupported types, and broken framing.
  - The equivalence check applies each image's layers as containerd does, and compares image-owned hard-link groups, device numbers, and attribute bytes, with the export kept as a cross-check.
  - Every Codex reproduction now fails as it should; 32 unit tests and 48 seeded defects.
- **`48d76501`.** The runtime image section states exactly what the gate reads and what the proof compares.
- **`6e39197f`.** Changelog and archived-checkpoint bookkeeping.

On real images (scratch run [38478603676](https://github.com/michaelyorkpa/Longtail-Forge/actions/runs/38478603676), and this pull request's qualification run [38479397188](https://github.com/michaelyorkpa/Longtail-Forge/actions/runs/38479397188)), the reference's 9 layers and the candidate's 2 produce the same 7,357 image-owned paths, with 2 hard-link groups, no extended attributes, and no devices. One canonical `verify:slice` at `6e39197f` passed the full gate (5,723 unit tests, 348 of 348 regressions), and all checks on `6e39197f` are green. Codex re-reviewed `6e39197f`. It closed F1 and requested two changes:

- **Hard-link metadata (R1).** Hard-link headers' mode, ownership, and attributes were dropped by the model. `d4b17084` now accepts a hard link only when its header repeats its target's mode, ownership, and attribute bytes, the one case in which containerd leaves the shared file unchanged. It refuses any other, and refuses a hard link to a symlink. Every real hard link in the published layers repeats its target.
- **PAX timestamps (R2).** Out-of-range PAX timestamps passed. `d4b17084` range-checks them to 64 bits, as Go does.
- **Bookkeeping.** `eeef1c78` documents the refusal boundary, and `e31847e9` records the fixes.

Results on the final head, `e31847e9`:

- **Local.** `verify:slice` passed the full gate (5,725 unit tests, and 348 of 348 regressions with one automatic flaky recovery in an unrelated task-reminder script).
- **CI.** Every check is green. Its qualification confirms the equivalence on real images under the new rule.
- **Review.** A review of `e31847e9` is pending.

## Not in this pull request

- **Merge, promotion, and publication.** These wait for Codex approval of the final candidate and for the protected gates.
- **The supervised preview deployment.** It follows publication and t
