author: ramazangirgin
body:
Closes #85

Implemented by the developer agent from the plan [`.plans/85-login-rate-limit-lockout.md`](https://github.com/ramazangirgin/trading-analysis-platform/blob/plan/85-login-rate-limit-lockout/.plans/85-login-rate-limit-lockout.md) (model: claude-sonnet-5-5),
one work package at a time.
Draft until the agents' review → fix rounds are done; see
[the agentic development flow](https://github.com/ramazangirgin/trading-analysis-platform/blob/main/docs/agentic-development.md).

## Summary

### WP1: Lockout and unlock in the identity core

- `User`: added `withFailedLogin`, `withLoginSucceeded` and `isLockedAt`.
- `LoginLockoutPolicy` reads `platform.login.max-failed-attempts` (default 5, range 1–100) and `platform.login.lockout-duration` (default 15m, range 1 minute–24 hours). Values outside the range fail startup with the property name.
- `AuthenticationService` now follows the five cases in the plan.
  - A locked account fails with `BAD_CREDENTIALS` even with the right password. It is not counted and the lock is not extended.
  - The 5th wrong password sets the lock and resets the count to 0.
  - A success clears count and lock, and any rehash goes into the same single save.
  - A normal login writes nothing.
  - Optimistic-lock conflicts are retried up to 3 times. After that the answer is still `BAD_CREDENTIALS`.
- Added `IdentityError.USER_NOT_FOUND`, `UnlockUserUseCase` and `UserLockService`. Unlocking an unlocked user writes nothing, an unknown ID gives `USER_NOT_FOUND`, and conflicts are retried.
- Updated the `AuthenticateUseCase` Javadoc.
- Tests: `UserTest`, `AuthenticationServiceTest` (all the cases in the plan), `LoginLockoutPolicyTest`, `UserLockServiceTest`, and a round-trip test in `JpaIdentityRepositoryTest`.
- The plan's WP1 steps are ticked and its status is set to done. Everything is committed with the `Work-package: WP1` trailer.

### WP2: IP limit, unlock endpoint and configuration in the BFF

- **IP limit**: `LoginAttemptLimiter` is a sliding window of failures per client address. It takes the `Clock`, the settings are range-checked at startup, and it tracks at most 10,000 addresses (expired ones are dropped first, then the one with the oldest latest failure). `LoginRateLimitFilter` answers 429 `too_many_login_attempts` with a rounded-up `Retry-After` for a blocked address on `POST /api/auth/login`. It counts only 401 answers. It uses `getRemoteAddr()` and is registered before `CsrfFilter` in `SecurityConfig`.
- **Unlock endpoint**: `UsersApiController`, `UsersApiDelegate` and `UsersApiDelegateImpl` give `POST /api/users/{id}/unlock` → 204. `SecurityConfig` requires `user:manage` for it, so a user without it gets 403 `forbidden`.
- **Error mapping**: `USER_NOT_FOUND` → 404 `user_not_found` was already in the mapper from WP1. I only added its row to the mapper test.
- **Config**: the four `platform.login.*` properties with `PLATFORM_LOGIN_*` overrides are in `application.properties`.
- **Tests**:
  - `LoginAttemptLimiterTest` and `LoginRateLimitFilterTest` are new and pass.
  - `LoginLockoutIntegrationTest` is new. It covers the lockout with the right password, expiry, an admin unlock, 401/403/404 on the unlock, and the 429 with `Retry-After`. It uses a `@Primary` `MutableTestClock`, with `platform.login.*` set low (3 failures, 10 per address).
  - `mise run check` passes. `./gradlew :backend:bff:impl:test` passes.

### WP3: Frontend messages, API types and docs

- Added `too_many_login_attempts` and `user_not_found` to `en.json` and `tr.json`.
- Added `POST /api/users/{id}/unlock` to `artifact/frontend/openapi.json` and regenerated `schema.d.ts` with `:frontend:pnpmApiTypes`.
- Added `LoginForm.spec.ts`: a 429 `too_many_login_attempts` error renders "Too many failed logins from this address." in English and the Turkish text in `tr`. The full frontend vitest suite passes (88 tests).
- README "Login": a new paragraph on lockout and the IP limit, with the four `PLATFORM_LOGIN_*` variables (defaults and ranges); a bullet for the unlock endpoint; "or 429 `too_many_login_attempts`" on the login bullet.
- Bumped the version to 4.3.0 with `scripts/version.sh bump minor`.
- Marked WP3 done in the plan.
- `mise run check` passes. Everything is committed with trailer `Work-package: WP3`.
- I did not run `:backend:test` or `mise run runner-test`: WP3 changes no backend or ta-runner code, and the version bump only touches `gradle.properties` and `ta_runner/__init__.py`.

## Not done or done differently

**WP1**: - I added `USER_NOT_FOUND -> HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND` to `IdentityExceptionToApiExceptionMapper`. This is a WP2 item, but the exhaustive switch no longer compiled without it. WP2 should still add its test.
- Docker is not available here, so the tests that need Testcontainers PostgreSQL did not run. That covers the `JpaIdentityRepositoryTest` round trip and the `:backend:test` Spring context tests. `:backend:domain:identity:core:test` and `:backend:bff:impl:test` pass. `ArchitectureTest` and `PersistenceArchitectureTest` also have no Docker-related failure.
- I did not run `mise run check`, `:frontend:build` or `mise run runner-test`. Only `mise run format` ran, and it finished without errors.

**WP2**: - **Integration tests not run.** This sandbox has no Docker, so every Testcontainers-based test in `:backend:test` fails at context start. That includes the existing ones (52 failures, all caused by `DockerClientProviderStrategy`). `LoginLockoutIntegrationTest` is therefore compiled, formatted and Checkstyle-clean, but has not run. Run `./gradlew :backend:test` where Docker is available, and look especially at the `@Primary` test clock bean.
- **"403 without `user:manage`" test.** It uses `TestSession.loggedIn`, which creates a user with no roles. The test doesn't insert a second user through `UserRepositoryPort` itself, as the plan said.
- **Admin used for the unlock tests.** The test creates a user with the seeded `ADMIN` role through `RoleRepositoryPort`, and doesn't rely on the first-admin bootstrap.
- **Two extra package-private methods on the limiter.** `trackedAddresses()` and `isTracking()` exist only so the memory-bound test can check the table.
- **Not in this package.** `openapi.json`, the frontend types, the i18n messages and the README are WP3. I did not bump the version.

**WP3**: - `mise run api-types` could not run. It needs a running backend, and neither Docker nor Podman is available here, so the PostgreSQL container can't start. I added the unlock path to `openapi.json` by hand, in the same springdoc style as the other `POST /{id}/…` endpoints, then generated `schema.d.ts` with `:frontend:pnpmApiTypes`. Springdoc may order the entries or describe the response (200 instead of 204) slightly differently, so run `mise run api-types` once when a backend is available.
- The new `LoginForm.spec.ts` doesn't mount `LoginForm.vue` itself. The project has no DOM test environment (vitest uses `node`) and no `@vue/test-utils`. It renders a small probe component with `useLabels().error`, the call `LoginForm` makes, through `vue/server-renderer`.
- No screenshot, as the plan says.

Before: in the point cloud module, every tag picked its own colour and icon. There was no way to group tags (electrical, plumbing…), show only one kind, or hand the client a document listing them.

After: a project can have tag types. These are optional, and without them nothing changes. One click adds an infrastructure set: electrical, plumbing, drainage, air conditioning, gas, communication and structure. Each type has a layer switch. Quick mode adds a numbered tag of the chosen type with every click on the scan. A "PDF report" button downloads a cover page with totals by type, followed by two tags a page, each with a picture taken in the scan where the tag is seen.

**How**
- New `src/js/20-viewer/09a-tag-types.js` adds the types, the types window, the layers, quick mode and the report. It uses `tagPose()`, now factored out of `flyToTag` in `09-tags.js`.
- Tags get an optional `ty`. Types are saved per model in localStorage (`tourViewerTagTypes:<model>`), in the project file (`extras.tagTypes`) and in the client package manifest (`tagTypes`, also in the list of update keys).
- The report draws each A4 page on a canvas, so Hebrew right-to-left text comes out correctly, and writes the pages as a JPEG-page PDF. It works offline and adds no library. Only the layers currently shown go into the report.
- A client who is allowed their own tags gets the types, quick mode and the report. Only the Studio edits the types.
- `tests/run.mjs` has a new point cloud section using `tests/fixtures/room.e57`, a 547 KB box room. It adds the infrastructure set, places tags in quick mode, switches a layer off, and checks the PDF page count.

author: fontanf
body:
## Problem

`compute_arc_arc_intersections` checks whether two concentric arcs are on the same circle by comparing the squares of their radii with the tolerance (`equal(rsq, r2sq)`):
- this is too strict for large radii: arcs on the same circle within the tolerance are considered on different circles, and get no intersection at all. Radii 100 and 100 + 1e-7 have squares that differ by 2e-5;
- this is too loose for small radii: arcs on different circles are considered on the same one, and overlapping. Radii 0.01 and 0.01004 are 4e-5 apart, but their squares differ by 8e-7.

## Change

The radii themselves are compared.

## Tests

- 2 new cases of `ComputeIntersectionsTest`, with the radii above. Both fail without the fix.
- All 578 tests pass.
- The random checks of the boolean operations (rectangles, star polygons, holes, circles and arcs, touching holes) still have no failures.

author: sergeiwallace
body:
## Summary

The endless `[session] session script updated — reloading...` loop was fixed in 71efc7c (#108), and that fix is still on `main`. On GNU coreutils the old mtime probe, `stat -f "%m" FILE || stat -c "%Y" FILE`, captured a filesystem report whose free-block counters change between reads. Every replacement child therefore saw a "changed" stable script at its loop top and exited 78 again.

The existing tests pull the `_file_mtime` helper out of the template and run it on its own. This PR adds tests that run the deployed artifact: the stable script exactly as `ai c` hands it to `tmux new-session` (supervisor, promoted child body, agent), in a real tmux pane. Where the host's `stat` is not GNU coreutils, a stand-in with GNU's measured behaviour takes its place.

- `test_given_gnu_stat_and_an_unchanged_stable_script_when_the_session_starts_then_the_agent_starts_without_reloading`
- `test_given_gnu_stat_and_one_stable_script_rewrite_when_the_session_starts_then_it_reloads_once_and_reaches_the_agent`. This is the positive control: a genuine rewrite still reloads, exactly once.

Also adds the missing changelog entry for the 0.8.0 fix.

## Verification

- Both tests pass on macOS (stand-in `stat`).
- I restored the old probe chain in `session_script.py` and both tests failed with the reported symptom: the pane filled with the reload line and the agent never started. Then I reverted that change.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright src/` are clean. 25 passed and 2 skipped across the reload, self-update and Ctrl+Z session suites.

author: javilianes8
body:
Improvement round for 0.2.0. The plan, sources and checklist are in `IMPROVEMENTS-round.md`.

## What changes

- `parse` / `parse_header` follow the client rules of RFC 2369 section 2: comments (nested, quoted pairs, RFC 2047 encoded words decoded), folding, and the three "ignore the rest" rules. `strict=True` raises `ListUnsubscribeError` with an offset.
- `build` validates every URI; `header_line` folds to 78 columns and refuses controls, Unicode line separators and lines over 998 octets; `sender_headers` returns both one-click fields.
- RFC 8058: `is_one_click` matches only the exact value (any case), `one_click_request` builds the POST (multipart or urlencoded) and refuses non-HTTPS URIs, user information and bad authorities.
- `actions` / `choose` pick how to unsubscribe; one-click only with a verified DKIM signature and `https` allowed.
- `signed_headers` / `dkim_covers` read the DKIM `h=` tag (RFC 6376 tag-list, VALCHAR).
- RFC 6068: `parse_mailto`, `build_mailto` and `Mailto.to_message` (only To, Subject, Keywords and the body; IDNA domains; no controls or line breaks in headers).
- `audit` lists problems with stable codes against RFC 2369, RFC 8058 and the bulk sender rules of Gmail and Yahoo.
- `listunsub` command and `python -m listunsub`: JSON report of a message, exit 0, 1 or 2.

## Evidence

- Tests against the RFC texts (examples, ABNF character sets, the RFC 8058 errata), fetched on demand by `scripts/fetch_upstream.py` and pinned by size and sha256 in `tests/upstream/MANIFEST.json`; nothing third-party is committed or shipped.
- README examples are executed, the typed API is checked with mypy, and an installed-wheel test builds, installs and drives the package and the command (`LISTUNSUB_E2E=1`).
- Gates: `ruff format --check .`, `ruff check .`, `mypy --strict src`, `pytest`, all green on a fresh clone.
- Mutation run: 476 mutants, 459 killed; the 17 survivors are equivalent (details in `IMPROVEMENTS-round.md`).
- Independent review: 11 findings, all fixed with regression tests in `tests/test_review_fixes.py`.

The canvas now draws the in-progress stroke and the accepted guides (still at most two) in document space. They follow the image through zoom and pan, including a moved, rotated, or flipped layer. Clear Guides, Cancel, and OK remove the overlay. The upright calculation and the stored coordinates are unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `ctest --preset windows-x64-release -R camera_raw_session --output-on-failure` — 8/8 passed, including `camera_raw_session.guided_lines`
- [x] The new test checks the live stroke, the accepted guide, zoom and pan alignment, Clear Guides, Cancel, and that OK bakes the same pixels as `renderCameraRaw` from the layer-unit coordinates rather than view coordinates
- [ ] Manual: Filters > Camera Raw Filter, Geometry, Draw Guides. Draw one or two lines, zoom and pan, Clear Guides, then Cancel. Draw again and confirm with OK

`guided_lines` runs on the normal Windows platform. The offscreen platform does not finish the swap-chain present used to read the canvas, so that case is not given `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`.

A before/after capture of the same guide gesture is in the local build output (`build/guide-shots/before-after.png`). It is not committed.

## Summary

Adds two features to the diff view and bumps the version to 1.2.0.

- **Tabs above the diff.** In the Changes view, each file you pick in the list opens as a tab in place of the file path. Tabs switch the diff and the list selection. Close a tab with its × button, a middle click, or Delete, or use the tab's context menu: **Close**, **Close Others**, **Close to the Right**, and **Close All**. Tabs for committed or discarded files close on their own.
- **Open in editor from the diff.** Right-clicking the diff text in the Changes or History view offers **Open in _editor_**. It uses the editor from Settings > Integrations, or the repository's own editor if it has one.

## Implementation notes

- Open tabs are stored per repository in `IChangesState.openDiffTabs`. They're kept as paths, because a file's ID changes along with its status.
- When the selected file goes away, `updateChangedFiles` now selects an open tab before falling back to the first file.
- Closing the last tab leaves the selection empty. Before this change, the next status refresh reselected the first file.
- Selecting several files still shows the "N files selected" pane without tabs.

## Testing

- 4 new unit tests in `update-changed-files-test.ts` cover the tab rules.
- The full unit suite passes: 1,827 of 1,828 tests pass, and 1 is skipped.
- `tsc` and ESLint are clean on the changed files.
- Tested by hand in a dev build.

author: tannerycity
body:
> **No hacer merge todavía:** pendiente de la aprobación final de Presidencia.

## Causa raíz
- La auditoría de `v2_chat_pulse` (DevTools, módulo Jugadores) **no confirmó dos pollers**. Hay **uno solo**: `pulsoMensajes()` en `v2/shell.js`, cada 30 s. `fetch.ts:17` y `shell.js` son la misma petición vista en dos niveles de la pila.
- Defectos reales del poller:
  1. **Contexto viejo** (líneas 283-300 del código anterior, `if(pulsoTimer)return;`): el intervalo y el listener se quedaban con el `ctx` del primer login. En el Inicio se puede salir y entrar con otra cuenta sin recargar. Entonces seguía preguntando por el **club anterior** (10 consultas en 5 min, 0 al nuevo), y una respuesta tardía podía pintar la campana o emitir `tos:pulso` en la sesión nueva.
  2. Sin deduplicación: 3 arranques simultáneos → 3 peticiones en vuelo.
  3. Sin mínimo al volver a la pestaña: 10 regresos en 60 s → 12 consultas.
  4. Sin espera creciente ante errores: 2 fallos/min sin red.
  5. No se detenía al cerrar sesión.
  6. Latente: `branding-auto.js` importa `shell.js?v=…`, otra copia del módulo con su propio intervalo (hoy no se duplica por la condición de `branding-auto`).
- `loadAnnouncements` también podía escribir datos de la sesión anterior en la campana.

## Qué cambia
| Archivo | Cambio |
|---|---|
| `v2/shell.js` | Poller único en `window.__tosPulso`, compartido por las dos copias del módulo. Detalle abajo. |
| `v2/shell.js` (`loadAnnouncements`) | Descarta respuestas de otra sesión. Solo escribe el globito como respaldo mientras el pulso no contesta; si ya contestó, pide pulso respetando el mínimo de 15 s, por ejemplo tras publicar un aviso. |
| `v2/shell.js` (`wireBell`) | El pulso arranca antes que la lista de avisos, así un cambio de sesión apaga lo anterior primero. |
| `v2/app.js` | `detenPulso()` en `SIGNED_OUT`. |
| `scripts/qa-humo-pulso.mjs` (nuevo) | 29 revisiones en Chromium con reloj controlado. |

Detalle del poller único:
- llave `organization_id:user_id` y **generación** para descartar respuestas tardías;
- una sola petición en vuelo;
- cada 30 s con la pestaña visible, 0 con la pestaña oculta y mínimo 15 s al volver;
- espera de 30 s → 5 min ante errores, que vuelve a 30 s con el primer acierto o el evento `online`;
- `detenPulso()` exportado.

**Sin cambios** en la respuesta de la RPC, en el evento `tos:pulso` (Mensajes), en la base de datos ni en RLS. Variables globales: solo `window.__tosPulso`, y desaparece la variable de módulo `pulsoTimer`.

## Pruebas
- `qa-humo-pulso`: **29/29**. Contra el código anterior: **15/29 fallan**, lo que confirma que detecta los defectos.
- `qa-humo-mensajes` (36), `qa-humo-inicio-cumple-fab` (43), `qa-humo-formacion` (59), qa-static, humo de navegador (57 pantallas) y barrera de suites: OK.
- Corrida completa local: **72/72 suites** OK.

### Antes vs. después (mismo arnés de medición, reloj controlado, Supabase simulado)
| Métrica | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| `v2_chat_pulse`/min, pestaña visible | 1.9 | 1.9 (se conservan los 30 s) |
| Pestaña oculta | 0 | 0 |
| 10 regresos a la pestaña en 60 s | 12 | 4 |
| Peticiones simultáneas con 2 arranques | 2 | 1 |
| 2 copias del shell | 4/min | 2/min |
| Consultas al club anterior tras cambiar (5 min) | 10 | 0 |
| Sin red | 2.0/min | 0.4/min |
| Fallas funcionales nuevas | — | 0 |

El p95 y la latencia en producción no se midieron. El procedimiento con DevTools está en la auditoría: filtrar Network por `v2_chat_pulse` con "Preserve log", 5 min visible, 10 cambios de pestaña y salir y entrar con otra cuenta en el Inicio.

## Riesgos
- Tras una caída de red larga, la campana puede tardar hasta 5 min en ponerse al día. Se mitiga con el evento `online` y con volver a la pestaña, que consultan al instante.
- Varias pestañas visibles consultan cada una por su cuenta. Es aceptable a la escala actual.

## Rollback
- **Revertir el commit del squash** (`git revert <sha>`). Restaura el poller anterior.
- No hay migraciones ni cambios de datos: el rollback es solo de frontend e inmediato al desplegar.

## Fuera de alcance (fase 2, no incluida)
**Hallazgo F:** `lastAt` en `private.query_chat_pulse` expone cuándo hubo actividad en chats privados ajenos.
- Ningún consumidor lo usa: ni el cliente, ni otras funciones SQL, ni las Edge Functions, ni las pruebas.
- La propuesta es eliminarlo, y está preparada aparte. **No se aplica aquí.**

author: andrebrait
body:
Fixes #3488.

## Summary

pfBlockerNG treated any NAT rule whose description merely *contained* `pfB DNSBL` as package-owned. This applied to both the enabled and the disabled `pfb_create_dnsbl()` branches, because `pfb_is_managed_obj()` itself used `str_contains`. A user port-forward named `my pfB DNSBL test` was therefore rebuilt or dropped on every DNSBL apply.

Following the owner decision recorded in the issue, NAT ownership is now the **exact** package-written description `pfB DNSBL - DO NOT EDIT` (`PFB_MANAGED_NAT_DESCR`). It is the only NAT description the package has ever written; `git log --all` shows no other.

- `pfb_is_managed_obj()`: the substring rule becomes `$descr === PFB_MANAGED_NAT_DESCR`. `PFB_MANAGED_NAT_LEGACY_PFX` is removed.
- `pfb_managed_obj_match()`: its only non-`pfB_` marker is now exact, so it reduces to the ownership gate plus the prefix check.
- `pfb_create_dnsbl()`: both branches classify through the shared predicate with `PFB_MANAGED_NAT_DESCR`.
- Knock-on behavior through the same predicate:
  - `pfb_collect_foreign_trackers()` now treats a lookalike `filter/rule` as foreign, so its tracker is reserved.
  - `pfb_deinstall_sweep_managed_objects()` no longer sweeps lookalike user rows.
- Accepted risk (owner decision): a package rule whose description an administrator hand-edited despite "DO NOT EDIT" is no longer recognized. The next apply adds a fresh managed rule beside it.

## Tests

- New `tests/php/DnsblNatOwnershipTest.php` covers:
  - an enabled apply and a disabled apply, each of which must preserve a lookalike user rule byte-identical;
  - a `pfb_is_managed_obj()` boundary provider: exact, `pfB_` prefix, bare legacy, trailing space, embedded, suffixed, and case variants.
- Red against `origin/devel` production gave `Tests: 12, Assertions: 15, Failures: 7.` with test hash `877a928732bf557251f66298328443f3201f6e6a`. Green with the same hash gave `OK (133 tests, 901 assertions)` over the four touched test files.
- Test maintenance: `ForeignTrackerCollectionTest`, `DnsblMarkedVipTest` and `SyncCopiedObjectsTest` no longer pin substring ownership.

Live smoke: not run. The existing smoke scenarios check the exact package rule by prefix and stay valid. No smoke scenario seeds a lookalike row.

author: labdennis
body:
Long simulation seeks collected every 15-step snapshot before eviction. The final one-time thinning could still leave more than the intended 256 checkpoints, and peak state storage grew with the entire seek distance.

Refs #1238: addresses checkpoint accumulation and the retained-count limit.

One insertion helper now enforces the 256-checkpoint limit both while generating snapshots and while merging them into a cache entry. It drops off-grid targets first, thins aligned snapshots when needed, and keeps the new exact target. The simulator still executes the same steps and returns the same state; repeated requests for the latest target reuse its `Arc` directly.

Validation on Windows / Rust 1.95, upstream `549e9d82`:

- Both new regressions fail with the original production code because the retained checkpoint count exceeds 256.
- All **457 Effects tests** pass, including particle/simulation image hashes. The final cache tests and strict all-target Effects Clippy also pass.
- An instrumented small synthetic state verifies retained counts and a peak bound of 514 live states across sequential warm-cache seeks (up to 256 old snapshots + 256 fresh snapshots + working state/pending clone). No large particle buffers or memory-exhaustion tests are needed.
- Forward/backward seeks, repeated targets and key eviction match a fresh deterministic simulation.
- Formatting, assets, layers and the full WASM gate (32 crates, one existing UI dead-code warning) pass. Full `xtask ci` stops at the unchanged `collapsible_match` finding in `crates/model/src/stl.rs:179`; this PR does not claim a green full workspace CI run.

The limit counts snapshots, not bytes: variable-sized states and concurrent runs still need a broader memory-budget design. Very large advances still execute synchronously and are not cancellable. Those remaining parts of #1238 are deliberately not marked closed by this focused fix.

Upstream main, issue status and open PRs were checked before publication. Existing broad performance PR #856 changes plane transposition in the same source file but does not touch `SimCache`; #885 also does not provide this checkpoint fix.

author: clodmony
body:
Group 1: Cleanup. Four issues, one commit each, except #31 and #32, which share one commit: both need protocol version 2 and both change the host's frame loop.

Closes #28
Closes #26
Closes #31
Closes #32

## #28: a frame driver that boots from the launcher
**Replayed:** `tests/coop/driver_launcher_boot_test.lua` restarts into the launcher with `POKEPORT_DRIVER` set. The driver boots Red from the launcher and runs to its end.
**Broke:** `main.lua:1108: attempt to index upvalue 'Importer' (a nil value)` (5/7 checks).
**Fix:** a marked guard after the driver's resume in `love.update`. If the driver booted a game, the launcher is gone and the frame ends there. 7/7.

## #26: the fork's own save folder; upstream's updater and cloud sync off
**Owner decisions:** the identity is `gen1recomp-coop`. Upstream saves come over by copying the folder by hand, as the docs describe; an import screen may come with #6. Recorded as G9 in `docs/coop/design.md`.

**Replayed:** `tests/coop/upstream_services_test.lua` spies on `Boot.run`, `Check.start` and `Check.download`. It fakes a sync engine that is enabled and linked (a device linked in upstream's launcher) and pretends to be a packaged build. It covers a fresh start, a game booted from the launcher and a `--update --sync` shortcut, and it checks `conf.lua`'s identity.

**Broke** (5/12):
```
FAIL no updater or sync call on a fresh start and a game from the launcher (got Boot.run=1, SyncEngine.new=1, noteResumed=2, sync update=8, want )
FAIL no updater or sync call on a shortcut that asks for an update and a sync (got Boot.run=1, Check.start=1, want )
FAIL the game saves under the fork's identity (got pokemon-love2d, want gen1recomp-coop)
```

**Fix:**
- `src/coop/Upstream.lua` with three marked hooks in `main.lua`:
  - the updater's boot shell no longer runs;
  - a launch request's `update` and `sync` tasks are dropped before the pre-launch screen;
  - `SyncEngine._shared = false`, so `SyncEngine.shared()` answers nil to every sync user (the game's save, focus and resume hooks, the pre-launch sync, the Box journal).
- `conf.lua` uses `gen1recomp-coop` (the second display uses `gen1recomp-coop-companion`). `POKEPORT_IDENTITY` still overrides it.
- The save editor's `SaveIO`, its README and `tools/modkit.py` follow the new name.

12/12. A real LÖVE 11.5 run with a private data folder created only `gen1recomp-coop/`. `docs/coop/launcher.md` gives both folders per OS and how to copy upstream saves over (the copy itself was not run).

## #32: per-link limits against message floods
**Broke** (before the fix): one link sends 4 × 100 KB a frame for 300 frames. Each frame costs about 26 ms and the link is never dropped:
```
== before (ab8cb475)
300 frames of 4 x 100 KB from one link: send + host frame worst 29.0 ms, mean 26.1 ms; flooder joined (nil)
== this branch
300 frames of 4 x 100 KB from one link: send + host frame worst 10.7 ms, mean 1.0 ms; flooder refused (flood)
```
The new `session_flood_test.lua` fails on the old code at `Host.FRAME_BUDGET` (nil); the old code has no limits at all.

**Fix:**
- Arriving text now waits on its link undecoded.
- Each frame the host decodes at most 256 KB or 64 messages per link (always at least one); the rest waits for the next frame.
- Each link has an allowance of 4 MiB and 512 messages, refilled at 1 MiB and 120 messages a second.
- A link over its allowance gets `rejected` `flood`. Its player leaves at once, nothing more it sends is read, and the link closes after the grace.

**Tests:** `session_flood_test.lua` (26 checks):
- a move every frame for 20 s, a 2 MiB message and a backlog of 200 small messages are no flood;
- a 3 MB burst is decoded a budget at a time over 10+ frames;
- a flood of large messages and a flood of small ones are each dropped with `flood` within a second, while another player's move goes through in every frame.

The ENet suite repeats the flood over real sockets.

**Faster decoder?** Measured, and not worth an upstream edit now. Scanning a string's plain run at once halved a 2 MiB string (22 → 12 ms) but saved only about 15% on structured data (about 46 ms per MB). The frame budget is what bounds a frame. The numbers are in `docs/coop/session.md`.

## #31: shared session logs
**Broke:** `session_logs_test.lua` on the old code. No line reaches another device:
```
FAIL the host logs that A and B share
FAIL A's line reached B
FAIL B's line reached A
FAIL the host keeps A's line in its log
```

**Fix:**
- Lines are numbered (`n`). A sharing client sends its own lines every 2 s in batches of at most 64 KB and 1024 lines, plus a last batch before its bye. A line over 8 KB goes with `data = { omitted_bytes }`, and lines that don't fit are counted in a `stream_dropped` line.
- The hello carries `logs = { share }` (the hello's `device` already names the device).
- The host:
  - takes only the sending device's lines;
  - keeps them in its log when it shares;
  - passes each batch on once to every other sharing device;
  - shares its own lines the same way, with a last batch before `ended`;
  - keeps a 256 KB backlog for late joiners.
- Received lines are stored with `relay` and never sent again.
- Sharing defaults on; `--coop-logs=off` / `POKEPORT_COOP_LOGS=off` turns it off until the launcher has a setting (#12).

**Tests:** `session_logs_test.lua` (37 checks) covers:
- two clients' lines reaching a third device;
- the backlog for a late joiner and its 256 KB cap;
- the 8 KB line and 64 KB batch caps;
- no relayed line sent on, and forged lines of another device refused;
- a device that does not share;
- the last lines before a bye and before `ended`.

The fuzz test has `log` in both directions and the hello's `logs`. The ENet suite sends a log line from one ENet player to another.

## Not run
- Neither the log sharing nor the flood limits were run in two real game processes (`--coop-host` / `--coop-join`). Only the ROM-free tests and the ENet suite were run, on one machine.
- Windows, macOS and mobile were not run.
- Copying an upstream save folder into the fork's folder was not run.

## Verify
`tools/verify.sh` at 601ef73d: tests 36 of 37 tiers passed, modlint ok, fixtures ok. The one failed tier is `T0 Android importer copy lifecycle`, which needs `javac` (not installed on this machine; CI has Java). The luacheck gate was skipped locally (no luacheck), so coop-ci runs it. The first run also failed `launch_uri_args_test` and `launch_prelaunch_bug1657`: upstream checks `main.lua` for the line `tasks = request.tasks or {}`. Fixed in 601ef73d by keeping that line and filtering the whole options table. The ENet suite (`love tests/coop/enet`, 45/45) and the co-op tier (10/10 suites) also pass on their own.

author: tauceti-ai-for-science
body:
This PR proves the eigenblock sine formula: the squared Frobenius sine between two coordinate blocks of orthonormal bases equals the cross-block sum of squared overlaps. For orthonormal bases `b`, `c` of `E` and a common index block `s`, `sinThetaSq` of the families `(bᵢ)_{i ∈ s}` and `(cⱼ)_{j ∈ s}` is `∑_{j ∈ s} ∑_{k ∉ s} ‖⟪bₖ, cⱼ⟫‖²` (`TauCeti.sinThetaSq_comp_subtypeVal_comp_subtypeVal_eq_sum_compl_norm_inner_sq`). It derives this from the basis-free identity `sin²_F Θ = ∑ⱼ ‖P_{Uᗮ} vⱼ‖²`, where `U` is the span of the first family (`TauCeti.sinThetaSq_eq_sum_norm_starProjection_orthogonal_sq`). The intermediate form `TauCeti.sinThetaSq_comp_subtypeVal_eq_sum_compl_norm_inner_sq` lets the second family be any orthonormal family indexed by `s`.

Supporting lemmas:

- `Orthonormal.starProjection_apply_eq_sum`: the projection onto the span `U` of a finite orthonormal family is `x ↦ ∑ᵢ ⟪vᵢ, x⟫ vᵢ`.
- `Orthonormal.norm_starProjection_sq_eq_sum`: Parseval on that span, `‖P_U x‖² = ∑ᵢ ‖⟪vᵢ, x⟫‖²`, obtained through the coordinate isometry `synthesisMapIsometry` and `norm_analysisMap_sq`.
- `OrthonormalBasis.span_range_comp_subtypeVal_eq_spanIndices`: the basis vectors indexed by a coordinate block span `spanIndices`.

Both projection lemmas take the subspace through `hU : span 𝕜 (range v) = U` rather than as an instance on the span itself. That way a caller can use `spanIndices s` or its orthogonal complement directly, without rewriting a `HasOrthogonalProjection` instance.

Roadmap target: `OperatorTheory/PrincipalAngles/README.md`, Part A, **Milestone: aligned bases** (`PA-A27`–`PA-A30`).

- `PA-A30` (eigenblock sine formula) is `sinThetaSq_comp_subtypeVal_comp_subtypeVal_eq_sum_compl_norm_inner_sq`.
- `PA-A29` (coordinate-block orthonormality) is Mathlib's `Orthonormal.comp` for the orthonormality half, together with `span_range_comp_subtypeVal_eq_spanIndices` for the span half.
- `PA-A27`–`PA-A28` are in the open PR #16047. Once it lands, nothing else in the milestone remains.

The consumer is `OperatorTheory/SpectralSubspacePerturbation/README.md`, Part D, `SSP-D07` (complement identity, `sinThetaFrobenius_eq_sqrt_sum_cross` in its `Suggested.lean`). That target states the same cross-block sum for blocks `span (bT '' s)` and `span (bS '' s)` of two eigenbases. The projection form here identifies `sinThetaSq` with `∑ⱼ ‖P_{Uᗮ} vⱼ‖²`, the squared Frobenius norm of the directed sine map on an orthonormal basis of `V`. This is the step `SSP-D07` needs once `sinThetaMap` is available.

Related open work: the older port #13864 contains a projection formula for spans of finite subfamilies (`Orthonormal.starProjection_span_image_apply`). It also has a projector-distance identity `∑ₖ ‖(P_v - P_u) uₖ‖² = 2 · cross sum`. It does not state the family-level `sinThetaSq` results above, and nothing here was taken from it.

Roadmap: OperatorTheory

author: ericsuh
body:
## Summary

Design-phase deliverables for Watchword, a native iOS/iPadOS/macOS password manager for a household or small group, plus the CI scaffolding and the first testable Swift modules.

### Documents (`docs/`)
- `00-research.md` — survey of 1Password (2SKD, keysets, vault keys, non-cryptographic revocation), Bitwarden (no org-key rotation), Apple Passwords (shared groups, CSV, Credential Exchange), KeePass-family sync; Apple APIs for AutoFill (passwords, passkeys, one-time codes, text-to-insert), `ASCredentialExportManager`/`ASCredentialImportManager` (iOS 26), LocalAuthentication/Keychain access control, CryptoKit HPKE and Secure Enclave, CloudKit encrypted fields and `CKShare`; HIBP range API; runner images and Swift Testing. Cited throughout.
- `01-prd.md` — goals, the four normative scenarios (Amazon retail vs AWS root, Google passkey + recovery codes, shared bank account, shared library card), functional requirements F1–F10, security requirements SEC1–SEC7, memory-safe-language and native-UI requirements.
- `02-architecture.md` — threat model, 1Password-style two-secret key hierarchy (account password + 128-bit Secret Key, PBKDF2 + HKDF, XOR, keyset, per-vault keys HPKE-wrapped to members), envelope format with AAD binding, local storage and Keychain layout, CloudKit primary transport and file-based (iCloud Drive / Files-app / Dropbox) secondary transport using per-device append-only logs, sharing protocol with fingerprint verification and key rotation on revocation, AutoFill scope matching with shadowing, unlock state machine, HIBP and strength design, import/export, module layout.
- `03-implementation-plan.md` — milestones 0–8 with exit criteria.
- `04-test-plan.md` — ports-and-fakes test architecture, end-to-end scenario tests, XCUITest plan, explicit adversarial security test requirements per layer, fuzzing, CI mapping.
- `adr/` — memory-safe language, native UI (no Electron/Tauri/Catalyst), KDF choice, Secret Key storage, HIBP-while-locked.

### Package and CI
- SwiftPM package (Swift 6 language mode) with `WatchwordModel`, `WatchwordMatching` (host normalisation + ranking that keeps the Amazon retail login off the AWS sign-in page), `WatchwordGenerator` (password/passphrase/PIN with entropy estimates, rejection sampling), `WatchwordEnvelope` (header parsing and KDF floors against downgrade).
- Tests: XCTest suite (`WatchwordMatchingTests`, 14 cases), Swift Testing suites (`WatchwordGeneratorTests`, `WatchwordEnvelopeTests`), and a tagged adversarial suite (`WatchwordAdversarialTests`); 46 Swift Testing cases in 8 suites.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: package tests on `macos-15`/Xcode 16.4 and `macos-26`/Xcode 26, separate adversarial job, `-strict-memory-safety` build, `swift format lint`, and an app-test job that activates once `Apps/project.yml` exists. Test steps run under `pipefail` and verify that both frameworks actually executed tests.
- `.github/workflows/security-nightly.yml`: long randomised adversarial runs and a gated fuzz job.

### Notes
- The Swift code was written without a local toolchain (the sandbox cannot download Swift); the follow-up commits on this branch are the fixes from the first compiles on CI (formatting, a `#expect` key-path limitation, a macro name collision, a test-authoring mistake, and a `tee` without `pipefail` that had masked a compile error).
- Primary sources that could not be fetched from the sandbox (1Password white paper, FIDO CXF spec, HIBP docs) are cited via secondary sources and flagged in `00-research.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] `package-tests` green on both runners
- [x] `adversarial-tests` green
- [x] `strict-memory-safety` green
- [x] `lint` green
- [x] `app-tests` reports skipped (no app project yet)

author: vthib
body:
If multiple literals are extracted from a string,
and the same atom is then extracted from those literals, only the first literal ends up being searched and matched, and the others do not match correctly.

This can happen for example on the string:

`{ b? 01 02 03 04 }`

this string is compiled into a set of 16 literals, and each literal gets the atom `01 02 03 04`. This ends up as only `b0 01 02 03 04` matching.

This did not affect that many strings in practice. From the rulesets used in benchmarks, we have:

- panopticon: 1 rule affected / 100
- signature-base: 28 / 5904
- orion: 4 / 176
- yara-rules: 10 / 12771
- reversinglabs: 0 / 1240
- atr: 0 / 167
- icewater: 0 / 16431
- c0ffee: 0 / 121

Regardless, this is a pretty ugly matching bug.

author: mustardtigerfpv
body:
The installer for the unified ExpressLRS builds in FormationFlight/FormationFlight#75.

The old page couldn't actually download anything. GitHub release assets redirect without CORS headers, so a page can't fetch them, and it wrote every image at 0x0, which is wrong for any ESP32. Now:

* It's a regular docs page, so it looks like the rest of the site
* Release, manufacturer, board, band, optional node name and group passphrase, then flash over Web Serial with esptool-js 0.6.1 or download a .bin for the node's Update page. Same flow as the ELRS web flasher.
* The board's layout is appended in the browser, byte-for-byte what `elrs_targets.py configure` writes (checked by SHA-256)
* `scripts/fetch_firmware.py` copies the newest 3 releases plus the `development` prerelease into the site at build time. The workflow rebuilds every 6 hours, or on dispatch, and deploys with `--no-history` so firmware doesn't pile up in gh-pages.

Until a release built by the firmware PR exists, the page just says there's nothing to flash yet. Hardware, Getting Started and Advanced are updated to match.

Draft alongside the firmware PR. Flashing over USB is untested on real hardware so far; download is tested.

author: cicalese
body:
Closes #1982.

Two failure paths printed Ansible's raw command error instead of a message.

**`extension set-version --ref nosuchref`** (`roles/extensions_skins/tasks/set_version.yml`):
- After the fetch, the ref is checked first (directly, or as `refs/remotes/origin/<ref>` for a branch only on origin). An unknown ref stops before checkout with "'nosuchref' is not a branch, tag, or commit in the repository of extension 'NumberFormat'. Nothing was changed." The working tree isn't touched.
- Any other checkout failure (for example local edits that would be overwritten) reports "Could not check out '<ref>' in extension '<name>': <git's error>".

**PR-mode `gitops push`** (`roles/gitops/tasks/push_compose.yml`): when `gh pr create` fails, the checkout still returns to main, and the command reports "Pushed branch '<branch>' to origin, but gh could not open the pull request", then either "Run 'gh auth login', then open it on GitHub or with 'gh pr create --head <branch>' in <instance path>" (when gh says it isn't logged in) or "Open it on GitHub …", plus gh's error on one line.

A failure of the `fetch --tags` step itself (e.g. a network error) is unchanged.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_command_failure_messages.py` (6) runs the real tasks against temporary git repos with a stub `gh`: unknown ref, tag, origin-only branch, checkout blocked by local edits, gh not authenticated, another gh error; the four failure-path tests fail on `main`. Unit tests (4739), validate, CI coverage, yamllint, ruff and ansible-lint pass.

author: estebanzimanyi
body:
The generator scopes a function named tposechain_*, or carrying _tposechain as a word, to the
temporal pose chain alone. The same rule reads tnpoint_* and _tnpoint as the type
NpointTypes::tnpoint(), so the generator registers the functions MobilityDB declares over the
temporal network point, among them startValue, route, atValue, eEqual and tDistance. Without it
reg_scope returns nothing for them and the generator skips them, while numInstants(tnpoint) is
answered through the generic surface.

Witness: the tnpoint tests added here call startValue, endValue, getValue, route, atValue,
minusValue, eEqual, aEqual, ?= and tEqual over tnpoint; none of them is registered before this
change, and each answers here, e.g. startValue(tnpoint '{Npoint(1,0.2)@2000-01-01,
Npoint(1,0.8)@2000-01-02}') = NPoint(1,0.2).

Measured: over the catalog of MobilityDB f935759e00, the generator unchanged reproduces the
committed surface byte for byte; with the rule, the registration union (scalar and table
functions) gains 46 entries, loses 0, and every added entry is over tnpoint. Each of the 46 is a
signature MobilityDB declares in mobilitydb/sql/npoint with the same arguments. The full suite
passes, 3185 assertions in 111 files, the extension loading without a duplicate overload.

Why: the bindings are generated from the catalog, so a type MobilityDB declares a function over
is reached by the generator's scope, not by hand registration.

## Egresos: la misma pantalla y el mismo funcionamiento en los dos CRM

Diego, 10/10: «Egresos se empareja: la misma pantalla y el mismo funcionamiento en los dos CRM (paridad). Se comparan las dos versiones, se queda con lo mejor de cada una y se lleva a los dos.»

El mismo PR va en diego-landaeta/CRM y en diego-landaeta/CRM-ISEIE, con los ficheros del módulo **idénticos**.

### Qué había
| | MultiCRM | CRM-ISEIE |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | dentro de `accounting` (`/api/accounting/expenses`), sin servicio | módulo `expenses` (`/api/expenses`) con servicio + además una copia en `accounting` sin usar |
| Ámbito | empresa + campus de la persona (#245) en el listado | solo un campus; con «todos» mandaba `-1` → 400 |
| Ver/editar/borrar uno | sin mirar el ámbito | sin mirar el ámbito |
| Totales | «0 registros · 0 €» siempre (no se rellenaban) | suma de las 20 filas cargadas |
| Paginación | estado a medias, nunca pedía la página | ninguna |
| Comprobante | por fetch con token | `<a href>` → 401 siempre |
| Alta con empresa puesta | `project_id: -1` → 400 | — |

### Qué queda (en los dos)
- **Un solo módulo `expenses`** (routes/controller/service/model/validation) en `/api/expenses`; `/api/accounting/expenses` sigue como alias (los comprobantes ya subidos guardaron esa dirección).
- **Por empresa**, como el resto de Finanzas: `issuerId` → sus campus con `proyectosDelAmbito`, dentro de los campus de la persona. Ver, editar y borrar uno también se recortan (404 si no es tuyo).

author: jimcode1090
body:
## Qué hace
Agrega la gestión de distritos (agregar, listar, editar, desactivar y activar) con JPA, completa la pantalla de Ubicaciones con la pestaña Distritos y cierra el bloqueo pendiente de provincias. No existe borrado físico: la baja cambia `estado` a `INACTIVO`.

## Historias
- **US-27** Gestionar distritos: se elige la provincia y el nombre no se repite dentro de la misma provincia.
- **US-10** Editar un distrito (nombre o provincia).
- **US-49** (CA2): no se puede desactivar una provincia que tiene distritos activos.

## Qué incluye
- `model/Distrito` (`@Entity`, tabla `distrito`, `@ManyToOne` a `Provincia`) y `@OneToMany(mappedBy)` en `Provincia`.
- `repository/DistritoRepository` (JPQL, `JOIN FETCH`, `em.getReference` para asociar la provincia, transacciones con rollback) y `listarActivas()` en `ProvinciaRepository`.
- Servlets en `/ubicaciones/distritos`: listar, `nuevo`, `editar` y `estado`.
- Vistas `distritos.jsp` y `distrito-editar.jsp`, y la pestaña Distritos en `_pestanas.jsp`.
- En provincias: columna "Distritos" (solo activos) y bloqueo al desactivar.

## Cómo probarlo
1. Abrir `http://localhost:8080/sismos-peru/ubicaciones/distritos`.
2. Agregar un distrito eligiendo una provincia (el selector muestra "Provincia (Departamento)"): aparece en la lista. Dejar el nombre o la provincia vacío: "Todos los campos son obligatorios.".
3. Repetir el nombre en la misma provincia: "El distrito ya existe en esta provincia". El mismo nombre en otra provincia sí se permite.
4. Editar el nombre y la provincia. Desactivar y activar.
5. En la pestaña Provincias, desactivar una con distritos activos: "La provincia tiene distritos asociados".

## Notas
- Pendiente para el PR de estaciones: el bloqueo "La provincia tiene estaciones asociadas" (US-49 CA3).
- Pendiente para el PR de sismos: el bloqueo "El distrito está asociado a sismos registrados" al desactivar un distrito (US-27 CA3).

author: jmsbooth
body:
## Increment 2 — observed provider-usage evidence for partial QA runs

Savant's chat-only Test Bench previously persisted aggregate provider token counts **only on a successful completed run**. A user could cancel while NIM/OpenAI was in flight, or Jev could fail, causing actually reported provider usage to disappear from the summary. This PR adds durable factual evidence while making no provider-invoice or actual-dollar claims.

**Functional implementation**
- Migration 0029: tenant/run composite FK, unique `(organization_id,run_id,case_index,phase)` `executor|judge` usage-receipt records, bounded provider model and positive input/output token counts, new summary counters `observed_executor_tokens`, `observed_judge_tokens`, `observed_usage_receipts`.
- Evaluator: async `onUsage` executed **immediately** after each validated executor and Jev response, before the next model call or grading; unknown usage never fabricated.
- Worker/store: one row-locked transaction per provider ACK with job/tenant/run validation; exact duplicate receipts do not increment; mismatched duplicates fail. Responses that arrive after cancellation can still be reported without resurrecting the canceled run or score.
- Tenant run summary/UI: disclose provider-reported executor and Jev tokens for completed, canceled and failed runs. Distinguish observed/acknowledged usage from invoices, late provider billing or unknown timeout side effects. Does NOT change daily admission reservations or chargebacks.

**TDD and safety evidence**
- [x] Unit evaluator callbacks: per-case order; cancellation after executor prevents judge; callback database outage halts following provider egress; invalid token counts do not create receipts.
- [x] Client and UI: tampered/negative/inconsistent receipt counters refused; no invoice/cost assertion; no public receipt mutation endpoint.
- [x] Isolated PostgreSQL script: canceled-after-NIM partial, completed two-phase, failed-judge one-phase, same-ACK idempotency, conflicting duplicate hard denial, ten concurrent duplicate ACKs, foreign-tenant FK, invalid amounts/case index/phase, no raw prompt/output/API key/provider error in audit or receipt rows.
- [x] PostgreSQL script wired into existing CI migration+tenant acceptance pipeline.
- [ ] Exact-head unit/lint/TypeScript/Next/secrets, PG migrations twice, high/critical dependency audit and preview READY **must pass**.
- [ ] Independent review and actual tenant/provider smoke; managed encryption-key provisioning/rotation/restore.

**Limitations:** provider-**reported** usage, not actual billable usage, rate-card-based costs, spend caps, invoice settlement or even evidence that an uncertain network call had zero cost. Parent PER-1441 remains open for true monetary settlement and global provider capacity. No production release.

Depends on draft PR #75 (PER-1444), stacked onto #74/#72/#70 and prior Test Bench increments.
Linear: https://linear.app/lattix/issue/PER-1447
Design: `docs/architecture/per-1447-observed-provider-usage-evidence.md`

author: cicalese
body:
Closes #1981.

On a gitops instance, `canasta extension add` auto-commits, and the commit included unrelated files that were already staged (a staged `config/settings/global/E2E.php` landed in "Add extensions NumberFormat").

The extension/skin commands commit locally per operation, and `enable`/`disable` already scope their commit with a pathspec; this scopes the rest of that family the same way:
- `_add_one.yml`: "Commit added …" commits only `.gitmodules` and `<dir>/<name>`; "Commit re-aligned …" only `<dir>/<name>`.
- `add.yml`: the composer.local.json commit commits only `config/composer.local.json`.
- `remove.yml`: lists which of its own paths are staged (`.gitmodules`, the changed settings files, composer.local.json, `<dir>/<item>`) and commits only those, skipping the commit when none are (a pathspec git doesn't know would fail the whole commit, e.g. removing an untracked orphan).

Anything else that was staged stays staged for its own commit. Switching add/remove to stage-only (as `config set` does) would change their output and commit messages, so it isn't done here.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_extension_gitops_commit_scope.py` (5) runs the real task commands in a temp git repo with an unrelated file staged, for add, re-align, the composer commit, remove and an untracked-orphan removal, asserting each commit holds only its own paths and the unrelated file stays staged; the add, re-align and composer tests fail on `main`. Unit tests (4738), validate, CI coverage, yamllint, ruff and ansible-lint pass.

Needs a hands-on check on a Compose gitops instance: with an unrelated file staged, `extension add` (one with a composer.json) and `extension remove` commit only their own paths.

author: notasithlord
body:
Prepare the 0.9.0 preview release with the pending P2P/discovery work from #524 and recovery fixes found during native-browser qualification.

Worker restarts could temporarily lose peer-policy authority and purge every discovery card, including the user's own published App. Policy outages now continue to deny traffic while reserving destructive cache removal for explicit bans. Renderer recovery could also let an install hold the publication lane while waiting for local bytes that needed the same lane to reseed; that request now returns an exact retryable pre-effect result until recovery settles, while preserving remote-seeder retrieval afterward. Adopting a surviving host no longer restarts a completed reseed pass.

Also corrects reseed compensation to call the network boundary and forwards the publisher namespace needed for cold DHT lookup. Discovery rollout remains opt-in and bounded; the existing signed metadata, runtime/WASM, consent, and sandbox boundaries remain in force.

Validation: regression tests reproduce the policy-cache loss, duplicate reseeding, and local-recovery admission defects before the corresponding fixes. The full functional suite reports 8,924 passing tests. Real packaged worker/renderer lifecycle tests pass locally and on the Mac cluster, including retained discovery, reinstallation of verified bytes, and teardown. Final preflight and all PR checks passed before merge. The tagged release run hit one 30-second vault-lock response timeout in the instrumented cold-consent test; it did not reproduce locally or in three consecutive native Chromium 155 cluster runs, and the failed gate passed on rerun. The original failure remains recorded in release run 38487005644 attempt 1; no timing threshold was relaxed.

author: jung-thomas
body:
## What Tom saw
"We deployed to production and I don't see any visual difference on the mission/group pages" (#2733).

## Root cause (not what the issue assumed)
The #2743 feature code **did** ship — the mission/group HTML has the `goal-completion` island mount + slugs. But the island `<script>` **404s**, so it never runs and renders nothing.

Mission/group detail pages are **SSR'd live** in the deployed `tutorials-srv` process (`x-content-source: rendered`) — not Hugo-baked, not HANA BLOBs. The renderer is esbuild-bundled into `srv/lib/_shared/content.bundle.mjs` and resolves island `<script>` paths via `islandSrc()`, which reads `island-manifest.json` **relative to the bundle's own dir**. No build step ever placed that file there, so `islandSrc()` fell open to the bare `/js/<name>.js` path. The deployed bundles are content-hashed, so bare paths **404**:

```
/js/goal-completion.js  -> 404   (island never loads)
/js/learning-path.js    -> 404   (also silently broken since the carve)
/js/nav-dropdown.js      -> 200   (also ships unhashed, survives)
```

Introduced when the renderer was carved `srv/lib/` → `packages/content/`: the manifest writer still targets `srv/lib/`, which no longer matches the renderer's `_dir`.

## Fix
- New `scripts/lib/copy-island-manifest.cjs` seeds `srv/lib/island-manifest.json` (built by `build:island-manifest`) beside **each** content bundle (`srv/lib/_shared`, `srv-qa/lib/_shared`) and into `packages/content/` for local `cds watch` + unit tests.
- Wired into `scripts/bundle-shared.cjs`. **Fail-open** when the source is absent (CI `deploy.yml` builds islands out of band — nothing to copy); **fail-loud** when present-but-empty (an empty `{}` bakes bare paths just as surely).
- `deploy-mta.cjs` Step 2.5 now also asserts a non-empty `srv/lib/island-manifest.json` in the local deploy path (it previously only checked the Hugo homepage).
- Stale docstrings + `.gitignore` updated.

Same bug affected the concept/puzzle/topic list pages (same bundled-renderer `_dir`) — this fixes all of them.

## ⚠️ Deploy note
These pages render **live**, so this ships via a **backend deploy** (local `build:deploy` → `mbt build` path, where the manifest exists at `before-all`). A **content rebuild does NOT re-render them** and will not fix this on its own.

## Tests
- `test/unit/bundle-shared-island-manifest.test.js` — `copyIslandManifestBeside` contract (4 tests, incl. fail-open on absent source, fail-loud on empty).
- Verified end-to-end: with the manifest seeded, `renderMissionBody()` emits `goal-completion-<hash>.js` instead of the bare path.
- Full unit suite: 11200 passing; the remaining failures in this un-set-up worktree are the documented fresh-worktree gaps (missing `konva`/`@imgly`/`3d-force-graph` vendor deps + un-baked `page-fallback` snapshot), not this change.

Fixes #2733

body:
Authenticated acceptance can reject observation windows when runner and database clocks differ. It can also lose the actual primary browser failure behind a caught step or detach a case-upload rejection from its owning test. This change uses database-owned observation cursors, drains per-test work before finalization, and reports only the canonical primary result through closed diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria: preserve all 108 requirements and request/session/server authority; reject runner-supplied upper bounds; preserve exact evidence windows; fail the owning test on upload rejection; never replace a primary failure with caught-step or teardown detail. No product runtime, migration, scoring, hosted gate or deployment change.

Verification: pre-fix real Playwright failure and independently skewed controller/reader reproduction both demonstrated the defects. Corrected local checks passed: 31 clock/controller/observer, 20 diagnostics/reporter, five control/queue, 60 runner/workflow (two Windows symlink cases skipped), typecheck, real bootstrap and two-origin tracking. Actual application Desktop/Pixel proof passed 2/2 with unchanged checkout. Catalog (108 requirements), provenance, CI contract and security hygiene pass. Final candidate 528aaf1a passed Linux PostgreSQL denial/zero-write correlation, native secret authority, the complete clean-checkout replay and connected-browser preparation. Independent verification of run 38476123859 confirms 94 browser cases, five EI cases, cleanup and zero provider/paid/foreign-write effects. The ordinary-CI report independently reconstructs 43 PASS / 65 BLOCKED, correctly excluding hosted proof. Local Docker is unavailable.

The historical hosted cause remains unproven. Run 38470948715 retains independently verified 61 PASS / 47 BLOCKED with cleanup verified and providers OFF. This PR makes no new hosted PASS claim and authorizes no hosted retry.

author: marcseeruphansen
body:
To ting fra aftenens afprøvning hos Gaardmester.

## Formularen tømmes ved skift

Trykker kunden Forudbestilling midt i at udfylde kassen, hentes siden forfra — og navn, adresse og telefonnummer går med. WooCommerce husker noget af adressen i sessionen, men ikke navnet, mailen eller telefonen, og kunden har ingen måde at vide hvilke.

Genindlæsningen sker kun med opdelt levering slået til (målt på gaardmester.dk: `SPLIT_ON = true`):

```js
if (SPLIT_ON) { window.location.href = ...; return; }   // hele siden forfra
jQuery(document.body).trigger('update_checkout');        // ellers: formularen bliver stående
```

Den er der af en grund — opdelings-banneret sidder over formularen, og WooCommerce tegner ikke den del om ved en genberegning. **Den beslutning er ikke rørt.** I stedet skrives det indtastede ned lige før, og lægges tilbage når siden kommer igen, hvorefter der kaldes en genberegning, så fragt og datoer passer til adressen i stedet for den forrige.

`sessionStorage`, ikke en cookie: det bliver i fanen, når aldrig serveren og forsvinder når fanen lukkes. Kun det kunden selv har tastet i den formular, og kun for at give det tilbage til dem. Felter serveren selv har udfyldt røres ikke — et felt den har udfyldt, er et felt den mente.

## Knapteksten løb ud over knappen på en telefon

Gulvet for, hvornår de to knapper lægger sig under hinanden, var 150 px. Målt hos Gaardmester kræver "NORMAL BESTILLING" 126 px tekst + 50 px polstring = **176 px**, og "FORUDBESTILLING" er ét ord, der ikke kan ombrydes — så det løb ud af sin egen knap.

Et fast tal kan ikke kende butikkens egne knaptekster eller temaets skriftstørrelse. Koden måler nu selv den bredeste tekst på én linje og bruger den som gulv.

## Hvad der mangler

**Gæstetesten.** Logget ind som administrator fylder serveren selv navn og adresse ud, og koden springer med vilje over felter, serveren har udfyldt — så en indlogget prøve kan ikke skelne "det virker" fra "det blev aldrig prøvet". Rettelsen ligger på Gaardmesters staging og skal prøves i et privat vindue.

Bekræftet er, at siden **faktisk** hentes forfra ved et skift: et mærke sat i hukommelsen før klikket var væk bagefter, og URL'en skiftede til `?oko_pre_order=0`.

## Gates

- `php -l`: ren, og det nye JavaScript er syntakstjekket med `node --check`
- phpcs: 56 — tegn for tegn som `main`
- standalone: **118 bestået, nul fejl**

author: tokenmp
body:
## 背景

#42 把 `Makefile` 的 `build` 收窄成 `go build ./...`（原来会往 `bin/` 丢文件，且与 `install` 重复），产物改由 `build-bin` 出，`lint` 也从「有 golangci-lint 就跑」变成硬依赖。README 这一节没跟上，两处已经是错的：

- `README.md:654`：`make build  # 产物在 bin/tokenmp` —— 不再是这个行为；
- `README.md:657`：`make lint  # go vet，装有 golangci-lint 时一起跑` —— 干净 PATH 下没有 golangci-lint 会直接 127 退出。

## 改动

按新的 `Makefile` 目标表重写这一节，补齐 `build` / `build-bin` / `install` / `test` / `lint` / `fmt` / `fmt-check` / `tidy` / `clean` / `check` / `tools`，并补一句本地要先装工具：新增的 `make tools`（`mise install`）读 `.mise.toml` 里 pin 的 Go 1.27 与 golangci-lint 2.14.0。这条对第一次 clone 的人是真需要，原文一个字没提。

💡 What: Replaced sequential `findFirst` and `create` operations with batched `findMany` and `createMany` in `app/api/profile/sync/route.ts`. Added intra-request Set deduplication to prevent accidental duplicate inserts.

🎯 Why: The previous implementation iterated over user lifestyle memories and executed a distinct read and write database query for each item, leading to an N+1 query performance bottleneck that scaled linearly with the number of memories. 

📊 Impact: Reduces database queries from 2N to 2 (one read, one write block) during profile synchronizations, significantly decreasing database load and round-trip latency.

🔬 Measurement: Review `app/api/profile/sync/route.ts` line 47 onwards to verify the `findMany` and `createMany` batching block. Monitor the APM duration for `POST /api/profile/sync` to observe the latency drop.

_Requested by **Stephen** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLnw537yAtFvs4fiTN4wT2?thread=cmsg_01NLnw537yAtFvs4fiTN4wT24wLPao6RPy4zz6cMvF7ksD)_

Before: on the demo's List page, clearing Item or Owner and then clicking another row or a status chip saved the blanks. Only the Save button checked required fields (follow-up from #16).

After: every save of the item panel checks them. Leaving the panel, clicking another row or clicking a chip while Item or Owner is empty shows the same red outlines and one message, and the panel keeps the record. The list's highlighted row stays on that item and the chip doesn't change.

How:
- **Kit (modKitUI).** `ShowDetail` and `ClearDetail` are now Functions that return False and change nothing when the detail form refuses the save. Access raises 2101 (or 2115) for a cancelled `Dirty = False`; before this change that surfaced as an error dialog. A new `SaveDetail host, detailCtl` does the same check for page changes that don't go through `ShowDetail`. Existing `ShowDetail ...` statement calls still compile unchanged (SPM's pgRecords and pgPersonnel).
- **Demo.** `subItem` gets `Form_BeforeUpdate` (`Cancel = Not CheckRequired(Me, REQUIRED)`), wired by `Ev F, "BeforeUpdate"`. Save keeps its own check so the focus can move to the empty field. `pgList.GridClick` puts the selection back on the panel's item when `ShowDetail` returns False, and `Chip` calls `SaveDetail` first.
- **Docs and tests.** The README catalog and the DESIGN_GUIDE list/detail section are updated, and there is one new `TestKit` check.

To see it (Navy, Midnight, Teal Navy):
1. On List, pick an item and clear Owner.
2. Click another row: you get the message, the panel stays on the item, and the highlight stays on its row.
3. Click a chip: same result, and the chip doesn't change.
4. Click into the search box: the same check runs as the focus leaves the panel.
5. Fill Owner and click another row: it switches normally.

body:
## Summary

Visiting `/api/cron/update-matches` now flips/refreshes the matches and replies with exactly `{"status": "ok"}`.

The route already existed but was protected by `CRON_SECRET` and returned a detailed payload. Per request, it is now a simple open endpoint:

- **`GET` / `POST`** both run the match update via `ensureFreshMatches(0, ...)` in `lib/sync/engine.ts` — every visit triggers a real update, and concurrent visits share one in-flight run instead of duplicating it.
- The response is **always** `{"status": "ok"}` (HTTP 200): source failures are isolated by the sync engine and previous data is preserved, so a flaky external source never fails the request.
- No `CRON_SECRET` is needed to visit this route anymore. `CRON_SECRET` still protects the other sync routes (`/api/cron/sync`, `/api/cron/sync-news`). Note the trade-off: anyone who knows the URL can trigger an update.

## Changes

- `app/api/cron/update-matches/route.ts` — rewritten as the simple endpoint above.
- `tests/update-matches.test.ts` — replaced auth-rejection tests with: visiting the URL (no auth) updates+persist matches and replies exactly `{"status":"ok"}`; same for POST; Vercel cron config still asserted.
- `README.md`, `.env.example` — docs updated to match (endpoint is open, response shape, curl example).

## Verification

- Live-tested against the dev server: `GET` and `POST /api/cron/update-matches` → `{"status":"ok"}` (HTTP 200), and the match store was actually updated.
- `npm test` — 64/64 pass.
- `npm run lint` and `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- The daily Vercel cron in `vercel.json` (`0 5 * * *`) still targets this path and keeps working without headers.

Audit item 2. Stacked on #203 (review the last commit).

A pull staged every entry in the response that its server had signed, so a peer could hand over records nobody asked it for.

- Both pull paths (cycle pull, urgent single-key pull) go through one `swarmStagePulled`: an entry stages only if it names a key this pull asked that peer for, is signed by the peer, and is the first answer for its key.
- Anything else is dropped unread; a response with unasked-for or repeated keys costs the serving peer one flat mark.
- Entries under another signer are still skipped without blame.

**Tested:** mixed response (asked, unasked type, unasked kind, repeated key, foreign signer); clean response; the same rule over HTTP through the urgent pull. Full suite locally: only the five known Windows-only failures. `gofmt`, `vet` clean.

**Not tested:** the workflow's node test list (no node on this machine).

**Consequence to check:** `type_name` and `structure_name` are served on request, but nothing requests them (demand is history, corporations, alliances). They could only arrive unasked before, so after this they do not arrive at all until demand includes them.

body:
## Summary
Closes #35.

Adds shared UI-only recipe and craft previews using native WoW `GameTooltip`. The full issue and both original TSM reference images informed the structure; the four new in-game screenshots informed the compactness polish.

The branch was created from freshly fetched `master`. No changes to Core statistics, measurement-coverage semantics, hover precedence, captured facts, SavedVariables schemas, or persistence fields.

## Architecture and Styling
- Add `UI/Tooltip.lua`, loaded after Components, with reusable titles, subtitles, sections, aligned rows, scope formatting, semantic colors and owner-aware lifecycle primitives.
- Gold headings, TSM-like light-blue labels, white ordinary/contextual text, gray muted negative/unavailable states, green observed positive outcomes, and amber partial coverage. Character names use recorded class colors when known.
- Recipe previews read public APIs for scoped durable history, character counts, output and supported aggregate outcomes. Craft previews describe one factual result with character/profession, precise local timestamp, quality, concentration and proc outcomes.
- Returned-material previews show at most two rows plus a remaining-item count; full ingredient allocation tables remain on Craft Detail.

## Screenshot-Driven Polish
- Combine period and character selection into one brief, wrapping scope line, such as `14 Sep - 13 Oct 2026 UTC / All characters`. Single-day periods collapse to one date; cross-year periods retain both years.
- Avoid repeating profession scope when it is already identified in the recipe subtitle. A different, empty or broader selected profession population remains explicit rather than being concealed.
- Keep the authoritative Resourcefulness numerator/denominator beside the rate, for example `31.8% (7/22)`. Replace multiple long explanations with at most one compact amber note: `22/98 authoritative; +21 unverified procs`.
- Without authoritative observations, known positives remain evidence only, for example `8 known procs; unverified`, never a computed rate or invented negative outcome.
- Omit the craft output-name row only when both known names match the recipe title. Always preserve produced quantity; different and unknown output identities remain visible.
- Preserve meaningful Multicraft bonuses and applied Ingenuity refunds, including `+14 extra` and `+218 refunded`. Shorten the partial-return note without changing what it means.
- Keep normal native `ANCHOR_RIGHT` positioning and explicitly enable screen clamping. No custom tooltip coordinates or scale overrides; titles/subtitles retain native wrapping and shared UTF-8-aware name bounds.

## Integration and Hover Precedence
- Replace generic column-text tooltips for recipe tables and every craft-history list. Migrate Catalogue and reagent-used recipe rows, recipe/craft detail titles, Outcomes quality-row backgrounds, most-crafted tiles, pinned recipes and non-item activity indicators.
- Concrete output, reagent and returned-item cells/icons retain native Blizzard item tooltips with safe name fallback. No global item-tooltip hooks or injected summary text.
- Child item hovers prevent parent overwrite; deferred owner-aware leave handling restores a still-hovered parent without a competing hide. Row reuse/reset, scrolling, refresh and hiding clear stale owned content.
- Preserve existing row navigation and propagated item-child clicks. Other specialized informational/control tooltips remain unchanged.

## Measurement Integrity
- Period, character and profession filters still apply to the same public API queries. Recipe outcome queries receive only supported dimensions; filtered durable history enforces profession scope and mismatched populations do not supply metrics.
- Multicraft and Ingenuity use their observed denominators. Resourcefulness uses only the authoritative cohort; additional legacy/unverified positives do not enter that rate.
- Missing craft measurements say `Not recorded`, unavailable aggregate measurements say `Not available`, and observed negative outcomes say `No proc`.
- Extra output remains an absolute measured bonus, not a fabricated percentage. Unknown character identities remain known-only counts. Pruned details retain durable history with an explicitly labeled UTC-day timestamp fallback.

## Validation
- PASS: `bash src/addon/scripts/package.sh`: trace, adapter, ledger, public API and addon/UI suites, plus creation and integrity/content checks of Core, UI and bundle ZIPs.
- PASS: targeted UI regressions after each substantive edit, editor diagnostics, `git diff --check`, and release-shell syntax checks.
- UI regressions cover scope/filters, single-day and cross-year labels, missing/mismatched profession selections, class colors, authoritative denominators, bounded legacy notes, partial/pruned history, omitted matching output names, differing outputs, preserved quantities/bonuses/refunds, native clamping/anchor calls, long/missing names, multi-output result rows, item fallback, parent/child/sibling hovers, deferred restoration, clicking, scrolling, hiding and row reuse.
- The unchanged additional CurseForge matrix gate was not run locally because the container lacks Python; GitHub CI installs its Python YAML prerequisite.

## Remaining In-Game Validation
- The four supplied screenshots establish the current styling, not the final edge/scale geometry. Recheck the polished layout near every screen edge and at small UI scales, especially long recipe names, partial Resourcefulness history and returned-material names.
- Lua mocks verify normal anchor/clamping calls, not native font metrics, screen geometry, hit-testing, asynchronous item loading, quality/effects, frame strata, taint or actual flicker.
- Move between row text, item cells and Highlights, then between sibling items and outside the journal; check filtering, scrolling, modal close and window hide, and confirm navigation.
- Public Core exposes one output identity per result record. Multi-output activities remain separate factual rows; no operation-wide output is synthesized. Exact last-crafted timestamps require retained detail, otherwise only the durable UTC day is available.

Documentation reflects the compact preview contract and live-client checklist. This PR remains open and must not be merged as part of this task.

body:
Adding a vLLM TorchTPU recipe for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 inference on Ironwood (tpu7x) with **llm-d prefill/decode disaggregation (1P1D)**, benchmarked with the InferenceX **AgentX** workload, under `inference/ironwood/vLLM/vLLM-TorchTPU/Qwen3.5-397B/llm-d-pd-1p1d`.

- Topology: two single-host tpu7x 2x2x1 slices, one prefill engine (PCP8, prefix caching, host KV-cache tier) and one decode engine (DP8, prefix caching).
- KV transfer: TorchTPU Raiden connector (`TPURaidenConnector`); on prefill it runs in `TPUMultiConnector` with `TPURaidenOffloadingConnector`.
- Router: llm-d Endpoint Picker in standalone mode with an Envoy sidecar as the model endpoint. Engines are discovered by pod label scoped to the release, so no Gateway API, InferencePool CRDs or cloud load balancer are needed. Decode runs the llm-d routing sidecar.
- Client: InferenceX AIPerf `inferencex-agentx-mvp` scenario on the `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k` traces, concurrency 32 for 3600 s.
- Pinned versions: vLLM TorchTPU nightly image and llm-d v0.11.0 router images (see the versions table in the README). Weights download from Hugging Face; no GCS bucket needed. Reservation and Kueue settings are optional.
- The README includes steps to verify that KV actually moved from prefill to decode.

The chart was installed as-is with `helm install` on a tpu7x GKE cluster: both engines became Ready, KV transfer through the router was confirmed in the logs with output identical to a direct decode request, and the full AgentX run completed with no failed requests.

author: jyviko
body:
Closes the implicit solver's first gaps (M4): reference points, kinematic and distributing couplings, moments, and the wedge6 element.

## What
- **wedge6** (`modelcraft-fem`): triangle × interval shape functions, 3-point triangle × 2-point Gauss rule, a new element table row, extrapolation. It passes the patch tests and converges like hex8 on the cantilever.
- **Reference points and couplings** (`modelcraft-solver::constraints`): every reference point a coupling names gets 6 dofs.
  - Kinematic coupling is a rigid link (RBE2 semantics).
  - Distributing coupling is a least-squares rigid fit with equal weights, the same weights the deck writers use.
  - Every constraint row and every prescribed value is removed by master–slave elimination, with the Abel–Shephard pivot choice, so the reduced matrix stays SPD with no penalty and no multipliers.
  - Reactions are T_pᵀ(Ku − f), including forces and moments at a reference point.
  - A model without couplings gives bit-for-bit the same numbers as before (hash-checked).
- **Moments and forces on reference points; BCs on all 6 dofs.** Static results include `reference_points`; `solve.probe` accepts reference point labels.

## Verification (analytic)
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| wedge6 patch test | displacement 1e-19, stress 1e-15 |
| wedge6 cantilever convergence | 64.6 → 3.0 % error over 4 meshes, rates 1.01 / 1.56 / 1.85 |
| Rigid motion through a prescribed reference point (kinematic and distributing, 4 element kinds) | displacement ≤ 1e-14, stress ≤ 2e-12 |
| Clamping through a fixed coupled reference point vs direct clamp | displacement difference 0; frequencies agree to 1e-9 |
| Distributing force vs equivalent pressure, Saint-Venant region | σxx 1.6e-6 (hex20), 1.1e-5 (hex8 incompatible modes) |
| Bending by a reference point moment through a distributing coupling | σ = Mz/I within 5.7e-4; deflection 1.7e-7 |
| Tube torsion by a moment on a kinematically coupled reference point | twist 0.010 %, surface τ 0.19 % |

## Concerns
- A distributing coupling whose reference point has a BC pivots a mesh dof onto all of the coupled dofs. That puts a dense 3N×3N block in K, which gets costly for very large faces.
- "Reference point not coupled" is reported by the solver. It belongs in `model.check`, so that deck exports report it too.

## Handoff
`.agent-files/handoffs/HANDOFF_solver-couplings-wedge.md` (local).
