No incluye CRUD, Storage ni búsqueda, ni toma ninguna de las decisiones R1–R9.

## Migración `20261013120000_rooms_deleted_account_writes.sql`

Es aditiva y sigue el mismo patrón que `housing_preferences`: cada política FOR ALL del propietario se divide por comando, `to authenticated`.

| Tabla | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|
| `rooms` | `rooms_owner_write` (ALL) | `rooms_{insert,update,delete}_own` |
| `room_addresses` | `room_addresses_owner_only` (ALL) | `room_addresses_select_own` (misma condición de lectura) + `room_addresses_{insert,update,delete}_own` |
| `room_images` | `room_images_owner_write` (ALL) | `room_images_{insert,update,delete}_own` |

- Las políticas de escritura mantienen la condición de propiedad y exigen además que el perfil del propietario exista y no tenga `deleted_at`. En UPDATE se exige en USING y en WITH CHECK.
- **No cambian:**
  - la lectura (`rooms_select_active_public`, `rooms_select_own` y `room_images_select`);
  - `rooms_admin_all` y el trigger de moderación;
  - los GRANT, funciones y triggers;
  - `service_role`, que tiene BYPASSRLS. No se añade ningún uso del cliente admin.
- **No oculta** las habitaciones activas de una cuenta desactivada: esa decisión es R7 y sigue pendiente.
- **Sin recursión:** las políticas de `profiles` no consultan tablas de habitaciones, y las de `rooms` no consultan `room_addresses` ni `room_images`.
- Pasan a ser 44 políticas (37 − 3 + 10).

## Pruebas

**`tests/db/15_rooms_integrity.sql`** (71 aserciones):
- **RI0:** estructura y GRANT.
- **RI1:** un propietario activo escribe en las tres tablas.
- **RI2–RI4:** otro usuario no escribe en filas ajenas, y ni él ni `anon` leen la dirección exacta.
- **RD0–RD5:** una cuenta que se desactiva a mitad del test, con el mismo JWT, ya no escribe, pero sigue leyendo sus filas.
- **RE1:** una cuenta desactivada desde el principio no crea habitaciones.
- **RX1–RX3:** el admin y `service_role` siguen pudiendo escribir.
- **RL1–RL2:** la lectura no cambia.
- **RI9 (control negativo):** si se reintroduce temporalmente la condición anterior a la 4.0, la cuenta desactivada vuelve a escribir.

Las negativas fallan por permisos, no por otra causa:
- con el GRANT intacto, un `42501` es de la RLS («new row violates row-level security policy»);
- cada INSERT rechazado se repite con los mismos datos y entra;
- cada UPDATE o DELETE que afecta a 0 filas va precedido de una comprobación de que la fila es visible.

**Infraestructura:**
- **P3 del preflight:** la lista exacta de 44 políticas, más una comprobación de que cada escritura de habitaciones exige `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- **`preflight-selftest`:** 6 mutaciones nuevas.
- **Recuentos:** pasan de 37 a 44 en `tests/db/10`, `13` y `14` y en `sql-suite-selftest`.
- **`migration-upgrade-selftest`:** UP6–UP7, con habitaciones creadas antes de la migración.
- **`validation-infra`:** el total de 44, las 14 políticas de habitaciones y la comprobación de P3.

## Resultados en local (PostgreSQL 16 del entorno)

- `test:db`: 376/376 (305 + 71). La línea base en `master` era 305/305.
- `test:infra`, todo en verde:
  - `sql-suite-selftest`: 78/78 («376 = 376»);
  - `preflight-selftest`: 50/50, con 42 mutaciones;
  - `migration-upgrade-selftest`: 10/10.
- `npm run test`: 1032/1032.
- `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check` y `git diff --check`, sin errores.
- **Mutaciones contra `test:db`:** 9/9 detectadas, sobre copias en el scratchpad.
  - Cuatro neutralizan la comprobación con `or true` sin quitar su texto; las detecta el comportamiento (RD2–RD4), no la guarda estática.
  - Las otras cinco: vuelve `rooms_owner_write`, UPDATE sin propiedad, dirección legible por todos, UPDATE de imágenes sin la comprobación, y sin la migración.

## Documentación

- `docs/DATABASE.md`, `docs/SECURITY.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md` (Fase 4 en curso, la 4.0 y las decisiones R1–R9 sin tomar) y `PROGRESS.md` (sesión 42).
- **`docs/SUPABASE_VALIDATION.md`:** se actualiza la descripción vigente de P3 y se avisa de que un run contra `roomly-validation-3` fallaría en P3 hasta resolver R8.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** solo la línea «Fase 4: no empezada», que contradecía a `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## Límites

- **Sin validar en Supabase real.** `roomly-validation-3` tiene las 37 políticas anteriores, y su workflow no aplica migraciones a un esquema que ya existe. No se ha lanzado ningún run.
- No cubre Storage, que todavía no existe.
- El mock de E1 no tiene habitaciones, porque la aplicación aún no las usa.

body:
## Egresos: la misma pantalla y el mismo funcionamiento en los dos CRM

Diego, 10/10: «Egresos se empareja: la misma pantalla y el mismo funcionamiento en los dos CRM (paridad). Se comparan las dos versiones, se queda con lo mejor de cada una y se lleva a los dos.»

El mismo PR va en diego-landaeta/CRM y en diego-landaeta/CRM-ISEIE, con los ficheros del módulo **idénticos**.

### Qué había
| | MultiCRM | CRM-ISEIE |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | dentro de `accounting` (`/api/accounting/expenses`), sin servicio | módulo `expenses` (`/api/expenses`) con servicio + además una copia en `accounting` sin usar |
| Ámbito | empresa + campus de la persona (#245) en el listado | solo un campus; con «todos» mandaba `-1` → 400 |
| Ver/editar/borrar uno | sin mirar el ámbito | sin mirar el ámbito |
| Totales | «0 registros · 0 €» siempre (no se rellenaban) | suma de las 20 filas cargadas |
| Paginación | estado a medias, nunca pedía la página | ninguna |
| Comprobante | por fetch con token | `<a href>` → 401 siempre |
| Alta con empresa puesta | `project_id: -1` → 400 | — |

### Qué queda (en los dos)
- **Un solo módulo `expenses`** (routes/controller/service/model/validation) en `/api/expenses`; `/api/accounting/expenses` sigue como alias (los comprobantes ya subidos guardaron esa dirección).
- **Por empresa**, como el resto de Finanzas: `issuerId` → sus campus con `proyectosDelAmbito`, dentro de los campus de la persona. Ver, editar y borrar uno también se recortan (404 si no es tuyo).
- **«De quién es»**: un campus, **toda una empresa** (nuevo, `expenses.issuer_id`) o general (solo super admin/soporte). Un gasto de empresa cuenta en la empresa y en cada uno de sus campus; los generales siguen contando en todos los ámbitos, como ya hacía el panel.
- **`GET /api/expenses/resumen`**: total, nº, sin campus y por categoría sobre todo el filtro (mismo WHERE que la tabla).
- El **panel de Finanzas** cuenta los egresos con la misma regla (`condicionDeAmbito`): listado y panel dan la misma cifra.
- Pantalla: tarjetas de totales, reparto por categoría (clic filtra), búsqueda, categoría, origen, fechas con atajos (este mes / mes pasado / este año), paginación de 50, CSV con el mismo filtro, `?new=1` abre el alta.
- Egresos automáticos (cuenta por pagar / Stripe): 409 al editarlos o borrarlos a mano.
- Hook de cuentas por pagar en MultiCRM: usa `expenseService.createFromPayable`, como ISEIE.
- MultiCRM: el buscador (Ctrl+K) y la tecla «n» apuntaban a `/accounting/expenses`, que no existe; ahora a `/finanzas/egresos`.

### Migración
`204_egresos_por_empresa.sql` (el mismo número en los dos): `expenses.issuer_id` + FK a `invoice_issuers` + CHECK «campus o empresa» + índice + permisos para `crm_user`/`crm_iseie_user`. **No mueve datos.** Idempotente. Sin aplicar.

### Pruebas
- `backend/tests/egresosParidad.test.js` (la misma en los dos, mocks de `db.js`): 27 ✓.
- `menuSinRutasRotas`: ✓ en los dos. `tsc --noEmit`: MultiCRM 0 errores; ISEIE 13 (los mismos ajenos de antes). `vite build`: ✓ en los dos.

author: ptone
body:
Refs ptone/scion#4817

## Summary
**C2, the broker half of the fix for the sync-create teardown.**

The problem: a synchronous create runs `Manager.Start` under the broker request's context. When the hub stops waiting, that context is cancelled mid-start. The hub can stop waiting through its 120s synchronous dispatch timeout and its control-channel cancel frame, the control channel closing, a hub restart, or a dropped HTTP request. The Kubernetes runtime then reads the start as abandoned and deletes the pod and its Secrets, often while the image is still pulling on a cold node. The broker also removes the agent's files.

This PR fixes that on the broker side:
- `pkg/runtimebroker/sync_start.go`: the create's registration context and the start context (`bind`) keep the request context's values (policy hook, skill resolver, hub defaults, worktree) but drop its cancellation.
- Once a start has begun, only these cancel it:
  - a stop, a delete, or a newer start of the name (through the launch registry);
  - broker shutdown;
  - the broker bound `api.SyncStartCeiling` (15m).
- Before the start begins, the request ending still ends the create with 409 `start_cancelled`, as before. This is checked after `buildStartContext`, at the async `handOff`, during the supersede wait, and again immediately before `bind`.
- New `pkg/api/start_bounds.go`: `SyncStartCeiling`, shared with the hub. C1 sizes its unconfirmed-create holds and run-adoption quiet period from it.
- `k8s_runtime.go` and `controlchannel.go`: comments only.

## Base and pairing
- **Based on upstream main**, which already contains #4701 (GCP#3396, merged upstream as 23f2789e). This replaces #4937, which was stacked on `scion/as-supersede-dev`. The 4 commits here are #4937's, cherry-picked onto upstream main without conflicts; the change is identical to the one reviewed there (verify review r5).
- **Pairs with #4936** (C1, as-teardown-dev, the hub half; stacked on #4891). C1 keeps the agent row and the start claim on the hub's own dispatch deadline instead of rolling the create back, and imports `api.SyncStartCeiling`. **The two land together.** On its own, C2 only keeps a start whose hub stopped waiting but sent no rollback delete. A hub that rolls the create back still ends the start with its delete, as today.

## Tests
- New in `sync_start_test.go`: the request ending does not cancel a running start; a delete (with the hub's projectId/runId/agentId) still cancels it after the request ended; the start has the broker bound.
- New in `sync_start_detach_test.go`: the request ending during the supersede wait, during build, before bind (sync), and before handOff (async) each give 409 with no start. A stop, a newer create of the name, and broker shutdown each cancel a start whose request has ended.
- Gates at 45d5135f (b02, coordinator-run, fault checks in a private copy of the repo):
  - guard: pkg/hub not imported by runtimebroker, runtime or api;
  - vet clean on all three;
  - 49/49 targeted tests pass by name;
  - all 12 named mutants plus both base-semantics targets KILLED (rc=1, named FAIL, line hit, no panic).
- Code review: async-start r1 to r4 (APPROVE at b9fd0f23), and r5 (APPROVE at 45d5135f: matching patch IDs, empty normalised diff-of-diffs).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- ptone/scion#4872: the start and restart of an *existing* agent (`startAgent`/`restartAgent`) still run under the request, so a sync start or resume over the hub's timeout is still torn down.
- With C1: a WARN log for a start that succeeds after its request ended, and a retry of the hub's rollback delete.

author: koftwentytwo
body:
## Summary

This is the core part of collaboration phase (g): the realtime channel and record version conflicts (spec `docs/COLLABORATION.md` §9.1 and §6.5, #1136). Presence itself is qbit-collaboration's job.

**Bus:**
- `RealtimeBusInterface`, `RealtimeMessage` and `InMemoryRealtimeBus` (the default), configured through `RealtimeMetaData`.
- `EsbRealtimeBus` (qqq-esb) publishes to `qqq.realtime`, configurable. Each pod consumes with a non-durable, non-shared subscription, the same as the ESB control topic, so every pod delivers to its own connections.
- Delivery is best-effort.

**Producers:**
- After commit, record changes publish `record.changed` (field names only, never values) and `record.deleted` on `record:{table}:{pk}`, plus `table.changed` on `table:{table}` (coalesced). This applies only to tables whose resolved features include PRESENCE or FOLLOW.
- The overlay publishes `metadata.changed`.

**`RealtimeHub`** (javalin), one per server:
- connections with channel security, and per-subscriber filtering of field visibility;
- a replay buffer with `resync`;
- limits on connections and channels;
- periodic re-checks (`channel-revoked`) and `session-ended`.

**Endpoints** (UI API 1.2.0, open entry):
- `GET /qqq/v1/realtime/stream` (SSE), with one typed schema per event;
- `POST /qqq/v1/realtime/subscriptions`, for the channels `record:`, `table:`, `user:me` and `instance`. Channels the user can't see are refused without saying why.

**Record versions:**
- `QTableMetaData.recordVersionField`, defaulting to the modify date.
- `UpdateInput.expectedVersions`.
- The v1 update takes `?expectedVersion=`; a stale version gets a 409 `RecordConflictV1`. Callers that send no version are unaffected.
- The check runs before the write; it is not an atomic compare-and-swap. That is documented.

Docs: `docs/misc/Realtime.adoc`, and the `UI-API-CHANGELOG.md` 1.2.0 entry. `MiddlewareVersionV1.FEATURES` lists `recordFeatures` and `realtime`.

## Test plan
- [x] Local: core green.
- [x] qqq-esb `verify`: 285 tests, including the embedded-Artemis realtime bus.
- [x] Javalin: the realtime stream and subscription tests (hello, refusal, record.changed delivery, replay and resync, 404 for another session's connection), 409 conflicts, and the UI API contract test against the regenerated `openapi.yaml`.
- [x] The remaining Windows-only javalin failures (static-file route providers) match develop.
- [ ] CircleCI.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ryansolid"} -->
_Requested by **Ryan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01UH2PzGJGK1iPC3PtHLeSDw?thread=cmsg_01UH2PzGJGK1iPC3PtHLeSDw6ZNYqxbXZr8oz3tKD85Lpx)_

Before: on a route with a bare `GET(fn)` source in `serverRouteComponent`, a link's preload and the render that followed it each sent the same request. Even with #680, a click sent two identical GETs, and with `no-store` the browser ran them one after the other.

After: the render mounts the call the preload already started, so one visit sends one request.

The preload's result is handed to the next render with the same args, once, within the same 5 s window `query()` gives a preload. A later visit calls fresh, as a bare GET always does. Concurrent preloads of the same args share one call. A failed preload isn't handed on, so the render retries. `query()` and `liveQuery()` sources, plain functions and the server render are unchanged. Because each result reaches exactly one render, a frame stream is never mounted twice, which answers the open question in the issue.

How: `handOffPreloads` in `src/serverRouteComponent.ts` wraps the source once, so it covers both `preloadRoute`'s `server.call` and the render's `call`. It tells them apart by `getIntent() === "preload"`, and keys by `JSON.stringify(args)`.

Closes #677.

## Testing
- Added four specs in `test/server-routes.spec.tsx` under "a bare GET source". Two of them fail without the fix.
- `pnpm test`: 700 + 96 server specs and types all pass
- `pnpm build`: clean

author: andrest50
body:
## Summary

Indexed messages carried `committee_uid` and `is_private`, copied from the parent mailing list at index time via the `groupsio-subgroup-committee` KV mapping. Any change to a list's committee or visibility left already-indexed messages stale, so weekly briefs could include or miss messages for the wrong committee.

This removes those copies. The committee association is now resolved from the mailing list at query time by the consumer (see the committee-service PR below).

## Changes

- `GroupsIOMessage`: remove `CommitteeUID` and `IsPrivate`, plus the `committee:` tag and parent ref. Messages keep `mailing_list:{uid}` and the `groupsio_mailing_list:{uid}` parent ref.
- Message handler: stop reading the `groupsio-subgroup-committee` mapping, which also removes the NAK that waited for it. The NAK on a missing group-ID → mailing-list mapping is unchanged.
- Subgroup handler: stop writing the `groupsio-subgroup-committee` mapping; remove `KVMappingPrefixSubgroupCommittee`.
- `docs/indexer-contract.md`: update the message schema, tags and parent refs, and document how to find a committee's messages.

## Deployment order

**Do not deploy until [lfx-v2-committee-service#228](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-v2-committee-service/pull/228) is live.** The committee service currently queries messages by the `committee:` tag; once it resolves a committee's lists first, nothing reads the removed fields. Deploying this first would make weekly briefs lose mailing-list activity.

## Notes

- Already-indexed messages keep the old fields until re-indexed; nothing reads them, so this is harmless.
- Existing `groupsio-subgroup-committee.*` keys in the KV bucket are left as orphans.
- Artifacts have the same fields but nothing queries them by committee; out of scope here.

## Testing

- `go test ./cmd/... ./internal/... ./pkg/... -race` passes
- New message handler test asserts no committee/visibility fields or tags are emitted and that no subgroup committee mapping is required
- `make lint` reports only issues that exist on `main` (gitignored `scripts/tmp` typecheck errors and one staticcheck finding in `pkg/constants/kv_keys.go`)

## Ticket

[lfx-self-serve#1844](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-self-serve/issues/1844)

author: peterichardson
body:
In the filter editor, a long pattern now scrolls, so you can see what you type. After a wide character or a tab, the cursor is in the correct column, and the status text does not cover the search badge.

## Changes

- `SearchPrompt::window` gives the part of a field that fits its width, and the cursor column in it. It keeps a scroll offset and moves it only when the cursor would go off one side, so movement inside the shown text moves the cursor, not the text. A wide character under the cursor is shown whole.
- The editor's five text fields draw through `window`. A tab draws as four blanks, as in the file lines.
- `SearchPrompt::cursor_column` (the bottom row) counts columns, not characters.
- The status row measures its badges with `UnicodeWidthStr::width`, and the search badge elides at 32 columns, not 32 characters.
- One `TAB` constant now serves the prompt and the editor's lines.

## Not covered

The bottom prompt row does not scroll. It shares the row with the badges and a message, and the issue asks for scroll in the editor fields only.

## Tests

Seven new tests (cursor after wide characters, a tab in a field, scroll on a long pattern and a long name, a wide character at the right edge, the bottom-row cursor, the search badge width). Each one failed before the fix. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` pass.

Fixes #361
Addresses F104 from the project review.

author: estarinazx
body:
Eligible Antigravity targets could appear as Medium-only in the Desktop catalog, and Responses forwarding could replace the caller's selected effort with the panel default. This patch advertises Low/Medium/High for eligible targets and preserves the selected literal value, with native descriptors and unsupported-effort guards intact.

It also adds `wisp antigravity-compat on|off|status`, an explicit Claude client compatibility option that defaults off in both Bridge hosts. Opted-in positioned-system Messages requests receive the client's supported capability rejection before credential lookup or provider dispatch. Fixed system instructions remain system instructions; later reminders may become user context and some feature reminders may be omitted. A new Claude conversation is needed after changing the option. Signed Desktop hoisting remains unchanged.

Release versions are terminal/npm **2.2.7** and companion **1.14.4**; wisp-slot is unchanged.

Validation:

- Pinned Bun 1.4.2: frozen-lock install, 1,347 core tests, 142 TUI tests, both typechecks and companion packaging passed.
- Windows compiled binary and extracted npm shell: packaged CLI/Desktop smokes and isolated compatibility-command checks passed. Local npm archive integrity and VSIX bundle contents verified.
- Actual installed Desktop backend loaded Low/Medium/High and retained High after catalog refresh/restart against synthetic upstream responses.
- Fresh combined independent review found no actionable defects; 50 synthetic local requests checked the affected boundaries.
- [All four native PR jobs passed](https://github.com/EstarinAzx/Wisp-Router/actions/runs/38475782114) at reviewed head `1ff61c8ac8a78795e30afa202b6ebb044367bf61`: Windows x64, macOS arm64, macOS x64 and Linux x64, including compiled CLI and signed Desktop smokes. The CI merge tree matches the reviewed source exactly.

Limits are explicit in the release notes. The bounded real-provider fallback comparison stopped on SAFETY, so cache benefit and historical plateau repair are not established. The separate actual-target effort check stopped at the first Low request with HTTP 429; Medium/High were not sent and usage/cause/target acceptance remain unknown. Interactive Desktop selection, provider-internal allocation and installed VS Code host behavior are not proved by the offline checks. Neither optional mode nor Desktop integration is enabled by this patch.

body:
## Summary

Adds manufacturer ID `0x046D` (NOVON) to `manufacturers.json`, plus device configuration files for the five certified NOVON Z-Wave products.

The manufacturer ID was assigned after the last registry refresh — `manufacturers.json` currently ends at `0x0466` (Nabu Casa) and jumps to `0x5254` (Remotec) — so these devices currently show up as `Unknown manufacturer 0x046d`.

| SKU | Product | Fingerprint | Certification | SDK |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVN-100 | On/Off Switch | `0x046d:0x2774:0x1a2d` | [ZC14-26090636](https://products.z-wavealliance.org/z-wave-product/novon-on-off-switch/) | 7.23.1 |
| NVN-110 | Dimmer Switch | `0x046d:0x2774:0x1a2e` | [ZC14-26090639](https://products.z-wavealliance.org/z-wave-product/novon-dimmer-switch/) | 7.23.1 |
| NVN-200 | On/Off Plug | `0x046d:0x27d8:0x1a2f` | [ZC14-26090637](https://products.z-wavealliance.org/z-wave-product/novon-on-off-plug/) | 7.24.1 |
| NVN-210 | Dimmer Plug | `0x046d:0x27d8:0x1a30` | [ZC14-26090638](https://products.z-wavealliance.org/z-wave-product/novon-dimmer-plug/) | 7.24.1 |
| NVN-220 | Outdoor Dual Plug | `0x046d:0x283c:0x1a31` | [ZC14-26090635](https://products.z-wavealliance.org/z-wave-product/novon-outdoor-dual-plug/) | 7.24.1 |

Each file links its user manual in `metadata.manual`.

## Templates

Adds `devices/0x046d/templates/novon_template.json` with the bases shared across these devices: `auto_timer`, `three_way_type`, `alternate_exclusion`, `switch_mode`, `led_color`, `intensity_1-7`, `indicator_brightness`, `factory_reset`.

Master templates reused: `led_indicator_three_options`, `led_indicator_four_options`, `orientation`, `base_0-65535`, `base_enable_disable`, `base_options_nounit`, `minimum_dim_level_1-99`, `maximum_dim_level_1-99`, `default_dim_level_0-99`, `state_after_power_failure_off_on_prev`.

## Source of the parameter data — worth flagging

**The Z-Wave Alliance certification records for all five products submit `min = 0, max = 0` for every configuration parameter**, and list only a subset of the parameters the user manuals document — the NVN-100 record certifies 4 parameters where its manual documents 9.

Parameter ranges, defaults and option meanings in this PR are therefore sourced from the published user manuals rather than the Alliance database. I'm flagging it explicitly so the disagreement doesn't read as an error during review. I'm raising the record quality internally as well.

## NVN-200: identification only

`nvn-200.json` deliberately contains no `paramInformation`. Its user manual is published as a scanned document with no recoverable text layer, so no parameter ranges or option meanings could be sourced for it. Its Alliance record lists parameters 3, 41, 42 and 84 with defaults but — as above — no usable ranges.

I would rather ship identification only than guess; the parameters can follow in a later PR once documented. The manufacturer/model labels still improve for users today.

## Associations, endpoints, compat

- **No `associations` blocks** — all five devices support Association Group Information V3, so group names and node counts come from the devices themselves.
- **No `endpoints` block** on the NVN-220 despite its two outlets: two Binary Switch endpoints over Multi Channel V4, handled natively.
- **No `compat` flags** — all five run SDK 7.23.1 or 7.24.1, so none of the `7xx`/`8xx` firmware-bug templates apply.

## Checks

- `yarn lint:configjson` — clean.
- `yarn lint:zwave` — **0 errors.** The 10 warnings it reports are all pre-existing on `master`; none are in `0x046d/`.
- Confirmed all five fingerprints resolve through `ConfigManager`, and diffed every resolved parameter (value size, range, default, options, unit) against the manuals.

Disclosure: I work at Novon; these are our own products.

author: philibea
body:
## Context

Next.js refuses to serialize `undefined` values in data returned from `getStaticProps`/RSC payloads (`"undefined cannot be serialized as JSON. Please use null or omit"`, vercel/next.js#14059). The codegen (companion MR in `pipelines`) now **omits absent response keys entirely**, so unmarshalers never emit an `undefined`-valued key.

## Change (response path only)

- `unmarshalDate`: returns `null` instead of `undefined` for a present-but-unparseable value. Needed because the codegen emits `unmarshalDate(data.x)` inside a presence-guarded key — the value itself must never be `undefined`.

Absent dates are handled by the codegen guard (key omitted), so this only covers the present-but-invalid case.

## Notes

- Request-side behaviour untouched (`resolveOneOf` unchanged).
- Companion codegen MR: `pipelines` `!968` (protoc-gen-sdk-ts marshalling template — omit absent response fields).

author: brendon
body:
## Description **Stacked on #1572**, which changes the same function in `checkBlockNesting`. The first commit here is #1572's; this PR's change is the second commit, c8b77d0d. Once #1572 is merged I'll rebase this onto `main`. Blocks pasted into a list item ended up directly inside the `
    `, `
      ` or `
      ` (#1573): ```html

        one

        two

      ``` `checkBlockNesting` moves the caret out of any block missing from `dtd.blockLimits` and stops at the first one listed. `ul`, `ol` and `dl` are listed but `li`, `dd` and `dt` weren't, so the caret left the item and landed in the list itself, and the item was removed when empty. 1. `li`, `dd` and `dt` join `blockLimits`. Like `td`, they hold flow content, so pasted blocks stay in the item: `

      • one

        two

      `. Chrome's and Safari's own `execCommand('insertHTML')` give the same result. 2. With `li` as a limit, a pasted list would go inside the item too, leaving an empty bullet above a nested list. So when a list is all of the inserted content and the caret's block limit is an `
    1. `, the list is unwrapped and the caret moves after the item, which is removed if it's empty. The pasted items join the list: `
      • x
      • y
      ` in place of an empty item, `
      • item
      • x
      ` after a non-empty one, and an `
        `'s items take the `
          `'s type. This also matches the browsers' own paste, except that they split an item when the caret is in the middle of its text, while this puts the items after it, as `checkBlockNesting` does with a table pasted into the middle of a paragraph. A list pasted into a table cell inside a list item stays in the cell, since the cell is the nearest limit. - `src/plugins/dtd/config.ts`: add `dd`, `dt` and `li` to `blockLimits` - `src/plugins/dtd/before-insert/check-block-nesting.ts`: unwrap a pasted list into the list item's list - `src/plugins/dtd/README.md`: the new defaults and the list behaviour - `src/plugins/dtd/dtd.test.js`: blocks pasted into `li` and `dd` items stay in them; a pasted list joins the list (empty item, non-empty item, `
            ` into `
              `, an item holding an empty paragraph, a nested list), the caret ends after its last item, and a list stays inside a table cell in an item I also checked the paste path in Chromium and WebKit. Suggested changelog line: > Blocks pasted into a list item stay inside it instead of landing directly in the list, and a pasted list adds its items to the list it's pasted into. ## Related Issue Fixes #1573 ## Checklist - [ ] There is an associated issue labeled `bug` or `enhancement` (#1573; I can't set labels on this repo) - [x] Code is up-to-date with the `main` branch - [x] `npm test` passes locally (Chrome Headless: 2454 passed, 9 skipped) - [x] New or updated tests validate the change 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

ctech-wallet as a participant of the ctech-account deletion saga (`docs/plans/2026-10-07-account-deletion-participant.md`):

- Idempotent purge: PII copied to a write-only retention table (5 years) then stripped; `wallet_users` anonymized; `wallet_audit` loses only `ip`/`user_agent`; the ledger is never touched.

- Fail-closed JWT revocation check on money/consent routes; erasure consumer + ack with a dedicated client.
- CDK: erasure queue + DLQ + alarm, state/retention tables, `gsi_user` on deposits/withdrawals/holds, scoped IAM (audit updatable only on ip/user_agent, retention write-only), env.
- Docs: ENDPOINTS, OPERATIONS runbooks, CLAUDE.md files, README, restoration spec.

## Before enabling in prod

Deploy DynamoDB first and wait for the three `gsi_user` indexes to be ACTIVE; seed the dedicated ack client and SSM parameters; add wallet to account's `ERASURE_PARTICIPANTS`; run the dev IAM check for `wallet_audit` (OPERATIONS §7).

`go vet`, `go test -race`, integration suite (DynamoDB Local), CDK tests (12), pix-gateway build/tests green.

author: ezraellette
body:
## description

Deepgram restarts its speaker numbers on each live stream, so the microphone and the meeting audio can both report `speaker 1`. Since #7281 the transcript panel shows these as `Microphone · speaker 1` and `Meeting audio · speaker 1`. Two places still used the raw label:

- The rendered transcript used by the summary prompt, the full meeting markdown, the meeting chat transcript and the transcript copy action. Adjacent mic and remote turns were merged into one `[speaker 1]` turn, so the summary agent saw remote speech attributed to the same person as local speech.
- The screen-reader live announcement.

This moves the panel's existing label code into `sourceQualifiedSpeakerName` in `meeting-context.ts` and uses it in both places. Custom names, `me` and empty labels are unchanged.

Scope: this deliberately does not relabel mic voices as `You`. #6625 keeps stream-local labels because one microphone can carry more than one person. Stored labels, `session_speaker_id` and speaker identity are unchanged. author: ph14
body:
## Behavior

An upper OCI layer containing only `restricted/file` used to change a lower
layer's explicit `restricted/` mode from 0700 to 0755. The staged tar extractor
created an implicit parent, and the layer merge treated its default mode as an
upper-layer directory update. The prepared rootfs also recorded that incorrect
mode, changing execution behavior and image identity.

Implicit upper parents now retain an existing lower directory's mode and owner.
New implicit parents remain root-owned with fixed mode 0755, and an explicit
upper directory header still replaces lower metadata. An opaque whiteout still
removes lower children, while the surviving directory retains its metadata,
including when an archive repeats the marker.
This corrects the prepared image identity for affected layered images.

Whiteouts also work under read-only lower directories for ordinary host users:
only the directories traversed or removed for a whiteout receive temporary
owner access, and their original modes are restored. Ordinary upper-file
addition under a read-only lower directory continues to preserve its mode.

Closes #549.

## Verification

- Red-before `apply_layer` regression: lower 0700 + upper child produced 0755.
- Red-before repeated opaque-whiteout regression: the second marker changed
  lower 0700 to the host-created 0755 directory mode.
- Green-after OCI library suites: 134 tests on macOS and 134 on msr1 Linux.
- Both hosts produce the same updated prepared-image identity golden.
- Red-before on ordinary-user macOS: nested entry and opaque whiteouts under
  lower 0555 directories failed with EACCES; the entry case succeeded as root
  on msr1. Green-after on macOS and unprivileged msr1 Linux for both whiteout
  forms, nonempty directory-tree deletion, and an ordinary upper-file addition.
  Removing the subtree-opening call makes the focused regression fail EACCES.
- OCI Clippy and repository pre-push checks passed.

author: zeroliu
body:
Relates to Brevilabs/obsidian-copilot-private#180

## Why

Every agent decides for itself when to summarize a long chat, and Copilot gave no way to change that. A user who wants long Claude, Codex or opencode sessions to compact earlier (cheaper turns, fewer hard overflows) or later had to edit each agent's own config file outside Obsidian. For opencode that did not work at all, because Copilot generates the whole opencode config. Today a Claude chat compacts around 967k tokens, Codex at the 500k Copilot sets, and opencode just before its model's window fills.

## What

Settings → Agents gets a **Custom auto-compact threshold** switch. Off keeps each agent's own default and sends nothing. On shows a **Compact at** slider (100k to 1M tokens, step 10k) that moves each agent's automatic compaction point. The agents keep a small reserve for the summary, so compaction starts slightly before the chosen size. The value is synced and is separate from the v3 chat's `autoCompactThreshold`.

| Agent | What the threshold does | When a change takes effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude | Becomes Claude's auto-compact window. Claude ignores any window under 100k and keeps a 33k reserve, so 100k compacts at about 67k. | Next message, no notice |
| Codex | Replaces `model_auto_compact_token_limit` in the CODEX_CONFIG Copilot already sets (500k by default). It also wins over the same key in a user CODEX_CONFIG override. | "Codex config has changed" with **Reload** (held while a chat is open) |
| opencode | Becomes `compaction.buffer`, the headroom opencode keeps below the model's window: smallest enabled-model window minus the threshold. Sent only when every enabled opencode model has a known window and the threshold is below it. | "opencode config has changed" with **Reload** |

- The 100k floor exists because Claude silently ignores smaller windows and Codex compacted after every tool call at 20k. Saved values outside 100k to 1M, or not numbers, are corrected or dropped when settings load.
- With several opencode models of different windows, opencode measures from the smallest, so larger-window models compact later than the value chosen.
- A `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` override in Claude's environment takes precedence over this setting, and turning the setting on re-enables Claude's auto-compaction even if it was off in Claude's own settings.
- Docs: new section "Choose when long chats compact" in the Agent Chat page.

## Non goal

- A "never auto-compact" choice. Codex has no off switch, so one control cannot offer it for every agent. Claude and opencode could support it later with a hard-overflow warning.
- Percentage-of-window thresholds. Only Codex takes a token count directly and the other two need the model's window anyway.
- opencode agent-native models (the `opencode/*-free` rows). Their records carry no context window, so the setting has no effect on them yet. A follow-up fills those windows from the model catalog, and this change needs nothing more once they exist.
- Changing the v3 chat's `autoCompactThreshold`, or the manual `/compact` command.
- Pinning Codex's `model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope`.

## Screenshot

Settings → Agents in the real plugin, with the switch on and the slider at 100k (dark):

![ui-2-custom-100k](![ui-2-custom-100k](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f7caa4e-1192-48ab-8d4c-c7065037a06a))

The two states of the control in the component gallery, switch off in light and switch on in dark:

![gallery-light-BackendDefault](![gallery-light-BackendDefault](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fb7c124-e1e8-43b6-a634-e69819115970))

![gallery-dark-CustomThreshold](![gallery-dark-CustomThreshold](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db014bca-30eb-4204-b57a-df52128ba4ec))

Claude with the threshold at 100k compacted on its second long read (76k to 19k tokens); the same two reads with the switch off reached 107k with no compaction:

![21-claude-on-done](![21-claude-on-done](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63a883d7-bb9c-483f-940d-e4614141d67a))

Codex with the threshold at 100k compacted at about 94k and kept working:

![32-codex-on-done](![32-codex-on-done](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e46743e-85ff-47be-b81c-b4d661c4635a))

Changing the threshold while a Codex chat is open offers a reload:

![30-codex-config-changed-notice](![30-codex-config-changed-notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a921211-8e5f-4dec-8b3c-85fb35f2a5c5))

## Risk

**Medium**

| Criterion | Status | Reason |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| No behavior change, or a cosmetic/copy/docs/config change visible where it renders, or deterministic tests cover the changed behavior | ✅ | Unit tests cover the setting's range handling, the Claude, Codex and opencode wire forms, "Backend default sends nothing" for each, the reload trigger, and the control; when an agent really compacts is human-verified |
| A defect would fail CI or be obvious on first use | ❌ | A wrong wire form passes CI and only shows as a chat that compacts at the wrong size |
| A revert fully restores prior state, including persisted data | ✅ | The new `agentMode.autoCompactTokens` key is optional; after a revert the old sanitizer drops it |
| No auth, permissions, secrets, or input-handling surface changes | ✅ | None touched |
| No public API, plugin API, message, or on-disk contract changes | ✅ | One optional settings key; absent means today's behavior |
| No core-path concurrency, async-lifecycle, or state-machine changes | ✅ | The reload reuses the existing hold-behind-Reload path with a new trigger |
| No hot-path behavior lacks deterministic coverage | ✅ | Each changed branch has a unit test |
| No new dependency | ✅ | Dependency manifests unchanged |
| Human-only behavior stays in one feature area and surfaces quickly | ✅ | Limited to long Agent Chat sessions; a wrong point is visible as the "Context compacted automatically" row |

Review: read `buildOpencodeConfig` and `opencodeCompactionBuffer` in `src/agentMode/backends/opencode/OpencodeBackend.ts` for the window rule, `mergeCodexConfigEnv` in `src/agentMode/backends/codex/codexConfigEnv.ts`, `ClaudeSdkBackendProcess.prompt` in `src/agentMode/sdk/ClaudeSdkBackendProcess.ts`, the `restartOnAutoCompactChange` subscriber in `src/agentMode/index.ts`, and `sanitizeAgentMode` in `src/settings/model.ts`; then run Verification steps 1 to 3.

## Verification

1. Open Settings → Agents. Turn on **Custom auto-compact threshold** and drag **Compact at** to 100k. Reopen settings and confirm the value stayed; turn the switch off and confirm the slider disappears.
2. Claude: with the switch on at 100k, start a Claude chat and ask it to read two large source files in full (for example `src/agentMode/session/AgentSession.ts`, then `src/agentMode/sdk/sdkMessageTranslator.test.ts`). A "Context compacted automatically" row appears once the chat passes about 67k. Repeat in a new chat with the switch off and confirm no compaction at the same size.
3. Codex: open a Codex chat, then change the slider. "Codex config has changed" appears with **Reload**; choose it. Keep reading large files until the chat passes about 100k and confirm "Context compacted automatically"; with the switch off (and Reload) the same reads do not compact.
4. opencode: with an agent-native model such as `opencode/Cat Jam Free`, changing the setting still offers a Reload but has no effect on compaction (known windows are missing until the follow-up). With a model whose context window is known (a Copilot Plus or catalog BYOK model), a 100k threshold compacts near 100k.

## Note

Verified against Claude Code 2.1.296, codex-acp 2.2.2 and opencode 2.0.22. Not verified: a Claude window larger than the model's own window (every Claude model available here has a 1M window), and a populated user `~/.claude/settings.json` was only checked with project settings. Evidence and logs are in the Step 8 evidence folder under `.context/compact-epic/evidence/s

author: mjtechguy
body:
## Limits for each person

**Admin → Directory → Limits** sets what applies to everyone; **Limits** on a row under **Admin → Users** gives one person, agent or service account values of their own.

| Limit | Counts | At the limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Storage | The Drive files and recordings a person owns (trash included) plus the mail in their mailbox | Uploads and copies are refused with the reason. New mail is turned away with `452 Mailbox is full`; other members of a group address still receive it |
| Messages sent per hour, per day | Messages the person sends. Notices Helix sends in their name (sharing, access requests) are not counted | The message is refused with the limit it reached, including an agent's send that a person has confirmed |

- Nothing is limited until an administrator sets a value. An empty value for one person means "use the default"; an empty default means "no limit".
- Storage is counted when needed (`helix_actor_storage_usage_bytes`), not kept in a counter, so it cannot drift. A file counts against its owner, whoever uploads it or adds a version.
- People see their own storage against their limit in the Drive sidebar.
- Changes are audited as `person_limits.updated`.

Before this the console had no way to set any limit: the Limits list on Workspace settings is display-only.

## Removed: limits that did nothing

- **Accounts**, **AI tokens per month**, **AI images per month** were stored and shown, and nothing in the server read them. They are removed from the settings and any saved values are dropped.
- **Mail sending "60 an hour, 200 a day"** was declared on the tools and shown on the Mail status page, and nothing applied it. Per-tool `rateLimit` declarations are metadata only; the registry enforces budgets for agents, not for people. The numbers are removed, and `MAIL_SEND_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR` / `_PER_DAY` are no longer read.

## Fixed: confirming an agent's mail failed

`mail.reply` from an agent is held for a person, as intended. When the person confirmed it, the send failed with "Mail thread not found": approved work ran inside the approver's request transaction with the approver's database identity, and mail row security lets a person reach only their own mailbox.

Approved work now runs as whoever asked for it. `withRequesterPostgresActor` sets the database actor to the requester inside a savepoint of the same transaction and restores the approver afterwards, on success or failure. It stays in one transaction because the approval's audit entries already hold the organization's audit-chain lock, which a second transaction would wait on. The registry gained a `runAsRequester` option for this; to keep the file inside its size limit, `resolveAutomationDecision` moved to `tools/automation-policy.ts`.

This applies to every confirmed action, not only mail.

## Testing

- `infra/scripts/production-boot-smoke.sh`: 92 checks pass. New: mail for a full mailbox is turned away, the limit is handed back and mail is accepted again, an agent's reply is confirmed and sent from the agent's mailbox, and a reply past the agent's sending limit is refused even when confirmed.
- Integration under the runtime database role: per-person limits (defaults, overrides, storage counting files and mail, full-mailbox refusal, sending limits excluding notices) and the requester identity switch (during, after, on failure, nested).
- Playwright with axe: the Limits page (2 tests). Unit: updated menus, settings page, routing.
- Live on the LAN demo with a real account (10 checks): the dialog from the Users row, a send refused at the limit, an upload refused, inbound mail answered `452 Mailbox is full`, the Drive sidebar meter, and everything restored.
- `pnpm format:check`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`, `quality:boundaries`, `quality:file-size`, `quality:duplicates`, knip.

Migration `0227_person_limits.sql`.

author: hamzamerzic
body:
Follow-up to #1853, covering the four points its final review left open.

## What changed

**Helper host start.** When a Codex helper host is cancelled while it starts, it closes itself under the lease lock. That close was awaited plainly, so a second cancel released the lock while the host was still shutting down. It is now settled, like the other two close sites under that lock. The process group is also captured before the cancel check, so this close ends the group instead of leaving it to the SDK's exit alone.

**Lint coverage for `run_in_threadpool`.** The lock lint in `tests/test_settled.py` only matched `asyncio.to_thread`. It now also matches Starlette's `run_in_threadpool` (bare, or through `starlette.concurrency` or `fastapi.concurrency`) and `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`. Applying it turned up five sites:

- Settled, because they write: recording an upload and its cleanup on failure (`routes/uploads.py`), discarding a draft (`routes/uploads.py`), and saving a chat checkpoint (`routes/chat_continuity.py`).
- Marked read-only: the provider sign-in check before a provider switch (`routes/chats.py`).
- Also settled, though the lint can't see it because it is reached through a called coroutine: the expired-upload sweep that a send runs under the chat lock (`upload_lifecycle.py`).

The policy text in `app/settled.py` now names these calls too.

**Update-batch races** (these predate #1853):

- **Retry.** `retry_start` reran the boot-time load while the server was serving requests, and that load changed records, saved them and woke progress listeners from a worker thread. The load now only reads the receipts and works out what their unfinished entries settled to, off the loop. The outcomes are applied on the loop, the settled receipts are written in one settled call, and the records become visible only once they are saved.
- **Prune during refresh.** A prune that ran during a refresh deleted a receipt that the refresh then wrote back. Two guards now prevent this, whichever runs first:
  - a save skips a record that is no longer current;
  - a prune skips a batch whose save is in flight, and the next prune removes it.

**Cancel just after a public write.** A new test cancels a single-PR Send just after `_submit_prepared_pr` has opened the PR and recorded a `complete` receipt. The settled call finishes first. The record is left `submitting` with its signed receipt, and the next Send settles that exact PR from the receipt, with no new push or create, then clears the receipt. This found no gap, so the route is unchanged.

## Tests

Each behaviour fix has a test that fails on main:

- `test_helper_hosts`: a cancelled Codex host start holds the lease lock through two cancels until its process group has been killed.
- `test_uploads`: cancelling an upload's record write, or a draft discard, holds the chat lock until the write ends.
- `test_settled`: the lint sees every plain thread call form. On main the lint itself reports the five sites above.
- `test_app_update_batches`:
  - a retry reads off the loop before any record is visible, and applies the outcomes on the loop;
  - a prune during a refresh is never written back;
  - a prune skips a batch whose save is in flight.
- `test_github_routes`: the post-write cancel recovery above. It is a regression guard and passes on main.

Runs:

- `test_settled`, `test_helper_hosts`, `test_uploads`, the chat route suites (`test_chats`, `test_chats_stream_*`, `test_chat_continuity`), `test_app_update_batches`, `test_github_routes` and the contribution suites: 1019 passed.
- Neighbouring suites (Codex runner, chat streams, skills context, platform tools, retired sessions): 383 passed.
- `scripts/test.sh --fast`: passed.
- `ruff check app tests`: clean.

## Problem and result

`python -m scripts.acceptance verdict` with no `--workspace` silently invented a fresh `run-<timestamp>` path, and with a missing path it crashed with a `FileNotFoundError` traceback. docs/acceptance.md also did not say that its commands rely on the two exports, that `rehearse` and `run` each seed their own workspace, or how `verdict` finds a run, and it still described the directory trust screen as unnamed and unanswerable (issue #383, shipped in 0.13.0), named only the default trust record paths and listed three of the five recognized dialogs.

`verdict` now resolves its run through `finished()`, which raises `BridgeError` with `next_command` (`ls -d ~/.local/state/parley-acceptance/run-*`) when no workspace is named or the path holds no `acceptance/` records; `main` prints it in the shared refusal shape and exits 2. Every flag now has `--help` text and `--lane` shows its `NAME:PROVIDER[:PROFILE]` format. The runbook states the same-shell requirement, passes `--workspace` to `run` and `verdict`, explains rehearsal workspaces, describes the `directory-trust` dialog and per-profile trust records, lists all five dialogs and adds a `directory-trust` proof step. body:
## Summary

Ports the six document text-sync guards that `extension/test/docs.test.ts`
(node) ran into `cmd/yt2column/extension_docs_test.go`, so they run under
`make test` without node or npm. Reuses the doc helpers in
`cmd/yt2column/docs_test.go` and `makefile_test.go`. The node copies are removed
in a later PR (phase 2). Covers steps 1-3 to 1-11 of the task 0012
implementation plan.

The extension ID is derived from the manifest `key` (base64 -> DER -> `x509`
parse/re-encode -> SHA-256 -> first 16 bytes -> digits `a`-`p`); no fixed ID is
stored in the test. The requested-permission list is read from code spans that
are item names (a code span followed by its parenthesised reason), so an
incidental code span inside a reason (`chrome.storage.session`) is not mistaken
for a permission and the comparison stays bidirectional. The plan 5.1 row
labels are built from numbers, keeping the literal `AC-<digit>` out of the Go
source.

Each of the six guards was break-checked before the commit, with the mutation
restored between runs; the operations and results are recorded in the commit
message of `cea59b6`.

## レビュー観点

- 拡張 ID を `manifest.json` の `key` から導出し（base64 → DER → `x509` で公開鍵に再エンコード → SHA-256 の先頭 16 バイト → 各桁 `a`〜`p`）、文書側に固定値を置かないこと（ステップ 1-4・1-5、AC-02、architecture §3.4）
- `sectionByHeadingPrefix` の境界（見出し行を結果に含めず、レベルを問わず次の見出し行の手前で止まり、見出しがなければ空文字列）が小さな単体テストで固定されていること（ステップ 1-4、architecture §3.2）
- 6 種の検査が `make test` で走り、node も npm も起動しないこと、かつ各 guard を実装したコミットで対象を壊すと落ちることを確かめてコミットメッセージに記録していること（ステップ 1-3〜1-10、AC-01・AC-11）
- `ext-` ターゲットの抽出規則（`Makefile` は行頭 `ext-<名前>:`、`CLAUDE.md` は行頭 `` - `make ext-<名前>` ``）と、`Makefile` から 1 件も集まらないときに失敗させること（ステップ 1-6、AC-03、architecture §3.3）
- 検査 6 の期待する行ラベルを `AC-<数字>` のリテラルで書かず、番号からヘルパで組み立てること（ステップ 1-10）

## Notes

- Critical-review (senior Go engineer / senior SRE) found no Critical or Major
  issues; the Minor findings were applied in a follow-up commit.
- `make fmt`, `make test`, and `make lint` pass.

author: mrbeldum
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2803. `ExtractIPFromXFFHeader` scans the `X-Forwarded-For` chain from the right, returning the first untrusted IP. Behind Azure Front Door that stops at the proxy's public egress IP instead of reaching the client: with `XFF: client, <Front Door egress>` and a private `RemoteAddr`, the extractor returns the egress IP.

This PR adds a new `TrustOption`, `XFFLeftmost()`, that opts into scanning from the left, returning the first untrusted IP from that direction. All existing trust options keep applying (a trusted leftmost entry is skipped), and default behavior is unchanged.

```go
e.IPExtractor = echo.ExtractIPFromXFFHeader(
    echo.XFFLeftmost(),
)
```

## Safety caveat

Only use `XFFLeftmost()` when the outermost proxy strips incoming `X-Forwarded-For` headers and is the sole writer of the chain. Otherwise the leftmost entry is client-controlled and can be spoofed (a client can prepend arbitrary addresses; Front Door appends the real client IP to the end). This is documented on the option and in the IP-address guide in `ip.go`. If the edge does not strip incoming headers, trust the proxy's address ranges with `TrustIPRange` instead.

## Tests

- Reproduced #2803 first: on the reporter's chain (`XFF: 203.0.113.195, 203.0.113.199`, `RemoteAddr: 10.0.0.5`) the default extractor returns `203.0.113.199` (the proxy); with `XFFLeftmost()` it returns `203.0.113.195` (the client).
- New `TestExtractIPFromXFFHeaderLeftmost`: 8 cases covering the reporter scenario, trusted entries skipped on the left, all-trusted fallback, invalid entry falling back to `RemoteAddr`, no-XFF fallback, multiple header values, bracketed IPv6, and composition with `TrustIPRange`.
- `go test ./...`: root package passes except 4 pre-existing environment failures (`TestEchoStaticRedirectIndex`, `TestStartConfig_*`) that fail identically on the clean tree; `middleware` fully passes. `gofmt` and `go vet` clean.

Prepared with AI assistance.

author: nethalo
body:
## What changes for an operator

A long-running command's daily beacon gains two fields. No other event carries them.

| Field | Values | When |
|---|---|---|
| `install_age` | `<7d`, `7d-30d`, `30d-90d`, `>90d` | every beacon |
| `previous_version` | major.minor | only the first beacon after that daemon is upgraded |

To compute them a daemon keeps `telemetry-install.json` in the telemetry folder: a calendar day (`first_seen`, never sent) and the last major.minor per daemon name. Neither is an identifier: every install that started that day, or runs that release, has the same values. `bintrail telemetry off` and the web interface toggle delete the file. `bintrail telemetry show` now prints the beacon as well, computed from the real record without writing anything.

`docs/TELEMETRY.md` ("No persistent identifier") is rewritten to say exactly this, including what it costs: on a small population two wide ranges and a version do narrow things down, which is why the ranges are wide, `previous_version` rides on one beacon, and neither is ever on an event with a `run_id`.

Schema version goes 1 → 2.

## Behaviour that had to be right

- **Sent only if it can be remembered.** The record is saved before the beacon is spooled; if it cannot be saved (or is there and cannot be read) the beacon goes out without the fields. If the beacon then cannot be spooled, including when it is dropped at the spool size cap, the daemon re-reads the record and takes back its own entry (only if it is still what it wrote, so another daemon's save in between survives). So `previous_version` is never repeated daily and never spent on an event that does not exist. `appendEvent` returns `errSpoolFull` instead of a quiet nil for that reason.
- **Per daemon, and only upgrades.** Two daemons can share the folder at different versions; with one shared value each would report the other's version as "previous" every day. Two processes can also share a daemon *name* (`bintrail stream` and `bintrail-pg stream`, or a rolling upgrade), so the record only moves up and only an upgrade is reported. A downgrade is not.
- **A tampered file puts nothing on the wire** beyond one of four ranges and an ASCII major.minor of at most three and four digits. Fields degrade one by one; a wrong type in one does not drop the other.
- **Opt-out, two fixes.** (1) A running daemon resolved consent once at start, so `telemetry off` typed next to it was recorded and ignored until the next restart. It now follows a recorded opt-out at its hourly check and deletes what it wrote in between (one direction only; a control that outranks the file keeps the decision). (2) The web interface stopped the live process *after* cleaning the disk, so a beacon in flight could write back what was just deleted. It now stops it first; `SetRuntimeConsent` and `Beacon` share the client's lock and the beacon re-checks consent inside it.
- The web interface no longer returns server paths or environment values in telemetry errors; they go to the server log.

## Tests

`internal/telemetry/install_test.go` has one test per rule above. Twenty-four single-site mutations of the new code (no restore, fields sent when the save fails, daemon ignoring a recorded opt-out, shared version, relative read with no folder, unreadable-as-empty, no re-check under the lock, cap returning nil, widened version bound, …) each turn at least one test red.

## Deployment order

The ingestion side already accepts and validates both fields and blanks them on any event that is not a beacon. A release of this is safe to ship.

## Known limits (documented)

- An install that was running before this release has no recorded start: its age counts from its first beacon on this release.
- A patch release is not a version change (the version is truncated to major.minor), and a downgrade is not reported.
- `previous_version` is spent when the beacon is spooled; a batch lost in delivery loses it.

author: satyajitghana
body:
## What & why

Vercel's per-path usage showed most outgoing bytes in two places. The first was JavaScript: every article page downloaded **every article's interactive widgets**, about 2.2 MB gzipped per view. The second was media served from Vercel instead of R2. This PR fixes the JavaScript, trims `/articles`, and makes the media-map step say why it fails.

## Type of change

- [x] Interactive component or site feature
- [x] Crew / tooling (skills, agents, hooks, scripts)

## Changes

- **Per-page widget loading.** `/articles/[slug]` imports MDX through one template-literal `import()`. Next does not code-split client components imported by a server component, so all 1,112 widgets sat in the route's entry chunk. The fix has three parts, and no article changes:
  - `lib/mdx/remark-lazy-widgets.mjs` rewrites each MDX import of a `"use client"` module under `components/articles/` into a small client loader.
  - `components/mdx/lazy-widget.tsx` pulls the widget from `components/mdx/widget-registry.generated.ts` with `React.lazy`, one chunk per widget.
  - Server-component imports are left alone.
- **Registry upkeep.** The registry is regenerated in `predev` and `prebuild` (`pnpm gen:widgets`). `pnpm validate:widgets`, now part of `pnpm validate`, fails when the committed registry is stale. The plugin is registered in `next.config.ts` and in `validate:mdx`.
- **`/articles`:** each description is cut to its opening sentences with `snippet(…, 320)`. Search is its only reader, since every rated card shows `why`.
- **`scripts/media-map.mts`:** the index fetch now sends a named `User-Agent` and retries 3 times. On failure it logs the HTTP status and Cloudflare's `cf-mitigated` header.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** documents the mechanism and the new check.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm validate` passes, including the new `validate:widgets`. ESLint is clean on the new files.
- [x] `pnpm build` passes. The largest function trace went from 108.8 MB to 90.3 MB.
- [x] Route entry JS for `/articles/[slug]` went from 7.36 MB raw / 2.00 MB gzipped to **0.43 MB raw / 0.12 MB gzipped**, read from the client reference manifest.
- [x] In headless Chromium, an article page loads about **0.8 MB raw** of JS, against about 7–8 MB before. Checked on budgetpix, representation-guidance, natura-1, groundingpi and `/articles`.
  - Widget HTML is server-rendered (the BudgetPix slider is in the raw HTML).
  - After hydration the slider updates the widget.
  - No hydration warnings. The only console error is `/_vercel/insights/script.js`, which exists only on Vercel.
- [x] `check:agents`: 56/56 against `next start`.
- [x] `/articles` HTML went from 2.80 MB to 2.56 MB raw.

## Notes

- **Not in this PR: why production serves no media from R2.** Every film, poster and figure on the live site is same-origin, although `NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_BASE` is set and the R2 index matches every file. This PR's logging will put the reason in the next build log's `media-map:` line.
  - The likely cause is Cloudflare's bot rules blocking the build's fetch of `media.thesatyajit.com/ai/index.json`.
  - The other possibility is a Vercel build command that skips `prebuild`.
- **Check on the preview:** that article widgets render and respond, and what the build log's `media-map:` line says.
